scenarios.scenario: First-time meeting (casual)
scenarios.context: Two people meet for the first time in a casual setting.

speakerA.en: Hi! I'm Alex.
Nice to meet you too. Are you new here?
Welcome! Where are you from?
I'm from Chicago. Do you like it here?
Great! See you at lunch.
Hey, I don't think we've met. I'm Jamie.
speakerA.fa: هی، فکر نکنم همدیگر را دیده باشیم. من جیمی هستم.

speakerA.en: How do you do? I'm Mr. Johnson.
speakerA.fa: خوشوقتم؟ من آقای جانسون هستم.

speakerA.en: I'm doing well, thanks. Is this your first time here?
Pleased to meet you. I'm Dr. Lee.
speakerA.fa: از دیدار شما خوشحالم. من دکتر لی هستم.

speakerA.en: The pleasure is entirely mine. I hope we can talk further later.
I'm good, thanks. Are you a friend of Julia's?
I'm from Toronto, but I live here now.
I'm a nurse at the city hospital. And you?

speakerB.en: Hi Alex, I'm Jordan. Nice to meet you.
Yes, I am. It's my first day.
I'm from Canada. And you?
Yes, I like it. Everyone is very nice.
Yes, see you later. Bye!
Hey Jamie, I'm Taylor. How are you?
speakerB.fa: هی جیمی، من تیلور هستم. چطورید؟

speakerB.en: Nice to meet you too, Chris. How's it going?
speakerB.fa: من هم از ملاقات شما خوشحالم، کریس. اوضاع چطوره؟

speakerB.en: How do you do, Mr. Johnson? I'm pleased to meet you.
speakerB.fa: خوشوقتم آقای جانسون؟ از ملاقات شما خوشحالم.

speakerB.en: Likewise, Dr. Lee. I've heard so much about your work.
It's an honour to meet you, Dr. Lee.
speakerB.fa: مایه افتخار است که شما را ملاقات می‌کنم، دکتر لی.

speakerB.en: Yes, we work together. Where are you from?
Oh, nice! What do you do in the city?
I'm a designer. I work from home.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about well-being (general)
scenarios.context: After greeting, one asks how the other is doing.

speakerA.en: Hello!
I'm fine, thank you. And you?
A little. I have a class at ten.
Thank you! Have a nice day.
How are you doing?
speakerA.fa: اوضاع چطوره؟

speakerA.en: How's everything going?
speakerA.fa: همه چیز چطور پیش می‌ره؟

speakerA.en: How's life treating you?
speakerA.fa: زندگی با شما چطور برخورد می‌کنه؟

speakerA.en: How have you been lately?
speakerA.fa: این روزها چطور بوده‌اید؟

speakerA.en: What's up with you these days?
speakerA.fa: این روزها چه خبر از شما؟

speakerA.en: Well, I'm here if you ever want to talk about it.
How was your weekend?
speakerA.fa: آخر هفته‌ات چطور بود؟

speakerA.en: How was your day?
speakerA.fa: روزت چطور بود؟

speakerA.en: How are things at work?
speakerA.fa: اوضاع سر کار چطوره؟

speakerA.en: That's great! Did you have a good trip last week?

speakerB.en: Hello! How are you today?
I'm good, thanks. Are you busy today?
Oh, I see. Good luck!
You too. Bye!
Pretty good, thanks for asking.
speakerB.fa: نسبتاً خوبم، ممنون که پرسیدید.

speakerB.en: Not bad, just busy as usual.
speakerB.fa: بد نیست، مثل همیشه مشغول.

speakerB.en: I'm doing well, actually. I just got a promotion.
speakerB.fa: در واقع خوبم. تازه ترفیع گرفتم.

speakerB.en: Could be better, but I can't complain.
speakerB.fa: می‌توانست بهتر باشد، اما نمی‌تونم شکایت کنم.

speakerB.en: It's been a bit stressful, but I'm managing.
speakerB.fa: کمی استرس‌زا بوده، اما دارم مدیریتش می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: My weekend was great! I went hiking.
speakerB.fa: آخر هفته‌ام عالی بود! رفتم کوهنوردی.

speakerB.en: My day was quite productive, thanks.
speakerB.fa: روزم نسبتاً پربار بود، ممنون.

speakerB.en: Work is hectic, but I enjoy it.
speakerB.fa: کار شلوغه، اما ازش لذت می‌برم.

speakerB.en: It was long, but good. I finished a big project.
Yes, it was wonderful. The weather was perfect.

scenarios.scenario: Greetings during the day
scenarios.context: People greet each other in the morning, afternoon, evening and at night.

speakerA.en: Good morning!
I'm fine, thanks. It's a nice day.
Good afternoon! Did you have lunch?
Good evening! Welcome home.
Good night. Sleep well!
Good morning! You're early today.
Good afternoon. Did you have lunch?
Good evening! Are you leaving now?
Good night! Sleep well. See you tomorrow.

speakerB.en: Good morning! How are you?
Yes, it is. See you this afternoon.
Yes, I did. Thank you.
Good evening! I'm tired today.
Thank you. Good night!
Yes, I have a meeting at eight o'clock.
Not yet. I'm going to eat in ten minutes.
Yes, I finished work early today.
You too. Get some rest!

scenarios.scenario: Chatting with a neighbor
scenarios.context: Two neighbors talk for a moment in the morning.

speakerA.en: Good morning! Nice weather today.
How is your family?
Everyone is well. Are you going to work?
Okay, have a good day!
Nice weather today. Are you going out?
How is your garden this year?
Did you hear the noise last night?
I'm going to the supermarket. Do you need anything?

speakerB.en: Good morning! Yes, it's sunny.
They are fine, thank you. And your family?
Yes, I am. I have a meeting at nine.
Thanks. You too. Goodbye!
Yes, I'm going to the market.
It's growing well. I planted tomatoes last month.
Yes, I did. I think it came from the street.
No, thank you. That's very kind of you.

scenarios.scenario: Greeting a colleague at work
scenarios.context: Two coworkers greet each other at the start of the work day.

speakerA.en: Good morning, David. Did you have a good weekend?
I stayed home and rested. Are you ready for the meeting?
No problem. Can I get you a cup of coffee?
Sure. Let's talk again at lunch.

speakerB.en: Yes, I did. I visited my parents. And you?
Almost. I need ten more minutes.
Yes, please. Black, no sugar.
Good idea. See you at twelve thirty.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting an acquaintance after a long time
scenarios.context: Two acquaintances meet again after several months and catch up.

speakerA.en: Hi, Sara! I haven't seen you in a long time.
What have you been doing?
That's great news! Do you like it?
We should have coffee soon.

speakerB.en: I know! It's been about six months.
I started a new job downtown.
I do. The people are very friendly.
Good idea. I'll send you a message.

scenarios.scenario: Small talk about weekend plans
scenarios.context: Two friends chat about what they are going to do at the weekend.

speakerA.en: Do you have any plans for the weekend?
That sounds nice. Where does she live?
Is it far from here?
Have a great weekend!

speakerB.en: Yes, we're going to visit my aunt.
She lives in a small town near the lake.
No, it takes about an hour by car.
Thanks. You too!

scenarios.scenario: Running into a neighbor after a long time
scenarios.context: Two neighbors meet on the street after not seeing each other for months.

speakerA.en: Hey, I haven't seen you for ages! Where have you been hiding?
That sounds tiring. Do you actually enjoy being on the road?
Well, you should come over for dinner once you've settled back in.
Perfect. It's been great catching up, even if it was only five minutes.

speakerB.en: I've been traveling a lot for work, so I've hardly been home.
Most of the time, yes, but I'm looking forward to staying in one place for a while.
I'd love to. I'll give you a call as soon as my schedule is clearer.
Same here. Let's not wait another six months next time.

scenarios.scenario: Chatting about the weekend at work
scenarios.context: Two colleagues talk about their weekends on Monday morning.

speakerA.en: Morning! Did you do anything interesting over the weekend?
That's a shame. I went hiking with some friends, and we got completely soaked.
Definitely, as long as the forecast looks better next time.
Sure, I'll send you the details once we've picked a date.

speakerB.en: Not really. I spent most of Saturday fixing my bike, and then it rained all day Sunday.
Honestly, that sounds more fun than my weekend. Would you do it again?
Then let me know. I've been wanting to get outside more often.
Great. Anyway, I should get some coffee before the meeting starts.

scenarios.scenario: Making small talk while waiting in line
scenarios.context: Two strangers talk while waiting at a busy café.

speakerA.en: This line is moving so slowly today, isn't it?
It's always like this on Fridays. Everyone seems to need coffee before the weekend.
Pretty often. They make the best cappuccino in the neighborhood.
I think you will soon. It looks like they've just opened another register.

speakerB.en: I know. I've been standing here for about ten minutes, and I'm already late.
You're right. Do you come here often, or is this a special occasion?
Good to know. I'll try it if I ever reach the front of this line.
Finally! Thanks for the company, it made the wait much more pleasant.

scenarios.scenario: Reconnecting with an acquaintance at a conference
scenarios.context: Two professionals meet again at a conference after several years.

speakerA.en: Well, this is a pleasant surprise. I don't think we've seen each other since the Lisbon summit.
Busy, but I can't complain. I took on a new role last spring, which has kept me on my toes.
It has its moments. I miss the hands-on work, but I enjoy mentoring younger colleagues.
You're too kind. Listen, the sessions are about to start, but let's grab a coffee afterwards and catch up properly.

speakerB.en: Has it really been that long? Time certainly flies. How have you been keeping?
Congratulations. I gather you've moved into management. Is it everything you hoped it would be?
That's what I've always admired about you. You seem to have a knack for bringing out the best in people.
I'd like that. I'll find you at the break, assuming the schedule doesn't overrun.

scenarios.scenario: Breaking the ice at a social gathering
scenarios.context: Two guests who don't know anyone else start a conversation at a party.

speakerA.en: I hope I'm not intruding, but you look about as lost as I feel. Do you know many people here?
Then we're in the same boat. I know the host through a friend, but he seems to have disappeared.
I couldn't agree more. Have you tried the canapés? I'm told they were made by a local chef.
Quite. Shall we introduce ourselves to a few people together? There's safety in numbers.

speakerB.en: Hardly anyone, to be honest. I only came because a colleague insisted I get out more.
It's a lovely place, though. Whoever organized this clearly put a lot of thought into the decor.
Not yet, but you've talked me into it. It beats standing awkwardly by the window.
Why not? Lead the way, and I'll follow your example.

scenarios.scenario: Making conversation with a taxi driver
scenarios.context: A passenger and a driver chat during a long ride into town.

speakerA.en: Busy night, is it? The streets seem unusually quiet for a Friday.
I don't blame them. I wouldn't be out myself if I weren't catching a late flight.
A bit of both, really. I'm attending a meeting, but I'm hoping to squeeze in some sightseeing.
So I've heard. Any recommendations for someone with only one free afternoon?

speakerB.en: You'd think so, but most people are staying in because of the weather. It's been a slow evening.
Business or pleasure, if you don't mind my asking?
In that case, you've chosen a good time. The city is at its best before the summer crowds arrive.
Skip the famous museums and wander through the old harbor district. It's where the city's real character shows.

scenarios.scenario: Navigating small talk at a diplomatic reception
scenarios.context: Two guests at a formal reception exchange pleasantries while sizing each other up.

speakerA.en: I don't believe we've had the pleasure. You must be the new cultural attaché everyone has been whispering about.
Modesty is a rare commodity at these gatherings, so I'll take it as a point in your favor.
It has been predictably cordial, which is to say that nobody has said anything of consequence.
Ah, but the art lies in knowing precisely when to land. I trust you'll know the moment when it comes.

speakerB.en: Guilty as charged, though I suspect the whispering has been rather more generous than the reality warrants.
Then I'll try not to squander it. Has the evening lived up to your expectations so far?
That's the beauty of the form. One can circle every topic of substance without ever landing on one.
I'll consider it my cue to stay close. Conversation of this caliber is rarely wasted on me.

scenarios.scenario: Rekindling casual conversation after an awkward silence
scenarios.context: Two colleagues attempt to smooth over a strained interaction in the elevator.

speakerA.en: It's remarkable how an elevator can make a minute feel like an hour, isn't it?
In fairness, our last exchange wasn't exactly a masterclass in diplomacy, at least not on my part.
That's generous of you. I'd hate for a single heated meeting to color everything that follows.
Then perhaps we could revisit the proposal over lunch, with a little less posturing on either side.

speakerB.en: Quite. I was beginning to suspect we'd both agreed to pretend the other wasn't here.
Let's not dwell on it. I'd say we both spoke more candidly than the situation called for.
Agreed. We work too closely for grudges to be anything but counterproductive.
I'd welcome that. Shall we say one o'clock, before the afternoon swallows us whole?

scenarios.scenario: Making conversation with someone from a vastly different background
scenarios.context: Two strangers at a long-haul layover find common ground despite their differences.

speakerA.en: Forgive the intrusion, but you've been staring at that departure board with the intensity of a man defusing a bomb.
Plenty, I'm sure, but airports have a way of rewarding the patient. Where are you headed?
That must be quite an emotional journey, as much as a physical one.
In my experience, the relationships that matter tend to prove sturdier than we fear.

speakerB.en: Has it been that obvious? My connection was delayed, and I'm calculating how many things could go wrong from here.
Nairobi, to see my daughter. She moved there three years ago, and this is my first visit.
It is. I find myself oscillating between anticipation and a faint dread of how much has changed.
I hope you're right. And you? You strike me as someone who knows his way around a layover.

scenarios.scenario: Running into a former colleague at a conference
scenarios.context: Two professionals meet unexpectedly years after working together.

speakerA.en: Good heavens, is that really you? It must be a decade since we last crossed paths, and you look remarkably unchanged.
Rather well, thank you. Life has taken me through three cities and two career changes since the old department was dissolved.
I'm entirely at your disposal until the keynote. Shall we find a quieter corner where we can actually hear ourselves think?
Then it's settled. I'll fetch the coffee, you save the seats, and we'll pretend we're not skipping the opening panel.

speakerB.en: You're too kind, though I suspect flattery is merely a way of buying time while you recall my surname. How have you been keeping?
So I'd heard through the grapevine, but I'd much prefer the unvarnished version from you, if you can spare a few minutes.
Splendid idea. The coffee here is dreadful, but the sofas are comfortable, and that counts for a great deal at these events.
Your reputation for tactful truancy precedes you. Lead the way, and I'll follow with a clear conscience.

scenarios.scenario: Making small talk with a stranger at a wedding
scenarios.context: Two guests who know hardly anyone else strike up a conversation at a reception.

speakerA.en: Forgive the intrusion, but you seem to be as much of a stranger here as I am. Are you with the bride's side or the groom's?
A tenuous connection, but a valid one. I'm here as the bride's former flatmate, which entitles me to a number of embarrassing anecdotes.
I make no promises, but I'll exercise discretion until at least the second glass. Have you tried the canapés? They're surprisingly inventive.
Anyone who can describe a canapé that way deserves company at dinner. Shall we see whether we've been seated anywhere near each other?

speakerB.en: The groom's, by a rather circuitous route. His mother and my aunt were at school together, which makes me a cousin by courtesy, I suppose.
I do hope you'll resist the temptation to share them during the speeches. Weddings tend to be unforgiving of well-meaning indiscretions.
I have, and I'm still trying to decide whether the beetroot one was a triumph or a cry for help.
Let's hope so. Otherwise I'm condemned to a table of the groom's accountants, who reportedly discuss depreciation for pleasure.

scenarios.scenario: Welcoming a long-standing client to a business lunch
scenarios.context: A manager exchanges pleasantries with a valued client before turning to business.

speakerA.en: Thank you for making the journey, Mr. Alvarez. I trust the traffic wasn't as punishing as the forecast suggested.
A wise strategy. Before we turn to the contract, I'd like to hear how your family is, if you'll permit a little indulgence.
I can sympathize; I went through the same adjustment two years ago. One eventually discovers that silence has its compensations.
Only when you are. The relationship matters more to us than any single clause, and I'd rather not rush it.

speakerB.en: It was manageable, thank you. I've learned to leave early and bring a good podcast, which turns most delays into something approaching leisure.
How kind of you to ask. My daughter has just begun her studies in Edinburgh, so the house is eerily quiet, and I'm not entirely reconciled to it.
So I'm told, though I'm still waiting for them to materialize. Now, I imagine you're eager to discuss the renewal terms.
That's precisely why we've stayed with you for so long. Shall we order first and negotiate over dessert?

scenarios.scenario: First-time meeting (casual) – full dialogue (A2)
scenarios.context: Two colleagues meet for the first time. You answer and ask back.

speakerA.en: Hi there! I don't think we've met. I'm Alex.
Oh, welcome! How are you finding it so far?
That's good to hear. Where did you work before?
About three years now. If you need anything, just ask me.
Sure! How about tomorrow at noon?

speakerB.en: Hi Alex! I'm Jordan. I just joined the team this week.
It's great, but there's a lot to learn. Everyone has been really helpful.
I worked at a small company downtown. What about you? How long have you been here?
Thanks, that's very kind. Maybe we can have lunch together sometime.
Sounds good. See you then!

scenarios.scenario: Asking about well-being – full dialogue (A2)
scenarios.context: Two old friends meet by chance. You ask the questions.

speakerA.en: Hey! Long time no see.
Pretty good, thanks. I've been busy with work lately. How about you?
That sounds tough. Are you getting enough rest?
Nothing special. Maybe I'll just relax at home.
Definitely! Let's text each other.

speakerB.en: Hey! Yes, it's been ages. How have you been?
Same here. I started a new project last month, so I'm quite tired.
Not really, but it should calm down soon. What are you doing this weekend?
That sounds nice. We should catch up properly soon.
Great. Take care!

scenarios.scenario: Saying good morning to a coworker
scenarios.context: Two coworkers meet at the office in the morning.

speakerA.en: Good morning, Sam!
I'm fine, thanks. Did you sleep well?
Not really. I'm a little tired.
Good idea. Thank you!

speakerB.en: Good morning, Lisa. How are you?
Yes, I did. And you?
Let's have some coffee.
You're welcome.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting a friend on the street
scenarios.context: Two friends meet by chance in the street.

speakerA.en: Hi, Maria! How are you?
I'm great, thanks. Where are you going?
Oh, nice. How is your mother?
Good. Say hello to her. Bye!

speakerB.en: Hi, John! I'm very well. And you?
I'm going to the market.
She's fine, thank you.
I will. See you soon!

scenarios.scenario: Small talk in the evening
scenarios.context: Two neighbors talk in front of their building in the evening.

speakerA.en: Good evening, Mr. Lee.
It was long, but good. And yours?
You need to rest now.
Have a nice evening!

speakerB.en: Good evening, Anna. How was your day?
It was busy. I worked a lot.
Yes, I'm going home to eat.
Thanks. Good night!

scenarios.scenario: Catching up with a former neighbor
scenarios.context: Two former neighbors meet by chance in the street.

speakerA.en: Is that you, Helen? I can't believe it! It's been years.
Pretty well, thanks. We moved to the other side of town two years ago.
I miss it sometimes, but the new house is bigger, and the kids have more space.
Twelve and nine already. We should meet for coffee and catch up properly.

speakerB.en: Daniel! You haven't changed a bit. How have you been?
I heard. Are you happy there? I remember you loved your old street.
That's good news. How old are they now?
I'd love that. Let me give you my new number.

scenarios.scenario: Making small talk at a work event
scenarios.context: Two people who don't know each other talk at a company party.

speakerA.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. Which department do you work in?
Oh, I've heard good things about your team. How do you find it so far?
That's great. I work in finance, so we don't see each other very often.
Absolutely. Perhaps we could have lunch together one day this month.

speakerB.en: I'm in marketing. I joined the company about six months ago.
I like it a lot. The people are friendly, and the projects are interesting.
True. Events like this are a good opportunity to meet people.
That would be nice. I'll send you an email on Monday.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting a neighbor in the elevator
scenarios.context: Two neighbors make small talk in the elevator on a Monday morning.

speakerA.en: Good morning! I don't think we've spoken before, although I've seen you here a few times.
I moved in about a month ago, and I'm still getting used to the building and the neighborhood.
It's quite nice so far, although the traffic in the morning is terrible. Have you lived here long?
That's a long time! You must know the area really well. Is there a good bakery nearby?
I'll try it this weekend. By the way, how was your weekend? Did you manage to get out of the city?
That sounds relaxing. Well, this is my floor. It was lovely talking to you, and I hope we'll meet again soon.

speakerB.en: Good morning! You're right, and I'm sorry that I haven't introduced myself. I'm Karen from apartment twelve.
Welcome to the building! You'll like it here. Most of the people are friendly, and it's usually quiet at night.
I know what you mean. I've been here for almost ten years, and I've never got used to the traffic.
I certainly do. There's an excellent bakery two streets away, and it opens at six, so you can get fresh bread before work.
It was pretty quiet, actually. We went to my sister's house in the countryside and spent most of the time in the garden.
Likewise! Have a great day, and if you ever need anything, just knock on my door.

scenarios.scenario: Running into an old classmate
scenarios.context: Two former classmates meet by chance in a supermarket and catch up.

speakerA.en: Is that really you? I haven't seen you since we graduated, which must be almost fifteen years ago!
I live in Leeds now, but I'm visiting my parents for a few days. What have you been up to all this time?
That's wonderful! I always knew you'd end up working with children. You were so patient with everyone at school.
I'm an engineer, and I've been working for a software company for the past eight years. It's busy, but I enjoy it.
I'd love that. Shall we exchange numbers, so that we can arrange something before I go back?
Great. I'll message you tonight. It was so good to see you after all these years!

speakerB.en: It is! I can't believe it. You haven't changed at all. What are you doing in town these days?
I'm still here. I became a primary school teacher, and I've been teaching the same age group for about ten years now.
That's very kind of you to say. And what about you? Last time we spoke, you were thinking about studying abroad.
That sounds impressive. We should definitely have a coffee together and talk about old times. Do you have any free time this week?
Of course. Here's my number. I'll introduce you to my husband too, and we could have dinner at our place on Thursday.
Same here! It's funny how some people from your past come back into your life when you least expect it.

scenarios.scenario: Making small talk at a professional conference
scenarios.context: Two attendees start a conversation during a coffee break at a conference.

speakerA.en: Hello, I don't think we've met. I was just wondering what you made of the keynote speech, since opinions seem to be quite divided.
I thought it was thought-provoking, although I'd have liked more concrete examples. Do you work in the same field as the speaker?
That must be fascinating. I've always been curious about how companies deal with change, particularly when employees are reluctant to adopt new methods.
That's a common obstacle. Have you found that communication tends to make the difference, or is it more a question of leadership?
I'd say it's a combination of both. By the way, would you be interested in joining the workshop this afternoon? I've heard that it's very practical.
Wonderful. Shall we exchange details, in case we don't have a chance to talk again before the end of the day?

speakerB.en: Hello, nice to meet you. I'm Claire. To be honest, I had mixed feelings about it. The ideas were interesting, but the delivery was a little long-winded.
I do, in fact. I advise organizations on restructuring, so I couldn't help comparing his points with what I see in practice every week.
It really is. The technical side is usually the easy part, whereas persuading people to leave their comfort zone is where most projects run into trouble.
I'd say it depends on the culture. Where trust already exists, a clear explanation is often enough. Where it doesn't, even the best leader may struggle.
I was planning to, actually. The speaker is supposed to be excellent, and it would be useful to hear some case studies rather than just theory.
Of course. Here's my card. I'd be glad to continue this conversation, and perhaps we could grab a coffee after the workshop.

scenarios.scenario: Reconnecting with a former colleague after years
scenarios.context: Two former colleagues meet at a train station and exchange news about their careers and lives.

speakerA.en: I can hardly believe it's you! It must be at least six years since we last worked together. You look exactly the same, if I may say so.
I left the company shortly after you did, and I've been freelancing ever since. It's been challenging, but I wouldn't go back to a regular office.
Mostly design projects for small businesses. I had never imagined that I'd be running my own studio, but one thing led to another, as they say.
To be honest, the freedom is wonderful, though the uncertainty can be stressful. Had I known how unpredictable the income would be, I might have hesitated.
That sounds like quite a change for you. I always thought you would stay in finance, so it's a real surprise to hear that you went into teaching.
I'd love to. Let's not let another six years go by. Why don't you give me your number, and I'll message you tonight?

speakerB.en: Is that really you? What a coincidence! And thank you, though I think the gray hair says otherwise. What have you been up to since the company reorganized?
That takes courage. I've often thought about doing something similar, but I've never quite dared to leave the security of a monthly salary.
That's wonderful. I remember how creative your presentations always were. People used to say that you'd end up on your own one day.
I can imagine. The first year is usually the hardest, but if you've survived that, you've probably built something solid. Do you enjoy it?
Life does take unexpected turns. I retrained as a teacher three years ago, and although the pay is lower, I've never felt more fulfilled in my career.
Definitely. It would be nice to catch up properly, without having to rush for a train. Here's my number, and I'll look forward to your message.

scenarios.scenario: Welcoming a visitor at a company reception
scenarios.context: A receptionist welcomes a visitor and makes them comfortable before an important meeting.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I have an appointment with Mr. Thompson at ten, but I'm afraid I'm a little early. Would it be all right if I waited here?
Thank you. The journey was easier than I expected, although I got slightly lost in the building. The entrance isn't very clearly marked from the street.
That would be lovely, I'd appreciate a coffee. Is it all right to take it with milk and no sugar? I've been traveling since five this morning.
It's my first visit to the city, actually. I'm only here for two days, so I'm hoping that this meeting goes smoothly, and that I can see a little of the center afterwards.
That's very kind of you. I may well take you up on the recommendation. A quiet restaurant would be ideal after such a busy day.
Thank you again for your hospitality. I must say, you've made me feel very welcome, and it's a pleasant way to start the day.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and welcome. Of course, please make yourself comfortable. Mr. Thompson is just finishing a call, and he'll be with you in about ten minutes.
I'm sorry about that. We've had several visitors say the same thing, and we're planning to put up a larger sign. Can I offer you something to drink while you're waiting?
Of course. Milk and no sugar, coming up. If you'd like, you can leave your coat here, and I'll hang it up. The weather has been a bit unpredictable this week.
Then you're in for a treat. The old town is only a short walk from here. If you tell me what kind of food you enjoy, I can recommend a few places that aren't too touristy.
I'm happy to help. There's a small restaurant by the river that serves excellent regional dishes, and it's quiet in the evenings. I'll write the address down for you.
It's a pleasure. Ah, I see that Mr. Thompson is ready. Please follow me, and I'll take you to the meeting room.

scenarios.scenario: Greeting a new neighbor with a gift
scenarios.context: A resident welcomes a new neighbor with a small gift and offers practical advice.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I hope I'm not disturbing you. I live in the apartment next door, and I wanted to welcome you to the building with a little something.
It's only a loaf of homemade bread and some jam. I wasn't sure what you'd like, but I find that people appreciate something simple when they're surrounded by boxes.
Not at all. I've lived here for almost twelve years, so if you have any questions about the area, from the best supermarket to which bus to take, I'd be glad to help.
The recycling is collected on Tuesday and Friday, and the bins are in the courtyard behind the building. The caretaker, Mr. Lopez, is very helpful if anything needs repairing.
I'd say that the building is quiet, on the whole. There's a family with young children upstairs, but they're considerate, and I've never had any complaints about noise.
Please don't hesitate to knock if you need anything. It's nice to have friendly neighbors, and I think that we'll get along very well.

speakerB.en: Good evening. Oh, how kind of you! Please come in. Excuse the mess, I've only been here since this morning, and I haven't unpacked anything yet. I'm Elena.
That's so thoughtful, and I'm starving, as it happens. I haven't had time to buy any groceries. Thank you very much, it's an extremely generous gesture.
That would be wonderful. I don't know the neighborhood at all, so any advice would be welcome. Is there anything that I should be aware of as a newcomer?
Thank you, that's really useful. I'd have found out the hard way. Is the building generally quiet, or is it the sort of place where you can hear everything through the walls?
That's a relief. I work from home a few days a week, so a quiet environment is essential for me. I'm sure I'll be very happy here.
I will, and I'm glad that I've met you so quickly. Once I'm settled, I'll invite you over for a coffee, to return the favor.

scenarios.scenario: Catching up with an old acquaintance at a book launch
scenarios.context: Two people who haven't seen each other for years run into each other at a book launch and catch up.

speakerA.en: Well, I never expected to see you here! It must be at least five years since we last met, and I have to say you haven't changed a bit.

A friend of mine edited the book, and she practically insisted I come. Not only did she promise me a signed copy, but she also swore the wine would be decent. What about you? I thought you'd moved abroad.
That's the way it goes, isn't it? Much as I'd love to travel more, I've been tied to the office for the past two years. Do you think you'll ever move back, or has the decision been made for you?

I'd say that's a very reasonable compromise. On the other hand, you could always spend part of the year here, provided your employer is flexible about remote work. Has anyone raised that idea with you?
Not yet, I'm afraid. What keeps me there is the people, since the work itself has become rather repetitive. Still, I'm starting to wonder whether comfort is a good enough reason to stay.
I'd love that. Come to think of it, there's a café around the corner that stays open late, in case this crowd gets too loud for us.

speakerB.en: Rarely do I get compliments that generous, so I'll take it gladly, although I suspect the lighting in here is doing most of the work. What brings you to a book launch, of all places?
I did, and I stayed far longer than I'd planned. What surprised me most was how quickly it began to feel like home. Never had I imagined I'd settle down there, but the job was too good to turn down.
To be honest, I'm torn. Much as I miss my family, I've built a life there, and as long as the visa situation stays stable, I'd rather not uproot everything. What I'd really like is a bit of both.
Not seriously. Rarely do companies like mine allow it, but it wouldn't hurt to ask. What about you? Are you still at the same firm, or did you finally make the change you always talked about?

In my experience, that's exactly the question worth asking early. Not that there's any rush, but I'd hate for you to look back in ten years and wish you had acted sooner. Shall we find a quiet corner and talk it through properly?
Perfect. Let's say hello to your friend and slip out before the speeches begin. Had I known this would be so enjoyable, I'd have started going to these events years ago.

scenarios.scenario: Sharing a table with a stranger at a crowded café
scenarios.context: A visitor asks to share a table with a local regular on a rainy Saturday, and they start chatting.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I hope you don't mind my asking, but is anyone sitting here? Every other table seems to be taken, and I'd rather not drink my coffee standing up.

I'm only visiting, so I wouldn't know. Having arrived last night, I've barely had a chance to look around. If I hadn't asked the receptionist for directions, I'd probably still be wandering in circles, whatever my phone claims about walking distances.
From Lisbon, although I've spent the last decade in Berlin. Having left a sunny autumn behind, I'm finding this drizzle rather hard to forgive, so I'd rather you didn't mention the weather.

A bit of both. I'm attending a conference, though I'd happily skip the sessions and explore. As far as I'm concerned, the best way to understand a city is to get lost in it, provided you've got a decent umbrella.
That sounds right up my street. To be honest, if I hadn't bumped into you, I'd have spent the whole afternoon in my hotel room. Is it very far on foot, or would you recommend taking the tram?
I'll bear that in mind. Thank you, you've been far more helpful than any guidebook. Advice from a local is worth more than anything I could find online.

speakerB.en: Not at all, please sit down. Having come here every weekend for years, I can tell you it's always like this around noon, however early you arrive.
Honestly, it's a confusing city for newcomers. If I hadn't grown up here, I'd have given up on the one-way system long ago. Where have you come from, if you don't mind my asking?

I wouldn't dream of it, but I should warn you that it only gets worse. Having lived through fifteen winters here, I can say that whoever invented central heating deserves a statue. Are you here for work or pleasure?
I couldn't agree more. If you've got time this afternoon, I'd suggest the old market by the river. Having been there countless times, I still find something new whenever I go, however briefly I stay.

It's about twenty minutes, so I'd walk, as long as the rain holds off. Having checked the forecast this morning, I'd say you'll get a dry spell after two. Whatever you do, try the cheese stand at the far end.
My pleasure. Enjoy the market, and if you ever come back, look me up. I'd be glad to show you the quiet corners instead of leaving you to the tourist trail.

scenarios.scenario: Greeting a former mentor after a public setback
scenarios.context: A former mentee runs into her old mentor at a trade fair soon after his company's very public failure.

speakerA.en: Henry, how wonderful to see you! I wasn't sure you'd come, given everything the papers have said lately, but I'm delighted you did. Rarely have I seen this hall so crowded, so tell me honestly, how are you holding up?

Only the headlines, which, by and large, I don't trust. What I'd much rather hear is your own account, if you feel like sharing it. Seldom does the full story appear in print, and I know how much that company meant to you.

I do, though I'd hate to claim any credit. Rarely does anyone listen in the middle of a success story, and in hindsight, the signs were everywhere. The more successful we became, the less we questioned things. Did anyone on your board push back?

I'd take stock before taking action. Should you rush into another venture, you'd carry the same habits with you. What matters at this stage is that you understand the pattern, and it's clear that you already do. Have you spoken to your team yet?

Write to each of them personally, and offer to be a reference. It's the small gestures that people remember. For what it's worth, I'd gladly work with you again, provided the ground rules were different. Would you ever consider mentoring a start-up of mine?

It's a logistics platform, still very small. Were you to look at the numbers, you'd see why I need a skeptical eye. Come to think of it, there's a session at four where I'm presenting. Shall we go together, and talk afterwards?

speakerB.en: Priya, it's a relief to see a friendly face. I very nearly stayed at home, but were it not for your invitation last spring, I'd have missed this entirely. Little did I imagine I'd be answering that question in public. What have you heard?

It meant everything, and that's precisely the difficulty. It wasn't so much a single mistake that sank us as a series of small compromises that I allowed. Had I listened to you three years ago, we might still be afloat. Do you remember what you said?

One person did, and I dismissed her as overcautious. Only now do I understand how valuable that dissent was. Mind you, hindsight is a cruel teacher, and I'd rather learn from it than drown in it. What would you do in my position?

To some of them, and that's been the hardest part. Not only did I let them down, but I also let down the people who trusted my judgment. Be that as it may, they've been remarkably generous. I'd like to repay that somehow. Any ideas?

You flatter me, considering my current record. Nevertheless, I'd be honored, as long as you promise to challenge me. At no point should a mentor be immune to criticism, as I've learned the hard way. What kind of start-up is it?

Gladly. It goes without saying that I'll be on my best behavior, but I'll certainly be honest. Rarely have I looked forward to a presentation so much. Lead the way, and thank you for not treating me like a stranger.

scenarios.scenario: Welcoming an overseas delegation at the airport
scenarios.context: A host from a trade council greets the leader of a visiting delegation after a long flight and explains the program.

speakerA.en: Ms. Tanaka, welcome, and please accept my apologies for the weather. No sooner had your plane been announced than the rain began, but I hope the flight itself was bearable. How was the journey?

Needless to say, we've kept the schedule light today. It's essential that you rest before tomorrow's talks, so the car will take you straight to the hotel. Had it not been for the strike, we'd have arranged a dinner as well. Is that acceptable?

The deputy minister and two senior advisers, all of whom have followed your work for years. It's my understanding that you'll be presenting the new energy proposal. Should you require additional equipment, I'd be glad to arrange it. What would suit you best?

None whatsoever. We've worked with interpreters throughout, and I'm inclined to think they make discussions more thoughtful, because everyone slows down. It's essential, though, that we circulate the documents tonight. Would you mind if I sent them to your hotel?

That was my colleague, Mr. Adeyemi, who'll meet you tomorrow. No sooner had he heard about your visit than he began working on it. Whatever you need during your stay, he'll be happy to help. Do you have any dietary requirements we should know about?

By all means. The car is just outside, and I've asked the driver to take the scenic route, in case you'd like a first look at the city. Not only will you see the harbor, but you'll also pass the old market.

speakerB.en: Thank you, and please don't apologize. Not only was the flight smooth, but the crew also upgraded most of us, which was a pleasant surprise. Having said that, I'm rather tired, so I'm afraid I may not be at my sharpest this afternoon.

More than acceptable. I'd insist, in fact, that the rest of the delegation be given the same consideration, since several are older than I am. Mind you, they'll never admit to being tired. Who will be joining us tomorrow from your side?

A second screen would be useful, as would an interpreter for the afternoon session. Not only are some of my colleagues unfamiliar with the technical terms, but they also prefer to discuss details in their own language. Is that likely to cause any difficulty?

Please do. I'd rather the team read them carefully than skim them over breakfast. Had it not been for your advance briefing, we'd have arrived rather unprepared. By and large, your office has been remarkably accommodating. May I ask who prepared it?

Two of us avoid shellfish, and one is vegetarian, but otherwise we're quite flexible. It's important that nobody feel awkward about declining food, as I find that happens often. All things considered, we're very grateful for such warm hospitality. Shall we go?

How thoughtful. I'm inclined to think this visit will be a success, if the welcome is anything to go by. Needless to say, I'm looking forward to tomorrow. Let me just gather the others, and then we'll follow you.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing oneself
scenarios.context: One person introduces themselves to another.

speakerA.en: Hello! What's your name?
I'm Tom. Nice to meet you.
Where do you work?
That's nice. I work in a bank.
Let me introduce myself – I'm Dr. Brown.
speakerA.fa: بگذارید خودم را معرفی کنم – من دکتر براون هستم.

speakerA.en: I don't think we've met. I'm Emily.
speakerA.fa: فکر نکنم همدیگر را دیده باشیم. من امیلی هستم.

speakerA.en: Allow me to introduce myself: I'm Professor Smith.
speakerA.fa: اجازه دهید خودم را معرفی کنم: من پروفسور اسمیت هستم.

speakerA.en: Nice to meet you, Mike. Do you work here?
I'm the new accountant. I started this week.
Thank you. That would be great.

speakerB.en: My name is Sara. What's your name?
Nice to meet you too, Tom.
I work at a school. I'm a teacher.
Oh, that's interesting!
Pleased to meet you, Dr. Brown.
speakerB.fa: از دیدار شما خوشحالم، دکتر براون.

speakerB.en: Oh, hi Emily! I'm Mike.
speakerB.fa: اوه، سلام امیلی! من مایک هستم.

speakerB.en: It's an honour, Professor Smith.
speakerB.fa: مایه افتخار است، پروفسور اسمیت.

speakerB.en: Yes, I'm in the marketing team. And you?
Welcome! Let me show you the kitchen.
Follow me. I'll introduce you to the others.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing two people to each other
scenarios.context: A third person introduces two strangers.

speakerA.en: Sara, this is my friend Ali.
Ali works with me. He's a doctor.
Sara lives next to me, Ali.
Good! Now you are friends too.
Let me introduce you to my colleague, Lisa.
speakerA.fa: بگذارید شما را به همکارم، لیزا معرفی کنم.

speakerA.en: This is my friend, Tom. Tom, this is Sarah.
speakerA.fa: این دوست من، تام است. تام، این سارا است.

speakerA.en: I'd like you to meet my brother, James.
speakerA.fa: مایلم برادرم، جیمز را ملاقات کنید.

speakerA.en: Have you two met? This is Maria.
speakerA.fa: آیا شما دو تا همدیگر را ملاقات کرده‌اید؟ این ماریا است.

speakerA.en: Allow me to present our new manager, Mr. Adams.
speakerA.fa: اجازه دهید مدیر جدیدمان، آقای آدامز را معرفی کنم.

speakerA.en: Have you met Maria? She works in my department.
Mr. Lopez, this is my sister, Elena. She's visiting from Spain.
Mr. Lopez is my neighbor. He lives next door.

speakerB.en: Hello, Ali. Nice to meet you.
Oh, that's great. I'm a teacher.
Yes, we are neighbors. We often talk.
Yes! Thanks for introducing us.
Hey Tom, how's it going?
speakerB.fa: هی تام، اوضاع چطوره؟

speakerB.en: Nice to meet you, James. I've heard a lot about you.
speakerB.fa: از ملاقات شما خوشوقتم، جیمز. چیزهای زیادی درباره شما شنیده‌ام.

speakerB.en: No, we haven't met. Hello Maria.
speakerB.fa: نه، همدیگر را ندیده‌ایم. سلام ماریا.

speakerB.en: How do you do, Mr. Adams? I'm pleased to meet you.
speakerB.fa: خوشوقتم، آقای آدامز؟ از دیدار شما خوشحالم.

speakerB.en: No, we haven't. Nice to meet you, Maria.
It's a pleasure to meet you, Mr. Adams. I look forward to working together.
Nice to meet you, Elena. Welcome to our city.
Yes, I live right next door. Please ask me if you need any help.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing family and friends
scenarios.context: A friend visits your home and meets your family.

speakerA.en: Hi! Thank you for inviting me.
Nice to meet you. You have a lovely home.
Hi, Sam. How old are you?
I like football too!
Mom, this is my coworker, Hannah. We work on the same team.
Hannah, this is my sister, Maya. She's a teacher.
And this is my grandmother. She doesn't speak much English.
Dinner is ready. Please sit down.

speakerB.en: Welcome! Come in. This is my mother.
Thank you. And this is my brother, Sam.
He's twelve. He likes football.
Great! Please sit down. Would you like some tea?
Nice to meet you, Hannah. Please make yourself at home.
Hi, Hannah. I've heard a lot about you.
That's fine. Hello, it's a pleasure to meet you.
Thank you. The food smells wonderful.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting a new classmate
scenarios.context: It is the first day of class and a new student arrives.

speakerA.en: Hi! Are you new here?
Nice to meet you, Nina. I'm Omar.
Yes, it's English class. Sit here, please.
Yes, she is very kind.
Don't worry. I can help you!
Hi, is this seat free? I'm Sofia.
I think so. I'm studying business. What about you?
Where are you from, Kenji?
Do you want to study together after class?

speakerB.en: Yes, I am. My name is Nina.
Nice to meet you, Omar. Is this your class?
Thank you. Is the teacher kind?
That's good. I'm a little nervous.
Thanks, Omar. You're very kind.
Yes, it is. I'm Kenji. Are you in my class?
I'm studying computer science.
I'm from Japan. I arrived here two months ago.
That would be great. Here's my phone number.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting the interviewer at a job interview
scenarios.context: A candidate arrives for an interview and meets the hiring manager.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm Nadia Karim. I have an interview at ten.
Thank you for seeing me today.
Yes, I did. The directions were very clear.
No, thank you. I'm ready.

speakerB.en: Good morning, Ms. Karim. I'm Paul Reed, the hiring manager.
You're welcome. Please have a seat. Did you find the office easily?
Good. Would you like some water before we start?
Great. Let me introduce you to our team leader, Anna.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself at a party
scenarios.context: A guest introduces himself to someone he does not know at a friend's party.

speakerA.en: Hi, I don't think we know each other. I'm Luis.
We studied together at university. And you?
That sounds interesting. What kind of project is it?
Good luck with the launch!

speakerB.en: Hi, Luis. I'm Amy. How do you know the host?
I work with Kate. We're on the same project.
It's a mobile app for travelers. We launch next month.
Thanks, Luis. It was nice talking to you.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself to a new neighbor
scenarios.context: A resident introduces herself to a person who has just moved into the building.

speakerA.en: Hello! I live in the apartment across the hall. I'm Rosa.
Welcome to the building! Do you need any help?
There's one two streets from here. It's open until ten.
Here's my phone number. Call me if you have any questions.

speakerB.en: Hi, Rosa. I'm Ben. I moved in yesterday.
Thanks. Where can I find the nearest supermarket?
That's very helpful. Thank you.
That's very kind of you. See you around!

scenarios.scenario: Introducing a new colleague to the team
scenarios.context: A manager has just brought a new employee to meet a team member.

speakerA.en: You must be Daniel. Our manager told me you'd be joining us today.
I'm Karen, and I've been on the design team for about five years. What was your previous job?
That's useful experience. We'll probably be working together on the new website.
Of course. Let me introduce you to the others first, and then we can talk over lunch.

speakerB.en: That's right. I'm really glad to be here, and everyone has been very welcoming so far.
I worked at a small advertising agency, mostly on websites and social media campaigns.
I hope so. Could you tell me how the team usually organizes its projects?
That would be great. Thank you for making me feel so comfortable.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing a friend to your family
scenarios.context: A guest meets his friend's parents for the first time.

speakerA.en: So you're the friend we've heard so much about! Please, come in.
Does he? I hope it's only good things. How did you two meet?
He told us you're studying engineering. What do you plan to do after you graduate?
That sounds like a wonderful goal. Dinner will be ready in a few minutes, so make yourself at home.

speakerB.en: Thank you for having me. Marco talks about you both all the time.
We were in the same class at university, and we ended up sharing an apartment.
I'd like to work for an environmental company, but I'm still looking at my options.
I brought some dessert, if that's all right. It's a recipe from my grandmother.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting someone at a networking event
scenarios.context: Two professionals introduce themselves at a business event.

speakerA.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Laura, and I work in marketing for a software company.
That sounds interesting. How did you get into that line of work?
I can understand that. We work with a few startups, so we might have something in common.
I do. Here you are. Feel free to email me if you'd like to arrange a meeting.

speakerB.en: Good to meet you, Laura. I'm Omar. I run a small consulting firm that helps startups with their finances.
I used to work in a bank, but I wanted to be more involved with young businesses.
Then we should definitely stay in touch. Do you have a business card with you?
Thanks. I'll write to you next week, once the conference is over.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing a speaker at a seminar
scenarios.context: A host introduces a guest speaker to an audience member before the event.

speakerA.en: Dr. Patel, allow me to introduce Ms. Chen, who has been following your research for years.
Likewise. Your recent paper on housing policy was the talk of our department.
Ms. Chen is a journalist, and she's hoping to interview you after the session.
That would be ideal. I'll keep my questions brief, since I know your schedule is tight.

speakerB.en: It's a pleasure to meet you. I've long admired your work on sustainable urban planning.
I'm flattered, though I suspect the credit belongs mostly to my research team.
I'd be glad to, provided it doesn't clash with the reception. Could we arrange something afterwards?
Not at all. I always welcome thoughtful questions, so please don't hold back.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself to a new team
scenarios.context: A new manager introduces herself to her team on the first day.

speakerA.en: Good morning, everyone. Let me start by saying how delighted I am to be joining you.
I hope that doesn't set the bar too high. I should explain a little about how I like to work.
I believe in open communication, so I'll be holding short one-to-one meetings with each of you this week.
That's precisely what I want to change. Nothing is too small to raise with me.

speakerB.en: Welcome. We've heard a great deal about your work at your previous company.
Please do. It would help us to know what to expect over the coming months.
That sounds sensible. Many of us have ideas that never reach management.
We appreciate that. I think you'll find the team keen to make a good impression.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing an old friend to a new partner
scenarios.context: A man introduces his long-time friend to his girlfriend.

speakerA.en: Sophie, this is Marcus, the friend I've been telling you about. We go back to our school days.
Only the flattering ones, I hope. Although knowing him, he's probably exaggerated the worst of them.
Please do. I'd love to hear how you two managed to survive a week in the rain.
The feeling is mutual. I'm glad he has such loyal friends around him.

speakerB.en: So you're the infamous Marcus. I've heard several embarrassing stories about you.
Hardly. I haven't told her about the camping trip yet, so you should count yourself lucky.
Another time, perhaps. Anyway, it's wonderful to finally meet you. Daniel doesn't stop talking about you.
Shall we sit down? I've reserved a table, and I'd like to hear everything about how you met.

scenarios.scenario: Presenting a distinguished guest at a formal event
scenarios.context: A host introduces a renowned scientist to a prospective donor.

speakerA.en: Allow me to introduce Professor Okafor, whose work on antibiotic resistance has reshaped the field.
Professor, this is Ms. Lindqvist, whose foundation has been instrumental in funding research of this nature.
We're drawn to projects where the odds are long but the potential payoff is transformative.
I'd be eager to hear the particulars, though I'll warn you that I'm a rather exacting listener.

speakerB.en: You're far too kind. I'm merely the visible face of a very gifted team who deserve the lion's share of the credit.
It's an honor. Your foundation's commitment to early-stage research is precisely what the field has been lacking.
Then I suspect we'll find we have a great deal to discuss. Our next phase is considerably more ambitious than the last.
I'd expect nothing less. Shall we find somewhere a little quieter, away from the clinking of glasses?

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself in a high-stakes interview panel
scenarios.context: A candidate introduces herself to a panel of senior executives.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm delighted to have the opportunity to speak with you, and I appreciate your time.
Certainly. I started in policy research, but I became increasingly drawn to the question of how ideas actually get implemented.
I realized that brilliant proposals often founder on mundane logistical failures, so I moved into operations to understand why.
Invaluably. It taught me that resistance to change is rarely irrational. It usually reflects legitimate concerns that have gone unaddressed.

speakerB.en: Thank you for joining us. Perhaps you could begin by giving us an overview of what brought you to this point in your career.
That's an unusual pivot. What prompted it, and what did you learn along the way?
And has that perspective served you in your most recent role, where you oversaw the restructuring?
A sound observation. We'd like to explore that further, if you're comfortable elaborating.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing two professionals with potential for collaboration
scenarios.context: A mutual acquaintance connects two specialists from different fields.

speakerA.en: I've been meaning to put the two of you in touch for ages. Dr. Hartmann, meet Ms. Sato.
Likewise. I've followed your research on behavioral economics with considerable interest, and I think it intersects with my work more than either of us might expect.
It's a gap I've been struggling to bridge. The engineering is sound, but uptake has been disappointing.
Not at all. I'd welcome any framework that helps explain why people ignore options that serve them.

speakerB.en: A pleasure. Your name has surfaced in several conversations recently, always in connection with the urban mobility project.
That's what struck me. You approach the problem from the infrastructure side, whereas Dr. Hartmann examines why people resist adopting the solutions.
Which is precisely the kind of problem my field is suited to dissect, if you'll forgive the clinical language.
I'll leave you to it, then. I suspect this introduction is going to prove more fruitful than I anticipated.

scenarios.scenario: Presenting a new director to a skeptical team
scenarios.context: A manager introduces a newly appointed director to a department that has seen many changes.

speakerA.en: Colleagues, allow me to introduce Dr. Okafor, who joins us as director of research after a distinguished decade at the Institute.
That's reassuring, since this team has weathered three reorganizations in as many years, and patience is in short supply.
Dr. Okafor has also kindly offered an open-door hour each Thursday, so please don't hesitate to take advantage of it.
With that, I'll leave you to get acquainted. Marcus, perhaps you could show Dr. Okafor the laboratory first?

speakerB.en: It's a pleasure to be here, though I'm conscious that arriving mid-project can feel intrusive. I intend to listen long before I propose anything.
Understandably so. I'd rather earn your confidence through results than demand it by virtue of my title.
I mean that sincerely. Candid criticism is far more useful to me than polite silence, so do bring both questions and objections.
I'd be delighted. Do spare me nothing; I'd prefer to see the place as it really is, flaws included.

scenarios.scenario: Connecting two guests who share a professional interest
scenarios.context: A host introduces two people who would clearly benefit from knowing each other.

speakerA.en: Priya, I must introduce you to Tomas. He has just published a study on urban beekeeping, and you've been wanting a conversation like this for months.
That's generous of you. I'd expected the planning authorities to dismiss it, so it's gratifying to find a reader who engaged with it seriously.
I'll leave the two of you to it, then. Tomas, do mind the host's wine; it has a reputation for being deceptively strong.
Practical use is exactly what we lack, so you'd be more than welcome. I'll send you the details tomorrow, along with a map.

speakerB.en: Tomas, I've admired your work for some time. Your argument about rooftop colonies was the most persuasive thing I read all year.
I run a community garden project, and we've been debating that very question. I'd value your perspective if you could spare an hour.
Noted, thank you. Priya, I'd be glad to visit the garden, provided I can be of practical use rather than merely an ornamental expert.
Excellent. Between us, we may have found the collaboration that neither of us had the nerve to propose.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself to a senior figure at a networking event
scenarios.context: A mid-career professional approaches a well-known industry leader.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I don't believe we've met; I'm Helena Brandt, and I lead the policy division at a small think tank across town.
Coming from someone of your standing, that means a great deal. I confess I was bracing for a rather chillier reception.
Then perhaps we could continue the disagreement over coffee next week? I'd welcome the chance to have my reasoning tested.
Thank you, I shall. I'll make sure to come armed with better evidence than I had tonight.

speakerB.en: Daniel Whitmore. I've read some of your commentary on the energy bill, and I thought your critique of the subsidy structure uncommonly sharp.
Not at all. I disagree with roughly half of it, but I respect anyone who argues with that degree of rigor.
I'd enjoy that. My assistant will find a slot, so do send her your card, and I'll look forward to the debate.
Do, by all means. Nothing sharpens an argument quite like an opponent who has done the reading.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing a friend to your roommate
scenarios.context: A student introduces his friend to his roommate.

speakerA.en: Jake, this is my friend Leo.
Leo is new in town. He's a student.
I live near the park. And you?
That's nice. Are you free now?

speakerB.en: Hi, Leo. Nice to meet you.
Welcome! Where do you live?
I live here with Peter.
Yes. Let's have some tea.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself at a new school
scenarios.context: A new student introduces himself to the teacher.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm the new student.
My name is Karim.
I'm from Egypt.
Thank you, teacher.

speakerB.en: Welcome! What's your name?
Nice to meet you, Karim. Where are you from?
That's interesting. Come in and sit here.
You're welcome.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting a friend's brother
scenarios.context: Two people meet at a friend's house.

speakerA.en: Hi! Are you Tina's brother?
Nice to meet you, David. I'm Kate.
Yes, we work together.
Really? She's very kind.

speakerB.en: Yes, I am. I'm David.
Nice to meet you, Kate. Are you Tina's friend?
That's great. She talks about you a lot.
Come in. Tina is in the kitchen.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing a colleague to a client
scenarios.context: A manager introduces a colleague to an important client.

speakerA.en: Mr. Thompson, let me introduce you to my colleague, Sara Nouri.
Thank you. I'm glad to finally meet you in person after all our emails.
Yes, I've been looking forward to presenting our ideas to you.
Shall we sit down? I'll start with a short introduction.

speakerB.en: It's a pleasure to meet you, Ms. Nouri. I've heard a lot about your work.
Likewise. Sara is in charge of the project we've been discussing.
Wonderful. I'm very curious to see what you've prepared.
Please do. We have plenty of time this afternoon.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself when starting a course
scenarios.context: A student introduces himself to the group on the first day of a course.

speakerA.en: Welcome, everyone. Let's start by introducing ourselves. Would you like to begin?
What made you decide to take this course?
That's a very common reason. Do you have any hobbies?
Great, thank you, Kian. It's nice to have you in the group.

speakerB.en: Sure. My name is Kian, and I'm an engineer from Shiraz.
I use English at work, and I'd like to speak more confidently.
I enjoy photography, and I also like cooking on weekends.
Thank you. I'm looking forward to learning with everyone.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing your partner to your parents
scenarios.context: A young man introduces his girlfriend to his parents at a family dinner.

speakerA.en: Mum, Dad, I'd like you to meet Elena. We've been together for almost a year now.
Elena, this is my father, Robert, and my mother, Susan. They've been looking forward to meeting you for weeks.
She works as a nurse at the children's hospital, which is why she's often busy in the evenings.
We met at a friend's party last spring. She was the only person who could explain the rules of the game we were playing.
Dad loves cooking, so if you ever want to learn some recipes, he'd be delighted to teach you.
Thank you both for inviting us. It means a lot to me that you've made her feel so welcome.

speakerB.en: Pleased to meet you, Elena. We've heard so much about you, and we're glad that you could join us tonight.
Please, make yourself at home. You must be hungry after your journey. Dinner will be ready in about ten minutes.
That must be a demanding job, but also a very rewarding one. We admire people who care for others like that.
That sounds like our son. He's always been shy, so it's wonderful that he found someone who can bring him out of his shell.
I'd love that. I've always enjoyed trying new dishes, although I'm afraid I'm not a great cook yet.
It's our pleasure. Now, let's sit down and eat. You two must tell us how you managed to find time to visit us.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself at a professional event
scenarios.context: Two professionals introduce themselves at a networking evening and exchange contact details.

speakerA.en: Hello, I don't think we've met. My name is Michael Brown, and I work in the finance department of a logistics company.
I've been in the industry for about twelve years, mostly in Europe, but my firm opened a new branch here last year.
That's interesting. I'm always looking for new ideas, especially on how to reduce costs without affecting the quality of service.
I'd be glad to. Here's my business card. Do you happen to know anyone who has experience with similar projects?
That would be very helpful. I'll send you an email tomorrow, and we can arrange a short meeting if you like.
Likewise. I hope we'll have the chance to work together on something in the future.

speakerB.en: Nice to meet you, Michael. I'm Priya Nair, a consultant who helps companies improve their business processes.
That's quite an achievement. Expanding to a new country is never easy, and I imagine that you've faced a lot of challenges.
In that case, we should keep in touch. I've recently completed a project for a company that had exactly that problem.
As a matter of fact, I do. A former client of mine, who runs a transport company, might be happy to talk to you.
Perfect. Here's my card as well. If you tell me what you need, I'll introduce you to him next week.
That would be great. It was a pleasure meeting you, and I'm sure we'll be in touch very soon.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing a new team member to a department
scenarios.context: A manager introduces a new employee to the team and explains how the group works.

speakerA.en: Everyone, I'd like to introduce Daniel, who has just joined us as our new data analyst. He comes with several years of experience in the retail sector.
Daniel, let me tell you a little about the people you'll be working with. Sofia leads the reporting team, and she's the person you'll go to for anything related to deadlines.
Marcus, sitting over there, has been here the longest, so if you ever need to know why something was done in a particular way, he's the one to ask.
We usually have a short meeting on Monday mornings, in which each of us explains what we're working on, so that nobody is surprised later in the week.
I'd suggest that you spend the first few days getting to know our systems, and then we'll gradually assign you to smaller projects before you take on bigger ones.
Welcome again. Don't hesitate to come to me if you have any questions. We've all been in your position at some point.

speakerB.en: Thank you for the warm welcome. I'm delighted to be here, and I'm looking forward to learning from all of you. I've heard a lot of good things about this department.
It's a pleasure to meet you, Sofia. I'd appreciate it if you could walk me through the reporting process at some point, because I'm eager to understand how it's structured.
That's very useful to know, Marcus. I tend to ask a lot of questions at the beginning, so I hope you won't mind if I come to you regularly.
That sounds like an effective way of keeping everyone informed. In my previous job, we only had formal meetings, and it often led to people working on the same problem twice.
That sounds reasonable. I'd prefer to understand the foundations before taking responsibility for anything important, so a gradual start suits me perfectly.
I will, and thank you. I'm confident that it won't take long for me to feel at home, given how friendly everybody seems to be.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself during a job-related networking call
scenarios.context: Two professionals meet through a mutual contact and introduce their backgrounds in a video call.

speakerA.en: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me. Our mutual friend suggested that we might have common interests, and I thought it was worth a conversation.
I've spent about ten years in sustainable architecture, and I'm currently exploring ways of applying that experience to urban planning, which is why I thought of you.
Exactly. I've noticed that many cities are keen on greener buildings, but they lack coherent strategies on a larger scale, which is a gap I'd like to help fill.
That's very encouraging. I'd be especially interested in learning what skills I'd need to develop, since my background has been mostly technical rather than political.
I'd be grateful for that. Could you perhaps put me in touch with someone who has made a similar transition, so I could hear about their experience first-hand?
Thank you. I'll send you a summary of my background by email, so that you have a clearer picture of what I've done.

speakerB.en: It's a pleasure to meet you. Our friend spoke very highly of you, and I was curious about how you got involved in sustainable design.
That's a valuable background. Urban planning is increasingly concerned with energy efficiency, so your expertise could be highly relevant, provided you're willing to learn about regulations.
You're right. The challenge is rarely the technology. It's coordinating the different parties involved, such as local authorities, developers, and residents, whose interests often conflict.
In that case, I'd recommend focusing on policy and communication skills. There are some short courses that might help, and I'd be happy to share a few suggestions.
I know someone who made exactly that change five years ago. She's now working for the city council, and I'm sure she'd be glad to talk to you.
Please do. I'll look through it before I contact her, and I'll introduce you personally, which usually makes the first conversation much easier.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing a guest speaker at an event
scenarios.context: An event host introduces a guest speaker and sets the scene for the audience.

speakerA.en: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us tonight. It's my great pleasure to introduce our guest speaker, Dr. Helen Park, who has worked in marine biology for over twenty years.
Dr. Park has led expeditions in the Pacific and the Arctic, and her research on coral recovery has been published in some of the most respected journals in her field.
Besides her scientific work, she is known for her ability to explain complex ideas in an accessible way, which is why she was invited to advise on several documentaries.
Tonight, she will talk about what can be done to protect coral reefs, and then she'll be taking questions from the audience, so please think about what you'd like to ask.
Before I hand over, I'd like to remind you that the session is being recorded, and that refreshments will be served afterwards in the foyer.
Please give a warm welcome to Dr. Helen Park.

speakerB.en: Thank you very much for that generous introduction, and good evening, everybody. It's a real honor to be here, and I'm delighted to see such a full room.
I must say that I'd never have expected an introduction like that. I'm only a scientist who happens to love the ocean, and who has been lucky enough to work with many remarkable people.
As a matter of fact, I used to be terrified of speaking in public. It was only when I realized that I was talking about something I truly cared about that the nerves began to disappear.
I'd like to begin by asking you a question. How many of you have visited a coral reef? Please raise your hands. That's more than I expected.
Thank you for the reminder. I'd be happy to stay for as long as people want to talk, so please come and find me during the break, and tell me what you think.
Now, let me start with a story that changed the way I look at my work. It happened about fifteen years ago, off the coast of Indonesia.

scenarios.scenario: Introducing two professionals who could collaborate
scenarios.context: A mutual acquaintance introduces two professionals and explains why they should meet.

speakerA.en: I'd like you two to meet, because I think you'll have a lot to talk about. Sara, this is Ahmed, who runs a small company that develops educational software.
Ahmed, Sara is a teacher and researcher, and she's been working on new ways of helping students who find reading difficult. I immediately thought of you when she described it.
Sara mentioned that she's been looking for someone who could turn her methods into a digital tool, and you've been wanting to expand into more specialized products.
I'll leave you to it. I'm sure there's more to discuss than I could possibly explain, and I'd rather not be the one to take credit if it turns into something.
Do keep me informed. I'd be very pleased if this introduction led to something concrete, and I'd be glad to help in any way I can.
Well, I'll go and get some more drinks. Please feel free to carry on without me.

speakerB.en: It's a pleasure to meet you, Ahmed. I've heard a good deal about your company, and I must admit that I've been looking forward to talking to someone with your experience.

That's exactly right. I've developed a set of exercises over the past three years, and the results have been encouraging, but I'm not a programmer, so I've struggled to make them available beyond my own classroom.
It's a pleasure, Sara. Our company has worked mostly on general learning platforms, but I've always wanted to do something more focused. Could you tell me a little more about your method?
Thank you for the introduction. Perhaps we could arrange to meet next week, and discuss it in more detail, so that we can see whether there's a basis for working together.
We certainly will. It's remarkable how often a single introduction can open up an opportunity that you'd never have found alone. I'm very grateful for your thoughtfulness.
Thanks. And you don't need to leave, but I won't stop you. Sara, shall we find a quieter corner where we can talk properly?

scenarios.scenario: Introducing yourself to a respected expert through a mutual contact
scenarios.context: At a networking dinner, a young policy researcher approaches a senior professor whom she knows only through a mutual friend.

speakerA.en: Professor Hale? Forgive the interruption. I'm Dana Whitmore, and I was hoping to introduce myself, since our mutual friend Tomas, to whom I owe a great deal, insisted that we'd get along.

I work in transport policy, in a department in which most people are economists, whereas my background is in sociology. It's thanks to that difference that I keep asking questions nobody else thinks of.
A study on how commuters adapt when a major route closes, which is more interesting than it sounds. Although the data is messy, it suggests that habits are far more flexible than planners assume.

I'd say that's the heart of it. As far as I'm concerned, a policy is only as good as the people who understand its everyday consequences. Would you mind if I sent you a short summary, in case it's of any use to your own work?
That's extremely generous of you. I should say that I'm still at an early stage, so the results may change, although I'm confident about the overall direction.
Thank you, that's reassuring. I'll send the summary by Friday, and perhaps we could meet at the conference in spring, on the understanding that you're not obliged to read every page.

speakerB.en: Not at all, any friend of Tomas is welcome here. He's someone for whom I have enormous respect, although he has a talent for volunteering me for things. What is it you do, Dana?

Which is precisely what any good team needs. I started out the same way, as an outsider whom nobody quite knew where to place. It is the awkward questions that tend to move a field forward. What are you working on at the moment?

That fits with what I've seen, and it's a topic on which I'd be glad to hear more. It is often the small behavioral details that decide whether a policy works, whereas the grand designs tend to get the headlines.

Please do. It would be a pleasure, since I'm currently supervising a student for whom this is a central question. Here's my card, and we can arrange a call once you've had a chance to organize your findings.

That's exactly the right attitude. To be honest, I'd be more suspicious of anyone who claimed to be certain at this stage. It is the willingness to revise that distinguishes a researcher from a salesman.
I'll hold you to that, though I promise nothing about reading every page. It was a pleasure meeting you, Dana. Do pass my regards to Tomas, to whom I owe a long-overdue reply.

scenarios.scenario: Welcoming a new team member and making the first introductions
scenarios.context: On her first morning, a new hire meets the colleague who will be mentoring her and gets her first round of introductions.

speakerA.en: Welcome, Priya! We've only spoken by email, so let me introduce myself properly. I'm Gareth, and I'll be the one showing you the ropes during your first few weeks, in case you were wondering.

That's perfectly natural, and you'll find the team very approachable. It's essential that you feel free to ask questions, however trivial they seem. Shall we start with a quick tour, so you can see who sits where?

Sensible. Let me introduce you to Hannah first, who manages our client accounts. Should you ever need a decision made quickly, she's the person to ask. She's rather direct, though, so don't take it personally.

Informal, as long as you don't mind a few questions. I'd suggest that you mention your background in logistics, since we've been looking for someone who understands supply chains, provided you're comfortable talking about it.
Roughly half are remote, so I've arranged a video call this afternoon. It's important that everyone see your face early on, otherwise it takes weeks for people to feel they know you.
Good idea, but keep it brief. And remember, if anything feels confusing at any point, you can always come straight to me. I'd rather you asked ten questions than struggled in silence.

speakerB.en: Thank you, Gareth, it's good to finally meet you in person. To be honest, I was a bit nervous this morning, since I don't know anyone here apart from the people who interviewed me.
That would be wonderful. I'd say the most useful thing for me right now is to learn who handles what, since I'd hate to send a request to the wrong person in my first week.
I appreciate the warning! I'd rather have honest feedback than polite silence. Should I prepare anything before we meet her, or is it more of an informal hello?
Of course. As far as I'm concerned, the best way to start a working relationship is to be clear about what I can offer. Will the rest of the team be around, or are some of them working remotely?
That makes sense, and I'm glad you thought of it. Should I send a short introduction to the group beforehand, in case people would like to know a little about me?
