I'm sorry to hear that, but it sounds like you made peace with the decision. Is moving abroad something you're seriously considering, or is it more of a daydream at this point?
My lips are sealed. On the other hand, if you ever need a reference, I'd be happy to write one. What I've seen of your work is more than enough to recommend you.

speakerB.en: You're not the first to say so. What happened was that I took a temporary job to pay off a loan, and I discovered I enjoyed solving problems that come with actual deadlines. The funny thing is, it's not so different from philosophy.

Exactly, and that's what I enjoy most. What I've learned is that every delay is really a trade-off between cost, time and the customer's patience. As it happens, I wrote my thesis on decision-making under uncertainty, which turned out to be surprisingly useful.

Occasionally, I'm afraid. What I wonder about isn't so much the jobs I didn't take as the city I didn't live in. I was offered a position in Vienna once, and although I turned it down, I still think about it now and then.

Family reasons, mainly. My father was ill at the time, and as long as he needed me nearby, there wasn't really a choice. What I'd say in hindsight is that I don't regret it, though I'd love to try living abroad now.

As it happens, I've been looking at opportunities in Lisbon. What attracts me most is the idea of starting from scratch, provided the salary covers the rent, of course. To be honest, I haven't told anyone at work, so please keep it between us.
That's very kind, thank you. And what about you? I've done most of the talking, so I'd like to hear what you'd change about your own career, if you could.

scenarios.scenario: Chatting with a stranger at a wedding reception
scenarios.context: Two guests who don't know each other end up next to each other at a wedding reception and discover what they have in common.

speakerA.en: I don't think we've been introduced. I'm Nadia, the bride's cousin on her mother's side, although most people here assume I'm a friend of the groom.

Guilty, I'm afraid. It turns out that arranging two hundred people is rather like solving a puzzle, although I'd say the real challenge was keeping certain relatives away from each other. How do you know the groom, exactly?
That's hard to believe, given what I've heard. He's said to be a terrible cook, which is why I'm surprised. Do you still see each other regularly, or has everyone drifted apart since graduating?

Not at all, I'm based in Edinburgh, where I work as a translator. It turns out to be a surprisingly lonely profession, although I'd say it suits me, since I prefer working in peace to sitting in meetings.

Mainly French and Spanish, but I'm learning Japanese as a hobby. It's said to be the hardest language for English speakers, and I'd say that's true, although the sense of progress when something finally clicks is enormously satisfying.
Ha! Then we're well matched. Shall we find our table before the speeches begin, in case we're seated next to the relatives I've been avoiding all afternoon?

speakerB.en: Nice to meet you, Nadia. I'm Callum, one of the groom's old college friends. No sooner had I sat down than I was told you were the person to ask about the seating plan, since you apparently organized half of it.
We shared an apartment for three years. It turns out he's considerably messier than he lets on, though I'm told that's changed now. No sooner had he moved out than he discovered he could cook.

We drifted, to be honest, but it turns out that a good friendship survives a long silence. No sooner had we started talking this morning than it felt as though no time had passed. What about you? Do you live nearby?

I'd have thought it would be fascinating. What languages do you work with, if you don't mind my asking? I'm told that translating from Japanese is notoriously difficult, even for people who've studied it for years.

That's the spirit. As far as I'm concerned, any skill worth having is difficult at first. No sooner had I learned to play the guitar than I wanted to learn the piano, and now I can barely play either.
Lead the way. It turns out I'm at table seven, so if you're nearby, I'll consider it a stroke of luck, and I promise to be good company.

scenarios.scenario: Meeting your fiancée's father over a first family dinner
scenarios.context: A young man meets his fiancée's father at dinner, and the two exchange personal questions.

speakerA.en: Adam, welcome, and please don't look so alarmed. Rarely have I eaten a meal this quietly with my daughter's guests, so let me start with an easy question. What do you do, and what drew you to it?

I taught history for thirty years, which explains my habit of asking questions. Not only did I enjoy it, but I also learned more from my students than from any book. What I'd like to know is what your family thinks of Lucia.

It's a very good one. Should you ever become less shy, I fear we'll lose the pleasant listener I see tonight. Mind you, Lucia tells me you're quite funny at home. What's the secret behind your sense of humor?
That you're patient, which is not a trait she values lightly. What I noticed, as well, is that you listen. Rarely do young men listen so carefully. Were you always like this, or did Lucia teach you?
I do, and I'd tell you if I didn't. All things considered, I think you'll suit one another well. Should you have any worries about the wedding, speak freely. What are your thoughts on where to live?

Very much. Not only would I see my daughter, but I'd also have someone to argue about old buildings with. Come to think of it, there's a house on my street that needs restoring. Would you take a look?

speakerB.en: Thank you, sir. I'm an architect, mostly restoring older buildings. What drew me was my grandfather, who was a carpenter. Were it not for his workshop, I'd probably have gone into finance. May I ask what you did?

They adore her, and my mother has already begun planning a visit. It's not that they were surprised, but that they were relieved, since I'm rather shy. Had I met her sooner, I'd have been far less lonely. Is that an acceptable answer?

Probably growing up with three brothers, where silence was a disadvantage. Needless to say, I learned to be quick. Not only do I enjoy making her laugh, but she's the only person who laughs at the right moments. What did Lucia say about me?

A bit of both, I suspect. Not until I met her did I realize how much I'd been rushing through life. By and large, I'd say she's made me calmer. It's not that I'm perfect, but I'm improving. Do you approve of that?

We've considered staying in the city, at least for a few years, since my work is here. Were it not for her job in the north, I'd say it was settled. Whatever we decide, we'd visit often. Would that please you?
I'd be honored, sir. For what it's worth, I feel considerably less nervous than an hour ago. Let me finish this excellent dinner, and then I'll happily come and see it.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing values and expectations with a prospective business partner
scenarios.context: Two professionals considering a joint venture ask each other personal questions about values, work habits and ambitions.

speakerA.en: Rashid, before we sign anything, I'd like to get to know you properly. Rarely have I started a partnership without asking personal questions, and I've regretted it each time. What would you say matters most to you in work?

Entirely, although I should say I'm a perfectionist. Not only do I review every contract twice, but I also revisit decisions long after they're made. Whatever you think of that, I'd rather you knew now. How do you deal with that sort of person?

I'm learning to. Were it not for a painful experience three years ago, I'd still be doing everything myself. Should you ever see me micromanaging, I'd appreciate it if you said so plainly. What about your own weaknesses?

Not at all, as long as we agree on how to decide things. What I'd propose is a rule that major decisions require both signatures. It's not that I distrust you, but that clear rules prevent resentment. Would you accept that?

I'm flexible, provided deadlines are met. Have I mentioned I have two children? Were it not for them, I'd work evenings, but I won't. Not only is that a personal limit, but it's also a matter of principle. Is that a problem?

Ideally, a team of twenty and a reputation for fairness. What matters is that we grow without losing our standards. Should we reach that point, I'd be proud. And you? Rarely do people answer that honestly.

speakerB.en: Honesty, without question. What I can't tolerate is being surprised by bad news. Had my last partner told me earlier about the debts, I'd have saved my company. Are you comfortable with that kind of directness?

Carefully, I suppose, but I'd rather work with a perfectionist than a careless colleague. By and large, the more precise a partner is, the fewer problems arise. What worries me is whether you can delegate. Can you?

Impatience, mostly. Never have I been able to wait for a slow decision, so I tend to push. Mind you, I've improved with age. Not that I've lost the urge, but I've learned to hide it better. Does that alarm you?

Willingly. In fact, I'd go further and suggest a monthly review, in case problems build up unnoticed. Needless to say, I'd expect the same discipline from myself. Come to think of it, what are your expectations about working hours?

Not in the least. I respect that boundary, and I'd hope you respect mine, which is Sunday. All things considered, we seem to share more values than I expected. What about long-term ambitions? Where do you see this in five years?

Much the same, with a little less ambition for size. For what it's worth, I think we'd work well together. Whatever the contract says, the conversation we've had tonight is the real foundation. Shall we shake on it?

scenarios.scenario: Extending an invitation (formal/informal)
scenarios.context: One person invites another to an event or meal.

speakerA.en: Hi! Are you free on Saturday?
I'm having lunch at my house. Would you like to come?
At one o'clock. Please bring a friend.
Would you like to join me for lunch today?
speakerA.fa: مایلید امروز با من ناهار بخورید؟

speakerA.en: Can you come to my place for dinner on Saturday?
speakerA.fa: آیا می‌توانید شنبه برای شام به منزل من بیایید؟

speakerA.en: We'd love to have you over for a barbecue this weekend.
speakerA.fa: ما خیلی دوست داریم شما را برای کباب آخر هفته مهمان کنیم.

speakerA.en: I'd like to invite you to a concert next Friday if you're free.
speakerA.fa: اگر آزاد هستید، دوست دارم شما را به یک کنسرت جمعه آینده دعوت کنم.

speakerA.en: Would you be interested in joining us for a hike on Sunday?
speakerA.fa: آیا به پیاده‌روی یکشنبه با ما علاقه‌مندید؟

speakerA.en: I'll wait for you outside the restaurant at one.
For Saturday, dinner is at seven. Can you bring dessert?

speakerB.en: Yes, I think so. Why?
That sounds great. What time?
Thank you. See you on Saturday!
I'd love to! What time?
speakerB.fa: با کمال میل! چه ساعتی؟

speakerB.en: That sounds great. I'll be there.
speakerB.fa: عالی به نظر می‌رسد. می‌آیم.

speakerB.en: Thank you for the invitation. I'd be delighted to come.
speakerB.fa: از دعوتتان متشکرم. خوشحال می‌شوم بیایم.

speakerB.en: I'd love to, but I'm afraid I have other plans.
speakerB.fa: خیلی دوست دارم، اما متأسفم برنامه دیگری دارم.

speakerB.en: I'm not sure yet. Can I let you know later?
speakerB.fa: هنوز مطمئن نیستم. می‌توانم بعداً به شما خبر بدهم؟

speakerB.en: Great. See you then.
Sure. I'll bring a cake.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a friend for coffee
scenarios.context: One friend invites another for a coffee break.

speakerA.en: Hi! Do you want to have coffee?
How about now? There's a café near here.
No, it's five minutes away.
I'll pay for the coffee.
Are you free for a coffee this afternoon?
There's a new café on Main Street. Do you want to try it?
Shall we meet there at half past three?
My treat this time. You paid last week.

speakerB.en: Sure! When?
Okay. Is it far?
Great. Let's go!
Thank you! That's very kind.
Yes, I finish work at three.
Sure. I heard the cakes are very good.
That works for me. I'll see you there.
Thank you! That's very kind.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting someone to a birthday party
scenarios.context: A friend invites a classmate to a birthday party.

speakerA.en: Hi! It's my birthday on Friday.
Thank you! Would you like to come to my party?
It's at my house. It starts at six.
Just bring yourself. See you there!
I'm having a birthday party next Saturday. Would you like to come?
It starts at six. We're going to have dinner and cake.
It's at my house, 12 Park Road. You can bring a friend.
Just bring yourself. I don't need any gifts.

speakerB.en: Happy early birthday!
Yes, I'd love to. Where is it?
Okay. Can I bring something?
Great. See you on Friday!
Thanks for inviting me! What time does it start?
That sounds great. Where is it?
Thank you. Should I bring a gift or something to eat?
OK, but I'll bring a small present anyway.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a colleague to a team lunch
scenarios.context: A coworker invites a colleague to lunch with the team.

speakerA.en: We're having a team lunch today. Do you want to join?
To the Italian restaurant near the office.
At half past twelve. We can walk together.
Great. See you at the entrance.
We're having a team lunch on Friday. Would you like to join us?
We're going to the Thai restaurant next to the office.
We're leaving at twelve thirty. Is that OK for you?
Great. Do you eat spicy food?

speakerB.en: Yes, thank you. Where are we going?
That sounds good. What time?
Okay. I'll be ready.
See you then!
Yes, thanks. Where are we going?
Nice. What time are we leaving?
Yes, that's fine. I'll finish my report before then.
A little, but please tell them not too spicy.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a friend to the cinema
scenarios.context: Two friends make plans to see a movie.

speakerA.en: Do you want to see a movie tonight?
There's a new comedy. It starts at eight.
It's in the city center. Let's take the bus.
Yes. See you at the bus stop.
Do you want to see a movie on Friday night?
There's a new comedy at the Grand Cinema. It starts at eight.
Yes, I'll book them now. Do you prefer seats in the middle?
Let's meet at seven thirty in front of the cinema.

speakerB.en: Yes! Which movie?
I like comedies. Where is the cinema?
Okay. Shall we meet at seven?
Perfect. See you!
Sure! What's playing?
That sounds fun. Can we buy the tickets online?
Yes, the middle is best. Thanks!
Perfect. I'll bring some money for popcorn.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a guest for dinner at home
scenarios.context: A host invites a new friend to have dinner at home.

speakerA.en: Would you like to have dinner at my house?
Tomorrow evening at seven. Is that okay?
It's 12 Green Street, the blue house.
Maybe some dessert. I'll cook the rest.
Would you like to have dinner at our house on Sunday?
Do you eat meat, or are you vegetarian?
No problem. I'll cook chicken with rice. Dinner is at seven.
Just some juice, if you like. We have everything else.

speakerB.en: Yes, I'd love to. When?
Yes, that's fine. What's your address?
Thank you. Should I bring something?
Okay. I'll bring a cake. See you tomorrow!
That's very kind of you. I'd love to.
I eat everything, but I don't like fish.
Sounds delicious. Can I bring something?
OK. I'll bring orange juice. Thank you again.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a colleague to a dinner party
scenarios.context: A woman invites her colleague to a dinner at her home.

speakerA.en: I'm having a few friends over for dinner on Saturday. Would you like to join us?
Around seven. There's no need to bring anything, but you're welcome to if you'd like.
No, not that I know of. I'll text you my address this afternoon.
Very casual. We just want everyone to relax and enjoy the evening.

speakerB.en: That's really kind of you. What time are you planning to start?
Then I'll bring a dessert. Is anyone in the group allergic to nuts?
Thanks. Should I dress up, or is it a casual evening?
In that case, I'll see you on Saturday. I'm really looking forward to it.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting someone to a wedding
scenarios.context: A friend hands over a wedding invitation and explains the details.

speakerA.en: I wanted to give you this in person. We're getting married in June, and we'd love you to be there.
It's in a small garden near the lake, and the reception will be in the hotel next door.
We've reserved some rooms at a special price. I'll send you the booking information soon.
Of course you can bring someone. Just let us know by the end of next month.

speakerB.en: Congratulations! I'm so happy for you both. Where will the ceremony take place?
That sounds beautiful. Is there anything I should know about transportation or accommodation?
Perfect. Could I bring a guest, or is it only for the people named on the invitation?
I'll confirm as soon as I check my calendar. Thank you for including me.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a neighbor to a community event
scenarios.context: A neighbor invites another resident to a street festival.

speakerA.en: Have you heard about the street festival this weekend? We're hoping to get everyone involved.
Yes, absolutely. There will be food stalls, live music, and games for the children.
We still need a few volunteers to set up the tables in the morning, if you have time.
Be there at nine and ask for Helen. She's organizing everything.

speakerB.en: I saw a poster in the lobby, but I wasn't sure it was open to all residents.
That sounds like fun. Is there something I can do to help with the preparations?
I can do that. What time should I arrive, and who should I speak to?
Great. I'll bring my kids too. It will be a good chance to meet the other families.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a business partner to a formal dinner
scenarios.context: A manager invites a client to a company dinner.

speakerA.en: We're holding a dinner next Thursday to celebrate the completion of the project. We'd be honored if you could attend.
Mainly senior staff and a few of our partners from the regional offices. It will be a fairly intimate gathering.
Business attire is sufficient. We want people to feel comfortable rather than overdressed.
By all means. The more, the merrier. I'll have the reservation amended accordingly.

speakerB.en: That's most gracious of you. May I ask who else will be present?
In that case, I'd be delighted. Is there a dress code I should be aware of?
Understood. Would it be appropriate to bring a colleague, as she's been closely involved in the project?
Thank you. We're looking forward to the occasion, and to strengthening our working relationship.

scenarios.scenario: Extending an invitation to a spontaneous trip
scenarios.context: A friend suggests an impromptu weekend away.

speakerA.en: I know it's short notice, but how would you feel about driving up to the coast this weekend?
You've been saying that for weeks. Surely you can spare two days to recharge?
Exactly. I've found a small guesthouse that has a room available, and it's reasonably priced.
That would be perfect. We could stay until Sunday evening and avoid the rush back.

speakerB.en: It's tempting, but I've got a pile of work I'm supposed to finish by Monday.
You have a point. I've been running on empty lately, and the sea air would do me good.
If I get up early on Saturday and finish the worst of it, I might manage to join you in the afternoon.
All right, you've persuaded me. I'll bring my laptop, but I promise not to open it.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting someone to join a community project
scenarios.context: A volunteer invites a neighbor to take part in a local initiative.

speakerA.en: We're setting up a community garden on the vacant lot by the school, and we'd love to have you involved.
Nothing too demanding. Most people contribute a couple of hours at the weekend, whenever they're free.
Not in the least. We have several experienced growers who are happy to share their knowledge.
That would be a tremendous help. We haven't managed to reach many residents so far.

speakerB.en: It sounds worthwhile. What would be expected of me in terms of time and commitment?
I'm not much of a gardener, I'm afraid. Would that be a problem?
In that case, I'd be glad to help. I could also assist with publicity, since I work in communications.
Then it seems like a good match. I'll send you the details of our first meeting.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a distinguished speaker to give a keynote
scenarios.context: A conference organizer formally invites a renowned expert to deliver the keynote address.

speakerA.en: On behalf of the organizing committee, I'd like to invite you to deliver the keynote at our annual symposium in March.
We'd like you to address the ethics of artificial intelligence in healthcare. A fifty-minute address followed by a moderated discussion should suffice.
We're finalizing the program, but we've confirmed two panelists whose views are likely to challenge your own, which we hope will make for a lively exchange.
That would be wonderful. We would of course cover your travel and accommodation, and we'd be delighted to host you for dinner the evening before.

speakerB.en: I'm honored that you thought of me. Might I ask what the committee has in mind in terms of theme and format?
That falls squarely within my current research, which is encouraging. Are there any other speakers I should be aware of?
I welcome that. Debate is far more instructive than agreement. Let me check my schedule and confirm by the end of the week.
That's most generous. I look forward to it, provided nothing unforeseen arises on my end.

scenarios.scenario: Persuading a hesitant friend to accept
scenarios.context: A woman gently encourages a reluctant friend to attend a school reunion.

speakerA.en: I know reunions aren't your thing, but I'd be really glad if you came on Saturday. It wouldn't be the same without you.
You'd be surprised how quickly the conversation finds its own level. Besides, half of them are just as apprehensive as you are.
Daniel and Priya have confirmed, and I believe Marta is flying in from Lisbon. You'd have plenty of familiar faces to anchor you.
Come for an hour. If it's unbearable, you can slip out, and I promise not to hold it against you.

speakerB.en: I appreciate that, truly. It's just that I haven't seen most of those people in twenty years, and I'm not sure what we'd talk about.
That's a comforting thought, though I'm not convinced it's an accurate one. Who else is going to be there?
Marta's coming? That does change things. I'd assumed it would be a room full of strangers wearing name tags.
Fine, you've worn me down. But I'm holding you to that escape clause.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a senior colleague without applying pressure
scenarios.context: A team leader invites a senior executive to an informal team dinner and leaves her free to decline.

speakerA.en: We're organizing a small get-together after the quarterly review, and the team would be delighted if you could join us, though I appreciate how packed your calendar is.
I understand the concern, but I think it would mean a great deal to them. It would be a chance to see you outside the boardroom.
Nothing elaborate. A relaxed dinner at the Italian place around the corner, with no speeches and no slides.
I can guarantee that, at least until dessert. I'll send out a formal invitation this afternoon.

speakerB.en: That's thoughtful of you. I'd hate for my presence to dampen the mood, though. People tend to behave differently when a senior executive walks in.
Put that way, I find it hard to refuse. What kind of event do you have in mind?
That sounds ideal. I'll confess I'm long overdue for an evening when nobody asks me for a decision.
Please do. And tell the team to treat me as an ordinary colleague, or at least to try.

scenarios.scenario: Extending a formal invitation to an awards dinner
scenarios.context: A host invites a distinguished guest to an event, mindful of protocol.

speakerA.en: I'm writing on behalf of the committee to invite you to our annual awards dinner. We'd be honored if you would join us as guest of honor.
A short address of no more than ten minutes, though we would leave the subject entirely to your discretion.
It's on the fourteenth of March, black tie, with drinks from seven and dinner at eight. Accommodation can be arranged if you require it.
Of course; we'd be delighted to have him. I'll have the formal invitation delivered to your office by the end of the week.

speakerB.en: That's a flattering proposition. May I ask what the occasion would require of me beyond my presence?
Ten minutes is a manageable sentence. When is the event, and is there a dress code I ought to be aware of?
That's very thoughtful. Might I bring my husband? He'd be mortified to be left out of an evening of this caliber.
Splendid. Please consider it provisionally accepted, subject to my diary, which is currently a field of landmines.

scenarios.scenario: Persuading a reluctant friend to attend a reunion
scenarios.context: A friend gently coaxes someone who is wary of facing the past.

speakerA.en: I know you're hesitant, but I think you'd regret missing the reunion. It won't be the same without you there.
Nobody is keeping score, I promise. Most people will be too preoccupied with how they look to pass judgment on you.
Both, probably, which is rather the charm of reunions. Come for an hour; if it's unbearable, I'll personally engineer your escape.
Naturally. A good friend always keeps an exit strategy in reserve, and I'm exceptionally good at feigning emergencies.

speakerB.en: I'm not sure I want to confront everyone's polite curiosity about what became of me. It feels like an audit of my life.
That's either comforting or deeply depressing. I can't quite tell which.
You'd really leave with me? That's a generous offer, considering how long you've been looking forward to it.
All right, you've worn me down. One hour, and I'm holding you to the emergency.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a business contact to an informal gathering
scenarios.context: A professional extends a casual invitation while keeping the tone appropriately light.

speakerA.en: We're having a few people over on Saturday evening, nothing elaborate, and it occurred to me you might enjoy meeting some of the team away from the office.
My sentiments exactly. It'll be a relaxed affair, and nobody will be expected to talk shop, though I can't guarantee they'll resist.
Just yourself. My partner has been planning the menu for days, and any addition would be treated as a criticism.
From seven onward. Come whenever you like; the evening tends to organize itself.

speakerB.en: That's a kind thought. I've always believed more is accomplished over a glass of wine than across a boardroom table.
I'll do my best to behave. Is there anything I can bring, or would that be considered presumptuous?
Understood. I wouldn't dream of meddling. What time would you like me to arrive?
Then I'll look forward to it. Please give my regards to your partner and tell them I'm already in their debt.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a neighbor for tea
scenarios.context: A woman invites her neighbor to her house for tea.

speakerA.en: Hello, Mrs. Green. How are you?
Very well. Would you like to have tea with me?
Today at four o'clock, at my house.
Just yourself. I have cake.

speakerB.en: I'm fine, thank you. And you?
That's kind. When?
Four o'clock is good. Can I bring something?
Wonderful. See you at four!

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a friend to the park
scenarios.context: Two friends make a plan for the afternoon.

speakerA.en: It's a nice day. Do you want to go to the park?
At two o'clock. We can play football.
Of course! The more, the better.
Perfect. Let's meet at the gate.

speakerB.en: Good idea! What time?
Great. Can my brother come, too?
Thanks. I'll bring some water.
OK. See you at two!

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a classmate to study together
scenarios.context: A student invites a classmate to study before a test.

speakerA.en: Hi, Nina. Do you have time after class?
We have a test on Friday. Do you want to study together?
Let's go to the library. It's quiet there.
Yes, that's fine. I'll bring my notebook.

speakerB.en: Yes, I do. Why?
Yes, please. Where do we study?
Good. Is three o'clock okay?
Me too. See you at the library!

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a friend to a weekend trip
scenarios.context: A friend invites another friend on a short trip to the lake.

speakerA.en: Are you busy this weekend?
A few of us are going to the lake on Saturday. Would you like to come?
We're going by car. It takes about two hours.
Yes, please. We'll leave at eight in the morning.

speakerB.en: Not really. Why do you ask?
That sounds great! How are you going to get there?
Can I bring some food for everyone?
Perfect. I'll be at your house at a quarter to eight.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a new colleague to a welcome dinner
scenarios.context: A team member invites a new colleague to dinner.

speakerA.en: Hi, Omar. We're having a welcome dinner for you on Friday.
The whole team. We reserved a table at an Italian restaurant.
At seven thirty. I can pick you up if you like.
Great. Please tell me if you don't eat something.

speakerB.en: Oh, that's very kind. Who is coming?
I love Italian food. What time should I be there?
That would be wonderful. I don't know the city well yet.
I eat everything. Thank you for being so friendly.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a friend to a housewarming party
scenarios.context: A woman invites a friend to celebrate her new home.

speakerA.en: We've finally moved into our new house, and we're having a housewarming party on Saturday.
From six o'clock onwards. There'll be food and music in the garden.
Not really, but if you'd like, a dessert would be wonderful.
Perfect. Feel free to bring someone with you, too.

speakerB.en: Congratulations! I'd love to come. What time should I arrive?
Sounds lovely. Is there anything I can bring?
I'll make my famous chocolate cake, then.
Thanks. I'll check if my sister is free and let you know tomorrow.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a business partner to a conference
scenarios.context: A manager invites a partner to a professional event.

speakerA.en: Our company is organizing a small conference next month. We'd be delighted if you could join us.
It's about new technology in education, and there'll be several guest speakers.
On the twelfth, at the Grand Hotel. Lunch will be provided.
Wonderful. I'll send you the official invitation with the full program.

speakerB.en: Thank you for thinking of me. What's the main topic?
That's right in my field. When and where is it taking place?
I'll have to check my diary, but I'm very interested.
Please do. I'll reply as soon as I've confirmed my availability.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting colleagues to a farewell party
scenarios.context: A colleague organizes a leaving party and invites a coworker to help and attend.

speakerA.en: Have you heard that Anna is leaving at the end of the month? We're thinking of organizing a small party for her.
I'm planning it for the last Friday, after work. We could use the meeting room, if the manager agrees.
Everyone's going to bring something. I was hoping you could be in charge of the drinks, since you know what people like.
We want to keep it a secret until the day itself, so please don't mention it to Anna if you see her.
Brilliant. I'll collect some money for a present too, but nobody is obliged to contribute. It's completely voluntary.
Thank you. I'm sure she'll be touched. I'll send everybody an invitation by email tomorrow morning.

speakerB.en: Yes, I heard the news yesterday. I was really sad, because she's one of the people I enjoy working with the most.
That's a lovely idea. When were you thinking of having it, and have you decided how many people you want to invite?
I'd be glad to help. Shall I buy soft drinks as well? Some people don't drink alcohol, and I'd hate to forget them.
Of course not. My lips are sealed. I won't say a word, and I'll make sure that nobody else mentions it either.
How much were you thinking of? I'd like to give something, but I can't afford very much at the end of the month.
Perfect. I'll also prepare a short speech, if you don't mind. I've worked with her for five years, so I have a lot to say.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a friend to a cultural festival
scenarios.context: A person invites a friend to a food and music festival and discusses the plan.

speakerA.en: Are you doing anything on Saturday afternoon? There's a food and music festival in the old town, and I thought of you.
It starts at noon and lasts until midnight. Apparently, there will be more than fifty stalls with food from different countries.
I'd love to try some dishes that I haven't had before. There's also a concert in the evening by a band that you like.
I was hoping you'd say that. Shall we meet at the station at one, so that we can avoid the biggest crowds?
Good idea. Since it might rain, I'll take an umbrella, and maybe you could bring a small blanket to sit on.
Wonderful. I'll buy the tickets online tonight and send them to you, so we don't have to queue at the entrance.

speakerB.en: Not yet. What's the occasion? It sounds like you have something in mind, and I'm always up for a good plan.
That sounds fantastic. I haven't been to a festival for ages. What kind of food are we talking about?
Which band is it? If it's the one that I'm thinking of, then I'd really like to see them live. Count me in!
Perfect. By the way, what should I wear? If it's going to be a long day, I'd rather be comfortable.
Good thinking. I'll also bring some cash, because I've read that not all of the stalls accept cards.
That's very kind of you. I'll pay you back on Saturday. I'm already looking forward to it.

scenarios.scenario: Organizing a reunion and persuading people to come
scenarios.context: A person calls an old classmate to invite her to a reunion and discusses logistics.

speakerA.en: I'm organizing a reunion for our graduating class, and I was hoping that you'd be able to come. It would be wonderful to see everybody after twenty years.
It's planned for the second weekend of October, at the old school hall. The headmaster has agreed to open it to us, and we're hoping for at least fifty people.
I understand that, but it would mean so much to everyone if you could make it. If it would help, we could arrange accommodation for people who are coming from far away.
That would be great. I'd also like to put together a slideshow of old photographs. Would you happen to have any pictures from the class trips?
Wonderful. If you could send them by the end of next month, I'd be extremely grateful. I'll pass the details on to the others in the meantime.
I'm so glad you'll be there. It won't be the same without you, and I'm sure there'll be a lot of stories to share.

speakerB.en: That's a lovely idea, and I'm flattered that you thought of me. I haven't been back to the town for years, so I'd be curious to see how much has changed.
That sounds promising. I'd certainly like to come, but I'll have to check my work schedule, as I may be traveling around that time, depending on a project.
That's very thoughtful of you. In that case, I'd say it's quite likely that I'll make it. Let me confirm by the end of the week, once I've spoken to my manager.
I've got a whole box of them in the attic, including the ones from the trip to the mountains, in which half of the class had fallen into the river.
I'll scan the best ones and send them to you. Some of them are quite embarrassing, so you might want to ask permission before showing them to the whole room.
I'm already looking forward to it. And thank you for taking the trouble to organize this. It must be a lot of work.

scenarios.scenario: Extending a formal invitation to a business dinner
scenarios.context: A manager invites a client to a dinner and explains the purpose and arrangements.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I'm calling to invite you and your colleague to a dinner next Thursday evening, which we're organizing to mark the completion of our joint project.
It'll take place at the Riverside Restaurant at seven thirty. It's quite a formal occasion, as several members of our board will be present, and they're eager to meet you.
That's very understanding. Should it be impossible for you to attend, we would, of course, be happy to arrange an alternative date, perhaps in the following week.
Excellent. Could you let me know about any dietary requirements, so that the restaurant can prepare accordingly? We'd like everyone to feel comfortable.
I'll make a note of that. Transport will be provided as well, so if you give me the address of your hotel, I'll arrange for a car to collect you.
It's our pleasure. We've valued working with your team throughout the project, and this is a small way of expressing our gratitude.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon, and thank you for the invitation. That's very kind of you. We'd be delighted to attend, although I'll need to check my colleague's availability first.
That sounds splendid. Is there a particular dress code? I'd like to make sure that we dress appropriately, since we haven't met the board members before.
I appreciate your flexibility. I'd say that Thursday should be fine, but I'll confirm by tomorrow morning, in case anything changes on our side.
Yes, my colleague is vegetarian, and I don't eat shellfish. Aside from that, there are no special requirements, but thank you for asking in advance.
That's most generous. We're staying at the Grand Hotel in the center, so a car at seven would be ideal. We'll be waiting in the lobby.
Likewise. It's been a pleasure to cooperate with your team, and we're looking forward to discussing possibilities for future work at the dinner.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting someone to a charity gala
scenarios.context: A person invites a colleague to a charity event and explains the details and dress code.

speakerA.en: I wanted to ask whether you'd be interested in joining me at a charity gala on the twelfth. It's in aid of the children's hospital, and our firm has booked a table for ten.
It's a formal evening, with dinner, a short auction, and a live band. The dress code is black tie, though I think that a dark suit would be perfectly acceptable for most guests.
Tickets are usually two hundred euros per person, but the company will pay for yours, since you've been working so hard on the hospital campaign. It's partly to say thank you.
If you'd like to bring someone with you, that's absolutely fine. I just need to know by Friday, so that I can give the final names to the organizers.
I understand that it's a lot to think about, and there's no pressure at all. Even if you can only stay for the dinner, it would be a pleasure to have you there.
Wonderful. I'll send you the details by email, including the address and the program for the evening. I'm confident that you'll enjoy it.

speakerB.en: That's very kind of you to think of me. I'd love to come, but I'd like to check a few details first. What kind of evening is it, and what would be expected of me?
Black tie is a little outside my comfort zone, since I don't own a tuxedo. Would it be inappropriate to wear a dark suit, or should I consider renting something?
That's very generous of the company. I hadn't expected that. In that case, I'd feel better about accepting, since it's not a cheap evening, and I might have hesitated otherwise.
Thank you. I might bring my partner, who has always been interested in supporting the hospital. Could I let you know by Thursday, in case I need to check her schedule?
I'll try to arrange everything so that we can stay until the end. It sounds like a worthwhile cause, and I'd be pleased to contribute something at the auction, if possible.
Thank you for thinking of me. I'll look forward to your email, and I'll tell you as soon as I've spoken to my partner.

scenarios.scenario: Arranging a surprise party with a partner's help
scenarios.context: A friend phones a partner to coordinate a surprise birthday celebration.

speakerA.en: Hi, it's Tom. I'm calling about Ellie's birthday next month. I'd like to organize a surprise party, but I need your help to make sure that she doesn't find out.
I was thinking of the first Saturday of the month, around seven in the evening. Is she usually free then, or does she have other plans that we'd have to work around?
That's perfect. Could you tell her that you're taking her out for dinner, and then make sure that you arrive at our friend's house by seven fifteen? The guests will be waiting inside.
I've already invited about twenty people, including her colleagues and a couple of friends from her university days. I wasn't sure whether to invite her parents, but I'd like them to be there.
Fantastic. And do you happen to know whether there's anything that she'd particularly like as a present, or that she'd prefer us not to give? I don't want to get it wrong.
Thank you so much. I'll send you a list of everyone who's coming, and we'll arrange a time to go over the details later this week.

speakerB.en: Hi, Tom. What a lovely idea! She's been feeling a bit low lately, so a surprise like this would be exactly what she needs. How can I help?
The first Saturday is fine. As far as I know, she has nothing planned, but I'll check her calendar and make sure that nobody else books her in. She tends to be spontaneous.
That should be easy. She loves going out to restaurants, so she won't suspect a thing. I'll book a table at her favorite place, and keep her there until about seven, then drive her over.

Her parents would be delighted. They're driving from the coast, so I'll call them and arrange it. Just make sure that they don't mention it on the phone to her. Her mother is not very good at keeping secrets.
She mentioned that she wanted a new camera, and she was looking at a particular model. If a few of you chip in together, it could be a gift from everybody. I'll send you the details.
Perfect. I can't wait to see her face. Let's keep in touch by messaging, and I'll delete everything on her side, in case she sees it by accident.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a reluctant colleague to a team retreat
scenarios.context: A manager tries to persuade a colleague who doesn't enjoy team-building events to join a weekend retreat.

speakerA.en: I wanted to catch you before the end of the day. We're organizing a weekend retreat for the department next month, and I'd really like you to come, albeit I know it's not everyone's idea of fun.

I understand the reservation, and I'd say you're not alone. Should you decide to come, you'd find it's much more relaxed than the usual team-building nonsense. It would be a shame if you missed the chance to talk to people outside your own project.

No climbing, I promise. It's mostly walking, a couple of workshops, and plenty of free time. Should anything feel uncomfortable, you're free to opt out, and nobody would think any less of you. It's worth bearing in mind that the director will be there too.

It's a converted farmhouse about two hours north, from Friday evening to Sunday lunchtime. Should the travel be a problem, I could give you a ride, since I'm driving up anyway. As far as I'm concerned, the car trip is half the fun.

Wednesday is perfect, and you'd still have until Thursday if you need it, since I have to book the rooms by then. It would be a shame to lose a place, even though several others would happily take it.
I'll ask the organizers, but I'd say it's very likely. Should there be any problem, I'll let you know straight away. It would be lovely to have you there, and I'm glad you're keeping an open mind.

speakerB.en: That's kind of you, but to be honest, I'm not sure it's for me. Retreats tend to involve trust exercises and awkward small talk, and I'd rather spend my weekend recovering from this month's deadlines.
Fair point, although I do see most of those people during the week. Should I be worried about the program? If it involves climbing walls or role-playing games, I'd rather withdraw now.

Now that is interesting. It would be worth coming just to have an informal conversation with her, since I've been hoping to discuss the new analytics project. Where exactly is the retreat, and how long would we be away?

That would help a great deal. On the other hand, my sister's visiting that weekend, so I'd have to check whether she minds being left alone for a day. Should I let you know by Wednesday, or is there a deadline?
I'll make sure to decide in time. To be honest, you've talked me round more than I expected. Should my sister be happy to come along, would it be possible to bring her to the Saturday dinner?
Thanks for being so patient with me. Should I forget to reply, feel free to remind me, because I tend to put off decisions that I'm secretly looking forward to.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting an old friend to an anniversary dinner at short notice
scenarios.context: A host calls a friend who is visiting town for a few days and invites her to a dinner celebrating a wedding anniversary.

speakerA.en: I know it's rather short notice, but I was wondering whether you might be free on Saturday evening. We're having a small dinner to celebrate our twentieth anniversary, and it wouldn't feel complete without you.

That's no trouble at all. I was thinking we could start at seven, so you'd have plenty of time to enjoy yourself and still get a decent night's sleep. Would you prefer a vegetarian option, or is it fine to leave the menu to chance?

Not at all, though I'd say that bringing yourself is enough. If you insist, bring whichever wine you'd like to share, provided you don't spend too much. I'd rather you save your money for the trip home.

About twelve, mostly old friends, so it's relaxed. Wear whatever you feel comfortable in, though I'd say a jacket wouldn't hurt, since my mother-in-law likes to remark on these things. She's coming, I'm afraid, however hard I tried to avoid it.

A few of them, yes. I was hoping you'd tell your story about the camping trip again, whenever the conversation dips. In case you've forgotten it, it's the one with the borrowed tent and the thunderstorm.
That would be me, of course, but I'll allow you the credit for one evening. I'll text you the address tonight, and please don't hesitate to call me if you get lost, whichever route you take.

speakerB.en: Twenty years already! Congratulations to you both. I'd be delighted to come, although I should warn you that my flight home leaves on Sunday morning, so I may have to slip away early, in case the traffic is bad.
Leave it to chance; I'll eat whatever is put in front of me. I was wondering whether I could bring something, a bottle of wine perhaps, or would that offend your sense of hospitality?
Understood. By the way, will there be many people? I was wondering whether it's a formal occasion, in case I should dress up a little more than I'd planned.
Ha! I'll make sure to look respectable. Will anyone from the old college group be there? I was wondering whether it might turn into a bit of a reunion.

How could I forget it? Fine, I'll tell it, as long as nobody expects me to be modest about my part. Just in case the details have drifted over the years, you'd better remind me who actually pitched the tent.
Perfect, I'll see you on Saturday. I wonder how long it's been since we last sat around a table together, and I think the answer is far too long. Thank you for including me.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting an estranged brother to a parents' anniversary
scenarios.context: A man phones his brother after two years of silence to invite him to their parents' fortieth anniversary dinner.

speakerA.en: Callum, thanks for picking up. I know it's been two years, and I wouldn't be calling were it not important. Rarely have I felt so nervous about a phone call, but Mom and Dad's fortieth anniversary is on the fourteenth, and I'd like you there.

Everyone, including Aunt Rosa and the cousins, though what matters is that Mom specifically asked for you. It's high time we stopped avoiding each other, and I'd rather you heard that from me than from a mutual friend. Would you consider it?

Nor have I, and I regret most of them. Were it not for my stubbornness, we'd have settled it in a week. I'm not asking you to forget anything, only to sit at the same table. Whatever you think of me, Mom shouldn't suffer for it.

Absolutely not. I suggest that we both agree to leave the house out of it entirely, at least that evening. It's not that the issue has vanished, but that the day belongs to them. Would you be comfortable with that arrangement?

At the old restaurant by the river, at seven. Little did I expect you to be so open to this, so I'm rather relieved. Should you prefer to arrive early and see Mom alone first, I could arrange that quietly. Does that appeal?
Thank you, truly. For what it's worth, I'd have understood if you'd said no. Needless to say, Mom will be overjoyed. Shall I tell her you're coming, or would you rather surprise her?

speakerB.en: Owen, this is unexpected. Had you called a year ago, I might have hung up. I'll listen, though, since it's about our parents. Not that I've forgotten the date, but I assumed I wasn't welcome. Who else is coming?

I'd be lying if I said I hadn't thought about it. Seldom does a week pass without my wondering how things went so wrong. Be that as it may, the argument about the house wasn't minor, and I haven't forgotten the things you said.

That's fair, and I admit I've been stubborn too. The longer I stayed away, the harder it became to return. What I'd like to know is whether you intend to bring the subject up at the party. I couldn't bear a scene.

I would, as long as we speak privately afterwards. Had we done that two years ago, we'd have spared ourselves a lot of trouble. Mind you, I'm not promising we'll resolve everything. Where is the dinner being held?

Actually, yes. It would make the first moment easier. Not only do I owe her an apology, but I also owe her a visit, which I've postponed for months. All things considered, I'm glad you phoned. I'll be there by six.
Let me surprise her. It's the least I can do, and she'll probably cry either way. Come to think of it, perhaps you could save me a seat nearby. Not that I need protection, but it would help.

scenarios.scenario: Inviting a visiting professor to a home dinner
scenarios.context: A host invites a visiting professor from abroad to dinner at her home and explains local customs.

speakerA.en: Professor Lindgren, I wonder whether you'd allow me to invite you to dinner at our home on Friday. Seldom do we have visitors of your standing, and my husband and I would be honored. Are you free that evening?

Please bring nothing but yourself, although a small gift is a lovely gesture if you insist. What I'd suggest is a box of sweets, since my children would be thrilled. Should you prefer, fruit is always welcome. Do you have any dietary restrictions?

Seven would be ideal. It's customary here that guests arrive a few minutes late, but you needn't follow that, since I know punctuality matters in your country. No sooner had I mentioned the time to my husband than he began planning the menu.

It is, though I'd rather you didn't feel obliged. We keep slippers by the door for visitors. What I should mention is that dishes are shared, so you'll serve yourself from the center. Does that seem unusual to you?

Two colleagues from our department and a neighbor who's fond of history. Were you to feel tired, please say so, and nobody will mind. It's essential that you feel comfortable, and we'd never wish to keep you late. Does that sound reasonable?

The pleasure is ours. For what it's worth, my daughter has been rehearsing a little welcome speech in Swedish. Needless to say, it's far from perfect. Shall I send you our address and a map, in case your driver is unfamiliar?

speakerB.en: How very kind of you. I'd be delighted, and I'm free until Saturday. Not that I expected such hospitality, since I've only been here a week. Had I known I'd be invited, I'd have prepared something to bring. What would be appropriate?

I eat nearly everything, apart from shellfish, which doesn't agree with me. Not only am I quite adventurous, but I'm also curious about local dishes. Were it not for conferences, I'd rarely eat at someone's home. What time shall I arrive?

Then I shall arrive at precisely seven, to be on the safe side, or perhaps five past, as a compromise. Mind you, I'm not certain what the etiquette is regarding shoes. Is it customary that guests remove them?
Not unusual, but delightful. The more communal a meal is, the more I enjoy it. By and large, my colleagues find sharing dishes surprising, but I find it warm. Might I ask who else will be present?

Entirely. It's not that I'm easily tired, but that I'd like to be fresh for Saturday's lecture. Not only will I enjoy the evening, but I'll also gain a better understanding of the city. All things considered, I'm very grateful.
Please do, and do tell her I'm honored. Come to think of it, I'd love to hear the speech, mistakes and all. I'll see you on Friday, and thank you again for such a thoughtful invitation.

scenarios.scenario: Polite acceptance
scenarios.context: Accepting an invitation gracefully.

speakerA.en: Would you like to come to dinner on Friday?
Great! Do you eat fish?
Good. Come at seven o'clock.
No, just come! See you Friday.
I'd love to come, thank you.
speakerA.fa: خیلی دوست دارم بیایم، ممنون.

speakerA.en: That would be wonderful. I'll be happy to join.
speakerA.fa: عالی خواهد بود. خوشحال می‌شوم ملحق شوم.

speakerA.en: Yes, I'd be delighted to accept.
speakerA.fa: بله، با کمال میل می‌پذیرم.

speakerA.en: Sounds perfect! I wouldn't miss it.
speakerA.fa: عالی به نظر می‌رسد! از دستش نمی‌دهم.

speakerA.en: I'll be there at seven o'clock sharp.
Can I bring a salad or some dessert?
Is there anything else I can do to help?

speakerB.en: Yes, I'd love to. Thank you!
Yes, I do. I like it very much.
Okay. Should I bring anything?
Thank you so much. See you then!
I'm glad you can make it.
speakerB.fa: خوشحالم که می‌توانید بیایید.

speakerB.en: Great! I'll count you in.
speakerB.fa: عالی! حساب شما را می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: Wonderful! We'll start around seven.
We'd be delighted to have you. Please bring a friend if you like.
Perfect, I'll see you then.
speakerB.fa: عالی، پس می‌بینمتان.

speakerB.en: A dessert would be wonderful. Thank you!
No, just come and enjoy the evening.

scenarios.scenario: Polite refusal
scenarios.context: Declining an invitation politely.

speakerA.en: Do you want to go to the park on Sunday?
Oh, that's a pity. Are you busy?
I understand. Maybe next time?
I'm sorry, but I won't be able to come.
speakerA.fa: متأسفم، اما نمی‌توانم بیایم.

speakerA.en: I'd love to, but I already have plans.
speakerA.fa: خیلی دوست دارم، اما از قبل برنامه دارم.

speakerA.en: Thank you so much for asking, but I can't make it.
speakerA.fa: خیلی ممنون که دعوت کردید، اما نمی‌توانم.

speakerA.en: I wish I could, but I'm afraid I'm busy that day.
speakerA.fa: کاش می‌توانستم، اما متأسفم آن روز مشغولم.

speakerA.en: Thank you for understanding. I'd love to meet up another time.
Maybe next time! Thanks anyway.
speakerA.fa: شاید دفعه بعد! به هر حال ممنون.

speakerA.en: I have to work late that evening.
Please send me some photos of the party.

speakerB.en: Thank you for asking, but I can't.
Yes, I have to visit my grandmother.
Yes, next time for sure!
No problem, maybe another time.
speakerB.fa: اشکال ندارد، شاید دفعه دیگر.

speakerB.en: That's a pity, but I understand.
speakerB.fa: حیف شد، اما متوجه می‌شوم.

speakerB.en: Don't worry, we'll catch up later.
speakerB.fa: نگران نباش، بعداً می‌بینمت.

speakerB.en: I completely understand. Let's plan for another day.
speakerB.fa: کاملاً درک می‌کنم. بیایید برای روز دیگری برنامه بریزیم.

speakerB.en: You're always welcome, whenever works for you.
speakerB.fa: همیشه خوش‌آمدید، هر وقت که برایتان مناسب بود.

speakerB.en: Of course. I'll invite you again soon.
I understand. Don't worry about it.
I will. I hope we can meet soon.

scenarios.scenario: Saying yes and asking for details
scenarios.context: A guest accepts an invitation and checks the time.

speakerA.en: I'm having a party tomorrow. Can you come?
You're welcome. It's at my house.
It starts at seven.
Until about ten o'clock.
Thank you for the invitation. I'd be happy to come.
What time does the party start?
Where exactly is the place?
Is there a dress code?

speakerB.en: Yes, I can. Thank you for inviting me.
What time does it start?
How long does it last?
Perfect. See you tomorrow!
Wonderful! I'm glad you can join us.
It starts at eight, but you can come earlier.
It's at 15 Garden Street, opposite the library.
No, just wear something comfortable.

scenarios.scenario: Saying no politely with a reason
scenarios.context: A person refuses an invitation and gives a simple reason.

speakerA.en: Do you want to come to the cinema tonight?
Oh, no problem. Is it a lot?
Good luck with your test!
Sure. Let's do that!
Thanks for asking, but I can't come on Saturday.
I'm visiting my grandparents that weekend.
I'm really sorry. I'd like to come another time.
That would be great. Thanks for understanding.

speakerB.en: Sorry, I can't. I have homework.
Yes, I have a test tomorrow.
Thank you. Let's go next week.
Great. Have a nice evening!
Oh, that's a pity. Is something wrong?
That sounds lovely. Please say hello to them.
Sure. We'll do something next month.
No problem. Enjoy your weekend!

scenarios.scenario: Not sure yet
scenarios.context: A person needs more time before answering.

speakerA.en: Can you come to my party on Saturday?
Of course. Do you have other plans?
No problem. Please tell me by Friday.
Thanks. I hope you can come!
I'm not sure if I can come. Can I tell you tomorrow?
I have to check my work schedule first.
Is it OK if I come a little late?
Thanks. I'll message you tomorrow morning.

speakerB.en: Maybe. Can I tell you tomorrow?
I'm not sure. I need to ask my mother.
Okay. I'll call you.
I hope so too. Thank you!
Of course. Take your time.
No problem. Just let me know by Thursday.
Yes, that's fine. We'll save you some food.
Perfect. I hope you can make it.

scenarios.scenario: Declining a colleague's invitation
scenarios.context: A coworker politely declines an invitation to a team event.

speakerA.en: We have a team dinner on Thursday. Can you come?
That's a pity. Is there a problem?
I'm sorry to hear that. Are you okay?
Good. Maybe next time then.
Thank you for inviting me to the team dinner.
I'm afraid I have another plan that evening.
Please have a nice time without me.
Yes, please invite me next time.

speakerB.en: Thank you, but I can't come.
Yes, I have a doctor's appointment.
Yes, I'm fine. It's just a check-up.
Yes, please invite me again!
You're welcome. Can you join us on Thursday?
That's a shame. We'll miss you.
We will. Maybe you can join the next one.
Of course. Thanks for letting me know.

scenarios.scenario: Changing the time of a plan
scenarios.context: A guest accepted, but needs to change the time.

speakerA.en: Hi! Are we still meeting at six?
Why? Is there a problem?
That's okay. Seven is fine.
No problem. See you at seven!
I'm sorry, but can we change the time? I can't come at six.
Could we meet at eight instead?
Thank you. My meeting finishes late.
I'll text you when I leave the office.

speakerB.en: Yes, but can we meet at seven?
I'm sorry. My bus is late today.
Thank you for understanding.
See you! Sorry again.
Sure. What time is better for you?
Eight is fine. Dinner will be a bit later.
No problem. I'll tell the others.
Great. See you at eight.

scenarios.scenario: Declining a party invitation because of work
scenarios.context: A man turns down a birthday party invitation because he has a deadline.

speakerA.en: We're celebrating my birthday on Friday night. I really hope you can make it.
Oh, that's a pity. Are you sure you can't take even a couple of hours off?
Don't worry, I understand. Maybe we can have lunch together next week instead.
Sounds good. Good luck with your work, and try not to stress too much.

speakerB.en: Thanks for inviting me. Unfortunately, I have an important deadline on Monday, so I'll be working all weekend.
I wish I could, but I'm already behind schedule. I'm really sorry to miss it.
I'd like that. Let's pick a day once the project is finished.
Thanks. Have a wonderful birthday, and I'll bring you a present when we meet.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting an invitation and asking for details
scenarios.context: A woman happily accepts an invitation to a weekend trip.

speakerA.en: A few of us are going camping by the river next weekend. Do you want to come along?
Just a sleeping bag and some warm clothes. We already have two tents and the food.
We're driving, and we plan to set off on Friday after work, around six.
That would be nice, thanks. We'll split the cost among everyone.

speakerB.en: I'd love to! I haven't been camping since I was a teenager. What should I bring?
That's easy enough. How are we getting there, and when are we leaving?
Perfect. I'll leave early so I'm not late. Can I contribute something for the gas?
No problem. I can't wait. It's exactly what I need after a stressful month.

scenarios.scenario: Refusing an invitation and suggesting an alternative
scenarios.context: Someone cannot go to the movies but proposes another plan.

speakerA.en: There's a new action movie opening tonight. Do you want to go and see it with me?
I'm sorry to hear that. Is it something serious, or just a cold?
That's wise. Would you like me to go anyway, or should we wait until you're better?
That works for me. I'll pick one that we'd both enjoy.

speakerB.en: It sounds fun, but I'm not feeling very well, and I'd rather stay home and rest.
Probably just a cold, but I don't want to risk making it worse.
Please go ahead without me. How about we see a movie together next weekend?
Thank you for being so understanding. Enjoy the movie tonight!

scenarios.scenario: Declining an invitation without causing offense
scenarios.context: A woman tactfully turns down a colleague's invitation.

speakerA.en: We'd love you to join us at the lake house for the weekend. It would be a good chance to relax.
Oh, that's a shame. Is it something we could work around?
I understand completely. Family should come first, of course.
Not at all. Perhaps we could arrange something next month, when things have calmed down.

speakerB.en: That's a very generous offer, and I'm touched you thought of me. Unfortunately, I'm not able to make it.
I'm afraid not. I've committed to a family obligation that I can't reschedule.
Thank you for being so understanding. I'd hate you to think I was turning you down lightly.
I'd welcome that. Please give my regards to everyone, and I hope the weekend goes well.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting with conditions
scenarios.context: A man accepts an invitation but mentions a scheduling limitation.

speakerA.en: We're having a small get-together on Saturday evening. Could we count on you to come?
That's not a problem. Come for as long as you like. We'd rather see you briefly than not at all.
Just yourself, though a bottle of something would be welcome if you insist.
Around eight, but people tend to drift in later. You won't be the last to arrive.

speakerB.en: I'd be happy to, although I may have to leave early. I'm flying out first thing on Sunday.
That's reassuring. Shall I bring anything? I wouldn't want to arrive empty-handed.
I'll see what I can find. What time do you expect things to get going?
Then I'll aim for half past. Thanks for including me. I've been looking forward to it.

scenarios.scenario: Turning down an invitation due to a prior commitment
scenarios.context: A professional declines a networking event.

speakerA.en: There's a networking evening on the fifteenth, and your name came up as someone we'd like to see there.
That's unfortunate. Is there any chance you could pop in later on?
I appreciate your honesty. Would you like us to send you the details of future events?
We'll make sure you're on the list. Thank you for letting us know so promptly.

speakerB.en: That's flattering, and I wish I could say yes. Regrettably, I've already agreed to attend another event that evening.
It's possible, but I wouldn't want to promise something I might not be able to deliver.
Please do. I'd be glad to participate in the next one, given more notice.
Of course. I hope the evening is a success, and I'd be keen to hear how it went.

scenarios.scenario: Declining a prestigious invitation diplomatically
scenarios.context: A director turns down an invitation to join an advisory board without damaging the relationship.

speakerA.en: We were hoping you'd consider joining our advisory board. Your expertise would be invaluable to us.
I'm sorry to hear that, though I respect your candor. Is there anything that might change the picture, such as a reduced time commitment?
That's a principled position, and I admire it. Might we revisit the question in a year or so?
That would be tremendously helpful. We'd value your recommendation.

speakerB.en: I'm genuinely flattered, and I've given it serious thought. Regrettably, I don't believe I could do the role justice given my current commitments.
That's a generous offer, but half-hearted involvement would serve neither of us. I'd rather decline now than disappoint you later.
I'd welcome that. In the meantime, I'd be happy to recommend a colleague who is better placed to take this on.
I'll send you her details tomorrow. Please extend my thanks to the board for the confidence they've shown in me.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting an invitation with reservations
scenarios.context: A guest accepts a dinner invitation but is candid about a possible conflict and a food allergy.

speakerA.en: We're having a few friends over on Friday, and we'd love for you to join us. Do say you'll come.
That's no problem at all. Come when you can and leave when you must, and we'll keep a plate aside for you.
Eight is perfect. Is there anything you don't eat? My husband tends to experiment whenever guests are involved.
Duly noted. We'll play it safe, though I can't vouch for the dessert.

speakerB.en: I'd like nothing better, though I should warn you that I may have to leave early. A project of mine goes live that weekend.
That's very accommodating. I'd hate to arrive late and disrupt the evening, so I'll aim to be there by eight.
I'm happy with anything, short of shellfish. I'm allergic, I'm afraid, and I'd rather not make an entrance of the wrong kind.
I'll take my chances. Thank you for including me, and I'll let you know by Thursday if anything changes.

scenarios.scenario: Withdrawing from an accepted invitation
scenarios.context: A woman apologizes for having to cancel after accepting, and offers to make amends.

speakerA.en: I'm afraid I owe you an apology. I won't be able to make it on Saturday after all, and I feel dreadful about it.
My father was admitted to hospital this morning. It isn't life-threatening, but I'd rather be at his side.
You're very understanding. I hate to leave you with an uneven table, though. Would it help if I found someone to take my place?
Then let me make it up to you. Once things settle down, dinner is on me, and I won't take no for an answer.

speakerB.en: Oh, that's a shame. We had been looking forward to seeing you. Has something come up?
Of course you must be there. Please don't give the party another thought; family comes first.
That's kind of you, but there's really no need. We'll manage. Just concentrate on your father.
I'll hold you to that. Send our best wishes to your father, and let us know if there's anything we can do.

scenarios.scenario: Declining a prestigious invitation without causing offense
scenarios.context: An invitee turns down a flattering offer for professional reasons.

speakerA.en: We'd be thrilled if you would deliver the opening lecture at our symposium this autumn. Your work is precisely what our audience needs.
That's a great pity, though I quite understand. Might there be a chance of rearranging your schedule?
Of course. Might you suggest a colleague whose work is comparable, so that we can salvage the occasion?
That would be enormously helpful. Perhaps we might hope to welcome you the following year?

speakerB.en: I'm truly honored, and it pains me to say that I must decline. I've already committed to a research trip during those weeks.
I wish there were, but the arrangements are fixed and involve several other people. I'd hate to let them down.
I'd recommend Dr. Nilsson, who is both brilliant and generous with her time. I'll gladly write to her on your behalf.
Please do ask again. I'd consider it a privilege, and I'll make sure my calendar is less obstinate next time.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting an invitation with a condition attached
scenarios.context: A guest accepts an invitation but has to explain a scheduling constraint.

speakerA.en: Are you able to join us for the charity gala on the twentieth? It would mean a great deal to the organizers.
That's perfectly acceptable. A discreet exit at ten is a small price for your company.
Excellent. We might even seat you near the door to spare you the awkwardness of a long goodbye.
Then we'll arrange that. May I put you down for the full dinner or merely the reception?

speakerB.en: I'd be delighted to, with one reservation. I have an early flight the next morning, so I'll need to slip away by ten.
You're generous. I'll make a point of arriving punctually so I can contribute properly before I vanish.
A thoughtful gesture, though I'd prefer to be near the speakers so I don't miss anything important.
The full dinner, please. If I'm going to leave early, I may as well do so on a full stomach.

scenarios.scenario: Withdrawing from a commitment after previously accepting
scenarios.context: Someone has to retract an earlier acceptance and handle the situation gracefully.

speakerA.en: Thank you for taking my call. I'm afraid I owe you an awkward explanation, and I'd rather do it by phone than by email.
I accepted your invitation to the retreat in good faith, but a family matter has arisen that I can't postpone.
It's nothing dire, but it demands my attention. I feel wretched about withdrawing so late, knowing you've planned around me.
That's very gracious of you. If a replacement would help, I know someone who could step in at short notice.

speakerB.en: Please, go on. I had a feeling there was something you wished to say, given the circumstances.
I'm sorry to hear that. I hope it isn't anything serious, and please don't feel obliged to elaborate.
These things happen, and I'd far rather you dealt with it than turn up preoccupied. Your absence will be felt, but we'll cope.
That would be a considerable help. Please send me their details, and know that there are no hard feelings.

scenarios.scenario: Declining a wedding invitation politely
scenarios.context: A friend explains why he cannot attend a wedding.

speakerA.en: Thank you so much for inviting me to your wedding. It means a lot to me.
I'm afraid I won't be able to make it. I'll be out of the country that week.
Unfortunately not. It's a business trip I can't postpone.
I'd love to take you both out to dinner when I get back.

speakerB.en: We hope you can come. It wouldn't be the same without you.
Oh, that's a pity. Is there any chance you could change your plans?
We understand. Work comes first sometimes.
We'd like that. We'll keep a table free for you.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting an invitation with a condition
scenarios.context: A colleague accepts an invitation but mentions a possible problem.

speakerA.en: We're organizing a team trip to the mountains next weekend. Are you in?
We're leaving on Saturday at noon, so you could still join us.
Fine. Would you like to share a car with Maria and me?
No problem. We'll pick you up at your place at half past twelve.

speakerB.en: It sounds great, but I might have to work on Saturday morning.
In that case, count me in. I'll confirm tomorrow after I talk to my manager.
Yes, please. I'll chip in for the petrol.
Thanks. I'm really looking forward to it.

scenarios.scenario: Declining politely because of a prior commitment
scenarios.context: A person turns down an invitation to a weekend trip while keeping the friendship warm.

speakerA.en: Thanks so much for inviting me to the lake house next weekend. It sounds like a wonderful idea.
Unfortunately, I won't be able to come. I promised my sister that I'd help her move on Saturday, and I can't cancel.
I'm really sorry. If I had known earlier, I could have arranged something different, but she asked me last week.
That's very understanding of you. Would it be possible to do something together the following weekend instead?
Fantastic. I could also bring some food, so that you won't have to do all the cooking for the group.
Thank you. Have a great time, and please send me lots of photos, so that I feel like I was there.

speakerB.en: That's a shame, but I understand. Family comes first, and I'm sure that your sister really appreciates your help.
Don't worry about it. We only decided last night, so there was no way for you to know. We'll try to organize something else.
Absolutely. We don't have any plans for that weekend, so we could go for a hike, or have a barbecue in the garden.
That would be great. Everyone loves your cooking, and it would make our lives much easier. We'll let you know the details soon.
We'll miss you, though. It won't be the same without you, but I'm looking forward to meeting up when we get back.
I will. Good luck with the move, and don't carry anything too heavy by yourself.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting an invitation and asking about details
scenarios.context: A guest accepts an invitation to a dinner and asks what to bring.

speakerA.en: Thank you for the invitation to dinner on Friday. I'd love to come, and I'm really looking forward to it.
What time should I arrive? I'll be leaving work at six, so I could be at your place by seven fifteen at the latest.
Of course. Is there anything I can bring? I'd be happy to prepare a dessert, or perhaps I could bring some wine.
Good point. I'll make a lemon cake, which I've been practicing recently, and I'll get a bottle of white wine as well.
I don't mind in the least. By the way, is anyone else coming, or is it only the two of you?
That's nice. I look forward to meeting them. Please let me know if anything changes before Friday.

speakerB.en: I'm delighted that you can come! It's been far too long since we last saw each other properly.
Seven thirty would be perfect. We'll have a drink first, and then we'll eat around eight, once everything is ready.
That's very kind of you, but you really don't have to bring anything. A dessert would be wonderful, though, since I never have time to bake.
My husband loves lemon cake, so you've made a very good choice. We'll have fish, so white wine will go well with it.
We've also invited our neighbors, Paul and Lena, who just came back from Italy. I think you'll enjoy talking to them.
I will. If you have any food allergies, tell me now, because I haven't finished planning the menu yet.

scenarios.scenario: Turning down a job offer graciously
scenarios.context: A candidate declines a job offer while keeping a positive relationship with the employer.

speakerA.en: Thank you very much for the offer. I've given it considerable thought, and I'm truly grateful that you chose me from so many applicants.
After careful consideration, I've decided that I can't accept the position. It was an extremely difficult decision, as I was very impressed by the team and the company.
The main reason is that I've received another offer that is closer to my long-term goals, and it would allow me to specialize in an area that I'm particularly passionate about.
I'd like to thank you for the time and attention that you gave to my application. Had circumstances been different, I would have gladly joined you.
That's very generous of you to say. I'd certainly like to stay in touch, and I'd be happy to recommend colleagues who might be suitable for the role.
Thank you for understanding. I wish you every success in finding the right person, and I hope our paths cross again in the future.

speakerB.en: Thank you for letting us know. I must admit that we're disappointed, because we were all impressed by you, and we had hoped that you'd become part of our team.
I appreciate that you've told us clearly and promptly. Many candidates delay their answer, which makes planning very difficult for us. May I ask what influenced your decision?
That's perfectly understandable. It's important to choose a job that matches your ambitions, and I can't blame you for following that path. Was salary a factor at all?
That's kind of you to say. If the other offer doesn't work out for any reason, please feel free to contact us again. The door is always open.
That would be very helpful. If you could send me a couple of names, I'll contact them next week. We're still hoping to fill the position before the end of the month.
Likewise. It was a pleasure meeting you, and I hope you enjoy great success in your new role.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting an invitation with conditions
scenarios.context: A person accepts a weekend invitation but needs to negotiate the timing and arrangements.

speakerA.en: Thank you for the invitation to your cabin in the mountains. I'd love to join you, although there are a couple of things that I need to sort out first.
My main concern is that I have a deadline on Monday morning. If I could bring my laptop and do a few hours of work on Sunday evening, it would be perfect.
That would be a big help. I wouldn't want to disturb the group, so I'd find a quiet corner, and I promise to be finished before dinner.
Also, I'm not much of a hiker, and I wouldn't want to hold anyone back. Would there be something less strenuous for those who don't feel like walking all day?
That sounds ideal. In that case, I'll accept with pleasure. Should I bring anything for the weekend, such as food or sleeping bags?
Perfect. I'll leave on Friday after work, and I should arrive by about eight. Thank you for being so flexible.

speakerB.en: I'm so glad you can come! We were afraid that you'd say no. What's the issue? We'll do whatever we can to make the weekend work for you.
That's no problem at all. There's a wireless connection at the cabin, and we have a small desk in the second bedroom, where you can work undisturbed.
Don't worry about it. We're not planning anything on Sunday afternoon, except perhaps a short walk, and you're welcome to join if you've finished.
Of course. We'll organize some alternatives, such as a visit to the village market or a boat trip on the lake, so everyone can choose what suits their energy.
We have plenty of blankets, so you don't need to bring bedding. If you could pick up some fruit and drinks on the way, that would be wonderful.
That's fine. Drive carefully, because the road is narrow and can be icy in the evening. Call me if you have any trouble finding the place.

scenarios.scenario: Declining extra work without damaging your relationship
scenarios.context: An employee politely refuses an additional project from a manager and offers alternatives.

speakerA.en: Thank you for thinking of me for the new project. I appreciate your confidence, and I can see that it's an interesting opportunity. However, I'm afraid that I'll have to decline.
