At the moment, I'm already responsible for three major deadlines, and if I took on anything else, I'd run the risk of doing all of them less well. I don't think that would be fair to you or to the team.

I understand that you're in a difficult position, and I'd like to help as much as I can. Would it be possible for me to contribute in a smaller role, perhaps by reviewing the plan or advising someone else?
Another possibility would be to postpone my involvement until the end of next month, when the current projects will be finished. If the timing is flexible, I'd be glad to take it over then.
I really appreciate that. I'd also suggest asking Peter. He has the necessary skills, and I believe that he recently finished a project, so he might have the capacity.
Thank you for being so understanding. I hope that this won't affect your opinion of my commitment, because I'm just as keen as ever to contribute to the success of the team.

speakerB.en: I understand, and I appreciate you telling me directly. It's not an easy request, and I know that you've been working under a lot of pressure. Can you tell me what's making it difficult?
That's a fair concern. I'd rather have three projects done properly than five completed carelessly. I only asked because the client specifically requested someone with your experience.
That's a constructive suggestion. A smaller role might actually work well. If you could review the plan for two or three hours a week, that would be enough to ensure that we're on the right track.
Unfortunately, the deadline can't be moved, since the client is expecting a first draft at the beginning of next month. But a reduced involvement from you might help us manage.
Peter's a good idea. I'll speak to him this afternoon. I hadn't thought of him, because he's usually so busy, but you're right, he finished his last project on Monday.
Of course not. In fact, it shows that you're honest about your limits, which is something that I value highly. Thank you for being open about it.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting a wedding invitation and explaining travel plans
scenarios.context: A guest replies to a wedding invitation and discusses logistics with the couple.

speakerA.en: Thank you for the invitation. I was so happy when I opened it, and I'd be absolutely delighted to attend. I wouldn't miss your wedding for anything.
I'll need to fly in, so I wanted to ask about the best way to get from the airport to the venue. I've looked at the map, and it seems quite far from the nearest town.
That's a great idea. If there's a shuttle, I'd much rather use that than hire a car, because I'm not familiar with the roads, and I wouldn't want to be late for the ceremony.
One more thing: I'm vegetarian, so I thought I'd tell you in advance, in case the caterers need to know. I hope that's not too much trouble for the kitchen.
Thank you. I'm planning to arrive the day before, and stay for two nights. Do you know whether there are still any rooms available at the hotel that you recommended?
Perfect. I'll make a reservation this evening. I'm so happy for both of you, and I can't wait to celebrate with you.

speakerB.en: We're so happy that you can come! It wouldn't have been the same without you. We were hoping that you'd say yes, but we didn't want to push you.
It's about forty minutes from the airport, and public transport is limited, I'm afraid. But we've organized a shuttle bus that will leave from the airport hotel at noon on the day before the wedding.

Exactly, it's much easier. There's another shuttle from the hotel to the venue on the day itself, which will leave at two. You'd have plenty of time to get ready, and you can relax during the journey.
It's no trouble at all. We already have a number of vegetarian guests, and the chef has prepared a special menu. Thank you for telling us. We'll add a note next to your name.
The group booking is still open until the end of the month, so you should be able to get a room. If you tell them that you're a guest at our wedding, they'll give you a discounted rate.
Thank you, that means a great deal to us. We'll send you the final program in a few weeks, and we'll see you very soon.

scenarios.scenario: Declining a close friend's invitation without causing offense
scenarios.context: A friend invites someone to a promotion party, but the guest has a work deadline and has to say no without hurting any feelings.

speakerA.en: I'm having a few people over for my promotion on Friday, and I'd be really disappointed if you couldn't make it. Everyone's been asking whether you'll be there, since you've been so busy lately.
That's a pity, but I understand. Is the deadline really immovable, or is there any chance you could finish early, as long as you pushed hard on Thursday?
I see your point. What if you came for an hour, just to say hello? Even if you didn't stay long, it would mean a lot, and nobody would expect you to stay until midnight.

Fair enough. On the other hand, I don't want you to feel that you're letting me down, because you aren't. Why don't we pick a date next week, so we can celebrate properly once your deadline has passed?
It isn't awkward at all. I'd say that being honest is the best thing a friend can do. Shall we say Wednesday, provided your schedule allows it, and I'll book that Italian place you like?
Consider it done. Good luck with the report, and don't work yourself into the ground. Had I known you were under this much pressure, I'd have offered to help.

speakerB.en: Congratulations, you deserve it! Much as I'd love to come, I'm afraid I've got a deadline on Monday, and I'd be poor company if I spent the evening checking my email. Had I known earlier, I'd have planned around it.

To be honest, it's out of my hands. The client has already moved it twice, so I'd rather not risk asking again. Much as I'd like to say yes, I'd only spend the party worrying, which wouldn't be fair on you.

That's a generous offer, and as far as I'm concerned it's tempting. Had it been any other week, I'd have jumped at it. The trouble is that an hour out would break my concentration for the rest of the night.
I'd love that. Much as I'm sorry to miss Friday, a quiet dinner would honestly suit me better. Had you suggested it earlier, I'd have saved us both this awkward conversation.
Wednesday works perfectly, as long as I've sent the report by then. I'll message you on Tuesday night to confirm, in case anything changes. And please save me a slice of the cake on Friday.
That's very kind, but you've already helped by being so understanding. I'll raise a glass to you from my desk on Friday, and we'll make up for it next week.

scenarios.scenario: Accepting a family invitation on a provisional basis
scenarios.context: A friend invites someone to a family reunion at a lake house, and the guest can only give a conditional answer because of work.

speakerA.en: The whole family is getting together at my parents' lake house in August, and everyone would love you to join us. Do you think you could take a few days off?
From the fourteenth to the seventeenth, although you wouldn't have to stay the whole time. Some people are only coming for the weekend, since it's a long drive for those who live in the city.
That's perfectly fine. I'd say a provisional yes is better than a polite no. Would you mind letting me know by the end of the month, though, so that I can sort out the sleeping arrangements?
Dogs are welcome, as long as he gets along with my mother's cat, which is a big if. On the other hand, there's plenty of space outside, so they could easily keep their distance.
Bring whatever you like, though desserts are always in short supply, so something sweet would be much appreciated. I'd rather have homemade than store-bought, if it isn't too much trouble.
A text is perfect. I'll put you down as a provisional yes, and I'll keep a bed for you unless I hear otherwise. It will be lovely to see you.

speakerB.en: It sounds wonderful, and I'd very much like to come. I may well be able to, provided that my manager approves the leave, which I'll know by the end of the week. When exactly were you planning to go?
That helps. I might well come for just two nights, unless the project deadline gets moved forward. To be honest, I'd hate to say yes and then cancel, so I'd rather give you a conditional answer now.

Of course, and I'll do my best to confirm sooner. Unless something unexpected comes up, I'm fairly confident it'll work. Would it be all right if I brought my dog, provided that he doesn't bother anyone?

I'll introduce them gradually, and he may well surprise us. He's very gentle, unless someone steals his food. Is there anything I can bring, perhaps something for the barbecue, provided you tell me what's needed?

My famous lemon tart, then, as long as the weather isn't too hot to transport it. I may well bake two, in case the first one doesn't survive the journey. Shall I confirm by text, or would you prefer an email?
I'm looking forward to it already. I'll message you as soon as my manager signs off, and, provided that all goes well, I'll arrive on the fourteenth with a tart and a very excited dog.

scenarios.scenario: Declining a fundraiser invitation on matters of principle
scenarios.context: A doctor politely turns down an invitation to speak at a charity gala because of the event's main sponsor.

speakerA.en: Dr. Patel, thank you for calling back. I hope you'll say yes, because it's not every day we manage to secure a speaker of your reputation. Rarely have our guests responded so warmly to an invitation, so may I count on you for the gala?

I see, and I appreciate your frankness. I wasn't aware you had reservations about them. What I'd like to understand is whether the issue is the company itself or the way it's being presented at our event.

I'm afraid that's unlikely, since the contract guarantees visibility. Had we known your feelings earlier, we might have negotiated differently. Be that as it may, the funds will pay for twelve scholarships. Does that alter your thinking in any way?

That's generous, and I'm sure the committee would be touched. Whatever you decide about the gala, your support matters. Should you send a donation directly, I'd see that it's allocated to the scholarship fund. Is that what you have in mind?

One or two have mentioned it quietly. Seldom do people speak up, because they fear causing offense. Mind you, your decision may prompt the committee to reconsider future sponsors. Would you mind if I raised it at the next meeting, without naming you?

Understood, and thank you for your honesty. For what it's worth, I respect your position, even though I'd hoped for a different answer. Needless to say, you'll be welcome at any future event. Shall I email you the donation details?

speakerB.en: Gloria, it is with real regret that I must decline. Were it not for the sponsor, I'd have accepted at once, since the cause is one I admire. Not that I doubt your intentions, but I'd rather not appear alongside that company's name.

A bit of both, honestly. It's the company's record on safety that troubles me, not the generosity of this particular donation. Little did I realize, until I read the program, that they'd be headlining. Would it be possible to remove their logo from my session?

It tempts me, I'll admit, but the more I consider it, the more I feel I'd be compromising myself. Under no circumstances do I want my refusal to damage the scholarships. Might I contribute privately instead, without attending?

Exactly. Not only would the money reach the students, but it would also spare us both an awkward evening. All things considered, I think that's the cleanest solution. May I ask whether other speakers share my concerns?

By all means, as long as it's presented constructively. What I'd hope for is a clear policy, so that nobody faces this dilemma again. It's not that I wish to criticize, but that I'd like the event to succeed without controversy.
Please do, and thank you for taking this so graciously. Come to think of it, I'd be glad to give a talk next spring, if the funding is arranged differently. Do keep me in mind.

scenarios.scenario: Declining repeated invitations from a persistent acquaintance
scenarios.context: A woman finally explains to an enthusiastic acquaintance why she keeps turning down his invitations.

speakerA.en: Anna, there you are! I've been trying to reach you all week. There's a barbecue at my place on Saturday, and I won't take no for an answer, since you've turned me down three times already. Rarely do I give up so easily, you know.

Of course I do, a little! What's keeping you so busy? Were it not for those commitments, you'd surely come. Come to think of it, you said the same last month, so I'm beginning to suspect something. Is it me, or the barbecue?

That's kind, but I'd rather know the truth. Not until you tell me can I stop wondering. Whatever the reason, I can take it, as long as it's honest. Is there something about my gatherings that doesn't suit you?

Well, that's a relief, and a surprise. I'd always assumed you were simply busy. What if I invited you for a quiet dinner instead? Just the two of us, or perhaps with my sister. Would that be more appealing?
Wednesday is perfect. What shall I cook? Not only am I a decent chef, but I've been dying to try a new recipe on someone. Were you to name a favorite, I'd attempt it. Is there anything you can't eat?

Agreed on both counts. For what it's worth, I'm glad you were honest, since I've been inviting you in entirely the wrong way. Needless to say, Wednesday at seven. I'll text you the address, and you'll have dessert duty.

speakerB.en: Victor, it's lovely to hear from you, and I appreciate your persistence. I'm afraid I can't make it, though. Not that I don't enjoy your company, but Saturdays are the only time I have to myself. I hope you don't take it personally.

Neither, I promise. It's not that I'm avoiding you, but that my week is demanding and I recover at home. Had I realized how my replies sounded, I'd have been clearer. Under no circumstances would I wish to hurt your feelings.

Honestly, large gatherings drain me. Seldom do I come home from one feeling anything but exhausted. By and large, I prefer quiet dinners with one or two people. Be that as it may, I'm grateful you keep thinking of me.

Much more, in fact. The fewer people there are, the more I enjoy myself. Should you choose a weekday evening, I'd be delighted. It's not that I dislike parties, but that I'm happier in smaller company. Does Wednesday suit you?

I'm not fussy, but I'd love something simple, perhaps pasta. All things considered, you'd be doing me a favor by letting me bring dessert. What time should I arrive? And please, no more barbecues for a while, at least not for me.
Perfect. Thank you for being so understanding, Victor. Come to think of it, this is the first time anyone has asked why I decline. I'll see you on Wednesday, and I promise to arrive hungry.

scenarios.scenario: Informal farewell
scenarios.context: Two people part ways casually.

speakerA.en: Bye, Anna! I have to go now.
Thank you. You too! Are you free tomorrow?
Great. See you tomorrow!
Catch you later!
speakerA.fa: بعداً می‌بینمت!

speakerA.en: It was great seeing you. Take care!
speakerA.fa: دیدار شما عالی بود. مراقب خودت باش!

speakerA.en: I've got to run. Talk soon!
speakerA.fa: باید بروم. به زودی صحبت می‌کنیم!

speakerA.en: See you around!
speakerA.fa: می‌بینمت!

speakerA.en: I have to run. I'm late for class.
Text me about the weekend!

speakerB.en: OK, Sam. Have a nice day!
Yes, I am. Let's meet at nine.
See you! Goodbye.
Bye! Take it easy.
speakerB.fa: خدا حافظ! سخت نگیر.

speakerB.en: See you later, alligator!
speakerB.fa: بعداً می‌بینمت!

speakerB.en: You too! Have a good one.
speakerB.fa: شما هم! روز خوبی داشته باش.

speakerB.en: Goodbye, and thanks for everything.
speakerB.fa: خدا حافظ و ممنون برای همه چیز.

speakerB.en: See you around!
speakerB.fa: می‌بینمت!

speakerB.en: Will do. Have a good one!

scenarios.scenario: Formal farewell
scenarios.context: Leaving a formal event or meeting.

speakerA.en: Goodbye, Mr. Brown. Thank you for the meeting.
Have a nice evening.
See you next week.
Goodbye, it was a pleasure meeting you.
speakerA.fa: خداحافظ، از ملاقات شما خوشحال شدم.

speakerA.en: Thank you for your time. I must be going now.
speakerA.fa: از وقتی که گذاشتید متشکرم. حالا باید بروم.

speakerA.en: I hope to see you again soon.
speakerA.fa: امیدوارم به زودی دوباره شما را ببینم.

speakerA.en: Please give my regards to your family.
speakerA.fa: لطفاً سلام مرا به خانواده‌تان برسانید.

speakerA.en: Thank you. I wish you every success, and I hope we meet again.
Thank you for your time. It was a pleasure meeting you.
I'll send you the documents tomorrow morning.
Please say hello to your family for me.
Goodbye. I hope we can work together soon.

speakerB.en: You're welcome, Mr. Lee. Thank you for coming.
Thank you. You too.
Yes, see you next week. Goodbye.
It was nice meeting you too. Goodbye.
speakerB.fa: من هم از ملاقات شما خوشحال شدم. خداحافظ.

speakerB.en: Thank you for coming. Have a safe journey.
speakerB.fa: ممنون که تشریف آوردید. سفر بخیر.

speakerB.en: It was a pleasure. I'll pass on your regards.
I hope we can meet again. Take care.
speakerB.fa: امیدوارم دوباره ملاقات کنیم. مراقب باشید.

speakerB.en: I will. Goodbye, and all the best.
speakerB.fa: حتماً. خداحافظ و بهترین‌ها را برایتان آرزو می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: The pleasure was mine. Have a safe trip home.
Thank you. I look forward to receiving them.
I will. Goodbye, and good luck with everything.
So do I. Take care.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a friend's house
scenarios.context: A guest says goodbye after a visit.

speakerA.en: It's late. I must go now.
Thank you for the tea. It was very nice.
Say hello to your mother.
Goodbye! See you soon.
Thank you for the lovely dinner. It's getting late.
I should go now. I have an early start tomorrow.
No, thanks. I'll take a taxi.
I will. Say goodbye to your parents for me.

speakerB.en: Already? Please come again.
You're welcome. I'm happy you came.
I will. Be careful on the road.
Bye! Call me tomorrow.
You're welcome. I'm so glad you came.
Of course. Do you need a ride to the station?
OK. Text me when you get home.
I'll tell them. Goodnight, and safe travels.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving work
scenarios.context: Two coworkers say goodbye at the end of the day.

speakerA.en: It's five o'clock. I'm going home.
Thanks. You too! Are you here tomorrow?
OK. See you tomorrow!
I'm leaving now. Are you staying late?
Don't work too hard. See you tomorrow.
Do you have any plans for tonight?
Sounds good. Enjoy your evening.

speakerB.en: Me too. Have a good evening.
Yes, I am. I start at nine.
Goodbye, Kate!
Yes, I need to finish this report.
Thanks. Have a nice evening!
I'm going to the gym and then cooking dinner.
You too. Say hi to your family.

scenarios.scenario: After class
scenarios.context: A student says goodbye to the teacher and a friend.

speakerA.en: Goodbye, teacher. See you on Monday.
Thank you for the lesson.
Oh, thank you! Here it is. Have a nice weekend!
Thank you for the lesson, Mr. Evans. Goodbye.
I won't. I'll finish it tonight.
Bye, Lena! Are you coming to the library?
OK. Have a good afternoon!

speakerB.en: Goodbye, Lucy. Have a good weekend.
You're welcome. Study well! Don't forget your book.
Thank you. You too!
You're welcome. Don't forget your homework.
Good. See you on Thursday.
Not today. I'm going home. See you tomorrow!
You too. Bye!

scenarios.scenario: At the airport or station
scenarios.context: A person says goodbye to a friend who is traveling.

speakerA.en: Your train is at ten o'clock.
Have a good trip!
Please call me when you arrive.
Goodbye! Take care.
Have a safe flight. Call me when you land.
Do you have your passport and ticket?
I'm going to miss you. Come back soon.
They're calling your flight. You should go.

speakerB.en: Yes. I must go now.
Thank you. I will miss you.
OK. I will call you tonight.
Goodbye! See you soon.
I will. Thank you for bringing me here.
Yes, I checked them twice.
I'll miss you too. I'll visit in the summer.
Goodbye! Take care of yourself.

scenarios.scenario: Saying good night
scenarios.context: Two people say good night at the end of the evening.

speakerA.en: I'm tired, Mom. I want to sleep.
Good night, Mom.
Thank you. See you in the morning.
It's late. I think I'll go to bed now.
Did you lock the front door?
What time do you wake up tomorrow?
Good night. Sleep well.

speakerB.en: OK, dear. It's late.
Good night. Sleep well.
Yes. See you in the morning!
Me too. I'm very tired.
Yes, I did. Everything is OK.
At six. I have an early meeting.
Good night. See you in the morning.

scenarios.scenario: Farewell to a colleague leaving the company
scenarios.context: Coworkers say goodbye on someone's last day at work.

speakerA.en: I can't believe it's already your last day. The office won't be the same without you.
Where will you be working from now on? Have you already found a new job?
That's an exciting step. I hope you'll keep in touch and let us know how it goes.
We'll have to organize a reunion in the summer. Everyone would love to see you.

speakerB.en: That's very kind of you to say. I'll really miss working with all of you.
Yes, I'm moving to a company in Boston. I'll be starting in about three weeks.
Of course. I'll send you my new contact details before I leave tonight.
That sounds like a great idea. Thank you for everything. Take care of yourself!

scenarios.scenario: Seeing a friend off at the airport
scenarios.context: Two friends say goodbye at the airport before a long flight.

speakerA.en: Have you got your passport and boarding pass? I don't want you to miss the flight.
You'll be fine. Just try to sleep on the plane, and call me when you arrive.
I'm going to miss you so much. The year is going to feel very long.
I'll hold you to that. Now go, or you'll be late for security.

speakerB.en: I've checked three times. I'm just nervous because it's such a long trip.
I will. I'll message you as soon as I get a signal at the other end.
It will pass quickly, and I'll come back for the holidays. I promise.
Goodbye! Look after yourself, and say hello to everyone for me.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a party early
scenarios.context: A guest explains that he has to leave a party earlier than the others.

speakerA.en: You're not leaving already, are you? The evening is just getting started.
What a shame. Thanks for coming, though. It meant a lot to me.
Let me walk you to the door. Are you sure you don't want a taxi?
All right. Let me know when you're back, and we'll arrange something.

speakerB.en: I'm afraid so. I have an early flight tomorrow, and I haven't finished packing.
Thank you for having me. The food was delicious, and I enjoyed meeting your friends.
No, thank you. The bus stop is close, and I like the fresh air.
I will. Have a great rest of the night, and goodbye to everyone!

scenarios.scenario: Bidding farewell before emigrating
scenarios.context: A man says goodbye to his best friend before moving abroad.

speakerA.en: I still can't quite believe you're leaving. It doesn't seem real that this is our last evening.
You're doing the right thing. It's an extraordinary opportunity, and you'd always have wondered otherwise.
We'll stay in touch. Distance doesn't have to change anything, as long as we make the effort.
Count on it. I've already been looking at flights for the spring.

speakerB.en: Neither can I. I've spent months planning, and now that it's here, I feel strangely reluctant.
I know, but leaving the people I care about is the hardest part of the whole thing.
I'll hold you to that. And you must come and visit as soon as I've settled in.
Then it's not goodbye, merely see you later. Look after yourself, my friend.

scenarios.scenario: Saying farewell at a retirement party
scenarios.context: A colleague gives a farewell speech to a retiring coworker.

speakerA.en: After thirty years with this company, it's hard to imagine the office without you.
You've been a mentor to so many of us, and your advice has often saved us from our own mistakes.
Whatever you call it, it made a difference. We'd like you to have this as a small token of our appreciation.
Say you'll visit us, and that you won't disappear entirely now that you have all this free time.

speakerB.en: Thank you. I'll miss it more than I expected, especially all of you.
You're giving me too much credit. I simply tried to pass on what others taught me.
That's very thoughtful. I'm genuinely moved. I hardly know what to say.
I promise. Retirement may free my schedule, but it won't free me from my friends.

scenarios.scenario: Parting ways after a short but meaningful encounter
scenarios.context: Two travelers who met on a trip say goodbye.

speakerA.en: Well, this is where our paths divide. It's been an absolute pleasure traveling alongside you.
We make a good team, don't we? Perhaps we should have planned the whole trip together.
True enough. Let's swap contact details before we go our separate ways.
Splendid. If you ever find yourself in my part of the world, you'll have a place to stay.

speakerB.en: The pleasure was mine. I doubt I would have made it through that mountain pass without your company.
Perhaps, although the unplanned parts were what made it memorable.
Of course. Here's my email, and I'll send you the photos as soon as I'm back home.
Likewise. Safe travels, and I hope the rest of your journey goes smoothly.

scenarios.scenario: Thanking a mentor on his last day
scenarios.context: A protégée says goodbye to her mentor on the day he retires.

speakerA.en: I wanted to say something before you leave, though I suspect no words will do justice to what you've meant to me.
Still, I'd be remiss not to acknowledge it. You taught me far more than the technical side of the work; you taught me how to think.
You have my word. I'll try to be as patient with them as you were with me, though I doubt I'll manage it.
I'll call so often you'll wish you'd stayed in the office.

speakerB.en: You needn't say anything. Watching you grow into the professional you are today has been reward enough.
That's the most gratifying thing anyone could say to me. Just promise you'll pass it on to those who come after you.
You'll find your own way, as you always have. And do keep in touch; retirement is bound to leave me with a good deal of time on my hands.
I'd welcome every call. Take care of yourself, and don't let anyone convince you that you're not ready for what comes next.

scenarios.scenario: Parting after a difficult family conversation
scenarios.context: Two brothers say goodbye after a tense but ultimately productive talk about a family dispute.

speakerA.en: I'm glad we finally had this conversation. I'd been dreading it for months, and it turned out to be far less painful than I'd imagined.
I don't expect everything to be resolved overnight, but I'd like to think we've made a start.
I'd like that. And whatever happens, let's not wait another five years before the next time.
Drive safely, and give my love to the children. Tell them their uncle is overdue for a visit.

speakerB.en: I felt the same. We've left too much unsaid for too long, and it's a relief to have it out in the open.
A start is more than we had this morning. I'll call you on Sunday, if that suits you.
Agreed. Life's too short to carry around grievances whose cause we can barely remember.
I will. Goodbye for now, and thank you for being willing to listen.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving after an international assignment
scenarios.context: A team says goodbye to a colleague returning to her home country after a two-year assignment abroad.

speakerA.en: Two years have flown by. I still remember your first week here, when you couldn't find the right meeting room.
You made it easy. You've left a real mark on this team, and I suspect the office will feel rather empty without you.
Then consider this a pause rather than an ending. Our door will always be open if you ever decide to return.
We'll hold you to it. Safe travels, and don't forget us once you're back among old friends.

speakerB.en: Please don't remind me. I must have looked completely lost, yet everyone went out of their way to make me feel welcome.
You're too kind. Leaving is harder than I expected; I've grown more attached to this place than I'd care to admit.
I may take you up on that. In the meantime, I'll be expecting visitors, and I'd like to repay your hospitality properly.
Never. Thank you for everything. You've made this feel less like a posting and more like a second home.

scenarios.scenario: Bidding farewell to a retiring colleague
scenarios.context: A team says goodbye to a respected colleague at the end of a long career.

speakerA.en: On behalf of everyone, I'd like to say how much we'll miss you. The department won't be the same without your quiet authority.
Nonsense. Thirty years of knowledge doesn't walk out of the door without leaving a gap behind it.
You must promise to visit. We'll need someone to tell us when we're repeating mistakes you already warned us about.
We'll do our best. Shall we have one last coffee before the speeches begin?

speakerB.en: That's touching, though I suspect you'll find the department runs rather more efficiently once I'm no longer rearranging the stationery cupboard.
I've been fortunate to work with such a capable group. I'm leaving with considerably more affection than I'd anticipated.
I shall return, if only to say I told you so. In the meantime, please look after each other, and don't let the sentiment fade.
By all means. I'd like to savor the last cup from that dreadful machine, for old times' sake.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a friend at the airport
scenarios.context: Two close friends part ways knowing they won't meet again for a long while.

speakerA.en: I hate airports. They're designed to make goodbyes as cold and efficient as possible, which is precisely what I'm trying to avoid.
We'll speak every week, and I'll visit as soon as I can arrange the leave. It won't feel as distant as you think.
Promise me you'll write, and not just the occasional message with a photograph of your lunch.
Go on, before I embarrass us both in public. Safe travels, and ring me the moment you land.

speakerB.en: I know. I keep telling myself it's only a year, and then I remember how long a year can be.
You always were the optimist. I'll rely on that, because I'm not nearly as convincing at the moment.
I promise. Though I make no guarantees about the lunch photographs; they're a vital part of my correspondence.
I will. Look after yourself, and thank you for everything. It's been far more than I could have asked for.

scenarios.scenario: Ending a business meeting on a cordial note
scenarios.context: Two professionals close a successful negotiation and take their leave.

speakerA.en: Thank you for a most productive meeting. I think we've made more headway in two hours than I'd dared hope.
Likewise. I'll have our legal team send over the draft by Friday, and then we can begin the finer points.
I shall. It would be a pleasure to continue the conversation over dinner when you're next in town.
I will. Safe journey back, and I hope the train is kinder to you than the one this morning.

speakerB.en: The pleasure was mine. It's rare to find counterparts who are both firm and fair, and I appreciate the spirit in which you negotiated.
Excellent. Please extend my regards to your colleagues and say how impressed I was by their preparation.
I'd welcome that, and I'll make a point of keeping the evening clear. Do let me know when you have dates in mind.
One lives in hope. Until next time, then, and thank you again for your hospitality.

scenarios.scenario: At the bus stop
scenarios.context: Two friends say goodbye when the bus comes.

speakerA.en: My bus is coming. I have to go.
You too! Say hello to your mother.
Thanks. Call me tonight.
Bye! See you next week.

speakerB.en: OK. It was nice to see you.
I will. Have a safe trip.
Yes, I'll call at eight. Bye!
See you!

scenarios.scenario: Saying goodbye to a neighbor
scenarios.context: A man says goodbye to his neighbor on moving day.

speakerA.en: Good morning, Tom. I'm moving today.
Thank you for everything. You were a great neighbor.
To another city, but it's not far.
I will. Please take care.

speakerB.en: Oh, really? I'm sad to hear that.
You were great, too. Where are you moving?
Then please visit us.
You too. Goodbye and good luck!

scenarios.scenario: Ending a phone call
scenarios.context: Two friends say goodbye at the end of a phone call.

speakerA.en: It's late, Anna. I need to go now.
Thank you for the nice talk.
Yes, I'll call you after lunch.
You too. Goodbye!

speakerB.en: Okay. Thanks for calling.
Let's talk again on Sunday.
Good. Have a good night.
Bye bye!

scenarios.scenario: Saying goodbye after a holiday stay
scenarios.context: A guest thanks a host family before leaving after a week-long stay.

speakerA.en: Thank you for everything. This week has been one of the best of my life.
I really mean it. Your family made me feel completely at home.
I'll write to you as soon as I get back. Please say goodbye to the children for me.
I will. Take care, and I hope to see you again soon.

speakerB.en: We're going to miss you. The house will feel very quiet without you.
You're always welcome here. Next time, you should stay for a whole month.
They'll be sad they missed you, but I'll pass on your message. Have a safe trip home!
Safe travels! Send us a message when you arrive so we know you're all right.

scenarios.scenario: Saying goodbye to a classmate at graduation
scenarios.context: Two classmates say goodbye on their last day at university.

speakerA.en: I can't believe it's already over. These four years went by so quickly.
I got a job in another city, so I'll be moving next month. What about you?
Let's make sure we keep in touch. Don't just disappear after today.
Definitely. Good luck with everything, and congratulations again!

speakerB.en: I know. I'm happy, but it's strange to think we won't see each other every day.
I'm staying here for now, but I might travel for a few months before I start working.
I won't, I promise. We can set up a group chat so the whole class can stay connected.
You too! I'm sure you'll do great things. Take care of yourself.

scenarios.scenario: Saying goodbye to a friend moving abroad
scenarios.context: Two close friends say goodbye before one of them leaves the country for several years.

speakerA.en: I can't believe this is really happening. In a few hours, I'll be on a plane, and everything will be different.
I'm going to miss you so much. I don't think I've ever had a friend who understood me the way that you do.
I promise that I will. We can talk on the phone every Sunday, and I'll send you photos of everything I see.
I'd love that. Once I've settled in, you should visit me. I'll show you the places I've told you about.
Now you're making me emotional. Thank you for everything, and especially for coming to the airport so early.
I will. Take care of yourself, and don't forget that wherever I am, I'll always be there for you.

speakerB.en: I know. I keep telling myself that it's an exciting new chapter, but it's still hard to say goodbye.
Don't say that, or I'll start crying right here. Promise me that you'll keep in touch, even when you're busy.
Good. And I'll tell you everything that happens here, even the boring things, so that you don't feel left out.
I'd really like to. Maybe next summer, if I can save enough money, I'll come and stay with you for two weeks.
It's the least I can do. Now go, or you'll miss your flight. Send me a message as soon as you land.
Safe travels, my friend. This isn't goodbye forever, only until we see each other again.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a workplace on the last day
scenarios.context: An employee says goodbye to a close colleague on her final day at a company.

speakerA.en: Well, that's it. I've handed in my laptop, cleared my desk, and now there's nothing left to do but say goodbye.
I've been here for nine years, so it's strange to think that I won't see you every morning when I come in.
I'm excited, but I'm nervous as well. I've never worked anywhere else, so I'm not sure what to expect.
I'll miss our lunch breaks the most. They were the best part of my day, even when work was stressful.
That's a great idea. Let's arrange a dinner next month, and you can tell me how things are going without me.
Thank you for everything. I couldn't have asked for a better colleague, and I wish you all the best.

speakerB.en: It doesn't feel real, does it? The office is going to be so empty without you. Who will I complain to now?
Nine years is a long time. I still remember your first day, when you got lost looking for the meeting room.
You'll be fine. You're talented, and any company would be lucky to have you. You're going to do amazing things.
Mine too. We still have to meet up, you know. Just because you're leaving doesn't mean we can't see each other.
Definitely. Don't forget to give me your new number, and let me know if you'd like me to recommend you to anyone.
You too. Keep in touch, and good luck with the new job. We'll be thinking of you.

scenarios.scenario: Saying farewell at the end of an international exchange
scenarios.context: Two exchange students say goodbye after a year studying together abroad.

speakerA.en: I can't quite believe that it's over. Looking back, the year seems to have passed in an instant, yet I feel like a completely different person from the one who arrived.
I think that's the greatest gift of an experience like this. You discover what you're capable of when you're far from everything familiar, and you come away with new confidence.
I'll never forget the night when we got lost on the way back from the festival, and we ended up walking for three hours. It was dreadful at the time, but now it's my favorite memory.
Whenever I think of this year, I'll think of you and the others, and I hope that distance won't prevent us from staying close, however difficult it might seem.
That's a promise I intend to keep. If you ever come to visit, you'll have a place to stay, and I'll show you everything that I'd have loved to show you here.
Safe journey, my friend. Don't forget to message me as soon as you land. Until we meet again.

speakerB.en: Neither can I. It feels like only yesterday that we met at the orientation, both of us terrified that we wouldn't understand a word anyone said.
I agree completely. I came here expecting to improve my language skills, but I've learned far more about myself than about grammar. I'm grateful for everything that happened.
How could I forget? We were soaked to the skin, and you insisted that you knew a shortcut. I still tease you about it whenever I tell the story.
It won't, as long as we both make the effort. Friendships that have been tested by experiences like these tend to last, even if we don't speak every week.
I'd like that very much. And I'll hold you to your promise. Next summer, I'm coming to see the place you've been describing to me for months.
I will. Thank you for making this year unforgettable. I hope all your plans work out, and that we'll look back on this moment with a smile.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a community after many years
scenarios.context: A long-time resident says goodbye to neighbors before moving away.

speakerA.en: I wanted to come and say goodbye in person, since I'm moving at the end of the week, and I'd never forgive myself if I left without thanking you.
Twenty years is a long time, and I've seen this street change in so many ways. Yet the sense of community has always remained, and that's what I'll miss most.
When my husband died, you were the ones who brought food and sat with me, even though we hardly knew each other at the time. I'll never forget that kindness.
I'm moving closer to my daughter. It's a sensible decision, but I'd be lying if I said it wasn't painful to leave the house where I raised my children.
I would be delighted. Please do come and see me, and I'll cook for you, as I used to, although I'm afraid the kitchen won't be quite as large.
Thank you. I think that being surrounded by people who care about you is the most valuable thing in life, wherever you happen to live.

speakerB.en: We were hoping that you'd stop by. The street won't be the same without you. Everyone has a story about how you helped them at some point.
That's very kind of you to say. You were always the heart of this neighborhood, organizing the summer gatherings, and remembering everybody's birthday.
That was the least we could do. You'd have done the same for any of us, and you did, many times. It's what makes this such a special place to live.
We understand, of course. Family should come first, and we're pleased that you'll have support. But you'll be sorely missed, and the house will feel empty.
We'd love to. We were already planning to visit you in the spring, and we'll bring the children, who are going to want to see your garden again.
Wise words. Take care of yourself, and remember that you'll always have friends here, no matter how far away you are.

scenarios.scenario: Saying goodbye to a mentor at the end of an internship
scenarios.context: An intern thanks a mentor and reflects on what they have learned before leaving.

speakerA.en: Before I leave, I wanted to thank you personally for everything that you've done for me. These three months have been more valuable than I could have imagined.
When I arrived, I was convinced that I knew what working in a company was like, but I quickly realized how much I didn't know, and you were always patient with my questions.
I'll never forget the day when you let me present to the client. I was terrified, but afterwards, you told me what I'd done well and what I could improve, and that made all the difference.
I'd like to stay in touch, if that's all right with you. I'd be grateful for any advice about my career, especially as I'm about to start applying for jobs.
Thank you. If I do end up working in this field, I hope that I'll be able to be the kind of colleague that you were to me.
Goodbye, and thank you once again. I hope our paths cross again before long.

speakerB.en: It's been a pleasure having you on the team. I must say that you've exceeded all our expectations, and I'd be delighted to recommend you for any position you apply for.
That's exactly what an internship is for. Nobody expects you to know everything, and your curiosity was one of the things that made you so enjoyable to work with.
You did very well that day, and I think you surprised yourself. Many people never get over the fear of speaking to clients, and you managed it within a few weeks.
Of course. Please keep in touch. Send me a message whenever you like, and let me know how the job search goes. I'm always glad to help, and I'd be interested in how you progress.
That's the best compliment I could hope for. I'm sure you'll do very well, whatever you decide to do. Wherever you end up, you'll bring energy and intelligence to the team.
Goodbye, and good luck. Don't forget us. And remember that the door here is always open, should you ever decide to come back.

scenarios.scenario: Ending a phone call politely with a talkative acquaintance
scenarios.context: A person tries to politely end a long call without offending the other person.

speakerA.en: It's been wonderful to hear all your news, and I'm so glad that you called. I'm afraid, though, that I'm going to have to leave in a few minutes, as I have an appointment.
I'd love to continue this conversation, but I really must be going. Could we pick it up at the weekend, when I'll have more time to listen properly?
That sounds lovely. Saturday afternoon would suit me better, around three. I'll call you, so you don't have to worry about the cost of the call.
Please give my regards to your family, and tell your sister that I was asking after her. I hope the move goes smoothly, and let me know if you need any help.
Of course. I'll be thinking of you. Take care of yourself, and don't work too hard. I'll speak to you on Saturday.
Goodbye for now, and thank you again for calling. Bye.

speakerB.en: Oh, is that the time? I didn't realize I'd been talking for so long. I'm so sorry for keeping you. I've been going on about my own problems, and I haven't asked about you at all.
Of course, of course. I understand completely. I just had so much to tell you, but it can wait. I'd like to hear about your news as well, so Saturday would be perfect.
That's fine with me. Afternoon is better for me too, since I'm usually busy in the morning. I'll be at home, so just call whenever you're ready.
I will, thank you. She'll be delighted that you asked. We're moving in two weeks, and I'm quite nervous, but your offer is very kind. I might take you up on it.
You too. It was lovely to talk, even if I went on a bit too long. I always feel better after speaking to you. We'll catch up properly on Saturday.
Bye, bye. Take care, and I'll talk to you soon.

scenarios.scenario: Saying goodbye to a colleague on their last day
scenarios.context: On her last day at the company, a colleague says goodbye to a teammate she has worked with for six years.

speakerA.en: I can't believe it's my last day. If it weren't for this team, I'd never have lasted six years in a job this demanding, so I wanted to thank you personally before I clear my desk.
To be honest, so am I. By the time I've settled in, I'll probably have forgotten where I put half my belongings. What I'll miss most is the lunchtime arguments about absolutely everything.

I'd say that's the sign of a good team. Wherever I go, I'll be looking for colleagues who disagree with me that cheerfully. Do you think the department will manage without me, or should I feel guilty?
That's reassuring. On the other hand, I hope you'll complain to me from time to time. If it weren't for the occasional gossip, I'd feel completely cut off, so please keep me posted.
I'm staying put, at least until the spring. By next summer I'll probably have moved, but I'll let you know the moment there's an address. In the meantime, let's meet for coffee every few weeks.
Let's do it. I'll send you an invitation tonight, and by the time I've left the building, it'll be done. Thanks again for everything. It's been a privilege to work with you.

speakerB.en: That's kind of you to say, but the credit is yours. Wherever you end up, they'll be lucky to have you. By this time next week, you'll have started a completely new chapter, and I'm still trying to get used to the idea.

Those won't be the same without you. If it weren't for your terrible taste in movies, we'd never have had such lively debates. No matter how often I tell people about them, they never believe how heated they got.

You shouldn't feel guilty for a second. By the end of the month we'll have reorganized the whole project, and honestly, you've left everything in better shape than we found it. We'll cope, no matter how much we complain.
I'll send you updates, I promise, wherever you are. Will you be moving as well, or will you stay in the city? I'd hate to lose touch, no matter how busy we both get.
Every month, at the very least. If it weren't for your reminders, I'd forget half my appointments, so you'll have to keep nagging me from a distance. Shall we put the first one in the calendar now?
The privilege was ours. Take care, and wherever you go, don't be a stranger. Come back and see us, no matter how big your new office turns out to be.

scenarios.scenario: Saying goodbye at the airport to a friend moving abroad
scenarios.context: Two close friends say goodbye at the departure gate just before one of them moves to another country.

speakerA.en: I still can't believe you're actually leaving. It feels like only yesterday that we were planning this, and now we're standing here with your suitcases, trying not to cry.
I'm holding you to that. Whenever you feel homesick, call me, no matter what the time difference is. I'd rather be woken at three in the morning than find out you were lonely.
To be honest, I'm bound to feel odd for a while. It won't be long before I stop expecting you to knock on my door, but I'd say that's just something I'll have to get used to.
I doubt that very much. On the other hand, I'm excited for you, since this is the opportunity you've dreamed of. I'd hate for you to turn it down because of me, so please don't feel guilty.
I believe you. Now, before they call your flight, take this. It's a small notebook, so that you can write down everything you want to tell me. It won't be long before it's full, I imagine.
Go on, they're calling your flight. Have a safe journey, and message me as soon as you land, even if it's just one word. I'll be waiting, no matter how late it is.

speakerB.en: Please don't, or I'll start too. It won't be long before we're laughing about this, and as soon as I've found a place, I'll send you the address so you can book your first visit.

That's a promise, although I'm bound to be busy at first. It's going to take time to settle in, but I'll make sure to call every Sunday, whenever the connection allows. What about you? Are you going to be all right?
Look, as soon as I've saved enough, I'll fly back for Christmas. It won't be long before the months have passed, and you'll be too busy with your new job to miss me properly.
I don't, really, though I can't help thinking about everything I'm leaving behind. As far as I'm concerned, friendships like ours don't depend on distance, and I'll prove it, whenever you need me.
That's a lovely idea, thank you. I'll fill it in on the plane, as soon as we've taken off, and read you the best parts whenever we speak. I'm bound to cry, but I'll try to do it quietly.
I will. Goodbye, my friend, and thank you for everything. It won't be long before we're sitting at our old café again, and I'll tell you every detail of the whole adventure.

scenarios.scenario: Parting from a host family after a year abroad
scenarios.context: An exchange student says goodbye to her host mother on the morning she leaves after a year abroad.

speakerA.en: Carmen, I've been dreading this moment all week. Scarcely had I packed my last suitcase when I realized how difficult it would be to leave. Rarely have I felt so at home anywhere, and I don't quite know how to thank you.

Never. I came expecting a polite, slightly distant arrangement, and what I found was a family. Had anyone told me last September that I'd cry at this door, I'd have laughed. What do you think the children will remember?

More than a little, I daresay. I arrived someone who panicked at every misunderstanding, and I'm leaving someone who can laugh at them. Such was the effect of your kitchen that I've also gained several pounds. Will you ever visit me?

They'd be thrilled, and my mother has already started planning menus. It would appear that two families are about to become one. Granted, they don't share a language, but I'll translate. What shall I tell them about you?

I'll write every week, if only to send photos. The fact remains that I wouldn't be who I am without this year. Little did I know, when I applied, how much it would change me. Is it all right if I hug the children now?
I'll go up. Suffice it to say that I wouldn't miss it. Thank you, Carmen, for everything, and for forgiving all my mistakes with the washing machine. I'll see you at the airport, won't I?

speakerB.en: Oh, sweetheart, you've thanked us a hundred times already. Suffice it to say that having you here has been a joy. Hardly had you arrived when the children adopted you as an older sister. Did you imagine you'd become so attached?

Your terrible jokes in Spanish, most likely, and the way you helped with homework. Not only did you teach them English, but you also taught them patience. In all fairness, they've taught you a little too, haven't they?

Provided that you promise to show us the city, of course. We've never been to Asia, and Miguel has already begun reading guidebooks. Should the visas be arranged, we could come next spring. Would your parents mind hosting us?

That we're not nearly as formal as we pretend. To my mind, the best hospitality is simply treating guests as relatives. Whatever happens, keep writing to us, and don't let a month pass in silence. Will you manage that?
Please do, but warn them, since Lucía has been hiding upstairs. Not that she doesn't want to say goodbye, but she's been crying since breakfast. Shall I fetch her, or would you rather go up yourself?
Of course, we're all coming. Not for the world would we let you leave alone. Go on, then, and when you return, please remember that this door will always be open.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a team after a contentious resignation
scenarios.context: A senior engineer says goodbye to her director after resigning following months of disagreement over a restructuring.

speakerA.en: Paul, I wanted to see you before I leave, since I'd rather part on good terms than on silence. Whatever our differences over the last year, I've learned a great deal from working here. Do you have a moment?

In all fairness, it wasn't one thing. Had the restructuring been explained earlier, I might have stayed. As it was, no sooner had one change been announced than another followed, and nobody consulted the people affected. Did you realize how that felt?

I'd have been honest with the team from the start. People can accept bad news, provided they hear it early. It's not so much the changes that upset them as the secrecy. Not that I expect you to apologize for the board.

Honestly, no, though it's kind of you to ask. I've accepted another offer, and I'm excited about it. Not only is the work interesting, but the culture seems more open. Mind you, I'll miss this team more than I can say.

Something short and warm, without any bitterness. I'd rather be remembered for the work than for the dispute. The fact remains that I've made friends here that I intend to keep. Would you object if I stayed in touch with them?

That would mean a lot, thank you. For what it's worth, I'm grateful you listened today. Needless to say, I'll finish the handover properly before Friday. Shall we say goodbye with a handshake, then, rather than an argument?

speakerB.en: Of course, Rachel, and I'm glad you came. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't disappointed that you're leaving. It's not so much that we're losing an engineer as that we're losing the person who held the team together. Why did it come to this?

Partly, and I should have done more about it. The decisions weren't entirely mine, though, which is no excuse. Were it not for pressure from above, we'd have handled it very differently. What would you have done in my place?

No, but I can acknowledge it, and I do. Looking back, I handled several conversations badly. Should you ever consider returning, I hope you'd feel free to say so. Is there anything we could change that might make you reconsider?
They'll miss you too. Many of them wouldn't have stayed this long were it not for your mentoring. What are you planning to say at the farewell lunch? I imagine they'll expect a speech.

Not at all, and I'd encourage it. By and large, the best leavers become the best allies. Whatever happens, I'd be glad to write you a reference, and I'd mean every word. Shall I draft something this week?
Gladly. Come to think of it, I'd like to shake your hand in front of the whole team on Friday. You've earned that, and so has the work you've done. Safe travels, Rachel, and good luck.

scenarios.scenario: Making a call
scenarios.context: Calling someone and asking to speak to them.

speakerA.en: Hello, this is Alex. Is John there?
Hi, John. Can we meet tomorrow?
At ten o'clock. Is that OK?
May I speak to Sarah, please?
speakerA.fa: لطفاً می‌توانم با سارا صحبت کنم؟

speakerA.en: Could I talk to the manager?
speakerA.fa: می‌توانم با مدیر صحبت کنم؟

speakerA.en: I'd like to leave a message for Mr. Smith.
speakerA.fa: می‌خواهم برای آقای اسمیت پیغام بگذارم.

speakerA.en: Could you tell her that Tom is calling?
Is she free now? It's important.
Yes, please ask her to call me back at 555-0198.

speakerB.en: Yes, this is John. Hi, Alex!
Yes, OK. What time?
Yes, that's fine. See you tomorrow.
Speaking. Who's calling?
speakerB.fa: خودم هستم. شما که هستید؟

speakerB.en: Please hold on. I'll see if she's in.
speakerB.fa: لطفاً گوشی را نگه دارید. می‌بینم آیا هست یا نه.

speakerB.en: I'm afraid he's not available right now. Can I take a message?
speakerB.fa: متأسفم او در دسترس نیست. پیغامی بگذارم؟

speakerB.en: I'll put you through to his office.
speakerB.fa: شما را به دفترش وصل می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry, she's in a meeting. Can I take a message?
Sure. I'll give her your message.

scenarios.scenario: Taking a message or handling wrong numbers
scenarios.context: The caller asks to leave a message or has dialled incorrectly.

speakerA.en: Hello. Is Mary there?
Can I leave a message?
Please tell her to call me. My number is 555-0199.
Thank you. Goodbye.
Can I leave a message for her?
speakerA.fa: می‌توانم برای او پیغام بگذارم؟

speakerA.en: Please tell him I called.
speakerA.fa: لطفاً به او بگویید من زنگ زدم.

speakerA.en: Could you ask her to call me back at this number?
speakerA.fa: می‌توانید از او بخواهید با این شماره به من زنگ بزند؟

speakerA.en: I'm sorry, I must have dialled the wrong number.
speakerA.fa: متأسفم، باید شماره اشتباهی گرفته باشم.

speakerA.en: I'll call back later. Thanks.
speakerA.fa: بعداً دوباره زنگ می‌زنم. ممنون.

speakerA.en: It's Peter Hayes. That's P-E-T-E-R, H-A-Y-E-S.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry. She isn't here.
Yes, of course.
OK. I have your number. I will tell her.
Goodbye.
Sure, what's the message?
speakerB.fa: حتماً، پیغام چیست؟

speakerB.en: I'll give him the message when he returns.
speakerB.fa: وقتی برگشت پیغام را به او می‌رسانم.

speakerB.en: Could you spell your name, please?
speakerB.fa: لطفاً اسمتان را هجی کنید؟

speakerB.en: I'm afraid you have the wrong extension.
speakerB.fa: متأسفم شماره داخلی اشتباه گرفته‌اید.

speakerB.en: No problem. I'll try again later.
speakerB.fa: اشکال ندارد. بعداً دوباره امتحان می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: Got it. I'll pass it on as soon as he comes back.

scenarios.scenario: Calling a friend
scenarios.context: Two friends talk on the phone.

speakerA.en: Hello, Tom. It's Lisa.
I'm fine, thanks. Are you free today?
Let's go to the park.
OK. See you at three!
Hi, Mia! Is this a good time to talk?
I'm calling about Saturday. Are we still meeting?
At two o'clock, at the central station.
Great. Call me if you have any problems.

speakerB.en: Hi, Lisa! How are you?
Yes, I am free after lunch.
Good idea. I like the park.
See you! Bye!
Hi! Yes, I'm just making tea.
Yes, of course. What time were we going to meet?
Perfect. I'll be there on time.
I will. Talk to you soon!

scenarios.scenario: Calling home
scenarios.context: A child calls a parent on the phone.

speakerA.en: Hello, Mom. It's me.
I'm at school. I'll be home at five.
Yes, everything is fine.
I will. I love you. Bye!
Hi, Mom! It's me. Can you hear me?
Yes, I'm fine. I'm calling because I'll be late tonight.
Maybe nine o'clock. I have extra classes.
Thanks, Mom. I'll call you when I leave.

speakerB.en: Hello, dear. Where are you?
OK. Is everything fine?
Good. Be careful on the road.
I love you too. Bye!
Yes, honey. Is everything OK?
How late? Dinner is at seven.
OK. I'll keep some food for you.
Be careful on the road. Love you.

scenarios.scenario: Booking a table
scenarios.context: A customer calls a restaurant to book a table.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want a table for two, please.
Tonight at seven, please.
My name is Ali.
Thank you. Goodbye.
Good evening. I'd like to book a table for Friday.
A table for four, please, at eight o'clock.
Yes, that's fine. Could we have a table near the window?
It's Rossi. R-O-S-S-I.

speakerB.en: Good evening. Which day?
Yes, we have a table at seven. What's your name?
Thank you, Mr. Ali. See you tonight.
You're welcome. Goodbye.
Certainly. For how many people?
I'm sorry, we're full at eight. Is eight thirty OK?
No problem. May I have your name?
Thank you, Mr. Rossi. Your table is booked.

scenarios.scenario: A bad line
scenarios.context: The phone line is not clear and the speakers cannot hear well.

speakerA.en: Hello? I can't hear you.
Can you speak louder, please?
Yes, a little. Can you say it again?
OK. I can hear you now. Thank you.
Hello? I can't hear you very well.
No, you're breaking up. Can you speak louder?
A little better. Could you repeat your last sentence?
Thanks. Let me call you back on my other phone.

speakerB.en: Hello? Can you hear me?
Sorry. Is this better?
Yes. I said, "Call me tomorrow."
Good. Talk to you tomorrow.
Sorry, the line is bad. Can you hear me now?
Is this better? I'll move to another room.
I said the meeting is at three o'clock.
OK. I'll wait for your call.

scenarios.scenario: Calling the doctor's office
scenarios.context: A patient calls to make an appointment.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want an appointment, please.
My name is Sara. I have a cold.
Tomorrow morning is better.
Thank you. See you tomorrow.
Hello. I'd like to make an appointment with Dr. Brown.
I have a bad cough and a sore throat.
Yes, that's fine. Do I need to bring anything?
OK. Thank you very much.

speakerB.en: Hello. What is your name?
OK, Sara. Can you come on Monday?
OK. Come at nine o'clock.
You're welcome. Goodbye.
Of course. What's the problem?
I see. Can you come tomorrow at ten?
Please bring your insurance card and an ID.
You're welcome. See you tomorrow.

scenarios.scenario: Calling to reschedule a doctor's appointment
scenarios.context: A patient calls a clinic to change an appointment.

speakerA.en: Hello, I'd like to reschedule my appointment with Dr. Evans, if that's possible.
It's Peter Collins, and it's on Thursday at ten o'clock in the morning.
Do you have anything available early next week? I'm free every day except Tuesday.
Monday works well for me. Could you send me a confirmation by email?

speakerB.en: Of course. Could you give me your name and the date of your current appointment?
Thank you, Mr. Collins. Unfortunately, Dr. Evans is fully booked on Thursday and Friday.
I can offer you Monday at two thirty or Wednesday at nine. Which would you prefer?
Certainly. You'll receive it within the next few minutes. Is there anything else I can help you with?

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a message for a colleague
scenarios.context: A caller asks to leave a message because the colleague is unavailable.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. Could I speak to Mr. Harris from the sales department, please?
Yes, please. Could you tell him that Anna Brown called about the contract?
It's B-R-O-W-N, and my number is 555-0142. It's quite urgent, so I'd appreciate a quick reply.
Yes, I'll be at my desk until six. Thank you very much for your help.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry, he's in a meeting at the moment. Would you like to leave a message?
Certainly. Could you spell your last name for me and give me your phone number?
I'll make sure he gets the message as soon as he's out. Can he reach you all afternoon?
You're welcome, Ms. Brown. Have a good day, and I'll pass it on right away.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a bad phone connection
scenarios.context: Two friends try to talk, but the signal is poor.

speakerA.en: Hello? Can you hear me? The line keeps cutting out on my end.
I'm on the train right now. Let me try moving closer to the window.
I was asking if you'd still like to meet on Saturday, or if you've changed your plans.
Good idea. I'll send you a message in about twenty minutes, when I arrive.

speakerB.en: Only half of what you're saying. I think you're in an area with a weak signal.
That's a little better. What were you saying about the weekend?
I'd still like to meet. Why don't you text me the time once you're off the train?
Perfect. Talk to you later, and have a safe trip.

scenarios.scenario: Making a formal inquiry by phone
scenarios.context: A customer calls a company to inquire about a service.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm calling to inquire about the maintenance contracts you advertise on your website.
On behalf of a small firm. We have around twenty employees and a number of aging computers.
Could you give me a rough idea of the cost, and whether there's a minimum term?
That would be very helpful. I'd also appreciate it if you could include details of your cancellation policy.

speakerB.en: Certainly. May I ask whether you're inquiring on behalf of a company or as a private individual?
I see. In that case, our business package would probably suit you best. It includes remote support and on-site visits.
It depends on the number of devices, but I can email you a detailed quotation by the end of the day.
Absolutely. May I take your email address and a direct number in case I need to clarify anything?

scenarios.scenario: Handling a complaint over the phone
scenarios.context: A customer service representative deals with a dissatisfied caller.

speakerA.en: I'm calling about an order that was supposed to arrive last week. I've been waiting for ten days now.
It's 48213. This is the second time I've had to chase this up, and frankly, I'm losing patience.
That's absurd. I double-checked the address when I placed the order.
I appreciate that, but I'd like some assurance that it won't happen again.

speakerB.en: I do apologize for the delay. Could you give me your order number so I can look into it?
I understand your frustration. It appears the parcel was returned to our warehouse due to an incorrect address.
I can see the mistake was ours, not yours. I'll arrange for it to be dispatched today with express delivery at no extra charge.
I'll note it on your account and ask my supervisor to follow up. You have my word that it will be handled properly.

scenarios.scenario: Conducting a phone interview
scenarios.context: A recruiter phones a candidate for a preliminary interview.

speakerA.en: Thank you for taking my call. Is this still a convenient time for a brief conversation?
Excellent. Let's begin with what attracted you to the position, given your current role.
Your résumé mentions you led a team of eight. What was the most difficult aspect of managing them?
That's helpful. We'd like to arrange a second interview in person. Would early next week suit you?

speakerB.en: Yes, certainly. I cleared my schedule this morning, so I'm all yours.
I'm drawn to the opportunity to work on larger projects, and I admire the company's reputation for innovation.
Balancing differing personalities while keeping everyone focused on shared deadlines, but I found that clear communication solved most problems.
Tuesday would be ideal. I'll look out for your email confirming the time and location.

scenarios.scenario: Delivering bad news to a client by phone
scenarios.context: A project manager calls a client to explain that a delivery will be delayed.

speakerA.en: Thank you for taking my call. I'm afraid I have some news you won't welcome, and I felt you deserved to hear it directly from me.
The software release will slip by roughly three weeks. A critical flaw surfaced during final testing, and we can't responsibly ship until it's resolved.
A data synchronization fault that only appears under heavy load. Our engineers have isolated the cause, but the fix requires rebuilding part of the architecture.
Entirely, and I'd like to send you a revised schedule in writing today, along with a partial credit on the next invoice.

speakerB.en: That sounds ominous. Please go ahead, and don't soften it on my account.
Three weeks is considerable, given that we've already announced the launch date. What exactly went wrong?
I appreciate the transparency, but you'll understand that this puts me in an awkward position with my own board.
Send me the schedule by close of business, and we'll discuss the credit once I've seen it. I'd rather have a late product that works than a punctual one that doesn't.

scenarios.scenario: Following up on an unanswered proposal
scenarios.context: A consultant phones a prospective client who has not replied to a detailed proposal.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon, Ms. Hale. I'm calling to follow up on the proposal I sent over two weeks ago. I wanted to make sure it reached you.
No need to apologize. If it would help, I'd be glad to walk you through the key points, so you needn't wade through the whole document.
That's a fair concern. We could phase the work, delivering the core features first and refining the remainder over the following quarter.
Then I'll prepare a revised version along those lines and have it with you by Thursday.

speakerB.en: It did, and I apologize for not responding sooner. The past fortnight has been, to put it mildly, chaotic.
That would be a great help. My main reservation is the timeline, which seems rather ambitious for a project of this scope.
Phasing would ease the pressure on my team, and it might make the budget easier to defend internally.
Please do. If the figures hold up, I see no reason why we shouldn't move forward before the month is out.

scenarios.scenario: Escalating a billing dispute to a supervisor
scenarios.context: A customer who was charged twice asks to speak to someone with the authority to fix the problem.

speakerA.en: I've now explained this to three different representatives, and nothing has been done. I'd like to speak to someone with the authority to resolve it.
I was charged twice for the same annual subscription, and every time I call, I'm promised a refund within five working days. That was six weeks ago.
That's precisely what I suspected. I'd appreciate it if you could process the refund now, while I'm on the line.
Thank you. I'd also like a reference number, in case I have to raise this again.

speakerB.en: I understand your frustration, and I apologize for the inconvenience. I'm the team supervisor, so please walk me through what has happened.
That shouldn't have happened. Let me check your account. I can see both charges, and no refund request has been logged against either.
I can authorize it immediately. You'll receive a confirmation email within the hour, and I'll add a note to the account to prevent any further delays.
Of course. It's four-seven-two-nine-one. And once again, I'm sorry it took as long as it did.

scenarios.scenario: Handling a difficult call from an irate customer
scenarios.context: A customer service representative stays composed under pressure.

speakerA.en: I've been passed between four departments in the last hour, and nobody seems able to tell me why my account was suspended.
That would be a refreshing change. I'm told the suspension was an error, yet no one has the authority to reverse it.
And what about the fee I incurred in the meantime? I had to use an alternative service, and it wasn't cheap.
That's fair, although I'd appreciate something in writing so I'm not relying on goodwill alone.

speakerB.en: I sincerely apologize for the runaround. Let me take ownership of this, and I won't transfer you until it's resolved.
I can see that the suspension was triggered by a billing discrepancy that has since been corrected. I'm reinstating the account now.
I'll credit the equivalent amount to your next statement and add a note so no one questions it later.
Absolutely. You'll receive a confirmation email within the hour, and I've noted my direct line should anything go awry.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a precise message for a busy professional
scenarios.context: A caller conveys an urgent but delicate matter to someone's assistant.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I'm trying to reach Ms. Reyes regarding the contract amendment, but I gather she's in meetings until late.
Please do. Could you tell her the counterparty has proposed a revision to clause nine, and that a response is needed before close of business tomorrow?
A call, if possible, since the nuances are difficult to convey in writing. I can be reached on this number after four o'clock.
Only that I'm grateful for her prompt attention. It's rather a delicate matter, and I'd like it resolved amicably.

speakerB.en: That's correct, I'm afraid. May I take a message, and shall I mark it as urgent?
Clause nine, response required by tomorrow evening. May I ask whether you would prefer a call or an email in reply?
I'll make sure she sees it the moment she's out. Is there anything else I should relay?
Understood. I'll pass that on, and you can expect to hear from her either this evening or first thing in the morning.

scenarios.scenario: Conducting a remote job interview by phone
scenarios.context: An interviewer and a candidate navigate the limitations of a telephone interview.

speakerA.en: Thank you for making time for this call. As we can't see each other, I'd suggest we err on the side of being explicit about anything unclear.
Let's begin with your most recent role. What would you say was your most significant contribution over the past two years?
That's considerable. What was the greatest obstacle you faced, and how did you handle it?
A sensible approach. I'll be discussing your candidacy with the panel this week and expect to be in touch by Friday.

speakerB.en: That makes sense. I'm happy to elaborate wherever my answers come across as too brief.
I led the migration of our legacy systems to a cloud platform, which reduced operating costs by nearly a third and improved reliability.
Resistance from colleagues who were wary of change. I addressed it by involving them early and demonstrating tangible benefits rather than imposing the plan.
Thank you. I'd welcome the opportunity to speak with the wider team, and I appreciate your thoroughness today.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a message
scenarios.context: A caller leaves a message for a colleague who is not there.

speakerA.en: Hello, could I speak to Mr. Jones, please?
Yes, please. Could you ask him to call me back?
My name is Laura Smith. My number is 555-0142.
That's right. Thank you for your help.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry, he's in a meeting. Can I take a message?
Of course. What's your name and number?
Let me repeat that: Laura Smith, 555-0142.
You're welcome. I'll give him the message.

scenarios.scenario: Calling customer service
scenarios.context: A customer calls about a problem with an internet bill.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon, customer service. How can I help you?
Can I have your account number, please?
I see the problem. You paid twice in May.
Yes, it will be in your account in three working days.

speakerB.en: Hello. I think there's a mistake on my bill this month.
Yes, it's 4 7 2 9 1.
Can you give me the money back?
Thank you. That's very helpful.

scenarios.scenario: Rescheduling an appointment by phone
scenarios.context: A client phones to change an appointment.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I have an appointment on Wednesday at ten, but I need to change it.
Would Thursday afternoon be possible? I have a meeting on Wednesday.
That would be perfect. Could you confirm it by email as well?
Yes, it's j-smith at example dot com. Thank you for your help.

speakerB.en: No problem. When would be more convenient for you?
Let me check. I have a free slot at three o'clock on Thursday.
Certainly. Could you spell your email address for me, please?
You're welcome. You'll receive the confirmation in a few minutes.

scenarios.scenario: Calling a company about a delivery
scenarios.context: A customer calls to ask about an order that has not arrived.

speakerA.en: Hello, I ordered a bookshelf ten days ago, and it still hasn't arrived.
It's 85-23-17. The website said it would arrive within a week.
Do you know when it will be delivered?
Thank you. If it doesn't come by Friday, I'll call again.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry for the delay. Could I have your order number, please?
I can see it here. There was a problem at the warehouse.
It should arrive on Friday. I'll send you a text message with the exact time.
Understood. Again, I apologize for the inconvenience.

scenarios.scenario: Calling to ask about a job advertisement
scenarios.context: A person phones a company to ask about a position and how to apply.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm calling about the advertisement for the office assistant position that I saw on your website.
I'd like to know whether the position is still available, and what kind of experience you're looking for.
I've worked as a receptionist for three years, so I have experience with phone calls and organizing appointments.
I see. Should I send my CV by email, or is it better to fill in the application form on the website?
Could you also tell me when you're planning to hold the interviews? I'd like to plan around them, if possible.
Thank you very much for your help. I'll send my application this afternoon and hope to hear from you soon.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and thank you for calling. Let me find out who is in charge of this. May I ask your name?
Yes, it is. We're looking for someone who is organized, and who has some experience in an office or in customer service.
That sounds like exactly what we need. Do you speak any other languages? It would be a great advantage in this role.
Either way is fine, but I'd recommend the form, because it makes it easier for us to review all the applications.
We'd like to receive applications by the end of next week, and the interviews will take place during the following week.
You're welcome. Good luck with your application, and please don't hesitate to call again if you have any questions.

scenarios.scenario: Leaving a message and asking someone to call back
scenarios.context: A caller speaks with a receptionist when the person they want is unavailable.

speakerA.en: Hello, could I speak to Mr. Alvarez, please? It's regarding the contract that we discussed last week.
I see. Do you know when he'll be back? I'm afraid that it's quite urgent, and I need an answer before tomorrow.
In that case, I'd like to leave a message. Could you ask him to call me back as soon as he returns?
My name is Helen Carter, and my number is 555 0142. It's about the delivery date, which has to be changed.
Yes, please. Tell him that the supplier has asked for a different schedule, and that we have to give them an answer today.
Thank you. I'll be in the office until six, so he can call me at any time before then.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon. I'm sorry, but Mr. Alvarez is in a meeting at the moment. Can I take a message?
He should be finished around three, but he often has other appointments afterwards, so I can't promise anything.
Certainly. Could you give me your name and telephone number, and tell me briefly what it's about?
Let me write that down. Is there anything else that I should mention, so that he knows how serious it is?
I'll make sure he gets the message as soon as he comes out of the meeting. I'll mark it as urgent.
Very good. I'll let him know. Thank you for calling, Ms. Carter, and have a pleasant afternoon.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a service contract by phone
scenarios.context: A customer calls a telecom provider to renegotiate an expensive contract.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm calling because my contract is about to expire, and I've noticed that the monthly price has risen considerably over the past two years.
I've been a loyal customer for more than a decade, and I'd expect that to count for something. Other providers are offering similar packages for almost half of what I'm paying now.
I appreciate that, but I'm not interested in a minor reduction. If you can't match the offer that I've received elsewhere, I'm afraid I'll have to terminate the contract.
