That's more reasonable. However, I'd also like the installation fee to be waived, and I'd need to have the new terms sent to me in writing before I agree to anything.
I'd like to think about it for a day or two. Could you hold the offer until Friday, and could you email me the details in the meantime?
Thank you for your cooperation. If everything is as you've described, I expect that we'll be able to reach an agreement.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and thank you for calling. I understand your concern. Let me look at your account to see what I can do to help you.
I can see that you've been with us for twelve years, and we truly value your loyalty. I'm able to offer you a ten percent discount on your current tariff for the next year.
I'm afraid that I can't match prices from other companies directly, but let me speak to my supervisor. There may be a retention offer that isn't normally available to new customers.
My supervisor has agreed to reduce your monthly fee by twenty-five percent for twenty-four months, and to waive the installation costs completely. Would that be acceptable?
Of course. I'll make a note on your file so that the offer remains valid until Friday at five, and I'll send the written conditions to your email within the hour.
You're very welcome. Should you have any further questions before making your decision, please call this number and ask for me directly.

scenarios.scenario: Conducting a phone interview for a position
scenarios.context: An interviewer and a candidate speak by phone about a job opening.

speakerA.en: Hello, this is Rachel Moore from Brightline Consulting. I'm calling about the phone interview that we scheduled for today. Is this still a good time for you?
Excellent. To begin with, could you tell me a little about your professional background, and what drew you to this particular position?
That's very interesting. Could you give me an example of a situation in which you had to deal with a difficult client, and explain how you resolved the problem?
That shows a good deal of initiative. Looking ahead, how do you see your skills contributing to a team that's currently expanding into new markets?
Thank you, that's helpful. Do you have any questions for me about the role or about the company, since this is also your chance to find out whether it's a good fit?
I'll certainly pass that on. We'll be in touch by the end of next week, and in the meantime, thank you very much for your time.

speakerB.en: Good morning, Ms. Moore. Yes, this is a perfect time. I've cleared my schedule, and I'm in a quiet room, so we shouldn't be interrupted.
Certainly. I've worked in project coordination for six years, mostly in the education sector, and I'm eager to apply those skills in a more international environment, which I find very motivating.
Last year, a client became very dissatisfied after a delay. I arranged a meeting, listened carefully to their concerns, and proposed a revised timetable, which restored their confidence in us.
I believe that my experience in managing cross-cultural teams would be an advantage. I'm also used to working under pressure, and I've learned to adapt quickly when priorities change.
Yes, I'd like to know how the team is structured, and what kind of support is offered for professional development, since continuing to learn is important to me.
Thank you, Ms. Moore. I appreciated the opportunity to speak with you, and I look forward to hearing from you next week.

scenarios.scenario: Disputing an incorrect utility bill by phone
scenarios.context: A customer calls an energy company about a bill that seems far too high.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm calling about my latest electricity bill, which is nearly three times higher than usual. I don't believe that I could have used that much energy.
My account number is 4471 2290. I live alone, I'm out most of the day, and nothing in my habits has changed. I've checked all my appliances, and nothing seems to be faulty.
I took a reading from the meter yesterday, and it shows a number which is considerably lower than the one on the invoice. Could the company have used an estimated reading?
That would explain it. Is it possible to correct the bill on the basis of my own reading, and adjust the amount accordingly, so that I don't have to pay for energy I didn't use?
I'd appreciate it if you could do that. I'd also like to receive the corrected bill in writing, and to be told how this mistake will be prevented in the future.
Thank you for your help. I'll send the photograph of the meter this afternoon, and I'll expect to hear from you within the week.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and thank you for calling. I'm sorry to hear about the problem. Could you give me your account number, so that I can take a look at your usage history?
Thank you. I can see that the last two bills were based on estimated readings, because our technician couldn't get access to your meter. That would explain the sudden increase.
Yes, that's quite likely. If you can send us a photograph of the meter, showing the date and the numbers clearly, we can recalculate the bill according to your actual consumption.
Certainly. Once I receive the photograph, I'll ask the billing department to issue a corrected invoice. The difference will be credited to your account, or refunded, if you prefer.
Of course. A written confirmation will be sent by email within five working days. As for prevention, I'd suggest that you register for our online system, where you can submit readings every month.
You're welcome. I apologize again for the inconvenience. If you don't receive anything by next Friday, please call back, and mention this reference number.

scenarios.scenario: Following up with a landlord about repairs
scenarios.context: A tenant phones a landlord after leaving a message about a repair that has not been done.

speakerA.en: Hello, Mr. Evans, it's Laura Chen from flat six. I left a message last week about the leak under the kitchen sink, and I haven't had any reply, so I thought I'd call again.

The problem has become worse since then. There's now a small puddle every morning, and the cupboard is beginning to smell of damp, which concerns me both for my belongings and for the structure of the building.
I understand that you're busy, but I'm worried that if it isn't dealt with soon, the water might spread to the flat below. Would it be possible to send someone this week?
Thursday would be fine. I work from home, so I can be here at any time. How long do you think it will take, and will they need to turn off the water supply?
That's helpful. I'll put some towels around the pipe, and I'll make sure that the cupboard is empty. Could you please send me a message to confirm the time, so that I have it in writing?
Thank you very much. I appreciate your prompt action. I hope that this will be resolved quickly, and I'll let you know if anything changes.

speakerB.en: Hello, Laura. Yes, I'm sorry for not getting back to you. I've been traveling, and I only listened to my messages this morning. Tell me exactly what's happening.
That doesn't sound good. I should have called you earlier. The pipes in that building are quite old, and I've been planning to replace them for some time. Has it affected anything else?
You're right to be concerned, and I'll take care of it immediately. I know a plumber who does emergency work. Let me ring him now and see if he's available on Thursday.
He should be able to come on Thursday morning, between nine and noon. It will take about two hours, and he'll have to shut off the water temporarily, but he'll warn you first.
That's an excellent idea, and I'll send you a message as soon as I've spoken to him. If there's any damage to your belongings, please keep the receipts, and I'll make sure that you're compensated.
Thank you for being so patient. I'll be in touch this afternoon. And please don't hesitate to call me directly in future if something urgent comes up.

scenarios.scenario: Calling a company about a billing error
scenarios.context: A customer phones a service provider after being charged twice for the same service.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm calling about an error on my latest bill. I was charged twice for the same service, and I'd appreciate it if you could look into it for me, since it's a substantial amount.

Certainly, it's 4471-2208. To give you some background, I was assured last month that the first payment had been canceled, so I was surprised to see it reappear. I'd appreciate it if you could explain how that happened.

Of course, although this isn't the first time something like this has happened. I was told in March that my account had been fixed, and yet here we are. I'd rather have the system checked than call every month.

I'd appreciate that. On the other hand, I'd like some assurance in writing, since I was promised a confirmation email last time and never received one. Could you possibly send me one as soon as the refund is approved?

Thank you, I appreciate that. There's one more thing. I'd appreciate it if you could have my account reviewed for any other duplicate charges, since I'd rather not discover another one in a couple of months.
That's very reassuring. So, to confirm, the refund will be processed within five days, and I'll receive both an email and the review results. Is that right?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. I'd be happy to help. Could I have your account number, please? Once I've pulled up your records, I'll check exactly what was billed and when.

Thank you. I can see both charges now. It appears the cancellation was never processed properly, which is clearly our mistake. I'd appreciate it if you could bear with me while I have the refund approved.

I completely understand your frustration, and I'll have the matter escalated to our billing department today. I was informed that cases like this usually take three to five business days, but I'll ask for it to be prioritized.
Certainly. I'll have a confirmation sent to your registered address right after the approval. To be honest, you shouldn't have had to chase us, and I'd like to apologize on behalf of the company.

That's a sensible request. I'll have a full review carried out over the last twelve months and note it on your file. I was told that the results are usually ready within a week, and I'll make sure you're informed.
That's exactly right. Here's your reference number, in case you need to call again. Thank you for your patience, and I'm sorry once more for the inconvenience. Have a good day.

scenarios.scenario: Returning a landlord's call about a delayed repair
scenarios.context: A tenant calls back the landlord after missing a call about a heating repair that has been postponed again.

speakerA.en: Hello, Mr. Alvarez? It's Sam Torres from apartment 6. I'm returning your call from earlier, which I missed because I was in a meeting. You left a message about the heating repair.
I had, as it happens. I was supposed to be at the office all day, and I rearranged my schedule so that I could let him in. To be honest, this is the third time the repair has been postponed.

I'd say tomorrow is better than waiting, provided that he can come before noon. I'm working from home in the afternoon, but I'm supposed to be on a video call, so I'd rather the noise didn't coincide with it.
Eight would be perfect, as long as he phones before he arrives. On the other hand, I don't want to pay twice for the same problem, so could you confirm that the new contractor's visit is covered?
Thank you, I'd appreciate that. In the meantime, I'm supposed to be keeping the apartment warm for my elderly neighbor, who's staying with me tonight. Is there any chance of a portable heater?
I'll be in from three o'clock. Thanks for being so understanding. I'll wait for your call about the contractor, and I'll keep my phone with me, in case you can't get through.

speakerB.en: Yes, thanks for calling back. The technician was supposed to come on Tuesday, but he's been delayed, and I wanted to let you know in case you'd already taken time off work to be at home.

I know, and I apologize. The company is supposed to send somebody within forty-eight hours, but they're short-staffed this week. Unless you'd rather wait, I can try another contractor who could come tomorrow.
That makes sense. I'll call him now and get back to you within the hour. Unless he's fully booked, he should be able to fit you in first thing, around eight o'clock. Would that be convenient?

Absolutely. The repair is covered under the maintenance agreement, so you won't pay anything, unless he finds damage caused by the tenant, which I'm sure won't be the case. I'll get that confirmed in writing.
Of course. I've got a couple in the storage room, and I'll have one brought up this afternoon, provided you're home to receive it. Otherwise, I'll leave it with the neighbor in apartment 5.
Perfect. I'll get back to you within the hour, I promise. Thanks again for your patience, Sam. Hopefully, this time the repair will actually be finished by tomorrow evening.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a settlement with an insurance adjuster
scenarios.context: A homeowner phones an insurance adjuster to discuss the settlement offered after a burst pipe damaged her apartment.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon, Mr. Reyes. I'm calling about the offer you sent regarding the burst pipe in my apartment. I'd have thought the figure would be higher, given the extent of the damage, so I'd like to understand how you calculated it.

Chiefly the cabinets and the electrical work. Not only were the cabinets ruined, but the wiring had to be replaced, and I have the electrician's invoice. Were it not for his quick action, the damage would have been far worse. Was that included in your calculation?

I'll send it within the hour. Little did I expect the process to be this complicated, since I've paid premiums for eleven years. To my mind, a claim should be simpler than this. Is there a way to speed it up?

The living room carpet and part of the sofa, which absorbed the water. Had I known the policy excluded upholstery, I'd have bought extra cover. What I'd like to know is whether the exclusion applies to damage of this kind.

Yes, about eighty pictures, with dates. Suffice it to say that I was thorough. I'd also kept receipts for the emergency drying equipment. Should those be reimbursed separately, or are they part of the same claim?

That would be much fairer, and I appreciate your help. The fact remains that I'd been dreading this call. Could you confirm the revised figure in writing, in case something changes? And when might I expect payment?

speakerB.en: Good afternoon, Ms. Novak, and thank you for calling. Our assessor valued the flooring and the lower walls at roughly four thousand dollars. Should you have additional documentation, I'm happy to review it. Which items concern you most?

It wasn't, I'm afraid, since the invoice didn't reach us. It would appear that something was lost in the process. Provided that the invoice is dated within the claim period, I can add it today. Could you email it to me?

I understand your frustration. Under no circumstances should a claim drag on for months, so I'll mark yours as a priority. In all fairness, delays usually arise from missing documents, not from reluctance to pay. What else do you need to replace?

It applies to gradual leaks, not sudden bursts, so in your case the sofa should qualify. Not that I can promise anything before reviewing the photographs, but I'm optimistic. Were you able to photograph everything before the cleanup?

They can be included, provided they're reasonable. I'd say the total could rise to around seven thousand, subject to approval. Granted, I can't guarantee it, but I'll argue your case. Would that be acceptable to you?

Certainly. You'll have the written confirmation tomorrow, and payment should follow within ten days of your acceptance. Thank you for your patience, Ms. Novak. Do call me directly if anything unexpected arises.

scenarios.scenario: Calling a journalist to correct a published error
scenarios.context: A researcher phones a journalist to correct a factual error in an article about her study.

speakerA.en: Good morning, Mr. Brandt. This is Dr. Hale from the university. I'm calling about your article on Tuesday regarding our water study. It would appear that a key figure was misreported, and I'd be grateful for a few minutes.

The article states that contamination rose by forty percent, whereas our study found four percent. Hardly had I read the headline when I began receiving worried emails from residents. Could the error have arisen from a typing mistake?

That's possible, and in that case, the fault may be partly ours. To be fair, the draft contained a typographical error that was fixed later. Whatever the source, the public is now misinformed. What can be done to resolve it?

Certainly, as long as it's accurate and brief. Were I to write something longer, it would only create more confusion. I'd suggest we say that contamination rose slightly, and then state the exact figure. Does that seem clear enough?

With some alarm, naturally. What worries me is that the incorrect number may stay in people's memory, however carefully it's corrected. Suffice it to say that corrections rarely travel as far as errors. Do you share that concern?

Not at all, and I'd welcome it. For what it's worth, your article was otherwise fair and well written. Needless to say, I'd rather work with a careful journalist than avoid the press. Shall I send my statement by noon?

speakerB.en: Good morning, Dr. Hale, and thank you for calling rather than writing angrily. Which figure do you mean? Not that I'd assume I'm right, but I did check my notes against the press release. Could you tell me what you found?

Quite possibly, and if so, I apologize. Were that the case, the correction should appear promptly. Let me pull up my draft. Ah, the press release itself says forty in one paragraph. Did your office perhaps send out two versions?

A correction is the obvious step, and I'd rather it were prominent than buried. Not only will I flag the error online, but I'll also add a note in tomorrow's print edition. Would you be willing to provide a short statement?

It does, and it's reassuring that you'd rather clarify than complain. Lest readers miss it, I'd also place a link to your original paper. Granted, few will read it, but it helps. How has the community reacted so far?

Honestly, I do. It's one of the unpleasant truths of my profession. The fact remains that I should have verified the figure with you directly. Would you mind if I called you next time before publishing?

Please do, and thank you for handling this so graciously. Come to think of it, I'd like to interview you again about the study itself. Perhaps we could arrange that next week, once the correction is out.

For three days. Is it a big car?
Can I pay with a card?

I'll take the basic one. Where do I return the car?

speakerB.en: OK. For how many days?
No, it's a small car. It's a good car.
Yes, you can. Here is the key.
It's in front of the office.
Yes, we have a compact car for $35 a day.
speakerB.fa: بله، یک ماشین کوچک با ۳۵ دلار در روز داریم.

Back here, by Monday at noon, with a full tank.

scenarios.scenario: Using the city bus
scenarios.context: Asking for directions and bus information.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. Where is the nearest bus stop?
Thank you. Is the bus to the park there?
How much is the ticket?
Thank you very much.
Which bus goes to downtown?
speakerA.fa: کدام اتوبوس به مرکز شهر می‌رود؟

speakerA.en: How often do the buses run?
speakerA.fa: اتوبوس‌ها هر چند وقت یک بار می‌آیند؟

speakerA.fa: آیا این اتوبوس در ایستگاه مرکزی توقف می‌کند؟

speakerA.en: Could you tell me when we get there, please?
Can you tell me when to get off?
speakerA.fa: می‌توانید به من بگویید کجا پیاده شوم؟

speakerA.en: How much is the fare?

speakerB.en: It's just around the corner.
Yes. Bus number five goes to the park.
It's two dollars.
You're welcome.
Take bus number 42.
speakerB.fa: سوار اتوبوس شماره ۴۲ شوید.

speakerB.en: They come every 15 minutes.
speakerB.fa: هر ۱۵ دقیقه یک بار می‌آیند.

speakerB.fa: بله، این اتوبوس به ایستگاه مرکزی می‌رود.

speakerB.fa: ایستگاه شما را اعلام می‌کنم. سه ایستگاه دیگر است.

speakerB.en: Of course. Get off at the third stop, near the library.
It's two dollars. You can pay the driver.

scenarios.scenario: Buying a train/plane ticket
scenarios.context: At a station or booking office.

speakerA.en: One ticket to Paris, please.
Here you are. What time is the train?
Which platform is it?
Thank you.
When does the next train to London leave?
speakerA.fa: قطار بعدی به لندن چه ساعتی حرکت می‌کند؟

speakerA.en: I need a one-way ticket to Paris.
speakerA.fa: یک بلیط یک‌طرفه به پاریس نیاز دارم.

speakerA.en: How much is a first-class ticket?
speakerA.fa: بلیط درجه یک چقدر است؟

speakerA.en: Is there a direct flight to Tokyo?
speakerA.fa: پرواز مستقیم به توکیو وجود دارد؟

speakerA.en: Is there a faster option with fewer stops?
I'd like to book a flight for next Monday.
speakerA.fa: می‌خواهم یک پرواز برای دوشنبه آینده رزرو کنم.

speakerA.en: In the morning, please. Is there a direct flight?

speakerB.en: OK. That's thirty dollars.
It's at ten o'clock. Here is your ticket.
It's platform five.
You're welcome. Have a good trip!
The next train departs at 10:15.
speakerB.fa: قطار بعدی ساعت ۱۰:۱۵ حرکت می‌کند.

speakerB.en: A one-way ticket is $45.
speakerB.fa: بلیط یک‌طرفه ۴۵ دلار است.

speakerB.en: First class is $150, economy is $90.
speakerB.fa: درجه یک ۱۵۰ دلار، اقتصادی ۹۰ دلار است.

speakerB.fa: یک پرواز متصل از طریق دبی داریم.

speakerB.en: Let me check availability for Monday.
speakerB.fa: بگذارید موجودی دوشنبه را بررسی کنم.

speakerB.en: Certainly. Would you like a morning or an afternoon flight?
Yes, there's one at 8:30. It costs $120.

scenarios.context: Hailing a cab and giving directions.

speakerA.en: Can you take me to the airport, please?
Is it far?
How much is it?
OK. Stop here, please.
How much will it cost to go to downtown?
speakerA.fa: به مرکز شهر چقدر می‌شود؟

speakerA.en: Please stop here. I'll get out.
speakerA.fa: لطفاً اینجا توقف کنید. پیاده می‌شوم.

speakerA.en: Could you drive a bit slower?
speakerA.fa: می‌توانید کمی آهسته‌تر برانید؟

speakerA.en: I'm in a hurry, please take the fastest route.
speakerA.fa: عجله دارم، لطفاً سریع‌ترین راه را بگیرید.

speakerA.en: Could you turn on the air conditioning, please?
Can you take me to the airport tomorrow at six?

speakerB.en: Sure, get in.
No, it's near. Ten minutes.
It's twelve dollars.
OK. Here we are.
That'll be about $20.
speakerB.fa: حدود ۲۰ دلار می‌شود.

speakerB.en: Here we are. That's $12.50.
speakerB.fa: رسیدیم. ۱۲ دلار و ۵۰ سنت می‌شود.

speakerB.en: I'll take the highway to save time.
speakerB.fa: برای صرفه‌جویی در وقت از بزرگراه می‌روم.

speakerB.fa: می‌توانید در حمل چمدان‌ها کمکم کنید؟

speakerB.en: Of course. It'll be cool in a minute.
Yes, just call this number the night before.

scenarios.scenario: Buying a bus ticket

Here you are. What time is the bus?
Is it a big bus?
Thank you.

Return, please. I'm coming back on Sunday.
Which platform does it leave from?
Can I pay by card?

It's at two o'clock.

You're welcome. Have a nice trip!
One way or return?
That's $38. The next bus leaves at four.
Platform 6, at the end of the hall.
Yes, you can. Please insert your card here.

scenarios.scenario: Taking the subway
scenarios.context: Someone asks a stranger about the subway.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. Where is the subway?
Is it far?
Which line do I take?
Thank you very much.
Excuse me, how do I get to the museum by subway?
Do I need to change trains?
Where can I buy a ticket?
Thank you. You've been very helpful.

speakerB.en: It's over there, on the left.
No, it's near. Two minutes.
Take the blue line.
You're welcome.
Take the green line and get off at Central Station.
No, it's a direct line. It takes about fifteen minutes.
There's a machine near the entrance.
No problem. Have a nice day!

Is the train late?

Is this the right platform for the Chicago train?
Do you know why it's late?
Is there a café nearby? I'd like to get a coffee.
I'll be quick. Can you watch my bag?

speakerB.en: Yes, it is.
No, it's on time.
Yes, please sit down.
You're welcome.
Yes, it is. The train is five minutes late.
There was a problem with the signals, I think.
Yes, there's one on the first floor.
Sure. I'll be here.

scenarios.scenario: Riding a bike
scenarios.context: Two friends talk about going to school by bike.

speakerA.en: Do you have a bike?
How do you go to school?
Is it far from your house?
Can I ride your bike?
Do you go to school by bike?
Isn't it dangerous in the traffic?
Where do you park your bike?
Maybe I should try it. It's good exercise.

speakerB.en: Yes, I do. It's red.
I go by bike.
No. It's ten minutes.
Yes, but be careful.
Yes, every day. It takes twenty minutes.
Not really. There's a bike lane most of the way.
There's a bike rack next to the main entrance.
You should! And it's cheaper than the bus.

scenarios.scenario: Missing the bus
scenarios.context: A person misses the bus and asks for help.

speakerA.en: Oh no! I missed the bus.
When is the next bus? I'm late for work.
That's too long. Can I take a taxi?
Thank you for your help.
Oh no! I just missed my bus.
Do you know the timetable for this evening?
I'm late for an appointment. Is there a faster way?
Good idea. Thanks for your help!

speakerB.en: Don't worry. Another bus comes soon.
It's in ten minutes.
Yes. There is a taxi stop here.
You're welcome. Have a good day.
Don't worry. Another one comes in ten minutes.
Yes, the last bus leaves at eleven.
You could take a taxi. There's a taxi stand over there.
You're welcome. Good luck!

scenarios.scenario: Buying a train ticket at the station
scenarios.context: A traveler asks about ticket options at the counter.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'd like a ticket to Chicago for tomorrow morning, please.
A round trip, please. Is it cheaper if I travel outside rush hour?
Then I'll take the nine forty-five. Do I need to reserve a seat in advance?
In that case, I'll reserve one. Which platform does it leave from?

speakerB.en: Certainly. Would you like a one-way or a round-trip ticket?
Yes, trains after nine thirty are about twenty percent cheaper than the earlier ones.
It isn't required, but I'd recommend it, because this train is usually quite full.
Platform four. Please make sure you're there at least five minutes before departure.

scenarios.scenario: Taking a taxi in a busy city
scenarios.context: A passenger talks to a taxi driver during a ride in heavy traffic.

speakerA.en: Could you take me to the central station, please? My train leaves in forty minutes.
Do you think we'll make it in time? I really can't afford to miss this train.
Thank you. I didn't realize the roads would be so busy at this hour.
Is it all right if I pay by card? I don't have much cash with me.

speakerB.en: No problem, but the traffic is terrible today because of the road work.
I'll take a different route through the side streets. It should save us about ten minutes.
It's always like this on weekday mornings. People are heading to work or school.
Yes, that's fine. We'll be there in about fifteen minutes.

scenarios.scenario: Missing the last bus and asking for help
scenarios.context: A tourist asks a local for advice after missing the last bus.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I think I just missed the last bus to the city center. Is there another way?
Do I need to buy a ticket in advance, or can I pay the driver?
Thanks for warning me. How long does the trip usually take?
I think I'll wait for the bus. It's cheaper, and I'm in no hurry.

speakerB.en: You're in luck. There's a night bus that runs every hour from the other side of the square.
You can pay the driver, but after midnight they only accept exact change.
About forty minutes, depending on the traffic. If you'd rather not wait, there's a taxi stand around the corner.
Sensible choice. Just keep an eye on your belongings, as the stop can get busy at night.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a canceled flight
scenarios.context: A passenger speaks to an airline agent after a flight is canceled.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I've just received a notification that my flight has been canceled. What are my options?
Tomorrow? I have an important meeting in the morning that I simply can't miss.
I'd be grateful. Am I entitled to any compensation, given the circumstances?
That's something, at least. Could you please put me on the evening flight if there's availability?

speakerB.en: I'm very sorry for the inconvenience. We can rebook you on the next available departure, which leaves tomorrow morning.
I understand. Let me check whether any other airlines have seats available on a flight this evening.
The cancellation was due to severe weather, so compensation isn't mandatory, but we will cover your hotel and meals.
I've found one seat. Let me confirm it and print your new boarding pass.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing public transport in a city
scenarios.context: Two residents compare commuting options.

speakerA.en: How do you get to work these days? I heard the metro line is closed for repairs.
That's dreadful. Have you considered cycling? The city has built a lot of new lanes recently.
I felt the same until I tried it. It's quicker than driving, and the exercise is a bonus.
I keep a change of clothes at my desk, and most buildings have showers these days.

speakerB.en: It is, so I've been taking the bus, which adds nearly forty minutes to my journey.
I've thought about it, but I'm wary of the traffic, especially in the rain.
You've almost convinced me. What do you do about arriving sweaty at the office?
I may give it a go once the weather improves. Anything is better than another winter on that bus.

scenarios.scenario: Renting a car abroad
scenarios.context: A tourist rents a car and asks about insurance and conditions.

speakerA.en: I'd like to rent a compact car for a week. Could you tell me about your rates and what's included?
What exactly does the basic insurance cover? I'd rather not be responsible for a huge bill if something goes wrong.
I see. What would it cost to reduce that excess to zero?
In that case, I'll take it. Is there a charge if I return the car with less fuel than I started with?

speakerB.en: Of course. The standard rate covers unlimited mileage, but insurance is an optional extra.
It covers third-party damage, but there's an excess of five hundred euros for damage to the vehicle itself.
An additional fifteen euros per day. Many customers consider it worthwhile, especially on unfamiliar roads.
Yes, you'll be billed at a higher rate for refueling, so I'd suggest filling up just before you drop it off.

scenarios.scenario: Coping with a transport strike
scenarios.context: Two commuters discuss alternative routes during a three-day rail strike.

speakerA.en: Have you seen the news? The rail union has announced a three-day strike starting tomorrow, so getting into the city is going to be a nightmare.
Apparently about a third of them, mostly at peak hours. Still, I wouldn't count on them being punctual.
There's a coach service from the outskirts that bypasses the center entirely. It takes longer, but it's reliable.
I'd wager half the city will be doing the same, so the networks are bound to be sluggish.

speakerB.en: Wonderful. I have a client meeting on Wednesday morning that I can hardly move. Do you know whether any services will run at all?
Then I'll have to consider alternatives. Driving is out of the question, given the congestion charge and the parking situation.
That might be my best option. Alternatively, I could work remotely and take the meeting by video.
A fair point. I'll take the coach and allow an extra hour, just to be safe.

scenarios.scenario: Rebooking after a missed connection
scenarios.context: A traveler negotiates with an airline agent after a delayed flight causes a missed connection.

speakerA.en: My inbound flight was delayed by two hours, and as a result I missed my connection to Singapore. I'd like to know what options are available.
That's unacceptable, I'm afraid. I'm due to chair a meeting at nine tomorrow, and that flight wouldn't land until the afternoon.
Via Dubai would add several hours, but it would at least get me there before the meeting. Is there a seat in business class?
I'll accept that, provided my checked luggage is transferred as well. I won't have it going astray on top of everything else.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry about that. Since the delay was on our side, we'll rebook you at no charge. The next available departure is tomorrow morning at seven.
I understand. Let me see whether another carrier has seats. There's a partner airline with a late-evening departure via Dubai.
Only economy is available on that routing. However, I can arrange lounge access and a meal voucher for the wait.
I'll flag it for priority transfer and give you written confirmation. Again, my apologies for the disruption.

scenarios.scenario: Debating a new transit proposal
scenarios.context: Two residents discuss a plan to build a tram line through their neighborhood.

speakerA.en: Did you attend the council meeting about the proposed tram line? I couldn't decide whether to be excited or alarmed.
That's what worries me. Several shopkeepers I know believe they won't survive the disruption, whatever compensation is offered.
Eventually, perhaps. The question is who bears the cost in the interim, and whether the council will actually keep its promises.
That's a reasonable condition. Perhaps we should raise it at the next consultation rather than grumbling about it afterwards.

speakerB.en: I did. On paper it's compelling: faster commutes, fewer cars, lower emissions. But the construction would disrupt the high street for at least two years.
It's a legitimate concern, although cities that have built lines like this tend to see foot traffic rise once they open.
Fair enough. Personally, I'd support it if the funding for affected businesses were guaranteed in writing.
I'll gladly add my name to a petition. Public pressure does tend to focus the minds of council members.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a severely delayed overnight train
scenarios.context: Two passengers cope with an unexpected delay and its consequences.

speakerA.en: Have you heard the announcement? Apparently there's a fault on the line, and no one can say when we'll be moving again.
I'll ask the conductor whether the company will cover a hotel if we're stranded overnight.
Under the passenger charter, we're entitled to compensation after a delay of this length. I have the relevant clause saved on my phone.
A lifetime of delays has made me something of a connoisseur. Shall we draft the claim together while we wait?

speakerB.en: Splendid. I have a connection in the morning that I can scarcely afford to miss, and the staff appear as informed as we are.
I wouldn't expect much, but it's worth pressing the point. Rail operators tend to be generous only when confronted.
Admirably prepared. I'd never have thought to look it up until I was already furious.
Why not? If nothing else, it will give us something productive to do while the train goes nowhere.

scenarios.scenario: Haggling over the fare with a taxi driver in an unfamiliar city
scenarios.context: A traveler tries to settle on a fair price while remaining courteous.

speakerA.en: To the airport, please. Before we set off, could we agree on a price? I'd rather not discover the figure at the end.
I appreciate the favor, but I was told by the hotel that a fare of around fifty would be typical for that distance.
Let's meet at sixty, and I'll gladly add a tip if the journey is smooth. That seems fair to both of us.
Splendid. I'm travelling light, so there's no need to load the boot, though I'd be grateful for a cool car.

speakerB.en: Meter is broken, I'm afraid. For the airport, I'd say eighty, which is already a favor to you.
The hotel gives you the tourist price in reverse. Traffic on that road is terrible at this hour, so sixty-five is the best I can do.
You drive a hard bargain, but I like your manner. Sixty it is, and I'll take the faster route.
The air conditioning works on a good day. Today appears to be one of them.

scenarios.scenario: Making a complaint about a cancelled flight
scenarios.context: A passenger asserts their rights politely but firmly at an airline desk.

speakerA.en: I'd like to discuss the cancellation of flight 412. I was informed only an hour ago, and no alternative was offered.
Under the regulations, a crew shortage doesn't qualify as extraordinary circumstances. I believe I'm entitled to both compensation and a refund.
I'd appreciate that. In the meantime, I'd like to be placed on the earliest available flight, even if it means a connection.
Thank you. Please also note the reference number, so that I won't need to repeat the entire story.

speakerB.en: I'm very sorry for the inconvenience. The cancellation was due to a crew shortage, and we're rebooking affected passengers as quickly as possible.
You appear to know the rules well. I'll need to escalate this to a supervisor, as I can't authorize compensation myself.
There's a departure this evening via Frankfurt with one seat left. I'll hold it while you speak with the supervisor.
Of course. It's on your confirmation slip, and I've added a note that you've requested compensation under the regulations.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about the ticket price
scenarios.context: A passenger asks about a ticket price at the station.

speakerA.en: Hello. How much is a ticket to Boston?
Is there a cheaper ticket?
I'm a student. Here is my card.
When does the train leave?

speakerB.en: It's twenty dollars.
Yes, a student ticket is ten dollars.
Thank you. Here is your ticket.
At nine thirty. Have a good trip!

scenarios.scenario: Asking about the platform
scenarios.context: A passenger asks which platform the train leaves from.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. Which platform is the train to Leeds?
Where is platform four?
Is the train on time?
Thank you. I must hurry.

speakerB.en: It's platform four.
Go straight and take the stairs down.
Yes, it leaves in ten minutes.
Have a good trip!

scenarios.scenario: A delayed train
scenarios.context: Two passengers wait for a train that is late.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, do you know why the train to Bristol is late?
How long do we have to wait?
I have a meeting at noon. Is there another way to go?
I'll wait a little longer, then.

speakerB.en: There's a problem with the signals, I think.
The board says another thirty minutes.
You can take the bus, but it's much slower.
Good idea. They usually fix these problems quickly.

scenarios.scenario: Losing a ticket
scenarios.context: A passenger loses his ticket and asks the staff for help.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I lost my bus ticket. What should I do?
This morning at the station, with my card.
It was about nine o'clock, and it cost eight dollars.
Yes, here it is. Thank you so much.

speakerB.en: When did you buy it?
Do you remember the time and the price?
I can check your card payment. Do you have your card?
I found it. Here is a new ticket for you.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about a connecting train
scenarios.context: A passenger asks the information desk about a trip with a change.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I need to get to Manchester. Do I have to change trains?
Is that enough time? I'm carrying a lot of luggage.
Which platform does the Manchester train leave from?
Thanks. Can I buy the ticket for the whole journey here?

speakerB.en: Yes, you change at Birmingham. The connection is about ten minutes.
It should be, but the next train is only half an hour later.
It usually leaves from platform six, but check the board when you arrive.
Yes, at the counter or the machine. A return ticket is cheaper.

scenarios.scenario: Getting around a new city by public transport
scenarios.context: A newcomer asks a local person how the metro system works.

speakerA.en: I've just moved here. Is it easy to get around by public transport?
Do I need a different ticket for each journey?
Where can I buy one?
Great. Is the metro busy in the morning?

speakerB.en: Very easy. The metro covers most of the city, and the buses fill the gaps.
No, you can get a monthly card. It's much cheaper if you travel every day.
At any metro station. You'll need a photo and your ID.
Between eight and nine it's crowded, so try to leave a bit earlier.

scenarios.scenario: Buying train tickets and choosing a route
scenarios.context: A passenger buys tickets and asks about the fastest and cheapest options.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'd like two tickets to Manchester for tomorrow, if there are still seats available.
We'd like to arrive before noon. What's the fastest connection you have, and how much does it cost?
That's a bit expensive. Is there a cheaper option, even if the journey takes a little longer?
I think we'll take the slower one. Do we need to change trains, and is there enough time to make the connection?
That's fine. Can we choose our seats now, or are they assigned automatically when we board?
Thank you. I'll pay by card, and could you please print the tickets for us?

speakerB.en: Good morning. Of course. Would you like to travel in the morning, and are you coming back on the same day?
The express train leaves at eight and gets there at ten thirty. A return ticket is eighty pounds for two people.
There's a regional train at eight forty, which takes four hours, but it only costs fifty pounds. You'd have to change at Birmingham.
You'll have twenty minutes at Birmingham, which should be plenty, and the second train leaves from the same platform.
You can reserve seats for a small extra fee, but if you don't, you simply sit in any free seat.
Certainly. Here are your tickets. Please check that the dates are right. Have a pleasant journey.

scenarios.scenario: Renting a car and discussing insurance
scenarios.context: A customer rents a car and asks about conditions and insurance.

speakerA.en: Hello. I'd like to rent a small car for five days. I've booked online, but I need to confirm a few things.
Yes, my reservation is under the name Johnson. I'd like to know what the insurance covers, because I've never rented a car before.
And if something happens to the car, for instance a scratch or a broken window, would I have to pay for it?
I'd prefer to have the full coverage, then. Also, is it possible to return the car at the airport instead of here?
Good. One more thing: does the car come with a full tank, and do I have to refill it before I bring it back?
Understood. I'll sign the contract now. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

speakerB.en: Hello, welcome. Could I have your name and driving license, please, so that I can find your booking?
I see it here. The basic insurance covers damage to other vehicles, but it doesn't cover damage to the car you're driving unless you add extra coverage.
Without extra coverage, you'd be responsible for the first four hundred euros. With full coverage, you wouldn't pay anything at all.
Yes, that's possible. There's a small fee for returning it at a different location, which is twenty euros in total.
It's given to you with a full tank, and it should be returned with a full tank, otherwise you'll be charged for the fuel.
Thank you. Here are the keys, and the car is parked in space twelve. Drive safely, and enjoy your trip.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing problems with the daily commute
scenarios.context: Two colleagues talk about their journeys to work and possible solutions.

speakerA.en: How was your commute this morning? Mine was terrible. The bus was so late that I almost missed my first meeting.
It happens at least twice a week now. I've been thinking about buying a bike so that I don't have to depend on the bus.
That's true, but cycling would save me money, and it'd probably be quicker than sitting in traffic every day.
I hadn't thought about that. How long does it take you to get to work, and where do you leave your bike?
That doesn't sound bad at all. Maybe I'll try it for a month and see whether I like it.
Good idea. If it works out, perhaps we could even cycle to the office together on sunny days.

speakerB.en: Don't remind me. The traffic was awful, and the train was so crowded that I couldn't even sit down.
I cycle to work every day, and I wouldn't change it. It's faster, healthier, and I don't need to worry about timetables.
The only disadvantage is the weather. When it rains heavily, I take the bus, and I always carry a waterproof jacket in my bag.
About twenty-five minutes, and there's a secure bike room in the basement of our building, which anyone can use for free.
You should. Start with a short route on the weekend, so that you know how to get there safely.
I'd love that. It would make the journey more enjoyable, and we'd have plenty to talk about on the way.

scenarios.scenario: Missing a connection and rebooking
scenarios.context: A passenger who missed a connecting train asks staff for help with a new ticket.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I've just missed my connection to Edinburgh because my first train was twenty minutes late.
I have a ticket for the six o'clock train. Is there any chance of using it for a later one, or do I have to buy a new ticket?
That's a relief. When is the next train, and is there still a seat available? I have to be there before ten tonight.
That's fine. Should I go to the platform now, or wait here until the train arrives?
Would it be possible to get a written note about the delay? I'm going to ask the railway company for compensation.
Thank you. I really appreciate your help, especially because I'm sure you've had a very busy day.

speakerB.en: Good evening. I'm sorry to hear that. May I see your ticket, please? Let me find out what I can do for you.
Since the delay was caused by the railway company, you don't have to pay anything. I'll just stamp your ticket, and you can take the next train.
The next one leaves at seven twenty from platform four, and there are plenty of seats. You'll arrive at nine fifteen.
You have about half an hour, so I'd suggest that you wait in the lounge, where it's warmer, and go to the platform ten minutes before departure.
Of course. I'll write it on the back of your ticket, and you can also fill in a compensation form on our website.
It's no trouble. I hope the rest of your journey goes smoothly, and have a pleasant evening.

scenarios.scenario: Talking to a taxi driver about the route
scenarios.context: A passenger discusses the route and the fare with a taxi driver on the way to the airport.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I need to get to the airport, please. My flight leaves in two hours, so I'd like to arrive as soon as possible.
Which way do you usually go? I've heard that the highway can be very busy in the morning, especially on Mondays.
I'd prefer to avoid any delays, so please choose whichever route is faster, even if it's a bit longer.
How much will the ride cost, approximately? I'd like to have enough cash in case your card machine isn't working.
That's fine. Would you mind turning the air conditioning on? It's rather warm in here.
Thanks. You can drop me off at departures, please. Here's the money, and you can keep the change.

speakerB.en: Good morning. No problem. Where are you flying to? Would you like me to help you with your luggage?
You're right. If we take the highway, we might get stuck in traffic. There's a road through the suburbs that's usually quicker.
Then we'll take the suburban road. It's about five kilometers longer, but we shouldn't have to stop for more than a couple of minutes.
It should cost around thirty-five euros, depending on the traffic, and we accept both cash and cards, so you don't need to worry.
Of course. I'll turn it on right now. Let me know if it's too cold, and I'll adjust the temperature.
Thank you very much. We've arrived with plenty of time to spare. Have a pleasant flight, and take care.

scenarios.scenario: Getting a monthly pass and asking about zones
scenarios.context: A new resident asks a ticket clerk about the best pass for daily commuting.

speakerA.en: Hello. I've just moved here, and I need to travel to work every day by bus and metro. Which ticket would you recommend?
I live in zone three, and my office is in zone one. I'll be traveling about twenty days a month, mostly during rush hour.
That sounds like a good deal. Can I use the same pass on the weekends, or is it only valid from Monday to Friday?
And what if I lose it? I'm quite forgetful, and I wouldn't want to pay for another one.
I see. Do I have to bring a photo with me, or can I take one here at the station?
Perfect. I'll go and get the photo now and come straight back. Thank you for your help.

speakerB.en: Hello, and welcome to the city. Let me explain the options. Do you know which zones you'll need to travel through?
In that case, I'd recommend the monthly pass for zones one to three. It's more expensive than single tickets, but if you travel that often, it will save you money.
It's valid for all days of the week and for all kinds of public transport, so you can also use it in the evenings and on weekends.
If it's registered in your name, we can replace it for a small fee of ten euros. If it isn't registered, I'm afraid that it can't be replaced.
You need a passport-size photo, and there's a machine just next to the entrance, which costs five euros.
You're welcome. Once you have the photo, come to window two, and I'll prepare the pass while you fill in the form.

scenarios.scenario: Debating public transport funding
scenarios.context: Two commuters discuss whether public transport should be free.

speakerA.en: I read that a few cities have made public transport free for everyone. Do you think that could work here, or would it create more problems than it solves?
Well, it would certainly reduce the number of cars on the road, which would improve air quality and ease congestion, particularly during rush hour.
But the money has to come from somewhere. If the fares were abolished, taxes would probably have to rise, and not everyone uses buses and trains.
That's true, though you could argue that everybody benefits from cleaner air and fewer traffic jams, even if they never travel by bus.
There's also the danger that services might become overcrowded, if the number of passengers increases without a corresponding investment in vehicles and staff.
Perhaps a middle path would be best: free transport for students and elderly people, and reduced fares for those on low incomes.

speakerB.en: It's an appealing idea, but I'm not convinced that it would achieve what its supporters promise. Some studies show that people simply switch from walking or cycling to the bus.
That's the theory, but the results have been mixed. In Tallinn, for instance, the number of passengers increased, but car use didn't drop as dramatically as expected.
Exactly. Ticket sales provide a substantial share of the operating budget in most cities. Without them, the quality of service could actually deteriorate.
That's a reasonable point of view. Public transport is often seen as an essential service, much like roads, and nobody expects to pay a toll every time they walk down the street.
That's what happened in some cities, where the system couldn't cope. If the quality falls, the very people who depend on it the most would suffer.
I think that's the fairest solution. It targets the people who need it, and it keeps enough revenue to maintain and improve the network.

scenarios.scenario: Reporting a serious delay and seeking compensation
scenarios.context: A passenger writes to and talks with an airline representative after a major disruption.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I'm contacting you about flight 481, which was delayed by seven hours last Tuesday, causing me to miss an important business meeting.
Besides the delay itself, I was given no information for the first three hours, and nobody offered us food or drink, even though this is required by regulations.
I've been informed that under European rules, passengers are entitled to financial compensation when the delay is more than three hours, unless it was caused by extraordinary circumstances.
I don't accept that explanation. Other flights departed from the same airport that evening, which suggests that the problem was technical, rather than related to the weather.
In that case, I'd like the airline to provide written evidence of the reason, and I'd also appreciate a response within fourteen days.
Thank you. I'll wait for your reply, but I should make clear that I'll take the matter further if I'm not satisfied with the outcome.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon, and thank you for contacting us. I'm sorry for the disruption caused to your journey, and I'll do my best to resolve the matter.
I understand your frustration. We did experience a communication problem on that day, and we should have provided refreshments much earlier. I apologize for that.
You're correct about the regulation. However, in this case, the delay was attributed to adverse weather conditions at the departure airport, which counts as an extraordinary circumstance.
I can see why you might think so, but the records indicate that the aircraft was held for safety reasons after a storm warning. Let me check whether there's any further information.
That's a perfectly reasonable request. I'll forward the full report to our compensation department, and you should receive a detailed answer within two weeks.
I understand. Please be assured that every complaint is reviewed carefully. In the meantime, I'd like to offer you a voucher as a gesture of goodwill.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing the shift to electric vehicles
scenarios.context: Two friends discuss whether switching to electric cars is a realistic solution.

speakerA.en: I'm thinking about replacing my car with an electric one, but I'm not sure whether it's truly better for the environment, considering how batteries are produced.
I've read that manufacturing the battery creates a lot of emissions, although over the car's lifetime, it still produces significantly less pollution than a petrol one.
Another concern is charging. I live in an apartment, and there aren't any public charging points on my street, so I'd have to depend on a station that's a few kilometers away.
On top of that, the purchase price is still considerably higher, even with the subsidies that the government offers at the moment.
It might make sense to wait a few more years, until the technology improves, and the charging network is more developed.
That's probably wise. In the meantime, I could use public transport more often, and rent a car only when I really need one.

speakerB.en: That's a common question. In most studies, an electric car overtakes a conventional one in terms of emissions after about two years of normal use.
That's right, particularly if the electricity comes from renewable sources. If it's produced by burning coal, the benefit is much smaller, so it depends on where you live.
That's definitely one of the main obstacles. Without a private garage, owning an electric car can be inconvenient, and relying on public chargers isn't always practical.
The running costs are lower, however. Electricity is cheaper than petrol, and there are fewer moving parts, so maintenance is less expensive in the long run.
It's a valid option, but I believe that waiting indefinitely isn't necessarily the answer either. Every year, the range improves, and the prices come down a little.
That's a sensible compromise. Honestly, the most environmentally friendly vehicle is the one that you don't use, so reducing the number of journeys already helps.

scenarios.scenario: Planning a complicated journey with a station agent
scenarios.context: A traveler plans a multi-leg trip with trains and a ferry and asks about connections and flexibility.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I need to get to the island of Capri from Rome, and I've been told that it involves several different connections. Could you help me plan the best route?
I'd like to leave tomorrow morning, and I'd prefer to arrive before lunchtime, if possible. Is that realistic, considering that I'll need to take both a train and a boat?
That sounds good. The risk is that if the train is late, I might miss the ferry. What happens in that case? Would my ticket still be valid for the next departure?
I'd rather have the flexible ticket, then, even if it costs a bit more. I'm going to be carrying quite a lot of luggage, so I'd also like to avoid unnecessary changes.
That's useful to know. Are there any places along the way where I could leave my bags, in case I have time to spare between the connections?
Perfect. I'll take the flexible ticket for both legs. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly, and for finding the best option for me.

speakerB.en: Good morning. Certainly. It's a popular route, so there are several options. First, you'd take a high-speed train to Naples, which takes about an hour and ten minutes, and then a ferry from the port.
Yes, if you take the eight o'clock train, you'd reach Naples at about nine fifteen, and the ferry leaves at ten thirty. You'd arrive on the island just before noon, which should suit you.

That's an important question. The train ticket is for a specific service, but the flexible fare allows you to take a later one if you miss it. The ferry is a separate booking, so you'd need to check with the company.
The flexible ticket costs fifteen euros more, but it gives you the peace of mind of being able to change at no extra cost. As for luggage, there's only one change, and it's on the same platform.
There are lockers at both Naples Central Station and at the port, which cost between five and ten euros, depending on the size. They're open from six in the morning until ten at night.
Excellent choice. I'll print the tickets, along with a note of the departure times and platform numbers, so you'll have everything in one place. Have a pleasant journey.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a canceled train at a busy station
scenarios.context: A traveler asks station staff about a canceled train and tries to find another way to reach an important meeting.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I've just seen the departures board, and my train to Manchester appears to have been canceled. Could you tell me what's going on, and whether there's any alternative service?
That's quite a delay. I'm supposed to be at a meeting by eight, so I'd better find another route. Is the 6:15 likely to be on time, or is it expected to be crowded after the cancellation?
Bus, you say? I hadn't thought of that. How long does it take, and where does it leave from? I'd rather go by road than wait around, as long as I'm not stuck in traffic.
Four hours would make me miss the meeting altogether. On the other hand, if the signal problem is fixed, the 6:15 should get me there by nine at the latest. I'd better phone my client and explain.
I'd appreciate a paper copy, in case the website is slow. To be honest, I'd rather sort it out now than forget, since I'll be rushing around all day tomorrow. Is there anything else I should keep?
Good idea. Thank you for being so helpful, especially in the middle of all this chaos. I'll go and find platform four, and I'd better call my client on the way.

speakerB.en: I'm afraid so. The 5:40 has been canceled owing to a signal failure, which is expected to be fixed within the hour. Passengers are being advised to take the 6:15, so as to avoid further delays.
It's likely to be busy, since two trains' worth of passengers are now being squeezed onto one. You'd better board early so as to be sure of a seat. Is it worth considering the intercity bus instead?

The bus is expected to take about four hours, as opposed to two by train, so you'd better allow for that. It leaves from the bus station, which is a ten-minute walk, so you'd need to leave right away.
That sounds wise. In the event of further delays, you're entitled to compensation, so you'd better keep your ticket. The refund form is available online, or I can give you a paper copy here.
Just your ticket and any receipts for expenses, so as to support your claim. Here's the form. I'd advise you to fill it in on the train, since the journey is expected to give you plenty of time.
You're welcome. The 6:15 is expected to be called in about ten minutes, so you'd better not wander too far. I hope the rest of your journey goes smoothly, and good luck with the meeting.

scenarios.scenario: Comparing ways to get to the coast for a long weekend
scenarios.context: Two friends weigh up driving, taking the train, or combining both for a holiday weekend by the sea.

speakerA.en: I've been looking at ways to get to the coast for the long weekend, and I can't decide between driving and taking the train. As far as I'm concerned, driving would be far more flexible, but I'd value your opinion.

That's a fair point, although the train is considerably more expensive, particularly if we book late. Rather than paying that much, it might be worth splitting the cost of gas and tolls between four of us.

I hadn't thought about parking. On the other hand, with a car we could stop at the villages along the way, rather than going straight to the resort. It would be worth seeing something besides the highway.

That's clever, since it combines the advantages of both. Whereas the train removes the stress of the drive, a rental would give us the freedom to explore. Would the rental cost less than a full week's gas?

Thanks, I'd appreciate that. I'll look into the train prices, and I'll see whether any early-booking discounts are still available. It's no use leaving it until the last minute, since prices only go up.

Perfect. Let's decide on Thursday, then, and send everyone the details. I'm already looking forward to it, whichever way we end up traveling. Rather than worrying about logistics, we should be thinking about the beach.

speakerB.en: To be honest, I'd lean toward the train. Driving would mean sitting in traffic for hours, whereas on the train we could relax, read, or chat. It's no use pretending the roads will be empty on a holiday weekend.

True, but it's worth remembering that parking at the coast is a nightmare, whereas the station is five minutes from the beach. Instead of saving money, we might end up spending it on parking fees and stress.

That's the most convincing argument yet. It's no use dismissing the scenery, and I'd say the journey is part of the holiday. What if we took the train there and rented a car locally for a day, instead of driving the whole way?
Probably, if we only keep it for a day. It would be worth checking a few comparison sites, rather than settling for the first quote. I can do that tonight, since I'm free after dinner.
Agreed. Instead of waiting until the weekend, why don't we both finalize everything by Thursday? That way, whoever finds the better deal can book it, and we'll avoid arguing about it later.
Exactly. It's no use stressing over it when we've got a plan. I'll message the others tonight, and I'll tell them to pack light, whatever we decide.

scenarios.scenario: Arranging accessible train travel with a rail operator
scenarios.context: A wheelchair user phones a rail operator to arrange assistance for a journey with a connection.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm planning to travel from Leeds to Edinburgh next Thursday, and I use a wheelchair. I'd be grateful if you could explain what assistance you can provide, since I've had mixed experiences in the past.

The ten-fifteen, which I understand has a change at York. Rarely does a connection go smoothly, so I'm anxious about the transfer. Were it not for the tight timing, I wouldn't worry, but there are only nine minutes. Is that enough?

It would, as long as someone is definitely there. No sooner had I arrived at a station last year than I discovered nobody had been informed. Suffice it to say that I missed my connection. Can you give me a reference number to quote?

Yes, preferably near the wheelchair space, since I'm traveling with my sister. Had I known earlier that you could arrange that, I'd have booked months ago. What happens if the train is cancelled on the day?

Of course, it's Helen Carter. One more point: I'd rather not wait on the platform for long, in case the weather is bad. Is there a waiting area near the ramp? And would someone accompany us to the carriage?

It's perfectly feasible. For what it's worth, this is the clearest explanation I've had from any operator. Needless to say, I'm very grateful. Could you read back the details, so that I can check everything is correct?

speakerB.en: Good morning, and thank you for calling in advance, as that makes things much easier. We can arrange a ramp at each station and reserve a space on the train. Should you need help with luggage, we'll add that. Which service do you prefer?

It's tight, I agree. Not only is the platform change at York busy, but the lifts are occasionally out of service. Provided that we send a member of staff to meet you off the first train, nine minutes should be manageable. Would that reassure you?

Absolutely, and I'll note the details in your booking. Should anything go wrong, call the number on the confirmation and quote it. In all fairness, errors do happen, but I'll flag your journey as a priority. Do you need a reserved seat as well?

Then we'd arrange alternative transport at no extra cost, and the assistance team would be informed. Not that I expect it to happen, but it's best to be prepared. Might I take your sister's name for the booking?

Yes, there's a heated lounge at both stations, and staff will escort you directly. Whatever the weather, you won't be left waiting outside. I'd also suggest arriving thirty minutes early, which allows us to prepare. Is that feasible?

Certainly. Thursday, the ten-fifteen from Leeds, assistance at both ends, a reserved wheelchair space, and a seat beside it for Ms. Carter. You'll receive written confirmation within the hour. Thank you for calling, and have a safe journey.

scenarios.scenario: Missing the last ferry to a remote island
scenarios.context: A traveler who has just missed the last ferry asks a harbor attendant about her options for the night.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I've just watched the last ferry leave without me. Scarcely had I reached the quay when the ramp was raised. I'd be very grateful for any advice, since I'm supposed to be on the island tonight. Is there anything that can be done?
With a friend who's expecting me for dinner. Were it not for the delayed bus, I'd have arrived in good time. What I'd like to know is whether there's any other way across, perhaps a private boat?

Please do. I'd be willing to pay a reasonable amount, although I'd rather not be overcharged. Not only am I tired, but I'm also carrying heavy luggage. Do you know what he usually asks for such a crossing?
Eighty is high, but if it's safe, I'd consider it. Scarcely had I begun to worry about the cost when I realized safety matters more. How reliable is the forecast tonight? I'd hate to take a risk.

She might be, though I can phone her. Suffice it to say that I'd rather arrive late than endanger myself. Is there somewhere nearby to stay, preferably inexpensive? I'm not particular, provided it's clean and quiet.
That would be wonderful, thank you. For what it's worth, you've been far more helpful than I expected. Needless to say, I'll make sure to arrive early tomorrow. What time should I be at the quay?

speakerB.en: I'm afraid the ferry doesn't run again until morning, and it's the last service this season. Had you arrived five minutes earlier, you'd have made it. Not that it helps now, of course. Where were you meant to stay on the island?

There's a fisherman, Olaf, who occasionally takes passengers, provided the sea is calm. Hardly anyone asks at this hour, though. Should he refuse, you'd be better off finding a room in town. Shall I call him for you?

Around eighty euros, I believe, but that depends on the weather. Whatever he says, you may negotiate. In all fairness, the crossing takes forty minutes in the dark, so he's entitled to ask for something. Would that be acceptable?

The wind is rising, to be candid, and Olaf is cautious. I'd be inclined to wait until morning, since the first ferry leaves at seven. Were the sea rougher, he wouldn't go at all. Is your friend likely to be anxious?
There's a guesthouse two streets away, run by my cousin. It's modest, but the breakfast is excellent. Should it be full, there's an inn by the church. Would you like me to ring ahead and check?

Half past six, to be safe. The ferry fills quickly, especially on market days. Come to think of it, I'll tell my cousin to prepare an early breakfast, so you won't miss it. Enjoy your stay on the island.

scenarios.scenario: At a gas station
scenarios.context: Refuelling the car and asking for services.

speakerA.en: Hello. Gas, please.
Twenty dollars, please.
Yes. Where is the toilet?
Thank you. Goodbye.
Fill it up with unleaded, please.
speakerA.fa: لطفاً باک را با بنزین بدون سرب پر کنید.

speakerA.en: Can you check the tire pressure?
speakerA.fa: می‌توانید باد لاستیک‌ها را چک کنید؟

speakerA.en: Could you put some oil in the engine as well?
I need some oil, please.
speakerA.fa: کمی روغن نیاز دارم.

speakerA.en: How much does it cost per gallon?
speakerA.fa: هر گالن چند است؟

speakerA.en: Please clean the windshield.
speakerA.fa: لطفاً شیشه جلو را تمیز کنید.

speakerB.en: Good morning. How much?
OK. Here is your gas. Anything else?
It's behind the shop.
You're welcome. Have a nice day!
That's $30, please.
speakerB.fa: ۳۰ دلار می‌شود، لطفاً.

speakerB.en: Your tires are fine, but you need a bit of air.
speakerB.fa: لاستیک‌ها خوب هستند، اما کمی باد نیاز دارند.

speakerB.en: Here's your oil. Do you want me to pour it?
speakerB.fa: روغن شما این است. می‌خواهید بریزم؟

speakerB.en: The price is $3.50 per gallon.
speakerB.fa: قیمت هر گالن ۳ دلار و ۵۰ سنت است.

speakerB.en: I'll clean it for you.
speakerB.fa: آن را برایتان تمیز می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: Done. Is there anything else you need?

scenarios.scenario: Auto repair shop
scenarios.context: Describing car problems and asking for repairs.

speakerA.en: Hello. My car is broken.
It doesn't start.
How much is a new battery?
OK. When is it ready?
My car won't start. Can you help?
speakerA.fa: ماشینم روشن نمی‌شود. می‌توانید کمک کنید؟

speakerA.en: There's a strange noise from the engine.
speakerA.fa: صدای عجیبی از موتور می‌آید.

speakerA.en: I think I have a flat tire.
speakerA.fa: فکر کنم لاستیکم پنچر شده است.

speakerA.en: How long will it take to fix the brakes?
speakerA.fa: تعمیر ترمزها چقدر طول می‌کشد؟

speakerA.en: Can you check the battery, too? The car didn't start this morning.
Please check the battery and alternator.
speakerA.fa: لطفاً باطری و دینام را چک کنید.

speakerA.en: How much will the repair cost?
When can I pick up the car?

speakerB.en: Hello. What's the problem?
OK. I will look at it. I think it's the battery.
It's one hundred dollars.
It's ready tomorrow.
Let me have a look under the hood.
speakerB.fa: بگذارید زیر کاپوت را نگاه کنم.

speakerB.en: It might be the spark plugs. I'll replace them.
speakerB.fa: ممکن است شمع‌ها باشد. عوضشان می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: You have a puncture. I can fix it in about 20 minutes.
speakerB.fa: پنچری دارید. می‌توانم حدود ۲۰ دقیقه‌ای درستش کنم.

speakerB.en: The brake pads are worn. It'll cost $150.
speakerB.fa: لنت ترمز سائیده شده. ۱۵۰ دلار می‌شود.

speakerB.en: Your battery is dead. You need a new one.
speakerB.fa: باطری شما تمام شده. به باطری جدید نیاز دارید.

speakerB.en: Let me check the battery. It looks old.
The repair costs about $60, including parts.
It'll be ready by five o'clock.

scenarios.scenario: Buying gas
scenarios.context: A driver buys gas and pays at the station.

speakerA.en: Pump number three, please.
Thirty dollars, please.
Can I pay by card?
Thank you.
Good morning. Pump number three, please.
Twenty dollars of regular, please.
Yes, please. Do you take credit cards?
Where is the restroom?

speakerB.en: OK. How much gas do you want?
OK. Thirty dollars on pump three.
Yes, you can. Here is the machine.
You're welcome. Drive safely.
OK. How much gas do you need?
Here you go. Do you want a receipt?
Yes, we do. You can pay inside.
It's behind the shop, on the right.

scenarios.scenario: Checking air and water
scenarios.context: A driver asks for air for the tires and water.

speakerA.en: Can I have some air, please?
Thank you. My tire is low.
Do you have water?
How much is it?
Excuse me, where can I put air in my tires?
How much air do I need?
Could you check the water in the engine, too?
Please fill it up. Thank you.

speakerB.en: Yes. The air is over there.
OK. I will help you.
Yes, we have water.
It's free.
There's a machine next to the shop. It's free.
Check the sticker on the door. It shows the right pressure.
Sure. Open the hood, please. It's a little low.
Done. Your car is ready to go.

scenarios.scenario: A flat tire
scenarios.context: A driver has a flat tire and asks a mechanic for help.

speakerA.en: Help! I have a flat tire.
Can you fix it?
How long will it take?
OK. I will wait here.
Thank you very much.
Hello, I have a flat tire. Can you help me?
It's on Elm Street, near the bank.
I have a spare tire, but I can't change it.
How much do I owe you?

speakerB.en: Don't worry. I can help.
Yes, I can. It's easy.
Twenty minutes.
All done. It's ready!
You're welcome. Drive safely.
Of course. Where is your car?
OK. I'll be there in fifteen minutes.
No problem. I'll change it for you.
It's $25 for the service.

scenarios.scenario: Asking for a car wash
scenarios.context: A customer asks for a car wash.

speakerA.en: My car is dirty.
Can you wash it, please?
How much is a wash?
OK. Is it ready now?
How much is a basic car wash?
Does that include the inside of the car?
OK. I'll take the full wash, please.
When can I come back for the car?

speakerB.en: Yes, it is very dirty.
Yes, of course.
It's five dollars. Please wait ten minutes.
Yes, it's clean now.
It's eight dollars. It takes about ten minutes.
No, cleaning the inside costs five dollars extra.
Great. Please leave your keys with me.
Come back in half an hour. It'll be ready.

scenarios.scenario: Getting a mechanic
scenarios.context: A driver calls for help on the road.

speakerA.en: Hello. I need a mechanic.
My car is on Park Street.
It's a white car.
Please come quickly.
Hello, my car has broken down on Highway 9.
I'm near exit 14. The engine just stopped.
How long will it take for the mechanic to arrive?
OK. Thank you very much.

speakerB.en: OK. Where are you?
OK. What color is your car?
OK. I understand.
OK. I'm coming in ten minutes.
Are you safe? Where exactly are you?
OK. Please turn on your hazard lights.
About thirty minutes. Please stay in the car.
You're welcome. Call us if anything changes.

scenarios.scenario: Filling up and checking the car at a gas station
scenarios.context: A driver asks the attendant for help at a gas station.

speakerA.en: Could you fill the tank with regular, please? And can you check the tire pressure too?
Yes, please. I've got a long drive ahead, and I want to make sure everything's fine.
Go ahead. How much will that cost altogether, including the gas?
Yes, please. Is there a car wash nearby, by any chance?

speakerB.en: Of course. Do you want me to check the oil level while I'm at it?
The oil is a little low, so I'd recommend adding about half a quart.
The total comes to sixty-two dollars. Would you like a receipt?
There's one just down the road, about two minutes from here. It's open until eight.

scenarios.scenario: Explaining a problem to a mechanic
scenarios.context: A driver describes a strange noise to a mechanic.

speakerA.en: My car has been making a strange noise when I brake, and it seems to be getting worse.
It's more of a squeal, and the steering wheel shakes a little at higher speeds.
How long will the inspection take, and is it expensive to replace them?
That's acceptable. Please go ahead, and call me if there's anything else wrong.

speakerB.en: Is it a grinding noise or more of a squeaking sound?
It sounds like the brake pads are worn out. I'd like to take a look at the rotors as well.
The inspection takes about half an hour. If we need to replace the pads, it'll be around two hundred dollars.
Will do. I'll let you know as soon as I've found out what's causing the problem.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a flat tire on the highway
scenarios.context: A driver calls a roadside assistance service after getting a flat tire.

speakerA.en: Hello, I've got a flat tire on the highway, and I don't have a spare in the trunk.
Yes, I've pulled onto the shoulder, and I'm waiting behind the guardrail.
I'm near exit twelve, heading north. The license plate number is KL68 XTR.
That's fine. Will he be able to fix it at the roadside?

speakerB.en: Are you in a safe place? Please make sure you're standing well away from the traffic.
Good. Can you tell me your exact location and the license plate number of your car?
Thank you. A technician will reach you in about forty minutes, and he'll tow the car if it can't be repaired.
Most likely, yes. If not, he'll take you and the car to the nearest garage.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating repair costs with a mechanic
scenarios.context: A customer discusses an unexpected repair bill.

speakerA.en: I was expecting the repair to cost around three hundred dollars, yet your estimate is nearly double that.
Is it essential to replace it now, or could it wait a few months?
That's fair, but I'd appreciate a more detailed breakdown of the charges before I agree.
Would you be able to offer any discount, considering I'm a regular customer?

speakerB.en: I understand the surprise. Once we opened the engine, we found that the timing belt was also worn.
I wouldn't advise postponing it. If it snaps while you're driving, the damage could cost several times more.
Certainly. Parts come to four hundred, and labor to roughly two hundred.
I could take ten percent off the labor, but I can't go lower on the parts.

scenarios.scenario: Buying a used car
scenarios.context: A buyer asks questions about a secondhand vehicle.

speakerA.en: The car looks in decent condition, but I'd like to know a bit more about its history.
What about accidents? I don't want to find out later that it was badly damaged.
I'd like to have my own mechanic examine it before I make a decision. Is that acceptable?
Thank you. If the inspection goes well, I'd be prepared to offer a little less than the asking price.

speakerB.en: It's had two previous owners, and the service record is complete. Everything has been done on schedule.
There was a minor collision four years ago, but it was repaired professionally, and I have the paperwork.
Absolutely. Any reputable seller would expect that. You're welcome to take it for a test drive as well.
We might be able to come to an arrangement, depending on what the mechanic finds.

scenarios.scenario: Explaining a breakdown to roadside assistance
scenarios.context: A driver describes engine trouble to a roadside technician.

speakerA.en: The engine cut out suddenly about ten minutes ago, and I haven't been able to restart it since.
The temperature gauge shot up, and there was a faint smell of burning. I pulled over right away.
I topped up the coolant two weeks ago, so it's possible something is wrong with the radiator.
Will it be possible to repair it here, or will the car need to be towed?

speakerB.en: Did you notice any warning lights or unusual noises beforehand?
