It's not a big problem, but I'm in a bit of a hurry. How long will a new dish take?
That's fine, as long as it doesn't take longer. I have a meeting at two.
That's very generous. I'll have a coffee, thank you.

speakerB.en: I'm so sorry about that. Let me check the order. You're right, I wrote it down incorrectly.
I'll ask the kitchen to prepare it right away. It should be ready in about ten minutes.
Of course. To apologize, we'd like to offer you a free dessert or coffee.
Certainly. I'll bring it with your meal. Again, I apologize for the inconvenience.

scenarios.scenario: Splitting the bill with friends
scenarios.context: A group of friends asks the waiter about paying separately.

speakerA.en: Could we have the bill, please? We'd like to pay separately, if that's possible.
By what each person ordered, please. I only had a salad and a juice.
Most of us, yes, but one of my friends only has cash.
Great. Is service included in the bill, or should we add a tip?

speakerB.en: Of course. Would you like me to divide it equally, or should I split it by what each person ordered?
Certainly. I'll print individual receipts. Will you all be paying by card?
That's no problem. I can take both kinds of payment at the table.
It isn't included, so a tip of about ten percent would be appreciated.

scenarios.scenario: Making a reservation for a special occasion
scenarios.context: A customer calls a restaurant to book a table for an anniversary.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I'd like to reserve a table for two on Saturday, preferably somewhere quiet. It's our anniversary.
That would be ideal, if possible. Do you have a table by the window, by any chance?
That sounds lovely, provided the weather holds. Do you have a heated area in case it's chilly?
Splendid. Might it be possible to arrange a small dessert with a candle? It would be a pleasant surprise.

speakerB.en: Congratulations. Let me see what we have. Would eight o'clock suit you?
I'm afraid those are all taken, but I can offer you a table in the corner of the terrace, which is far more secluded.
Yes, we have outdoor heaters, and blankets are available upon request.
Certainly. Just leave it with me, and we'll make sure everything is prepared.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing the quality of a meal
scenarios.context: Two diners share their opinions about their dishes.

speakerA.en: How's your fish? Mine is slightly overcooked, to be perfectly honest.
That's the problem with these upscale places. You're paying for the presentation rather than the substance.
True, but I'd rather have a hearty meal in a simple setting than a work of art on an enormous plate.
I can't argue with that. The service has been impeccable, I'll give them that.

speakerB.en: Mine is quite good, although the portions seem tiny considering the price.
I wouldn't go that far. The ingredients are fresh, and the sauce is excellent.
It's a question of taste. Some people enjoy the whole experience, including the ambience.
Shall we mention the fish to the waiter, or is it not worth making a fuss?

scenarios.scenario: Handling a complaint as a restaurant manager
scenarios.context: A manager responds to an unhappy customer.

speakerA.en: I'd like to speak to the manager. We've been waiting over an hour for our main courses.
We ordered at seven, our starters arrived at half past, and no one has told us anything since.
I appreciate your candor, but we have tickets for a show at nine, and we can't stay much longer.
That's a gesture I'd welcome, although what I'd really value is some assurance that it'll be ready in fifteen minutes.

speakerB.en: I'm the manager. Please accept my sincere apologies. May I ask what has happened so far?
That's unacceptable, and I take full responsibility. We're short-staffed this evening, but that's no excuse.
I'll ask the kitchen to prioritize your order immediately, and the first round of drinks will be on the house.
I'll personally ensure it is. Should it take any longer, I'll take the meal off your bill.

scenarios.scenario: Navigating a tasting menu with dietary restrictions
scenarios.context: A waiter and two diners discuss allergies and substitutions before a tasting menu.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I understand one of you has dietary restrictions. Might I ask what we should be mindful of before I walk you through tonight's tasting menu?
Certainly. The kitchen can adapt most courses, and I'd suggest replacing the lamb with our line-caught sea bass, which pairs beautifully with the wine flight.
I appreciate you raising it. I'll flag your allergy to the chef personally, and your dishes will be prepared at a separate station.
For a menu of this length, the pairing is more rewarding, since each glass is chosen to complement a specific course. I can arrange a non-alcoholic pairing for your partner if preferred.

speakerB.en: I'm allergic to tree nuts, and my partner avoids red meat. We'd rather not compromise the experience, though, if that's at all possible.
That sounds delightful. Is there any risk of cross-contamination with nuts? I ask only because my reactions can be severe.
That's reassuring. And would you recommend the wine pairing, or is it better to choose a bottle?
Then we'll take the pairing. Thank you for being so attentive.

scenarios.scenario: Hosting a business lunch
scenarios.context: A host entertains a prospective partner at a restaurant, balancing small talk with business.

speakerA.en: Thank you for making the time. I thought a relaxed lunch might suit our conversation better than another conference room.
It's a favorite of mine. Do order whatever appeals, and perhaps we can touch on business once we've settled in.
In that case, a crisp white from the Loire. Now, I wanted to get your reaction to the terms we discussed last week.
I anticipated that. I'm open to a compromise, provided we can agree on a minimum order volume.

speakerB.en: I couldn't agree more. Conference rooms rarely inspire candor. This is a charming spot, by the way.
Gladly. I'll have the grilled trout, and I'll defer to your judgment on the wine.
I've reviewed them carefully. Broadly speaking, we're aligned, though I'd like to revisit the exclusivity clause.
That strikes me as a sensible basis for negotiation. Let's see whether dessert sweetens the discussion.

scenarios.scenario: Giving feedback to the chef
scenarios.context: A diner compliments the chef and offers a small, constructive criticism.

speakerA.en: Forgive the interruption, but I wanted to thank you personally. The duck was easily the best I've had in years.
It shows. If I may offer one small observation, the sauce was a touch salty for my taste, though that may simply be me.
I'd hate to detract from an otherwise outstanding meal. The texture of the skin alone was worth the trip.
Please do. We'll certainly be back, and I'll be recommending you to anyone who will listen.

speakerB.en: That's very kind of you. We spent months perfecting that dish, so it's gratifying to hear it appreciated.
I welcome it. We adjust the seasoning constantly, and honest feedback is the only way we improve.
That's the result of a two-day curing process. I'll pass your comments on to the team, who will be delighted.
Then dessert is on the house, with my compliments. It's the least I can do.

scenarios.scenario: Sending back a dish tactfully
scenarios.context: A diner raises a problem with a meal without causing a scene.

speakerA.en: Forgive me for troubling you, but I wonder whether the kitchen might reconsider this risotto. It's rather underdone at the center.
I'd be grateful. I don't wish to make a fuss, but I'd rather not pretend it's acceptable when it isn't.
That's extremely generous, though quite unnecessary. A properly cooked dish would be apology enough.
Everything else has been excellent, particularly the service. Please don't let this overshadow what has otherwise been a lovely evening.

speakerB.en: I'm so sorry, sir. That isn't the standard we aspire to. May I take it back and have the chef prepare a fresh portion?
Not at all; we'd much prefer to hear about it. Could I offer you a glass of wine while you wait, with our compliments?
I'll personally ensure it's right this time. In the meantime, is there anything else at the table that needs attention?
You're very gracious. The chef will be mortified, and I suspect you'll find the second attempt rather more than satisfactory.

scenarios.scenario: Choosing wine with a sommelier
scenarios.context: A guest seeks advice on a bottle to suit a varied menu and a modest budget.

speakerA.en: We're having the duck and the sea bass, and I'm at a loss. Could you steer us toward something that wouldn't betray either dish?
That sounds promising. Might you suggest something that doesn't lean too heavily on the upper end of the list?
I'll trust your judgment. I do prefer something understated over a wine that announces itself too loudly.
Splendid. And if we find we've underestimated our thirst, I assume you'll gently suggest a second bottle?

speakerB.en: A wise approach. A good Burgundy would be versatile, with enough acidity for the fish and enough body for the duck.
Certainly. There's a village-level Pinot Noir from a small producer that punches well above its price, and it's decanted beautifully.
Then this is precisely right. It's elegant, with red cherry and a hint of earth, and it won't overpower the food.
I shall hover discreetly, and appear only when the glasses begin to look conspicuously empty.

scenarios.scenario: Settling the bill and addressing an error
scenarios.context: Two friends notice a mistake on the check and resolve it politely.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I believe there may be a slight error on the bill. We seem to have been charged for two desserts we didn't order.
I thought as much. It's easily done in a busy dining room, and we're not in the least aggrieved.
Might we also split the amount between two cards? It's become something of a ritual among us.
Thank you. For the record, the pistachio dish we did order was remarkable, and I'd be grateful if you'd pass that on.

speakerB.en: Let me look at that for you. You're quite right; the table next to yours must have had their order added to your check in error.
That's very understanding. I'll have the bill corrected immediately, and I'm sorry for the oversight.
Of course. Let me process the first card, and then the second, and I'll apply the service charge evenly.
I'll relay it to the kitchen. Compliments are in short supply on a Friday evening, so they'll be thrilled.

scenarios.scenario: Booking a table by phone
scenarios.context: A customer calls a restaurant to book a table.

speakerA.en: Good evening, Blue Garden Restaurant.
Of course. For how many people?
For which day?
Okay. What is your name?

speakerB.en: Hello. I want to book a table, please.
For four people, at eight o'clock.
This Saturday, please.
My name is Reza Ahmadi. Thank you.

scenarios.scenario: Ordering fast food
scenarios.context: A customer orders food at a fast food restaurant.

speakerA.en: Hi. What would you like?
Anything to drink?
Eat here or take away?
That's six dollars.

speakerB.en: I'd like a burger and fries, please.
A small cola, please.
Take away, please.
Here you are. Thank you!

scenarios.scenario: Choosing a dessert
scenarios.context: After the meal, a waiter asks about dessert.

speakerA.en: Would you like dessert?
We have ice cream, cake and fruit.
Good choice. Anything else?
With milk or lemon?

speakerB.en: Yes, please. What do you have?
I'd like the chocolate cake.
Yes, a cup of tea, please.
With lemon, please. Thank you.

scenarios.scenario: Saying what you can't eat
scenarios.context: A customer tells the waiter about food he cannot eat.

speakerA.en: Are you ready to order?
Yes. We have vegetable soup and pasta.
No, there isn't.
Anything to drink?

speakerB.en: Yes. I don't eat meat. Do you have vegetarian food?
Is there any egg in the pasta?
Then I'll have the pasta, please.
Just water, please. Thank you.

scenarios.scenario: The food is cold
scenarios.context: A customer tells the waiter that his soup is cold.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. My soup is cold.
Thank you. Can I have a hot one?
That's okay. I'll wait.
Yes, it's hot. Thank you!

speakerB.en: I'm very sorry. Let me take it.
Of course. It will take five minutes.
Here is your new soup. Is it good now?
You're welcome. Enjoy your meal.

scenarios.scenario: Waiting for a table
scenarios.context: A couple arrives at a busy restaurant without a reservation.

speakerA.en: Good evening. Do you have a table for two?
No, we don't. Is it possible to wait?
That's fine. Can we wait at the bar?
Thank you. Is there a menu we can look at?

speakerB.en: Do you have a reservation?
Yes, there will be a free table in about fifteen minutes.
Of course. I'll call your name when it's ready.
Yes, here you are. Please take a seat.

scenarios.scenario: Recommending a dish
scenarios.context: A waiter helps a customer choose a main dish.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, what do you recommend today?
Is it spicy?
Sounds good. And what about the soup?
I'll have the soup first and then the fish.

speakerB.en: The grilled fish is very popular. It comes with rice and vegetables.
Not at all. It has just a little lemon and garlic.
The tomato soup is made fresh this morning.
Excellent choice. Would you like something to drink?

scenarios.scenario: Asking about a special dish of the day
scenarios.context: A customer asks the waiter about the daily special before ordering.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, what's the special of the day?
That sounds tempting. Is it a big portion?
I think I'll try it. How long will it take?
That's fine. Could I also have a glass of sparkling water?

speakerB.en: Today we have grilled salmon with lemon butter and roasted vegetables.
It's quite generous, but if you're very hungry, I can add a side salad.
About fifteen minutes. The fish is cooked fresh when you order.
Of course. I'll bring it right away while you wait.

scenarios.scenario: Celebrating with a group reservation
scenarios.context: A woman calls to reserve a table for a family celebration.

speakerA.en: Hello, I'd like to reserve a table for ten people this Saturday evening.
It's my parents' anniversary, so we'd like a quiet corner if possible.
That sounds perfect. Is there a minimum amount we have to spend?
Could you send me the menu by email so we can decide in advance?

speakerB.en: Certainly. May I ask what the occasion is?
We have a private area at the back. It would be ideal for a group.
No, but we'd recommend choosing from our set menu for large groups.
Of course. I'll send it this afternoon along with a confirmation.

scenarios.scenario: Complaining about a very slow order
scenarios.context: A customer politely complains to a waiter about a long wait and a wrong dish.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, we ordered our main courses almost an hour ago, and nothing has arrived yet.
I understand that you're busy, but we've been waiting much longer than the other tables around us.
Well, the pasta I ordered was meant to be vegetarian, but this one has bacon in it, so I can't eat it.
I'd appreciate that. If the dish had been brought out on time, I probably wouldn't have noticed.
That's very kind of you, but I'd rather just have the soup, since we're in a hurry now.
Thank you. Next time, I'll make sure to book a table in advance so that this doesn't happen again.

speakerB.en: I'm terribly sorry about that. Let me find out what's happened in the kitchen right away.
You're right, and I apologize. We've had a large group in tonight, which has slowed everything down.
Oh dear, that's our mistake. I'll take it back immediately and ask the chef to prepare a new one.
Of course. To make up for the trouble, I can offer you both a free drink while you wait.
Certainly. The soup can be ready in five minutes, and I'll make sure the wrong dish isn't added to your bill.
We'd be happy to see you again. Here's a card with our number, in case you'd like to reserve a table.

scenarios.scenario: Reserving a table for a birthday dinner by phone
scenarios.context: A caller books a table for a group and asks about the menu and special requests.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I'd like to book a table for eight people this Saturday, if you have anything available.
Around seven thirty would be ideal. It's my sister's thirtieth birthday, so we'd like somewhere reasonably quiet.
That would be perfect. Also, one of our guests doesn't eat meat. Do you have a good vegetarian menu?
Wonderful. Is it possible to bring our own cake, or would that cause any problems for the kitchen?
That's fair enough. Could you also tell me whether the table has been reserved under my name already?
Great, thank you for your help. We're really looking forward to it, and I'm sure everyone will enjoy the evening.

speakerB.en: Good evening, and thank you for calling. Let me check what we've got on Saturday. What time were you thinking of?
Happy birthday to her! We have a table by the window at seven thirty, which is usually less crowded than the main room.
Yes, we do. Our vegetarian menu includes a mushroom risotto and a roasted vegetable lasagna, both of which are very popular.
You're welcome to bring a cake, but we'd have to charge a small fee if the staff cut and serve it.
Of course. It's booked now under your name for eight guests at seven thirty. May I take a contact number as well?
Thank you. If you need to change anything, please call us at least a day before so that we can rearrange the table.

scenarios.scenario: Ordering with dietary restrictions
scenarios.context: A customer with a nut allergy asks the waiter for advice before ordering.

speakerA.en: Hello. Before I order, I should mention that I'm allergic to nuts, so I have to be very careful.
I'd like to know which dishes are completely safe. I had a bad reaction once after eating a sauce that I thought was plain.
The grilled salmon sounds good. Does it come with anything that might have been prepared with nut oil?
Could you please ask the chef to double-check, and also make sure that my plate is prepared separately?
That's a relief. For dessert, would you recommend the fruit salad, or is it better to avoid anything with sauce?
Perfect, I'll have the salmon and the fruit salad. Thank you for being so helpful and taking this seriously.

speakerB.en: Thank you for letting me know. Your safety is very important, so I'll explain exactly what's in each dish.
That's understandable. All our sauces are listed in the menu, and the dishes marked with a star contain no nuts.
The salmon is served with lemon butter and steamed vegetables, so there shouldn't be any nut oil involved at all.
Of course. I'll speak to the chef right now and tell him that everything must be prepared on a clean surface.
I'd say the fruit salad is the safest choice, because it's served without sauce. The chocolate cake, however, may contain traces of nuts.
You're very welcome. I'll bring your meal personally, and please tell me if anything doesn't look right.

scenarios.scenario: Splitting the bill after a group dinner
scenarios.context: Friends and a waiter sort out how to divide the bill at the end of a meal.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, could we have the bill, please? We'd like to pay separately if that's possible.
There are four of us. Two of us had the fish, and the others shared a large pizza and a salad.
That would be great, because I only had a glass of water, and I don't think it's fair that I pay for the wine.
Thanks. Oh, and I think there's a mistake here. We were charged twice for the bread basket.
I see. Could you also tell me whether the service charge has already been included in the total?
Good to know. In that case, I'll leave a small extra tip, since the service was really excellent tonight.

speakerB.en: Of course. Would you like me to divide it equally, or would you prefer a separate bill for each person?
That's no problem at all. If you tell me who had what, I'll print four different bills in a minute.
Absolutely. I'll make sure that the wine is only added to the bills of the people who actually drank it.
Let me check. You're right, and I apologize. I'll remove it from the bill straight away and bring you the corrected version.
Yes, it's included, and it's ten percent of the total. It's written at the bottom, just above the final amount.
That's very generous of you, and I'll pass your kind words on to the rest of the team. Thank you for coming.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing a business idea over coffee
scenarios.context: Two acquaintances meet at a café to talk about starting a small company together.

speakerA.en: Thanks for meeting me. I've wanted to talk to you about my idea ever since we met at the conference.
I'd like to start an online shop that sells handmade products from local artists, which are hard to find in big stores.
Exactly. I've already spoken to a few artists, and most of them said they'd be glad to work with us if the commission is fair.
That's what worries me as well. If we spent too much on advertising, we might run out of money before we made any profit.
I'd be happy to invest some of my savings, as long as we write down clearly who is responsible for what.
Wonderful. Let's meet again next week, and I'll bring a simple plan with the costs and the first steps.

speakerB.en: I'm glad you called. Your idea sounded interesting, and I've been thinking about it a lot since then. Tell me more.
That's a clever niche. Customers today are tired of cheap, mass-produced goods, and many of them are willing to pay more for something unique.
Good. The most difficult part will be finding enough customers at the beginning, because nobody knows our brand yet.
We should start small, and use social media to promote the products, which would cost far less than traditional advertising.
That's sensible. I could take care of the website and the finances, while you deal with the artists and the deliveries.
Agreed. I'll think about a name for the shop, and we can compare our ideas when we meet. Shall we order another coffee?

scenarios.scenario: Fixing a mistake with a takeaway order
scenarios.context: A customer calls a restaurant after receiving the wrong food from a delivery.

speakerA.en: Hello, I'm calling about the order that was delivered to my apartment about twenty minutes ago.
The problem is that I asked for two chicken burgers, but the driver brought me two veggie burgers, and one portion of fries is missing.
My order number is 4829, and I paid online. I'm not angry, but I'm hungry, and I have guests who've been waiting for a long time.
I'd rather have the right food, if it can be delivered quickly. Do you know how long it would take?
That's acceptable. Will I need to give the wrong burgers back to the driver when he arrives?
Thank you for sorting this out so quickly. I'll definitely order from you again, as long as the service stays this good.

speakerB.en: Good evening, and thank you for calling. I'm sorry to hear that there was a problem. Could you tell me what happened?
I'm very sorry about that. It seems that someone in the kitchen mixed up the orders. May I have your order number, please?
Thank you. I can see it on the system. I'll send the correct burgers and the missing fries right away, and I won't charge you for them.
It should take around twenty minutes, since we're quite busy tonight, but I'll ask the driver to come straight to you.
No, you can keep them. It would be a waste of food, and we'd prefer that you simply enjoy them if you like.
We appreciate your patience, and we'll add a discount to your next order. Enjoy your meal, and have a nice evening.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing how food culture is changing
scenarios.context: Two friends compare traditional home cooking with today's restaurant and delivery habits.

speakerA.en: I've noticed that fewer people cook at home nowadays, and I wonder whether we'll lose a lot of our food traditions as a result.
I'd say that's partly true, although I'd argue that technology has also made it easier for people to discover recipes from all over the world.
That's a fair point, but when I was growing up, meals were an occasion for the whole family, whereas now everybody eats at different times in front of a screen.
I wish I had paid more attention to my grandmother when she was cooking, because many of her recipes were never written down and have been forgotten.
Perhaps we ought to do something about it before it's too late. If more people took the time to cook together, the tradition might well survive.
I'm convinced that it would. Let's organize a cooking evening next month, and ask everyone to bring a dish that has been passed down in their family.

speakerB.en: That's an interesting observation, and I suspect it has a lot to do with how busy our lives have become, rather than with a lack of interest in food.
Absolutely. Not only can people watch a chef from another continent online, but they can also order unusual ingredients, which would have been impossible twenty years ago.
Admittedly, delivery services are convenient, yet they often replace the experience of sitting at a table and talking, which is arguably more important than the food itself.
That's a pity, because recipes are a kind of living memory. Had your grandmother's dishes been recorded, they might have become a precious part of your family's history.
I think the key is to make it enjoyable rather than a duty. People are far more likely to continue a habit if it's associated with good company and laughter.
What a wonderful idea. I'd love to bring my mother's lentil soup, and I'll ask her to explain the recipe so that I can finally write it down properly.

scenarios.scenario: Handling a formal complaint about service
scenarios.context: A diner raises a serious complaint with the restaurant manager after a poor experience.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I'd like to speak to you about our experience tonight, because I feel that several things could have been handled much better.
To begin with, we were seated twenty minutes after the time of our reservation, and nobody apologized or even explained what the delay was.
Furthermore, my colleague was served a dish containing shellfish, even though we had specifically informed the waiter that she's allergic, which could have had serious consequences.
I appreciate that, but I'd like to be assured that proper procedures will be followed in future, since this wasn't simply a matter of taste.
That's reassuring, although I would prefer to see some concrete action, such as additional training for the staff who take the orders.
Very well. I'll accept the offer on this occasion, but I hope you understand why we'll be hesitant to return unless matters improve.

speakerB.en: Good evening, and thank you for raising this with me directly. I'm genuinely sorry to hear that your evening hasn't met our usual standards.
You're quite right to be concerned. We had an unexpected number of walk-in customers, but that's no excuse for failing to keep you informed.
That's completely unacceptable, and I take full responsibility. Had the kitchen been properly notified, the dish would never have left the pass. Is she feeling well?
Of course. I've already spoken to the head chef, and we'll be reviewing the way in which allergies are recorded and communicated between the front of house and the kitchen.
That's entirely fair. I'll arrange a training session for all service staff this week, and I'll personally make sure that it's documented.
I understand perfectly. Please allow me to remove the entire bill from tonight, and I hope that in time you'll give us the opportunity to earn back your trust.

scenarios.scenario: Debating tipping customs
scenarios.context: Two travelers discuss how tipping practices differ between countries and whether they are fair.

speakerA.en: I've never fully understood why tipping is expected in some countries, while in others it's considered unnecessary or even slightly insulting.
In the United States, for instance, servers depend on tips for most of their income, which seems to me an unfair system, since the customer is effectively paying part of the salary.
I take your point, but I'd argue that it also encourages better service, because waiters know that their earnings are directly related to how they treat people.
That may be true in theory, but in practice, tips are often influenced by factors that have nothing to do with performance, like how crowded the restaurant is.
If I had to choose, I'd prefer a system where staff receive a decent wage and prices are higher, so that nobody has to calculate percentages at the end of a meal.
I suppose that's what I'd choose as well. At the end of the day, what matters is that the people working in restaurants are treated fairly, whichever system is used.

speakerB.en: That's a subject on which opinions vary enormously. In Japan, for example, leaving money on the table can cause confusion, because good service is simply taken for granted.
It is a controversial arrangement, and critics claim that it makes workers vulnerable, since their income can fluctuate from one night to the next.
That's the standard defense of the system. Yet research suggests that customers rarely tip according to the quality of service, so the link isn't as strong as people believe.
Exactly. A busy Friday evening may bring generous tips even if the service was mediocre, whereas a quiet Tuesday could leave an excellent waiter with almost nothing.
Several European countries operate that way, and restaurant owners there say that it creates a more stable and professional working environment for everyone involved.
Well put. Whichever approach a country takes, travelers should do some research before they go, so that they don't unintentionally offend anyone or underpay the staff.

scenarios.scenario: Asking a waiter to explain an unfamiliar menu
scenarios.context: A diner in a foreign restaurant asks the waiter to explain dishes and make suggestions.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I'm afraid I don't recognize most of the dishes on this menu, so I'd appreciate it if you could explain a few of them to me.
The one called 'ragù alla bolognese' sounds familiar, but I've been told that what we call it abroad is quite different from what's served here. What's the difference?
That sounds delicious. I'm not a big fan of very rich food, though. Would you say that it's particularly heavy, or could I manage a full portion followed by a dessert?
In that case, I'd go for the half portion and perhaps share something with my friend. What would you recommend as a starter that wouldn't be too filling?
Excellent. And if I wanted to try something typical of this region, which wine would you say goes best with it? I'd prefer something light.
Thank you, you've been extremely helpful. I'll have exactly what you suggested, and I'll let you know if I'd like anything else.

speakerB.en: Good evening, and of course. Many of our guests are visiting from abroad, so I'm used to explaining the menu. Which dishes would you like to know about?
Good question. The authentic version is made with much less tomato, and it's cooked slowly for hours with a little milk, which makes it creamier and milder than the one that most tourists expect.
It's fairly substantial, I must say. If you'd like to leave room for dessert, I'd suggest the half portion, which is quite generous anyway, and which many of our regular customers choose.
I'd recommend the grilled vegetables with a drizzle of olive oil, or the seasonal soup. Both are light, and they would balance the richness of the main course nicely.
A local white wine from the hills would suit you well. It's dry and crisp, and it doesn't overpower the food. I can bring a small glass to taste before you decide.
My pleasure. If you need anything else, please just let me know. I'll bring the wine for you to try in a moment.

scenarios.scenario: Politely complaining about an overcooked steak
scenarios.context: A diner explains to the waiter that her steak is not cooked the way she ordered it and asks for a replacement.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I hate to make a fuss, but I ordered my steak medium-rare, and this one is practically well done. Would it be possible to have it replaced, if it isn't too much trouble?

I'd rather wait for the steak, as long as it's cooked properly this time. I'd ordered it specifically because it was recommended by a friend, so I'd hate to leave disappointed. Would it be possible to bring some more bread meanwhile?

That's very generous, thank you. I'd ordered the wine to go with it as well, and I'm wondering whether it would be possible to hold off on serving it until the steak arrives. It would be a shame for it to go warm.
Not yet, I'd like to see how this goes first. On the other hand, my friend ordered the fish, and she says it's rather bland. Would it be possible to bring a little extra seasoning or a lemon wedge?

I appreciate that. I'd say the service has been excellent in spite of the mix-up, and I'd rather give constructive feedback than leave quietly. Would it be possible to speak to the manager afterwards, just to pass it on?
It looks perfect, thank you. I'd ordered it with rather high hopes, and this one lives up to them. Would it be possible to have the bill split between the two of us when we're done?

speakerB.en: I'm terribly sorry about that. Allow me to take it back to the kitchen right away. Would it be possible for you to wait about ten minutes, or would you prefer something else from the menu?

Certainly, I'll bring some right away, and allow me to offer you a complimentary starter while you wait. Let me assure you that the chef will prepare the new steak personally, to make sure it meets your expectations.
Of course. Allow me to keep it chilled until then. To be honest, I'd have suggested that myself, so thank you for mentioning it. Would you like me to bring the dessert menu in the meantime?
Certainly. Allow me to bring a selection of sauces and some fresh lemon right away. Let me assure you that we take every comment seriously, and it's helpful to hear what could be improved.
Of course, I'll ask her to come to your table once you've finished. Allow me to say that we're grateful for your patience. Here comes your steak, and I do hope it's cooked to your liking this time.
Certainly. Allow me to take care of that whenever you're ready. And let me assure you that the starter and the replacement are on the house. Please enjoy the rest of your meal.

scenarios.scenario: Deciding where to eat for a celebration dinner
scenarios.context: Two friends compare an Italian restaurant and a Thai restaurant before booking a table for Saturday.

speakerA.en: I've been trying to book somewhere for Saturday, and I can't decide. Neither of the places we usually go to feels right for a celebration, so I thought I'd ask what you fancy before I choose.

Good point. I'd say the new Italian place on Mill Street is quiet, although it's rather pricey. Either that, or the little Thai restaurant by the park, which does a lovely banquet, so long as we book early.

Both, I believe. You can order either the set menu or à la carte, so long as the party isn't larger than six. On the other hand, the Italian place has a terrace, which would be lovely if the weather holds.

I'll ask them about both options. To be honest, I'm easy either way, as long as the food is good. Do you have any dietary restrictions I should mention when I book, in case there's anything the kitchen needs to know?
Nothing at all. I'd say let's go for the Italian, then, since it's got both the terrace and the quieter atmosphere. Either way, I'm looking forward to it, and I'm glad we've sorted it out.
Ha, I remember that. I'll do it tonight, and I'll send you a confirmation. Neither of us will have to think about it again, so long as nothing changes at the last minute.

speakerB.en: To be honest, I'm happy with either Italian or Thai, so long as the place isn't too noisy. Neither of us enjoys shouting across a table, and I'd like to hear what you've been up to lately.

I've heard that the Thai place is fantastic, but it gets crowded. Neither of us wants to wait an hour for a table, so I'd suggest reserving for seven rather than eight. Is it a set menu, or can we choose?

That's a strong argument. Neither of us has had a proper evening outside since the spring. If it's dry, we could have the terrace, and if it isn't, we could simply move indoors, so long as they've got a table.

Only that I can't eat shellfish, so neither the seafood pasta nor the prawn starter would be wise. Apart from that, I'll try anything, so long as it's well made. What about you? Anything I should know?
Agreed. Shall I call them, or would you rather do it? Either I'll ring tomorrow morning, or you can book online tonight, so long as we don't both end up booking, as happened last time.
Perfect. Then it's settled. Seven o'clock on Saturday, terrace if the weather allows. I'm already looking forward to it, and I'll bring a little something for the occasion.

scenarios.scenario: Resolving a lost reservation on a busy night
scenarios.context: A customer's confirmed table booking has been lost on the night of his wife's birthday, and the host tries to put it right.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I have a reservation for eight o'clock, under the name Whitfield. Hardly had we sat down at the bar when we were told the table was unavailable. I'd have thought a confirmed booking would be honored.

Six of us, and it's my wife's birthday. Not only did I call last week, but I also received a confirmation email, which I can show you. Were it not for this occasion, I'd be less concerned. How long would the wait be?

Possibly, though the email clearly says the eighteenth, which is today. Had I realized there'd be a problem, I'd have confirmed by phone. Suffice it to say that I'm not trying to make a scene. Is there a solution?

That would be generous, thank you. To my mind, a sincere apology and a prompt solution matter more than the compensation. Whatever happens, I'd like my wife's evening to be pleasant. Might we sit near the window?

Two glasses of the house red, three sparkling waters and a gin and tonic. By and large, I'd say you've handled this graciously. Were it the other way round, I'd be nervous too. Could you also keep the cake we ordered chilled?
Quieter, please, she'd be mortified by a song. For what it's worth, I'm glad we stayed instead of leaving in annoyance. Needless to say, we'll come back. How soon can we expect the table?

speakerB.en: Good evening, Mr. Whitfield, and I'm terribly sorry. It would appear that your reservation wasn't entered correctly. Should you be willing to wait, I'll do everything I can to seat you. How many are in your party?

Probably thirty to forty minutes, I'm afraid, since we're fully booked. Provided that you don't mind a table by the kitchen, I could seat you sooner. Let me check the email, though. Ah, it appears the booking was made for the nineteenth. Was that perhaps a typing error on our side?
Absolutely, and I appreciate your patience. In all fairness, the mistake is ours, so I'd like to offer a table within fifteen minutes and a complimentary bottle of wine. Would that be acceptable?

I'll do my best. Should the window table become free, it's yours. Meanwhile, may I bring a round of drinks to the bar? Not that it makes up for the delay, but it's a small gesture. What would everyone like?

Of course. Not only will we keep it cold, but we'll bring it out with a candle at the right moment. It's not so much a favor as a proper way to apologize. Would your wife prefer a song, or something quieter?
Ten minutes, I promise. Come to think of it, I'll escort you personally once it's ready. Thank you again for your understanding, and please enjoy the drinks while you wait.

scenarios.scenario: Asking a restaurant owner about a family recipe
scenarios.context: A diner compliments the owner of a small restaurant on a stew and asks about the history behind the recipe.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, are you the owner? I simply have to compliment you on the stew. Rarely have I tasted anything so rich and so balanced, and I'm curious about where it comes from. Is it a family recipe?
Only a modest one, I'm afraid. Were it not for my grandmother's cookbook, I'd probably live on pasta. What struck me was the depth of flavor, which I can't identify. Is there some secret ingredient?

That makes sense. Not that I'd have the patience at home, with my schedule. Little did I expect a simple stew to be so memorable. Where did your grandmother learn the recipe? Was it passed down for generations?
I'd love to. To my mind, food is the best way to understand a culture. Should you have a few minutes, I'd be fascinated. What made your family leave in the first place?
It does, and it adds something to the meal. Granted, a plate of stew doesn't explain history, but it does preserve a piece of it. Were you ever tempted to modernize the recipe? Many chefs would.

Definitely. For what it's worth, you've made my evening, and I'll recommend this place to everyone. Needless to say, I'll be back. May I have the bill, and could I buy a jar of the sauce, if you sell it?

speakerB.en: Thank you, that's very kind. Yes, it was my grandmother's, and I've changed almost nothing. Not only is it a family tradition, but it's also the dish that gave me the courage to open this place. Are you a cook yourself?

It's not so much a secret ingredient as a slow process. The meat is marinated overnight, and the sauce simmers for six hours. Whatever shortcuts people take, they lose that depth. Suffice it to say that patience is the main ingredient.

From her own mother, in a village in the mountains. By and large, the recipe has traveled with the family through three countries. Each place added something small, like the herbs here. Would you like to hear the story?

Work, mainly, and later a war that drove my parents out. In all fairness, they rarely talked about it. Not until I opened the restaurant did I understand how much they carried. Does that make sense to you?

Often, but I'd hate to betray my grandmother. Provided that the guests enjoy it, why would I change anything? Mind you, I've introduced vegetarian versions, which she'd have found hilarious. Would you like to try one next time?
We do, but I'll give you the jar as a gift. Come to think of it, you're the first guest who has asked about the story. Thank you for listening, and please come again soon.

scenarios.scenario: Buying clothes or asking for prices
scenarios.context: At a clothing store, looking for an item.

speakerA.en: How much does this shirt cost?
I like this blue shirt.
Yes, please. Do you have a small size?
It's good. I'll take it, please.
Do you have this in a larger size?
speakerA.fa: این رو سایز بزرگتر دارید؟

speakerA.en: I'm just looking, thanks. I'll let you know if I need help.
speakerA.fa: فقط دارم نگاه می‌کنم، ممنون. اگه کمک خواستم می‌گم.

speakerA.en: Can I try this on? Where are the fitting rooms?
speakerA.fa: میشه این رو پرو کنم؟ اتاق پرو کجاست؟

speakerA.en: This jacket is a bit too tight. Do you have it in a medium?
speakerA.fa: این کت یه کم تنگه. سایز متوسطش رو دارید؟

speakerA.en: I'd like to return this pair of shoes. I have the receipt.
speakerA.fa: می‌خوام این کفش رو پس بدم. رسیدم رو دارم.

speakerA.en: This feels like good quality. Is it on sale?
speakerA.fa: به نظر کیفیت خوبی میاد. حراج هست؟

speakerA.en: I'll take this one. Can I pay by credit card?
speakerA.fa: این یکی رو می‌خرم. می‌تونم با کارت اعتباری پرداخت کنم؟

speakerB.en: It's nice. Do you want to try it?
Yes, we do. Here you are.
OK. Cash or card?
Let me check our stock in the back.
speakerB.fa: بگذارید موجودی انبار رو چک کنم.

speakerB.en: Take your time. Just shout if you need anything.
speakerB.fa: وقت بذارید. اگه چیزی خواستید صدا بزنید.

speakerB.en: Of course, they're right over there.
speakerB.fa: حتماً، اونجا هستند.

speakerB.en: I think we have a medium. I'll bring it for you.
speakerB.fa: فکر کنم سایز متوسط داریم. برات می‌آورم.

speakerB.en: No problem. Let me see the receipt. Would you like a refund or exchange?
speakerB.fa: اشکالی نداره. بذارید رسید رو ببینم. پول نقد می‌خواید یا تعویض؟

speakerB.en: It's a new arrival, so it's not on sale yet.
speakerB.fa: تازه وارد شده، پس هنوز حراج نیست.

speakerB.en: Yes, we accept all major credit cards.
speakerB.fa: بله، همه کارت‌های اعتباری اصلی رو قبول می‌کنیم.

scenarios.scenario: Buying a T-shirt
scenarios.context: A customer buys a T-shirt in a clothing store.

speakerA.en: I want a T-shirt, please.
Blue, please.
I'm medium. How much is it?
OK. I'll take it.
I'm looking for a T-shirt for my brother.
Medium, I think. Do you have it in blue?
I'll take the dark blue one. How much is it?
Great. Can you put it in a gift bag?

speakerB.en: OK. What color do you want?
What size are you?
It's ten dollars.
Thank you. Here is your bag.
What size does he wear?
Yes, we have light blue and dark blue.
It's $15, but today it's on sale for $12.
Certainly. It's free of charge.

scenarios.scenario: Trying on clothes
scenarios.context: A customer tries on a jacket in a shop.

speakerA.en: Can I try this jacket?
It's too big.
Yes, please.
It's perfect. I like it!
Can I try this jacket on, please?
It's a little tight around the shoulders.
This one fits well. Does it come in black?
I'll take the black one.

speakerB.en: Yes, of course. The fitting room is there.
Do you want a small one?
OK. Here you are.
Great! It looks very good on you.
Yes. The fitting room is on the left.
Let me bring you a bigger size.
Yes, we have it in black and brown.
Excellent choice. Come to the cashier, please.

scenarios.scenario: Buying shoes
scenarios.context: A customer buys a pair of shoes.

speakerA.en: I want black shoes.
Size forty-two.
They are small.
They are good. How much are they?
OK. I'll take them.
I'd like to see those brown shoes in the window.
I'm a forty-two. Are they comfortable?
They're a bit big. Do you have a smaller size?
These are perfect. Do they have a guarantee?

speakerB.en: OK. What's your shoe size?
Here you are. Try them on.
OK. Try size forty-three.
They are fifty dollars.
Thank you. Here is your bag.
Certainly. What size are you?
Yes, they're very comfortable. Try them on.
Let me check. Yes, here's a forty-one.
Yes, a one-year guarantee. Keep your receipt.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about prices
scenarios.context: A customer asks the price of things in a small shop.

speakerA.en: How much is this bag?
How much are these socks?
The bag is expensive.
OK. I'll buy this one.
Excuse me, how much are these apples?
And how much is this bag of rice?
Is there a discount if I buy two?
OK. I'll take two bags and one kilo of apples.

speakerB.en: It's twenty dollars.
They are five dollars.
Look at this bag. It's cheaper.
Good choice!
They're two dollars a kilo.
That's five dollars. It's a special offer.
Yes, two bags cost nine dollars.
That's eleven dollars in total.

scenarios.scenario: At the supermarket
scenarios.context: A customer asks a worker for help at a supermarket.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. Where is the milk?
Do you have fresh bread?
How much are the apples?
I want two kilos, please.
Excuse me, where can I find the milk?
Do you have fresh bread today?
Where are the shopping baskets?
Thank you. One more question: when do you close?

speakerB.en: It's over there, next to the eggs.
Yes, we do. It's at the front.
They are two dollars a kilo.
OK. Here you are.
It's in aisle four, next to the cheese.
Yes, the bakery section is at the back.
They're at the entrance, on your right.
We close at ten o'clock tonight.

scenarios.scenario: Looking for a gift
scenarios.context: A customer looks for a gift for her mother.

speakerA.en: I need a gift for my mother.
It's nice. What colors do you have?
I'll take the red one.
Yes, please. Thank you.
I'm looking for a gift for my mother.
She likes gardening and reading.
That's a nice idea. How much is it?
Yes, please. It's her birthday tomorrow.

speakerB.en: How about a scarf?
We have red, green and white.
Good choice. Do you want a gift bag?
You're welcome. Have a nice day!
What does she like?
How about a beautiful book about flowers?
It's $24. We can wrap it for you.
Wonderful. I'll wrap it with a nice ribbon.

scenarios.scenario: Paying at the cashier
scenarios.context: A customer pays for things at the cashier.

speakerA.en: Here are my things.
Can I pay by card?
Here is my card.
Can I have a bag, please?
Good evening. I'd like to pay for these, please.
Yes, here it is.
Yes, one large bag, please.
Can I pay with my phone?

speakerB.en: OK. That's twenty-five dollars.
Yes, you can.
Thank you. Please wait a moment.
Yes. Here is your bag. Have a nice day!
Do you have a loyalty card?
Thank you. Do you need a bag?
That's five cents extra. The total is $32.40.
Of course. Just tap here.

scenarios.scenario: Returning an item without a receipt
scenarios.context: A customer tries to return a jacket to a clothing store.

speakerA.en: Hello, I'd like to return this jacket. I bought it last week, but it's too small.
Unfortunately not. I think I lost it, but I paid by credit card.
Of course. Here you are. Is it possible to exchange it for a larger size instead?
Please. I hope it fits better this time, since I really like the color.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt with you?
In that case, I can look up the purchase with your card. Could I see it, please?
Yes, we have the same jacket in medium. Would you like to try it on?
The fitting rooms are over there. Let me know if you need any help.

scenarios.scenario: Looking for a gift in a department store
scenarios.context: A shopper asks an assistant for advice on a birthday gift.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I'm looking for a gift for my sister. She loves cooking but already has a lot of equipment.
She has several cookbooks already. Do you have anything a bit more unusual?
That sounds perfect. How much do they cost, and are they available as gift sets?
Great, I'll take one. Could you also include a card where I can write a message?

speakerB.en: How about a good set of knives or a nice cookbook? Those are very popular gifts.
We just got in some spice sets from different countries. They come in a lovely wooden box.
They're thirty-five dollars each, and we can wrap them for free if you like.
Certainly. I'll bring everything to the counter in a minute.

scenarios.scenario: Comparing prices and deciding what to buy
scenarios.context: Two friends compare two similar products before buying.

speakerA.en: I can't decide between these two headphones. They look almost the same to me.
How much longer does the more expensive one last?
I travel a lot, so that would be useful. Is it worth the extra fifty dollars?
You've convinced me. Do you think we can ask for a discount?

speakerB.en: The cheaper pair has a shorter battery life, but the sound quality is about the same.
About ten hours more, and it also has better noise cancelling.
If you use them every day, I think so. You'll probably save money in the long run.
It's worth a try. Stores often give a small discount if you ask politely.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a price at a market
scenarios.context: A tourist haggles with a vendor over a handmade item.

speakerA.en: This rug is beautiful. Could you tell me how long it took to make?
It's certainly a remarkable piece, but the price is rather steep for my budget.
I'd be prepared to pay two hundred, which is what I've seen similar ones go for elsewhere.
Let's meet in the middle at two hundred and forty, and I'll take it right now.

speakerB.en: Roughly three months. My grandmother wove it by hand, using techniques passed down in our family.
For work of this quality, I'd say it's more than fair. However, I might be able to lower it slightly.
Two hundred is out of the question. I could go down to two hundred and eighty, and that's my final offer.
You drive a hard bargain, but you obviously appreciate good craftsmanship. Agreed.

scenarios.scenario: Making a complaint about a faulty product
scenarios.context: A customer returns a defective appliance and asks for a refund.

speakerA.en: I bought this blender two weeks ago, and it has stopped working altogether.
Here it is. I've used it only a handful of times, so I'd say it's clearly a manufacturing defect.
Honestly, I'd prefer a refund. I'm not confident that another one of the same model would last any longer.
How long will it take to show up in my account? I'm planning to buy a different brand straight away.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Could I see your receipt and take a look at the unit?
It does look as though the motor has burned out. Would you prefer a replacement or a refund?
That's your right under our policy. The money will be returned to the card you used for the purchase.
Usually within five working days, although it can take a little longer depending on your bank.

scenarios.scenario: Deciding between quality and price
scenarios.context: Two shoppers debate whether to invest in a more expensive item.

speakerA.en: I can't decide whether to spend more on a good winter coat or settle for a cheaper one.
But a good coat costs almost four times as much, and I only wear it for a few months.
That's a fair argument. Still, I hate spending money on something that might go out of fashion.
You've given me plenty to consider. Perhaps I'll wait for the end-of-season sales and see what's reduced.

speakerB.en: In my experience, it's false economy to buy cheap. I replaced mine every other year until I bought a quality one.
Over five or six winters, though, the cost per wear works out far lower.
Choose a classic design in a neutral color, and it won't look dated.
A shrewd move. You could end up with the better coat at a price you can justify.

scenarios.scenario: Seeking expert advice before a major purchase
scenarios.context: A customer consults a sales specialist about buying a high-end camera.

speakerA.en: I'm looking to invest in a serious camera, but the sheer number of options is overwhelming. Where would you suggest I start?
Mostly travel photography, with the occasional portrait. I'd prefer something I can carry all day without it becoming a burden.
What about the lenses? I've heard they can end up costing more than the camera itself.
That's sensible advice, and refreshingly free of pressure. Could I try the model you mentioned before committing?

speakerB.en: It depends largely on what you intend to shoot. Are you after landscapes, portraits, or something more demanding such as wildlife?
Then a mirrorless model would suit you well. It's considerably lighter than a traditional SLR, and the image quality is exceptional.
They certainly can, so I'd advise starting with a single versatile lens and expanding only once you know what you're missing.
Of course. Take your time, and I'll bring you the lens as well so you can judge the whole package.

scenarios.scenario: Weighing an extended warranty
scenarios.context: A customer questions whether an extended warranty is worth the price.

speakerA.en: The television is exactly what I wanted, but I'm not convinced about the extended warranty. What does it actually cover?
Three years is a long time, and the premium is nearly a fifth of the price. Do many customers end up making a claim?
I appreciate your honesty. In that case, I'll pass, since my credit card offers some purchase protection anyway.
Good point. I'll read the fine print this evening before the return window closes.

speakerB.en: It covers parts and labor for an additional three years, including faults the manufacturer's warranty excludes, such as power surges.
To be candid, relatively few do. Modern televisions are quite reliable, so it's more a matter of peace of mind than financial necessity.
That's a perfectly reasonable decision. Do check the terms of that protection, though, as they often have a lower claim limit.
Wise. And should you change your mind, you can add the warranty within thirty days of purchase.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing ethical and sustainable shopping
scenarios.context: Two shoppers talk about paying more for ethically produced clothing.

speakerA.en: I've been trying to buy fewer but better clothes lately. This jacket is double the price of a mainstream one, but it's made from recycled materials.
That's a fair skepticism. I did some research, and this brand publishes its supply chain audits, which is rare.
Exactly. And if it lasts ten years rather than two, it works out cheaper in the long run.
Perhaps, but I'll admit I still struggle with the upfront cost. Not everyone has that luxury.

speakerB.en: I admire the sentiment, but I wonder how much of that is genuine and how much is clever marketing. Labels can be misleading.
That does carry weight. Transparency is usually a better indicator than any logo or slogan.
That's the argument I find most persuasive. Cheap clothes are often a false economy, however tempting they look on the rack.
True, and that's a point conveniently ignored by those who preach sustainability. Buying secondhand might be a more accessible compromise.

scenarios.scenario: Seeking a refund on a defective garment without a receipt
scenarios.context: A shopper tries to return an item that has faded after only a few washes.

speakerA.en: I bought this coat last month, and after two washes the color has faded dramatically. I'd like to return it, if possible.
I'm afraid I've mislaid it, but I paid by card, and the transaction should appear on your system if you search by date.
It was the fourteenth, and the card ends in 7731. I'd be happy to show my statement if that would assist.
A refund, please. I'd rather not risk another coat from the same batch, though I do appreciate your flexibility.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt? Our policy generally requires proof of purchase.
That could work. Could you tell me the approximate date and the last four digits of the card?
That won't be necessary; I've found the transaction. Given the fault is evident, I can offer a full refund or an exchange.
Understood. The funds should reach your account within five working days, and I'll note the fault on the file.

scenarios.scenario: Bargaining at a market stall for a handmade item
scenarios.context: A buyer negotiates respectfully with an artisan who is proud of the craft.

speakerA.en: This is exquisite work. I can see that every stitch was done by hand, which makes me hesitant to haggle at all.
I wouldn't dream of disputing the labor. Still, I'm a student, and the figure is a little beyond my means. Is there any flexibility?
A tenth is gracious. Would you consider a slightly larger reduction if I bought the matching scarf as well?
That's a fair bargain, and I'm delighted with it. I'll recommend your stall to everyone I know.

speakerB.en: You have a good eye. It took me nearly three weeks, so the price reflects the labor rather than any inflated profit.
For someone who appreciates the craft, I might shave off a tenth, but no more. I couldn't live with myself otherwise.
Now we're speaking the same language. Both for a fifth off the total, and I'll wrap them properly.
Please do. Word of mouth is the only advertising I've ever trusted.

scenarios.scenario: Comparing electronics with a knowledgeable shop assistant
scenarios.context: A customer weighs two laptops against specific professional needs.

speakerA.en: I'm choosing between these two models for video editing. The specifications look similar, but I suspect the details matter.
Cooling is a significant consideration, since my previous laptop throttled itself into uselessness after an hour of rendering.
What about the warranty? I've been burned before by manufacturers who treated claims as a personal affront.
That's persuasive. I'll take the second, though I'd like a modest discount for the trouble of such extensive deliberation.

speakerB.en: They do. The first has a faster processor, but the second offers a superior display and considerably better cooling under sustained load.
Then I'd lean toward the second. It will maintain performance far more consistently, even if its benchmark scores appear lower on paper.
This brand offers three years with on-site repair, and it has a reputation for honoring it without fuss.
I can include a protective case and a memory upgrade at no charge, which should more than compensate for your diligence.

scenarios.scenario: Asking for a different size or color
scenarios.context: A customer wants a different size and color of a shirt.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. Do you have this shirt in a bigger size?
Large, please. Do you have it in blue?
Can I try it on?
It's perfect. I'll take it.

speakerB.en: Yes, we do. What size do you want?
Yes, here is a blue one in large.
Of course. The fitting room is over there.
Great. Please pay at the cashier.

scenarios.scenario: Returning an item
scenarios.context: A customer returns a bag to the shop.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want to return this bag.
It's too small for me.
Yes, here it is. I bought it yesterday.
Yes, please.

speakerB.en: What is the problem?
Do you have the receipt?
That's fine. Do you want your money back?
Here you are. Have a nice day!

scenarios.scenario: Exchanging a gift
scenarios.context: A customer wants to change a sweater that was a gift.

speakerA.en: Hello. I got this sweater as a gift, but it's too big.
Yes, here it is. Can I exchange it for a smaller size?
Do you have it in the same color?
Yes, please. It fits me well.

speakerB.en: Do you have the gift receipt?
Sure. Let me check if we have a medium.
Yes, here is a medium in gray. Would you like to try it?
Perfect. Then the exchange is done.

scenarios.scenario: Bargaining at a market
scenarios.context: A customer bargains over the price of a bag at a market.

speakerA.en: How much is this leather bag?
That's too expensive for me. Can you lower the price?
What about forty-five? I'll buy it right now.
Okay, fifty. Could you put it in a bag for me?

speakerB.en: It's sixty dollars.
For you, fifty-five.
Fifty is my last price. It's real leather.
Of course. Thank you, and come again!

scenarios.scenario: Complaining about a faulty product
scenarios.context: A customer returns a defective product to the store.

speakerA.en: Hello, I bought this hair dryer last week, and it has stopped working.
Yes, here it is. I only used it three times.
I'd prefer a refund, if that's possible.
How long will that take?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry about that. Do you have your receipt with you?
Thank you. It's still under guarantee, so you can either exchange it or get a refund.
Of course. It will go back onto the card you used to pay.
Usually three to five working days. I'll give you a confirmation slip.

scenarios.scenario: Comparing two products before buying
scenarios.context: A customer compares two laptops with the shop assistant.

speakerA.en: I'm trying to decide between these two laptops. What's the main difference?
I mostly use it for studying and traveling. Which would you suggest?
Is the price difference worth it, though?
All right, I'll take the lighter one. Does it come with a case?

speakerB.en: The first one is lighter and has a better battery. The second is more powerful.
In that case, the lighter one. You won't need all the extra power.
If you travel a lot, definitely. A long battery life really matters.
It doesn't, but I can offer you a good one at a reduced price.

scenarios.scenario: Returning a jacket without a receipt
scenarios.context: A customer asks to return a jacket and discusses options with a shop assistant.

speakerA.en: Hi there. I bought this jacket two weeks ago, but it's too small, and I'd like to return it.
Unfortunately, I can't find the receipt. I think I left it in the bag, which I've thrown away by mistake.
I paid by card, so you might be able to find the transaction on your system. Could you try that for me?
Here you are. If you find it, could I exchange it for a larger size, or maybe a different color?
The blue one looks nice. If it fits properly, I'll take it. Could I try it on before deciding?
It fits perfectly. Thank you for being so flexible. I'll definitely keep my receipts from now on.

speakerB.en: Hello. I'm sorry that it didn't fit. Do you have the receipt with you, or the original packaging?
That's a bit of a problem, because our policy says that we need proof of purchase. Do you remember how you paid?
Yes, we can do that. Could I see your card, please? If the payment was made in this store, we'll find it.
Found it. Since it's within fourteen days, I can exchange it for you. We have this jacket in a large, in black and blue.
Of course. The fitting rooms are just behind you. Take as much time as you need.
I'm glad it works. I'll process the exchange now. Here's your new receipt, and please keep it somewhere safe.

scenarios.scenario: Comparing two laptops before buying
scenarios.context: A customer asks a salesperson for advice on choosing between two laptops.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I'm looking for a laptop that I can use for both studying and watching films. Could you recommend one?
I'd like to spend less than seven hundred euros. I don't need anything fancy, but it has to be reliable.
What's the main difference between these two? They look very similar to me, but the prices are quite different.
Battery life is important, because I often work in the library, where there aren't many sockets available.
That makes sense. Does the cheaper one come with a warranty, and what would be covered if something went wrong?
Thank you for the clear explanation. I'll go with the cheaper one, since it meets everything I need.

speakerB.en: Certainly. May I ask what your budget is, and what kind of programs you'll be using most often?
In that case, there are two models that would suit you. This one is lighter, and the other one has a faster processor.
The more expensive laptop is faster and has a better screen, but for studying and films, the cheaper one is perfectly adequate.
Then the cheaper model is the better choice. Its battery lasts about ten hours, whereas the other one only lasts around six.
Both come with a two-year warranty. If the laptop breaks because of a manufacturing fault, we'll repair or replace it free of charge.
A wise decision. I'll get one from the storeroom. Would you like to add a protective case at a reduced price?

scenarios.scenario: Choosing a retirement present for a colleague
scenarios.context: A shopper asks an assistant for help choosing a present for a colleague.

speakerA.en: Hello, I wonder if you could help me. I need a present for a colleague who's retiring next week.
I don't know her very well, but I know that she loves gardening and has recently moved to a smaller house.
I'd prefer something useful rather than decorative. I'm thinking of spending around forty euros.
The gardening set looks nice. Is it possible to have it wrapped, and could I add a card as well?
That would be wonderful. I'd like to write something short, wishing her a happy retirement and thanking her for her help.
Perfect. Thank you for your recommendations. It would have taken me hours to decide without your help.

speakerB.en: Of course. Retirement gifts are always special. Could you tell me a bit about her interests?
That's helpful. For someone who enjoys gardening, we have a good selection of tools, plant pots, and books about growing vegetables.
For that price, I'd suggest this gardening set. It includes a small shovel, gloves, and a watering can, and everything is high quality.
Certainly. We offer free gift wrapping on the second floor, and you can choose from several types of paper and ribbons.
There's a table with pens next to the counter. Take your time, and I'll wrap the present while you write.
It was my pleasure. I'm sure she'll appreciate it, and I hope she enjoys her retirement.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a late online delivery
scenarios.context: A customer phones customer service about a package that hasn't arrived.

speakerA.en: Hello. I ordered a pair of shoes on your website ten days ago, and they still haven't arrived.
The website said that delivery would take three to five working days, and I haven't received any message about a delay.
My order number is 7731. I need the shoes for a wedding this weekend, so it's quite urgent.
I understand that, but if they don't arrive by Friday, I'll have to buy another pair somewhere else. Could you speed things up?
In that case, I'd like to cancel the order and receive a refund if it hasn't been delivered by Thursday evening.
Thank you. I'll wait for your email, and I hope this can be solved without any more problems.

speakerB.en: Hello, and thank you for calling. I'm sorry that you've had to wait so long. May I have your order number, please?
Let me check the system. I see that your package was sent from our warehouse on the fourth, but it seems to have been held up at the delivery center.
I apologize for the confusion. I've contacted the courier, and they say that it should be delivered within two days.
I can arrange express delivery at no extra cost. If it's sent today, it should arrive by Thursday at the latest.
Of course, that's your right. I'll make a note on your account, and the refund will be processed within three working days.
You'll receive a confirmation email within the hour. Once again, I'm sorry for the trouble. Is there anything else I can help you with?

scenarios.scenario: Bargaining at a street market
scenarios.context: A tourist negotiates the price of a souvenir with a seller at an outdoor market.

speakerA.en: Hello. That scarf is beautiful. Could you tell me how much it is, please?
That's quite expensive. I've seen similar ones in other stalls for much less. Is the price negotiable?
I'd be willing to pay twenty-five euros. It's a good price, and I'd also buy a second one if you offered a discount.
Thirty is still more than I wanted to spend. What if I took two scarves for fifty euros in total?
That's a fair compromise. Could you also tell me whether the scarves are made of silk or cotton?
Wonderful. I'll take one in blue and one in red. Thank you, and I hope you have a good day.

speakerB.en: Good morning! That one is handmade, and it's only forty euros. It's the best quality you'll find in this market.
I'm sorry, but each one takes many hours to make, so I can't go too low. Where are you from, by the way?
Twenty-five is too low, my friend. If you buy two, I'll let you have them for thirty each, which is already a special price.
You drive a hard bargain! Fifty-five for two, and I'll throw in a small bag to carry them. That's my final offer.
They're pure silk, and they've been dyed with natural colors. They'll last for years, as long as you wash them gently.
Thank you! I'll wrap them for you now. Come back if you visit again, and I'll give you an even better price.

scenarios.scenario: Choosing furniture for a new apartment
scenarios.context: A couple talk to a store assistant while choosing a sofa and a table.

speakerA.en: We've just moved into a small apartment, and we're looking for a sofa that doesn't take up too much space.
We'd like something comfortable, because we spend most of our evenings watching films. Do you have anything that can also be used as a bed?
This one looks perfect, but the fabric seems delicate. We have a cat, so it needs to be easy to clean.
That's good to know. We'll also need a dining table for four people, but it has to fit in a very small kitchen.
The folding one is a clever idea. How soon could everything be delivered, and is assembly included in the price?
That sounds fair. We'll take the sofa and the table, and I'd like to pay a deposit today.

speakerB.en: Congratulations on your new home! We have a wide range of compact furniture. What kind of style do you prefer?
Yes, this model turns into a double bed in seconds, and it has storage space underneath for blankets and pillows.
In that case, I'd recommend this gray one. It's made from a special fabric that resists scratches, and you can wipe stains off easily.
We have a folding table that seats four when it's open, but which takes up very little room when it's closed against the wall.
Delivery usually takes about two weeks, and assembly is included if you spend more than five hundred euros, which you would in this case.
Perfect. I'll prepare the paperwork now. A deposit of twenty percent is enough, and you can pay the rest when the furniture is delivered.

scenarios.scenario: Comparing online and in-store shopping
scenarios.context: Two friends discuss the advantages and disadvantages of shopping online versus in physical stores.

speakerA.en: I've almost stopped going to shops altogether. Everything is cheaper online, and it's delivered to my door without any effort.
I agree that it's convenient, but I find that I return about half of what I order, because clothes never look the same on a screen as they do in reality.
That's one of the hidden costs. Returning items takes time, and in some cases you have to pay for postage, which cancels out the discount.
Another issue is that small independent shops can't compete with large platforms, so our towns may end up with empty streets and nowhere to meet.
I think the best approach is to use both. If I know exactly what I want, I buy it online, but for anything that I need to see or try on, I go to a store.
Agreed. Let's go shopping this weekend and have lunch in town, and support the local businesses for a change.

speakerB.en: I understand why. It saves time, and comparing prices takes just a few seconds. I can hardly remember the last time that I went to a large shopping center.
Fit is the biggest problem for me as well. Sizes vary between brands, and unless you've tried something on, you never really know whether it's going to suit you.
Exactly. Environmentalists also point out that the packaging and the transport of returned goods produce a significant amount of waste, which isn't often mentioned in advertisements.
That's a serious consideration. A lively high street is more than a place to buy things. It's part of the social life of a community, and once it disappears, it's hard to bring back.
That strikes me as a reasonable balance. Online shopping is excellent for routine purchases, whereas in-person shopping offers service and experience that a website can't replicate.
That would be a pleasant change. And if I find something I like, I promise not to look it up online afterwards to check whether it's cheaper.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a refund for a faulty product
scenarios.context: A customer insists on a refund for an expensive appliance that stopped working.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I bought this coffee machine from your store six weeks ago, and it stopped working yesterday, which is frankly unacceptable for a product at this price.
I've followed the instructions carefully, and I've cleaned it regularly. I have the receipt and the box, so I'd like a full refund, please.
I'm aware that there's a repair policy, but I've already lost confidence in the product. Had I known it was so unreliable, I would never have bought it.
I'd rather not wait three weeks for a repair when the fault clearly existed from the start. Under consumer law, I believe I have the right to a replacement or a refund.
In that case, I'd accept a replacement, provided that it's a different model, since I don't want to experience the same problem again.
That seems fair. Thank you for being cooperative. I'll bring the old machine back tomorrow, and I'd appreciate a written confirmation of what we've agreed.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon. I'm sorry that you've had trouble. May I see the receipt and the machine? I'd like to check what the problem is before deciding how we can help.
Thank you. I can see that it's within the warranty period, and there are no signs of misuse. Normally, we'd send it to the manufacturer for repair, which takes about two weeks.
I understand your frustration. However, our policy states that a repair must be offered first, unless the fault is considered serious or the repair is likely to be unsuccessful.
You're correct that the law protects customers in cases like this, and I wouldn't dispute it. Let me speak to the manager, since a refund requires his authorization.
That's possible. We have another model in stock, which is slightly more expensive, but I'm sure the manager will allow you to exchange it without any additional charge.
Of course. I'll prepare a document for you straight away, and we'll apologize again for the inconvenience. We'd like you to be satisfied with your purchase.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing the ethics of fast fashion
scenarios.context: Two friends discuss the environmental and human costs of cheap clothing.

speakerA.en: I've been reading about fast fashion, and I'm starting to feel uncomfortable about buying a t-shirt for the price of a sandwich.
Behind that price, there are workers who are paid very little, and a huge amount of water and chemicals, which pollute rivers in many producing countries.
The difficult part is that ethical brands are often more expensive, so it isn't always realistic for people on a tight budget to choose them.
Maybe the answer isn't to buy more expensive clothes, but simply to buy fewer items, and to keep them for longer. Second-hand shops are also an option.
I've started doing that, and I've discovered that it's actually quite enjoyable to find unique pieces. I'd never have thought of it a few years ago.
If more of us changed our habits, even slightly, the industry would eventually have to adapt. Consumers have more power than they realize.

speakerB.en: It's an unpleasant truth. Some estimates suggest that the fashion industry produces more carbon emissions than international flights and shipping combined.
And many of the garments are worn only a few times before being thrown away, which makes the whole system extremely wasteful, besides being unfair to the workers.
That's a fair point. It would be unrealistic to expect everyone to change overnight. Nevertheless, there are ways of reducing the impact without spending much more.
I like that idea. A well-made jacket that lasts ten years costs less in the long run than a new cheap one every season, even if the initial price is higher.
It's also a matter of mindset. We've been trained to see clothes as disposable, whereas previous generations treated them as something to repair and pass on.
I agree. And governments could help by introducing regulations that make companies responsible for the full life cycle of their products.

scenarios.scenario: Buying a mattress and comparing warranty terms
scenarios.context: A customer weighs different mattresses and asks about trial periods and guarantees.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm looking for a new mattress. My back has been bothering me recently, and I suspect that the old one is partly to blame.
I'd like something firm, but not too hard. I've tried a few in other shops, and they all felt either like a board or like sleeping on a cloud, so I can't tell what suits me.
That's interesting. How long is the trial period for this one? It's difficult to judge a mattress after a few minutes, and I'd want to be sure before I commit.
And what exactly does the guarantee cover? I've had bad experiences in the past with warranties that excluded almost everything, once you read the small print.
That's more generous than I expected. If I decided to return it after the trial, who would pay for the collection, and how long would it take to get my money back?
That sounds fair. I'll take the medium-firm one, provided that you can deliver it by Friday. I'd like to have it ready before my guests arrive on the weekend.
