speakerB.en: Good morning. I'm sorry to hear that. A good mattress can make a big difference. Let me ask a few questions, so that I can recommend something appropriate. How do you usually sleep?

That's a common experience, because comfort is very personal. For back problems, I'd suggest a medium-firm model with zoned support, which gives firmness under the hips, and softer areas for the shoulders.
This model comes with a one-hundred-night trial. You can sleep on it for three months, and if you aren't satisfied, you can return it or exchange it for another one without any penalty.

It covers manufacturing defects, such as sagging of more than two centimeters, for ten years. Normal wear is excluded, but there's nothing unusual in the conditions, and I'd be happy to show you the document.
We arrange the collection free of charge, and the refund is made within fourteen days after we receive it. All that's required is that the mattress is clean, and kept with its protective cover.
Friday is possible, if you order today. Delivery takes place between eight and twelve, and the delivery team will take away your old mattress for a small fee, if you wish.

scenarios.scenario: Returning a faulty blender and asking for a refund
scenarios.context: A customer returns a blender that stopped working after two weeks and discusses her rights with the shop assistant.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I bought this blender two weeks ago, and it stopped working yesterday. Despite following the instructions carefully, it just won't start, so I'd like to return it and have a refund, please.
I do, here it is. I'm aware that you have a thirty-day return policy, but I believe I'm also entitled to a refund under the warranty, regardless of whether I've used the product. Is that correct?
I understand. As far as I'm concerned, it was simply defective. I used it only three times, and I was careful, so I'm entitled to expect better. In spite of the price, it feels rather cheaply made.

On the other hand, I've lost some confidence in the brand. Regardless of how good the replacement is, I'd rather have my money back. Would it be refunded to my card, or would it take the form of a voucher?
That's good to hear. I'd also like to mention that the packaging was damaged when I bought it, and I should have noticed that at the time. Despite my doubts, I went ahead, which was a mistake.
Thank you, I'd appreciate that. Is there anything else I need to sign, or have we covered everything? I'm in a bit of a hurry, in spite of the pleasant service.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt with you? Regardless of the reason for the return, we normally need proof of purchase, although we can look up the transaction if you paid by card.

That's right. Faulty goods can be returned within the warranty period, regardless of the store policy. Despite that, I'd need to check whether the damage was caused by misuse, which would void the guarantee.

I've had a look, and I can't see any signs of misuse. Despite the inconvenience, I'm happy to process the return. Would you prefer a full refund, or would you like to exchange it for a different model?
It would go back to your card, and it should appear within five to seven business days. In spite of what some people think, we don't force vouchers on anyone if they're entitled to a refund.

Please don't blame yourself. Regardless of the packaging, you couldn't have known. I'll note it on the form, so that we can report it to the supplier, which might help us avoid the same problem in future.
Just this form, please. There you are, all done. Regardless of how this turned out, thank you for your patience, and I hope you'll give us another chance. Have a pleasant afternoon.

scenarios.scenario: Choosing a birthday gift with a sales assistant
scenarios.context: A shopper looking for a thirtieth-birthday present for his sister weighs up two options with the help of an assistant.

speakerA.en: I'm looking for a gift for my sister's thirtieth birthday, and I'm completely lost. She likes cooking and traveling, but I'm torn between a good knife set and a travel camera. Do you have any suggestions?
Around two hundred dollars, though I could stretch it a little if it's worth it. I'd say the knives are the safer choice, but the camera is far more exciting, whichever way you look at it.
Fair enough. Which brand would you recommend? I've seen a few at different prices, and I can't tell whether the more expensive ones are really that much better than the cheaper ones.
It looks lovely. On the other hand, would she be able to exchange it if it didn't suit her? She's rather particular, and I wouldn't want to give her something that ends up in a drawer.
That's a clever idea. I'd also like something small to go with it, perhaps something that isn't nearly as expensive. Do you have any suggestions, such as a cookbook or a nice apron?
I'll take the cookbook, then, and the knife set with a gift receipt. Thank you so much, you've saved me a lot of time. I was dreading this, to be honest, but it's been surprisingly painless.

speakerB.en: Happy to help. If I were you, I'd go for the knife set rather than the camera, since it's something she'll use every day. Cameras are not nearly as practical, and they date quickly. What's your budget?

That's true, but excitement doesn't always last. A decent knife set is not nearly as flashy as a camera, but it's more likely to be appreciated in the long run. Whichever you choose, I'd go for a reputable brand.

The mid-range ones are the best value. The cheapest sets are not nearly as durable, whereas the premium ones are slightly better but considerably more expensive. I'd go for this one, which is well within your budget.
Absolutely. We offer a gift receipt, so she can exchange it for whichever set she prefers. I'd go for the gift receipt rather than a fixed gift voucher, because it gives her more flexibility.

A cookbook would be perfect. I'd go for the one on regional Italian cooking rather than a general one, since it's more personal. Or, whichever you prefer, there are some lovely aprons on the second floor.
My pleasure. I'll wrap both for you, whichever paper you like, and I hope your sister loves them. Please come back and let us know how it went, since we always enjoy hearing feedback.

scenarios.scenario: Choosing a suit for an important interview on a limited budget
scenarios.context: A job candidate asks a shop assistant for help choosing a suit that looks sharp without going over a tight budget.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I have an interview at a law firm next Tuesday, and I need a suit that looks professional without costing a fortune. To be honest, I've never owned a proper one, so I'm not sure where to begin. Could you point me in the right direction?

I can spend about three hundred dollars at most. Since I'll probably wear it to weddings and meetings as well, I'd like something versatile. Were it not for the interview, I'd have bought something cheaper, but as far as I'm concerned, first impressions are worth the investment.

It's not so much the price as the risk of looking cheap up close. Interviewers notice details, don't they? Not only do I want the jacket to fit properly, but I also want the trousers to be the right length, in case I'm asked to stand and present.

Yes, please. Honestly, this one feels more comfortable than I expected. I'd say it's slightly loose around the shoulders, though. Is that something you can adjust, or would I need a smaller size instead?

Much better, and it's not so much a suit as a statement of intent. Seriously though, which shirt and tie would you pair with it? I'd rather not spend extra on things I might not need, although a good tie is probably worth it.

I do, and it's nearly new. So with the suit, the tie and the alterations, I'll be just under budget. Thank you for being so honest instead of pushing the expensive option. Should I get the job, I'll definitely come back to tell you.

speakerB.en: Of course, and congratulations on the interview. Not only does the fit matter, but the color does too, so I'd say navy or charcoal is the safest choice. May I ask what your budget is, and how often you expect to wear it after the interview?

That's a sensible way to look at it. Should you choose this wool blend, it'll hold its shape for years, although it costs a little more than the polyester one. On the other hand, the cheaper jacket looks fine from a distance. What worries you most, the price or the quality?

They do notice, so you're right to care. The good news is that alterations are free with any suit over two hundred dollars, as long as you collect it within a week. Were you to take the wool blend, I'd suggest shortening the sleeves by a centimeter. Shall we try it on?

Shoulders are the hardest part to alter, so a smaller size is probably wiser. Let me bring the next size down. In my experience, a suit that fits snugly at the shoulders makes people look confident, even if they happen to be nervous. How does it feel now?

A plain white shirt and a dark burgundy tie, and you're set. Not only will it look sharp, but together they cost under fifty dollars. On the other hand, if you already own a decent white shirt, you can save that money. Do you have one at home?

Please do, we'd love to hear how it goes. Collect the suit on Friday, and should anything need adjusting, bring it back straight away. As far as I'm concerned, the best advertisement is a customer who walks into a room feeling ready. Good luck!

scenarios.scenario: Persuading a friend to reconsider an impulse purchase
scenarios.context: Two friends discuss whether one of them should buy an expensive leather jacket she has just fallen in love with.

speakerA.en: I've just seen the most beautiful leather jacket in the window of that boutique. No sooner had I tried it on than I knew I had to have it. It's six hundred euros, but I'd say it's an investment. What do you think?

I haven't, although the shop assistant said it's the last one in my size. The more I think about it, the more I want it. Much as I'd like to wait, I'm afraid it'll be gone by tomorrow. Isn't that a good reason to buy it today?

I could ask, although they may refuse. What bothers me is that I haven't bought anything for myself all year. It's not so much the jacket as the feeling of treating myself after a hard few months. Does that sound unreasonable?

Probably, yes, since the leather is outstanding. But if I'm honest, the price is the only thing holding me back. I'd say the quality justifies it, although I realize my trip fund would suffer. Which matters more to you, a jacket or a holiday?

Almost every day in autumn, honestly. It's old and worn at the elbows. No sooner does the weather turn cold than I reach for it. So I'd say the new one would pay for itself within a couple of seasons.

I'll give it a go. Thanks for not just telling me what I wanted to hear. Even if they say no, I'll know I thought it through. And if I do buy it, you're coming with me to pick a scarf. As far as I'm concerned, you owe me that.

speakerB.en: To be honest, six hundred is a lot, especially since you told me last week that you were saving for the trip. What I'm wondering is whether you'd still love it in a month. Have you looked at anything similar for less?

As far as I'm concerned, that's exactly the sales trick that makes people spend more than they planned. The more urgent it feels, the less carefully we think. On the other hand, if you truly love it, it might be worth a day of reflection. Could you ask them to hold it overnight?

Not at all, and it's a fair point. What I'd suggest is setting a limit, so that a treat doesn't become a regret. Suppose you waited until the weekend and compared three jackets, would you feel less pressured? And would you still go for this one if it cost a hundred euros less?

For me, it'd be the holiday, but I'm not you. The more you wear a jacket, the better value it becomes, so it depends on how often you'd actually use it. How many times a week do you wear your current one?

Then that changes things. A jacket you'd wear daily is a very different purchase from a dress you'd wear once. What I'd do is call the boutique tomorrow, ask for a small discount, and see whether they'd match any online price. Would you be comfortable negotiating?
Deal, although I'm choosing a cheap one! Honestly, I'm glad we talked it through. Whether you buy it or not, it'll be a decision you made calmly, and that's what really matters in the end.

scenarios.scenario: Checking in and asking about facilities
scenarios.context: Arriving at the hotel and checking in.

speakerA.en: Hello. I have a room. Here is my passport.
Where is my room?
What time is breakfast served?
Is there a bus stop near here?
Hello, I have a reservation under the name Smith.
speakerA.fa: سلام، من یه رزرو به اسم اسمیت دارم.

speakerA.en: Is there a gym or swimming pool in the hotel?
speakerA.fa: آیا هتل باشگاه یا استخر داره؟

speakerA.en: Could I have a room with a view, please?
speakerA.fa: میشه یه اتاق با منظره داشته باشم؟

speakerA.en: The air conditioning in my room isn't working properly.
speakerA.fa: سیستم تهویه اتاقم درست کار نمی‌کنه.

speakerA.en: I'd like a wake-up call at 7 AM tomorrow.
speakerA.fa: فردا ساعت ۷ صبح زنگ بیدارباش می‌خوام.

speakerA.en: I'm afraid I lost my room key. Can I get a new one?
speakerA.fa: متأسفم کلید اتاقم رو گم کردم. یه جدید می‌تونم بگیرم؟

speakerA.en: I'd like to check out now. Could I settle the bill?
speakerA.fa: می‌خوام الان تسویه کنم. میشه صورتحساب رو تسویه کنم؟

speakerA.en: What time can I have breakfast here?
Could you carry my bags to the room?

speakerB.en: Thank you. Please sign here.

speakerB.en: Breakfast is from seven to ten in the restaurant.
Certainly. The porter will take them up.

scenarios.scenario: Booking a room by phone
scenarios.context: A guest calls a hotel to book a room.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want a room, please.
For two people.
Two nights, please.
That's good. My name is Ben.
Hello. I'd like to book a room for two nights.
From the tenth to the twelfth of March.
Does that include breakfast?
OK. I'll take it. My name is Mark Wilson.

speakerB.en: Yes. For how many people?
For how many nights?
OK. A room is eighty dollars a night.
Thank you, Ben. See you soon.
Certainly. What dates, please?
We have a double room for $90 a night.
Yes, breakfast is included in the price.
Thank you, Mr. Wilson. Your booking is confirmed.

speakerA.en: Hello. I have a room.
My name is Anna Brown.
Is there an elevator?
Thank you very much.
Good evening. I'd like to check in, please.
Here you are. I booked a single room.

What time is check-out tomorrow?

Yes, Ms. Brown. Your room is two-oh-five.
Yes, it's there on the right.
You're welcome. Enjoy your stay!
Welcome. May I have your name and passport?
Yes, room 305 on the third floor.
It's behind you, next to the stairs.
Check-out is at noon.

scenarios.context: A guest asks about the room at the front desk.

speakerA.en: Does the room have a bathroom?
Is there a TV?
Is there a window?
Is the room quiet?
Excuse me, does the room have a balcony?
Is there a hairdryer in the bathroom?
Could I have an extra pillow?
Thank you. Can I get a wake-up call at six?

speakerB.en: Yes, it does. It has a shower.
Yes, there is. It's on the wall.
Yes, there is. You can see the park.
Yes, it is. It's very quiet.
Yes, it has a small balcony with a nice view.
Yes, there is. Also free shampoo and soap.
Of course. I'll send one to your room.
Certainly. We'll call you at six sharp.

scenarios.scenario: Breakfast and Wi-Fi
scenarios.context: A guest asks about breakfast and the internet.

speakerA.en: Is breakfast free?
Where is the restaurant?
Is there Wi-Fi in the hotel?
Thank you. See you at breakfast.
Is breakfast included in the price?
Do you have vegetarian options?
Is there Wi-Fi in the rooms?
The connection is slow in my room. Can you help?

speakerB.en: Yes, it is. It's free for guests.
It's on the first floor.
Yes, there is. The password is on the card.
You're welcome. Have a good night!
Yes. It's served on the first floor from seven.
Yes, we have fruit, eggs, cheese and cereal.
Yes, it's free. The password is on your key card.
I'll ask our technician to check it.

scenarios.scenario: A problem in the room
scenarios.context: A guest calls the front desk about a problem.

speakerA.en: Hello. I have a problem.
There is no hot water.
I need more towels, please.
Thank you very much.
Hello. There's a problem with my room.
The air conditioning doesn't work.
Also, there are no towels in the bathroom.
How long will it take?

speakerB.en: What's the problem, sir?
I'm sorry. I'll send someone now.
Of course. I'll bring them in five minutes.
You're welcome. Is there anything else?
I'm sorry to hear that. What's wrong?
I'll send someone right away.
I'm very sorry. We'll bring clean ones.
About ten minutes. Thank you for your patience.

scenarios.scenario: Checking out
scenarios.context: A guest checks out and pays the bill.

speakerA.en: I want to check out, please.
It's room two-oh-five.
Can I pay by card?
Thank you. Goodbye.
Good morning. I'd like to check out, please.
It's 412. Could I have the bill?
Can I pay by credit card?
Could you call a taxi to the airport?

speakerB.en: Yes. What's your room number?
OK. The total is one hundred sixty dollars.
Yes, you can.
Goodbye. Have a safe trip!
Certainly. What's your room number?
Here you are. The total is $240.
Yes, of course. Please enter your PIN.
Yes, it will be here in five minutes.

scenarios.scenario: Checking in with a reservation problem
scenarios.context: A guest arrives at a hotel, but there is a problem with the booking.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Taylor for three nights.
That's strange. I received a confirmation email, and it says tonight.
I've been traveling all day, so I really need a room tonight. Is there anything available?
Thank you, that's very helpful. Does the room have a view of the city?

speakerB.en: Let me check. I'm sorry, Mr. Taylor, but I can only see a booking for tomorrow night.
Could I see the email, please? Ah, I see. There was a mistake on our website.
Yes, we have a room on the fourth floor, and we'll give you a discount for the inconvenience.
It faces the garden, which is quieter. Breakfast is served from seven to ten.

scenarios.scenario: Reporting a problem with the room
scenarios.context: A guest calls the front desk to complain about the room.

speakerA.en: Hello, this is room 312. The air conditioning isn't working, and it's very hot in here.
Yes, I've tried several times, but nothing happens. The room is almost unbearable.
Thank you. If it can't be fixed quickly, would it be possible to change rooms?
I'd appreciate that. I have an early meeting tomorrow and need a good night's sleep.

speakerB.en: I apologize for that. Have you tried adjusting the temperature on the control panel?
I'll send a technician right away. It should take about fifteen minutes.
Of course. I'll check which rooms are available and let you know in a few minutes.
Understood. We'll do everything we can to solve the problem tonight.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about hotel services and checkout
scenarios.context: A guest asks the receptionist about facilities and checkout time.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, what time is checkout tomorrow? My flight doesn't leave until the evening.
That would be great. Is there somewhere I could shower afterwards?
Perfect. And is it possible to order a taxi to the airport in the afternoon?
Thanks. Could you also prepare the bill tonight, so I don't have to wait in the morning?

speakerB.en: Checkout is at eleven, but we can store your luggage until you're ready to leave.
Yes, there's a changing room next to the gym, and you're welcome to use it.
Certainly. Just let us know a few hours in advance, and we'll arrange it.
Of course. I'll leave it in an envelope at the desk with your name on it.

scenarios.scenario: Requesting an upgrade and special services
scenarios.context: A guest speaks to the concierge about arrangements for his stay.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I wonder whether it might be possible to upgrade to a room with a view of the sea.
How much is the difference? If it's reasonable, I'd be happy to pay it.
That sounds fair. Also, could you arrange a table for two at the rooftop restaurant this evening?
Half past eight would be ideal, and my guest is vegetarian.

speakerB.en: I'll check availability, sir. There is a premium for those rooms, but we do have one free for tonight.
It's sixty dollars a night. That includes complimentary access to the executive lounge.
Certainly. Do you have a preferred time, and are there any dietary requirements we should know about?
I'll inform the kitchen. Your luggage will be taken to the new room while you have lunch.

scenarios.scenario: Complaining about noise at a hotel
scenarios.context: A guest phones the front desk late at night to report a disturbance.

speakerA.en: I'm sorry to call at this hour, but the noise from the room next door has been going on since eleven.
It's 508. It sounds like a party, and I have an early start tomorrow.
I appreciate that, but this isn't the first time. It was just as loud last night.
That's a considerate offer, although I'd rather not have to pack my belongings at midnight.

speakerB.en: I apologize for the disturbance. Could you tell me your room number so I can look into it?
I'll send someone from security to speak to the guests immediately.
In that case, I'd be happy to move you to a quieter room on a higher floor, if you'd prefer.
I understand. Let's see whether the situation improves, and if not, call me back and we'll arrange the move.

scenarios.scenario: Disputing the hotel bill at checkout
scenarios.context: A guest queries unexpected charges on his final bill.

speakerA.en: Before I settle the bill, could you explain this charge for the minibar? I haven't touched it.
That can't be right. I wasn't even in the room on Tuesday evening, as I was at a conference dinner.
Whatever the cause, I'm not prepared to pay for something I didn't consume.
Thank you. I'd also like a receipt that itemizes everything, since my company will require it.

speakerB.en: Let me look into that. Our records show that a bottle of wine and some snacks were taken on Tuesday.
It's possible that the room was entered by a previous guest, or that an error was made when logging the items.
Quite understandable. I'll remove the charge, and I apologize for the inconvenience.
Of course. I'll print it now, and send a digital copy to your email.

scenarios.scenario: Arranging a conference stay for a group
scenarios.context: An event coordinator negotiates group rates and facilities with a hotel manager.

speakerA.en: We're organizing a three-day conference for about eighty delegates, and we're considering your hotel as the venue. Could we discuss what you can offer?
That sounds suitable. We'd also need a block of forty rooms. What would the group rate be, assuming we guarantee the booking?
That's a good start. However, our budget is fairly rigid, so I'd like to know if there's flexibility on the catering costs.
That would make a real difference. Could you put the proposal in writing so I can present it to my committee?

speakerB.en: We'd be delighted to host you. We have a ballroom that seats a hundred and twenty, plus four breakout rooms, all with full audiovisual equipment.
For a block of that size, I can offer a fifteen percent reduction on the standard rate, with complimentary breakfast included.
There may be. If you commit to our full-day catering package, I could waive the room hire fee for the ballroom.
Certainly. You'll have it by tomorrow morning, along with a provisional hold on the dates for seventy-two hours.

scenarios.scenario: Arranging accessible accommodation
scenarios.context: A guest confirms accessibility arrangements for a relative who uses a wheelchair.

speakerA.en: I'd like to confirm the arrangements for my stay. My mother uses a wheelchair, so accessibility is a priority for us.
Excellent. Is the route to the dining room step-free? On our last trip elsewhere, we found the restaurant was reachable only by stairs.
That's thoughtful, though I suspect she'll insist on managing by herself. She's fiercely independent.
Thank you. It's rare to find a hotel that anticipates these needs rather than treating them as an afterthought.

speakerB.en: Of course. I've noted that on your reservation. You're booked into a ground-floor room with a roll-in shower and wider doorways.
Everything on the ground level is fully accessible, including the restaurant and the garden terrace. I can also arrange for a staff member to assist at mealtimes if she'd like.
I quite understand. We'll make the assistance available discreetly, and she's free to decline it.
We try to. Please don't hesitate to let me know if anything falls short of your expectations during your stay.

scenarios.scenario: Giving constructive feedback at checkout
scenarios.context: A guest gives candid but fair feedback when the manager asks about the stay.

speakerA.en: I hope you enjoyed your stay. May I ask how you found everything, from the service to the room?
I'm glad to hear it. Was there anything that fell short of your expectations?
I'm sorry about that. That's not the standard we aspire to, and I'll investigate why the first request wasn't dealt with promptly.
Thank you for your candor. As a gesture of goodwill, I'd like to offer you a discount on your next visit.

speakerB.en: Largely very pleasant, actually. The staff were exceptionally courteous, and the location couldn't be better.
Since you ask, the air conditioning in my room was erratic, and it took two requests before someone came to look at it.
I'd appreciate that. It was a minor irritation in an otherwise excellent stay, so I wouldn't want it to overshadow the rest.
That's most gracious, and I'll certainly take you up on it. I expect to be back in the spring.

scenarios.scenario: Complaining about noise and requesting a room change
scenarios.context: A guest politely but firmly asks for a quieter room late at night.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I'm sorry to trouble you at this hour, but the room I've been given is directly above the bar, and the noise is unrelenting.
I'd rather not wait until midnight, given that I have an early meeting. Is there a quieter room available on a higher floor?
That would be ideal, provided there's no additional charge. I hadn't expected to be relocated on account of a design flaw.
That's very gracious. I'd also appreciate a late checkout tomorrow, to make up for the lost sleep.

speakerB.en: I do apologize, Madam. Our records show that the bar closes at midnight, but I can understand your frustration in the meantime.
Let me check. I can offer you a corner suite on the seventh floor, which is considerably more secluded.
There will be no charge whatsoever, and I'll have your belongings moved by the porter so you needn't lift a finger.
Certainly. I'll arrange it for two o'clock, and a complimentary breakfast will be sent to your room.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a conference booking with a hotel's events manager
scenarios.context: A planner discusses terms, flexibility and contingencies for a three-day event.

speakerA.en: We're expecting about two hundred delegates, though numbers could fluctuate by twenty percent, so flexibility is crucial.
Could we extend that to seven days? Delegates have a habit of committing late and cancelling later.
Excellent. We'll also need dependable connectivity in all the meeting rooms, as several sessions will be streamed.
That would be reassuring. Please include these points in a revised proposal, and I'll put it before my committee this week.

speakerB.en: We can accommodate that. Our standard contract allows adjustments up to fourteen days beforehand without penalty.
I'd have to refer that to my director, but given the size of the booking, I suspect she'll be amenable.
The entire conference wing has a dedicated fiber line, and I'd be happy to arrange a technical rehearsal the day before.
You'll have it by Wednesday. I'd also suggest a site visit, so that you can see the spaces for yourselves.

scenarios.scenario: Handling a lost item after checkout
scenarios.context: A former guest contacts the hotel to recover something of sentimental value.

speakerA.en: I stayed with you last weekend, and I fear I left behind a watch in the bedside drawer. It belonged to my late father.
Room 412, from Friday to Sunday. It's a silver watch with a green leather strap, and there's an inscription on the back.
What a relief. I'd been dreading that it had been discarded or taken, and I couldn't bear the thought.
That's more than generous. Please let your housekeeping staff know how grateful I am for their honesty.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that, and I understand how much it must mean. Could you give me your room number and the dates of your stay?
Let me consult the lost property register. Yes, housekeeping has logged a watch matching that description, and it's safely in our office.
We take such items seriously, particularly those with personal significance. We'll insure it and send it by courier at our expense.
I shall, and I'll include a note with the parcel. It's rare to be able to deliver such unambiguously good news.

scenarios.scenario: Asking for extra things
scenarios.context: A guest calls the front desk for extra items.

speakerA.en: Hello, front desk. How can I help you?
Sure. Anything else?
No problem. We will bring them now.
You're welcome. Have a good night.

speakerB.en: Hello. I'm in room 305. I need two more towels.
Yes, one more pillow, please.
Thank you very much.
Good night.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about breakfast and check-out time
scenarios.context: A guest asks the receptionist about breakfast and check-out.

speakerA.en: Good evening. Can I help you?
It's from seven to ten in the restaurant.
It's at twelve o'clock.
Yes, of course. We keep it for you.

speakerB.en: Yes. What time is breakfast?
And what time is check-out?
Can I leave my bag here after that?
Great. Thank you.

scenarios.scenario: Asking for a late check-out
scenarios.context: A guest asks if he can leave the room later.

speakerA.en: Good morning. My flight is in the evening. Can I check out later?
Around four o'clock, if possible.
And after two? Is there an extra charge?
I'll take until two, then. Can I leave my luggage here after that?

speakerB.en: Normally check-out is at twelve. What time would you like?
I can give you until two without extra charge.
Yes, it's twenty dollars for each extra hour.
Of course. We'll keep it safe at the reception.

scenarios.scenario: Complaining about noise
scenarios.context: A guest complains about noise from another room.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, I'm in room 214. There's a lot of noise next door.
For about two hours. I can't sleep.
Thank you. Is there another quiet room?
That would be great. Thank you for your help.

speakerB.en: I'm very sorry. How long has it been like this?
I'll call the guests in that room right now.
Yes, we have one on the fifth floor. I can move you.
Please wait a minute. A porter will help with your bags.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a booking problem at check-in
scenarios.context: A guest finds that his reservation cannot be found at the front desk.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Karimi, but you can't seem to find it.
About three weeks ago, through your website. I have the confirmation email here.
That's frustrating. I've been traveling all day, and I really need a room tonight.
That's very kind of you. Could you also arrange breakfast for tomorrow?

speakerB.en: I'm very sorry, sir. Could you tell me when you made the booking?
Thank you. I see it now. It was entered for next week by mistake.
I understand. We still have a room available, and I'll give you a discount.
Certainly. It's included, and I'll make sure it's on your booking this time.

scenarios.scenario: Asking for recommendations from the concierge
scenarios.context: A guest asks the concierge what to do in the area.

speakerA.en: Excuse me, we're staying for three days. What would you recommend we see?
Is there anything that isn't too touristy?
Wonderful. Could you recommend a restaurant with traditional food?
That would be great. Please make it for tomorrow at eight.

speakerB.en: The old town is a must. You can easily reach it on foot in twenty minutes.
Yes, the local market on Saturday mornings is popular with residents.
I'd suggest the Blue Door. It's small, so I can book a table for you.
Of course. I'll confirm it with them and leave a note in your room.

scenarios.scenario: Asking to change a noisy room
scenarios.context: A guest asks the receptionist to move to a quieter room.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I'm staying in room 305, and I'm afraid I have a problem with the noise.
There seems to be a party on the floor above, and the music has been playing since nine o'clock.
I did, but nothing changed. I have an important meeting early tomorrow, so I really need to get some sleep tonight.
That would be ideal. Is there a room available on a higher floor, away from the street?
Thank you. Would it be possible for someone to help me with my luggage? I've already unpacked quite a lot.
That's very kind of you. I appreciate how quickly you've dealt with this, and I'm sorry to trouble you so late.

speakerB.en: Good evening, sir. I'm sorry to hear that. Could you tell me exactly what the problem is?
I apologize. That shouldn't be happening. Have you already called the front desk to complain about it?
I understand completely. Let me see what we can do. If there's a quiet room available, I'll move you at once.
We have a room on the seventh floor facing the garden. It's much quieter, and it has a slightly bigger bed.
Certainly. I'll send a porter to your room straight away, and I'll have the new key card ready in two minutes.
It's no trouble at all. We want you to be comfortable, and I'll speak to the guests upstairs about the noise.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about facilities and checking out early
scenarios.context: A guest asks about the hotel's services and arranges an early departure.

speakerA.en: Hello. I'd like to check out tomorrow morning at six, because I have to catch an early flight.
Yes, please. Could you also tell me whether breakfast could be prepared earlier, perhaps around five thirty?
That's a good solution. By the way, is there a place in the hotel where I can print my boarding pass?
Thank you. I've also been wondering whether I'm able to leave my luggage here until the afternoon on the last day of my stay.
Excellent. Finally, could you arrange a taxi for me at a quarter to six tomorrow?
That's very helpful. Thank you for making everything so easy. I've really enjoyed my stay.

speakerB.en: Of course. Since you're leaving so early, I'd suggest settling your bill this evening, so that you won't have to wait in the morning.
Our restaurant doesn't open until seven, but we can prepare a packed breakfast for you, which will be left at the desk.
Yes, there's a business corner next to the lobby with a printer that guests can use for free at any time.
Certainly. Our storage room is open until midnight, and your bags will be kept safely for as long as you need.
No problem. I'll book it now. The driver will wait outside, and the fare to the airport is usually around thirty euros.
It's a pleasure. We hope you'll stay with us again, and we wish you a safe flight.

scenarios.scenario: Booking rooms for a business group by phone
scenarios.context: A caller reserves several rooms for colleagues attending a conference.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I'm calling to reserve five rooms for a conference that takes place in the first week of May.
We'll need them from the third until the seventh. Four of them should be singles, and one should be a double.
Do you offer any discounts for group bookings? We'll be staying for several nights, so it should be worth it.
That sounds reasonable. Is breakfast included in the price, and is there a room where we could hold a small meeting?
Great. I'd like to confirm the booking, but could you send the details by email first, so I can show them to my manager?
Thank you very much. I'll get back to you by tomorrow afternoon to confirm everything.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon, and thank you for calling. Let me check our availability for those dates. How many nights will you be staying?
Yes, we have enough rooms available. May I ask what the name of the conference is? Many of our guests are attending it.
Yes, groups of five rooms or more receive a ten percent discount, and the rate applies to all nights of your stay.
Breakfast is included, and we have a meeting room for up to ten people, which can be reserved for an additional fee.
Certainly. I'll send you an email with all the details, and I'll hold the rooms for you until the end of tomorrow.
That's fine. If you need to make any changes, please let us know as early as possible. We look forward to welcoming you.

scenarios.scenario: Arranging a late check-out and a room upgrade
scenarios.context: A guest talks to reception about staying longer and moving to a better room.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm checking out today, but my flight doesn't leave until the evening. Would it be possible to keep the room until five?
I understand. I wouldn't mind paying an extra fee, as long as I don't have to carry my luggage around the city all day.
That sounds reasonable. And for my next stay, I'd like to ask about the possibility of an upgrade to a room with a balcony.
I'll be back in March for a week. It's for our anniversary, so I'd like something a bit more special than a standard room.
That would be lovely. Could you add a note to my booking, so that nobody forgets it?
Thank you so much. You've been very helpful, and I'm already looking forward to the next visit.

speakerB.en: Good morning. Let me see what I can do. Normally, check-out is at eleven, but it depends on how busy we are today.
We'd be able to offer you a late check-out until three o'clock free of charge. After that, we'd have to charge half of the room price.
Of course. We have deluxe rooms with balconies and a view of the sea. They cost around forty euros more per night.
Congratulations in advance! If you book directly with us, we can usually offer a complimentary bottle of wine and a late check-out as well.
Certainly. I'll write it down on your reservation, and the manager will make sure that the room is prepared for you.
It's been a pleasure having you with us. Have a safe flight, and we'll see you in March.

scenarios.scenario: Reporting a problem with the air conditioning
scenarios.context: A guest calls the front desk to report that the room is too hot and needs repair.

speakerA.en: Hello, this is room 412. I'm calling because the air conditioning doesn't seem to be working, and the room is extremely hot.
I tried to turn it on a few hours ago, but it only blows warm air. I've opened the window, but the street is too noisy to sleep with it open.
I'd prefer that someone comes to fix it, but I have to go out in half an hour, so I won't be in the room.
That's fine. I'll leave the key with you at the reception desk, so that the technician can enter.
Thank you. If it can't be repaired today, would it be possible to move to another room for tonight?
That's very kind. I appreciate your help, and I'm sure it will be resolved quickly.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon. I'm very sorry for the inconvenience. Could you tell me what exactly is wrong with it?
I understand, and I apologize. That shouldn't have happened. I'll send our technician up as soon as possible to check the system.
No problem at all. He can go in while you're out, as long as you give us permission. Is that all right with you?
Of course. We'll take care of it, and I'll make sure that the room is cooled down by the time you return.
Yes, if it can't be fixed, we'll upgrade you to a suite on the sixth floor at no extra charge. We'll move your luggage as well.
It's the least we can do. If there's anything else you need, please don't hesitate to call me directly.

scenarios.scenario: Giving feedback at check-out
scenarios.context: A guest shares opinions about the stay with a receptionist while checking out.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'd like to check out, please. Here's the key card. Everything was fine, except for a few small things.
The room was clean and comfortable, but the breakfast was disappointing. There wasn't much choice, and the coffee was cold.
Also, the Wi-Fi was very slow in the evenings. I had to work remotely, and the connection kept dropping during my calls.
On the other hand, the staff were always polite and helpful, and I especially liked the location, which was very convenient.
I'd be happy to. If you improved the breakfast and the Internet, I'm sure it would be one of the best hotels in the city.
Thank you. I'll write a review online as well, and I'll mention the good points too.

speakerB.en: Good morning. Thank you for staying with us. Please tell me what we could improve. We take our guests' opinions seriously.
I'm sorry to hear that. We've received a similar comment recently, and the manager is already looking into changing the supplier.
That's a problem we're aware of, and we're planning to install a faster system next month. I apologize for the trouble it caused.
I'm glad that you noticed that. Our team works very hard, and I'll make sure that they hear your compliments.
Would you mind filling in our feedback form? It only takes a minute, and it helps us to decide what to change first.
That would mean a lot to us. We hope to welcome you back soon, and thank you again for your honest feedback.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a booking error for a group
scenarios.context: A travel organizer resolves a reservation mistake with a hotel manager.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm afraid there's been a serious misunderstanding regarding our group booking. I reserved twelve rooms for this week, yet your system only shows eight.
I have the confirmation email here, which clearly states twelve rooms from the tenth to the fourteenth. I paid the deposit in full three months ago.
I appreciate that, but I'm responsible for a group of delegates who are arriving in two hours, and I can't simply ask them to find accommodation elsewhere.
That's a possibility, but it would have to be of comparable standard and close to the conference venue. Otherwise, I'm afraid we'd have to consider canceling altogether.
I'd also expect the cost of any transport between the two hotels to be covered, and a reduction in the rate for the inconvenience.
Very well. If you can put that in writing, I'll inform the delegates, and I trust that this will be resolved before the evening.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and thank you for explaining the situation. I'm very sorry. Let me check the reservation system and see how this could have happened.
You're right, and I can see the email in our records. It appears that part of the booking was lost when the system was updated last month. That's entirely our fault.
Of course. Let me see what I can arrange. We can accommodate eight of your guests here, and I'm trying to find rooms for the remaining four in a partner hotel nearby.
The partner hotel is a four-star property, about five minutes away by car. We'd provide a shuttle service, so your guests wouldn't need to arrange transport on their own.
That's entirely reasonable. We'd cover all transport costs, and I'd be prepared to offer a twenty percent discount on the whole booking, as well as a complimentary breakfast.
I'll prepare a letter confirming all of this within the hour. Once again, I apologize, and I'll personally make sure that your group is looked after.

scenarios.scenario: Weighing different types of accommodation
scenarios.context: Two friends compare hotels, hostels, and rentals before booking a long trip.

speakerA.en: We need to decide where to stay in Lisbon. I've been comparing hotels and private apartments, and I can't make up my mind.
Hotels are certainly more convenient, since breakfast and cleaning are included, but over ten nights, the price adds up to a considerable amount.
On the other hand, an apartment would give us more space and a kitchen, which would save money on meals. But there's the risk of unreliable hosts.
I'd also like to be in a central area, because I don't want to spend half of every day on public transport, even if it means paying a little more.
How about a compromise? We could stay in a small apartment hotel, which offers a kitchen, but also has a reception desk and regular cleaning.
Then let's book it. If we don't like it after the first few nights, we could always switch, as long as the cancellation policy is flexible.

speakerB.en: I know what you mean. Each option has strengths and weaknesses, and it all depends on what matters most to us during the trip.
True. And hotels tend to offer a sense of security, which counts for a lot when you're in a country that you don't know very well.
That's what worries me too. I've heard stories of people who arrived at an apartment, only to discover that it didn't match the pictures at all.
Location is crucial. Staying slightly outside the center might be cheaper, but we'd lose a lot of time and spend more on transport, which defeats the purpose.
That sounds like an excellent solution. I've seen a place near the river, which has good reviews and a rooftop terrace. It's slightly above our budget, but it might be worth it.
Agreed. I'll check the conditions again before we pay. The last thing we want is to be stuck with a non-refundable booking that doesn't suit us.

scenarios.scenario: Praising and critiquing a stay in a review conversation
scenarios.context: A guest talks to a hotel manager about what impressed and what disappointed during their stay.

speakerA.en: Thank you for asking about my stay. On the whole, I was very impressed, although there were one or two points that I think deserve your attention.
The staff were exceptionally friendly, and the room was spotless. I particularly appreciated the way the receptionist remembered my name and my preferences.
My main complaint is the noise from the street. Although the windows are supposedly soundproof, I could hear traffic until after midnight, and it affected my sleep.
I also felt that the breakfast could have been better organized. On the second morning, we waited for fifteen minutes just to find a table, which seemed unnecessary.
I'd also suggest labeling the dishes, because many guests have dietary requirements, and it's not always obvious what is vegetarian.
I'd be delighted to. If these issues were addressed, I believe the hotel would be among the best in the region, and I'd happily recommend it.

speakerB.en: We're delighted to hear that, and we value your honest opinion. Please tell me what we could have done better, as we're always looking for ways to improve.
Thank you. I'll pass that on to the team, and I'm sure it will mean a lot to them. We pride ourselves on creating a personal atmosphere for every guest.
I'm sorry to hear that. We've received similar comments before, and we're considering installing double glazing. In the meantime, we could offer earplugs or a room facing the courtyard.
That's a good point. We've had an increase in guests recently, and the dining room hasn't kept up. We're thinking of extending the opening hours to spread out the demand.
That's an excellent suggestion, and one that should have been implemented much earlier. I'll speak to the chef this afternoon about adding clear labels to everything on the buffet.
That's very kind of you. Would you mind if I quoted your comments in our internal report? And please accept a voucher for a discount on your next stay.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a long-term stay rate
scenarios.context: A guest planning a month-long stay negotiates the price and conditions with the manager.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I'm planning to stay in the city for a month while I work on a project, and I wondered whether you offer special rates for long-term guests.
I'd need a room with a desk and reliable Internet, because I'll be working from the room most days. A small kitchen would be a bonus, but it's not essential.
I appreciate that. The nightly rate that I saw online would come to more than I'd budgeted, though. Is there any possibility of a discount, if I paid for the entire stay in advance?
That's closer to what I had in mind. Would housekeeping be daily, or could it be reduced to twice a week? I'd prefer fewer interruptions while I'm working.
That sounds perfect. And what happens if I need to leave a few days early, because the project finishes sooner than planned? I wouldn't want to lose money.
Thank you. If you can put all of this in writing, I'll confirm the booking this afternoon, and I'll make the payment by transfer.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon, and welcome. We do have a long-stay program, which is quite popular with business travelers. May I ask when you'd arrive, and how many people would be staying?

We have a few studio apartments on the fourth floor, which have a kitchenette and a proper work desk. The fiber-optic connection is very reliable, and there's a business center on the ground floor too.
For a month, we could offer a twenty-five percent reduction on the standard rate. If you pay everything in advance, I could add a further five percent, which brings it to a competitive level.
Certainly. Our standard policy is daily cleaning, but we can arrange it for two or three days a week, and we'll change the towels and linen whenever you ask.
If you leave early, we'd refund the unused nights, minus a handling fee of one night's rate. If you give us at least a week's notice, we'd waive the fee entirely.
Of course. I'll prepare an agreement with all the details, and I'll send it to your email within the hour. Once you've confirmed, we'll reserve the apartment for you.

scenarios.scenario: Complaining about a noisy room and asking for a change
scenarios.context: A guest tells the receptionist that her room is far noisier than she was promised and asks for compensation.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I'm afraid I have a problem with my room. I was led to believe that it would be quiet, but there's a loud party on the floor above, and I'd be grateful if you could do something about it.

Room 412. To be honest, it's not just tonight. I was led to believe that the hotel prided itself on peaceful rooms, but last night there was construction noise until late, and I'd be grateful if you could explain.
That would be ideal, as long as it's genuinely quiet this time. I was led to believe that I'd booked a room overlooking the garden, and so far I've only had a view of the parking lot.

That's acceptable. On the other hand, I'd like some kind of compensation, since I've lost two nights' sleep and I've got an important meeting tomorrow. I'd be grateful if the hotel could take that into account.

That's a fair start. As far as I'm concerned, a discount would be appropriate, since the problem was mentioned neither on the website nor when I checked in. I'd be grateful if you could confirm that in writing.
Thank you, I appreciate that. I'll pack my things and wait in the lobby. I was led to believe that service was a priority here, and I'm glad to see that, at least, is true.

speakerB.en: I'm so sorry to hear that. May I ask which room you're in? I'll send someone up to speak to the guests right away, although I should say that these things are sometimes difficult to control.

I do apologize. There's some renovation work on the ground floor, which should have been mentioned at booking. I'd be happy to move you to a quieter room on the other side of the building, if you wish.
Let me check. As it turns out, we have a garden-view room available on the seventh floor, and it's well away from the renovation. I'd be grateful if you could give me ten minutes to have it prepared.
I understand completely. I'd like to offer you a free breakfast for the remainder of your stay, and I'll speak to the manager about a discount on tonight's rate. Would that be acceptable?

Of course. I'll have the manager send you a confirmation by email, as soon as she's approved it. As it turns out, she's still in the building, so I should be able to get a decision within half an hour.
Thank you for your patience. A porter will help you with your luggage, and I'll bring your new key personally. Once again, my sincere apologies, and I hope you have a restful night in your new room.

scenarios.scenario: Arranging a late check-out and asking about facilities
scenarios.context: A guest asks the receptionist about late check-out, luggage storage, the spa and an invoice before an evening flight.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I wonder if you could tell me what time check-out is, and whether there's any possibility of a late departure. My flight doesn't leave until the evening, and I'd rather not wander around with my luggage.

Not yet. I was going to ask whether the hotel could arrange one, and what it would cost. I'd also like to know whether there's a place to store my bags after check-out, in the event that I decide to go sightseeing.

That's fine. To be honest, I'd also like to know whether the spa is open in the morning. I wonder if I could use it before I leave, provided it isn't too crowded, since I've had a rather exhausting week.
Splendid. On the other hand, I'm not sure whether I'll have enough time to eat breakfast beforehand. Could you tell me whether the restaurant serves a continental option, in case I'm in a hurry?

That would be perfect. I wonder if I could ask one more thing. Could you tell me whether the hotel offers an invoice for business expenses? I'd need it for my company, and I'd like to know whether it can be sent by email.
Wonderful. Then I think that covers everything. Thank you for being so accommodating. I wonder whether I might also have a wake-up call at seven, in case my alarm fails me.

speakerB.en: Good morning. Check-out is at eleven, but I could certainly arrange a late departure until two, provided that the room isn't needed. Could I ask whether you've booked a taxi to the airport, in case you need one?

Certainly. We can store your luggage free of charge, as long as it's collected by closing time, which is ten o'clock. As for the taxi, I'd be happy to book one, though I can't tell you the exact price until we've confirmed the pickup.
The spa opens at eight, and it's usually quiet on weekday mornings. I can tell you that guests may use it free of charge until check-out, as long as they book a time slot at least an hour in advance.
It does, and it's available from six-thirty. In the event that you're short of time, we can also prepare a breakfast box for you to take away, provided you let us know by tomorrow evening.
Of course. We can issue a full invoice with the company's details, as long as you provide them at check-out. In case you forget, I'll note it on your reservation so that nothing is overlooked.
Certainly, I'll arrange it right away. Have a pleasant evening, and please don't hesitate to call reception if you need anything else. We'll make sure everything is ready for your departure tomorrow.

scenarios.scenario: Disputing an unexpected charge on the final bill
scenarios.context: A guest notices charges she does not recognize while checking out and speaks to the front desk manager.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm checking out of room 412, and there are a couple of charges on my bill that I don't recognize. To be honest, I was under the impression that breakfast was included in my rate. Could you take a look at it with me?

There's a fee of forty dollars for the minibar, and I haven't touched it. Had I known about the breakfast change, I'd have eaten at the café next door. I'd say a hotel should mention it, whatever the small print says.

Only the housekeeper, as far as I know. I was out at a conference from eight until late every day. I wouldn't mind paying if I'd used it, but I'd rather not pay for something I didn't. Whatever the explanation, I'd like it corrected.

The minibar refund on my card is fine, of course. For the breakfast, I'd say a credit is worth it, since I travel here for work quite often, provided that it doesn't expire too quickly. How long would it be valid?

To be honest, it was excellent apart from this. The room was quiet and the staff were helpful. Whatever else happens, I'll still recommend the hotel to my colleagues. I just wish the billing were clearer, since mistakes like this make guests lose trust.

Email would be perfect, thank you. I've got a taxi waiting, so I'd appreciate it if we could finish up quickly. As far as I'm concerned, you've handled this very professionally. I'll book again as long as the rate stays reasonable.

speakerB.en: Certainly, madam. Let me pull up the booking. It appears that breakfast was included on the first two nights only, since the promotional rate expired on Thursday. Which other charges are you concerned about?

I understand your frustration. Regarding the minibar, our system registers an item when the sensor detects it's been moved. Provided that you didn't open it, we can remove the charge. Did anyone else have access to the room during your stay?

That's perfectly reasonable. I'll refund the minibar charge to your card now. As for the breakfast, the booking confirmation says it was included for the full stay, so the mistake is ours. Would you prefer a refund for that part as well, or a credit toward a future stay?

Twelve months from today. Whichever you choose, I'll note it on your profile so there are no surprises. Had we caught the error earlier, we'd have corrected it at check-in. May I ask whether the rest of your stay was satisfactory?

Thank you, that means a lot, and your feedback is fair. We're reviewing our billing process, and I'll pass your comments to the manager. Should you decide on the credit, I can have it emailed to you within the hour. Which would be more convenient?

Of course. The refund and the credit are both processed, and you'll receive the confirmation shortly. Had I realized you were in a hurry, I'd have started with the receipt. Safe travels, and we look forward to welcoming you back.

scenarios.scenario: Booking a small conference room and catering for a workshop
scenarios.context: A project coordinator discusses room hire, equipment and catering for a two-day workshop with the hotel's events manager.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I'm organizing a two-day workshop for about thirty people next month, and I'd like to know what your conference rooms can offer. To be honest, my biggest concern is that the room be quiet, since we'll be running group discussions. What do you recommend?

A horseshoe would be ideal, so that everyone can see each other. We'll also need a projector, two microphones and reliable Wi-Fi. It's essential that the connection not drop, in case we run an online session on the second day. How stable is your network?

That sounds sensible. Now, as for catering, I'd like coffee in the morning and a proper lunch, although I'm wary of anything too heavy, since people get sleepy in the afternoon. As far as I'm concerned, a light lunch keeps the energy up. What do you offer?

Yes, three vegetarians and one guest with a nut allergy. It's vital that the kitchen be informed in advance, in case of any cross-contamination. I'd also like to know what happens if the numbers change, since two people may drop out.
That's fair. I'd like a total price covering room hire, equipment and two days of catering. I'd also hope for a discount, since we're booking two full days. I'd say that's reasonable, isn't it?

Please do. I'll need to run it by my manager, but I'm fairly confident she'll agree. It's essential that she see the figures today, in case another group is interested. Thank you for being so helpful and transparent about the costs.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon, and thank you for considering us. I'd say the Garden Suite is your best option, as it's on the ground floor, away from the lobby. It holds up to forty people. Would you prefer a classroom layout or a horseshoe arrangement, and what equipment will you need?

It's very stable, and we have a technician on call all day. Should anything go wrong, he can reach the room within two minutes. On the other hand, the microphones are an extra fifty dollars per day. I'd suggest that we test everything the evening before. Would that suit you?

We offer a buffet with salads, grilled fish and vegetarian options, plus fruit and coffee in the afternoon. In my experience, groups like to eat in a separate room so as to stretch their legs. Should we reserve the terrace for lunch, weather permitting? Do any guests have dietary restrictions?

Allergies are taken very seriously here, so I'll flag it with the chef today. If the numbers change, you may adjust them up to forty-eight hours before the event without any charge. After that, we'd charge for the confirmed number. Is that acceptable?

It is, and I can offer ten percent off the room hire, provided that you confirm by Friday. The total comes to just under four thousand dollars. I'd recommend that you pay a deposit of twenty percent, so as to secure the dates. Shall I send you the full quotation by email?

My pleasure. I'll send the quotation within the hour, and I'll hold the Garden Suite until Friday at no charge. Should you have any further questions, don't hesitate to call me directly. We'd be delighted to host your workshop.

scenarios.scenario: Talking about symptoms and seeing a doctor
scenarios.context: Feeling unwell and going to the pharmacy or doctor.

speakerA.en: I'm sick.
I have a headache.
I want to see a doctor.
Thank you for your help.
I don't feel well today. I think I'm coming down with something.
speakerA.fa: امروز حالم خوب نیست. فکر کنم دارم مریض می‌شم.

speakerA.en: I have a headache and a sore throat.
speakerA.fa: سردرد و گلودرد دارم.

speakerA.en: I need to see a doctor. Is there a clinic nearby?
speakerA.fa: باید دکتر ببینم. درمانگاهی نزدیک اینجا هست؟

speakerA.en: Do you have anything for a cough and fever?
speakerA.fa: برای سرفه و تب چیزی دارید؟

speakerA.en: I've been feeling nauseous all morning.
speakerA.fa: تمام صبح حالم به هم خورده.

speakerA.en: I think I might have an allergic reaction to something I ate.
speakerA.fa: فکر کنم به چیزی که خوردم واکنش آلرژیک دارم.

speakerA.en: I need to make an appointment with Dr. Johnson for this afternoon.
speakerA.fa: باید برای امروز بعد از ظهر با دکتر جانسون وقت بگیرم.

speakerA.en: Okay, I'll take the earliest slot tomorrow, please.
Yes, please. I don't want to go alone.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry. What's wrong?
Take some medicine and rest.
OK. I'll call the clinic.
You're welcome. Get well soon!
You look pale. You should lie down and rest.
speakerB.fa: رنگت پریده. باید دراز بکشی و استراحت کنی.

speakerB.en: That sounds awful. How long have you had these symptoms?
speakerB.fa: وحشتناک به نظر میاد. این علائم رو چند وقته دارید؟

speakerB.en: Yes, there's a walk-in clinic just two blocks away.
speakerB.fa: بله، یه درمانگاه بدون نوبت فقط دو خیابون اونورتره.

speakerB.en: I recommend this syrup for the cough and these tablets for fever.
speakerB.fa: این شربت رو برای سرفه و این قرص‌ها رو برای تب توصیه می‌کنم.

speakerB.en: Have you tried drinking ginger tea? It helps with nausea.
speakerB.fa: چای زنجبیل رو امتحان کردید؟ به حالت تهوع کمک می‌کنه.

speakerB.en: Stay calm. I'll call an ambulance if it gets worse.
speakerB.fa: آروم باش. اگه بدتر شد آمبولانس می‌گیرم.

speakerB.en: He is fully booked today. The earliest slot is tomorrow morning at 10.
speakerB.fa: امروز کاملاً پر است. اولین نوبت موجود فردا صبح ساعت ۱۰ هست.

speakerB.en: Do you want me to go with you? I'm free this afternoon.
OK. Take some water with you, and let's go.

scenarios.scenario: Feeling sick
scenarios.context: A person tells a friend that they feel sick.

speakerA.en: I don't feel well.
I have a cold.
Yes, a little.
OK. I'll drink hot tea.
You don't look well. What's the matter?
Did you eat something strange?
You should go home and rest.
Drink some water, and call me later.

speakerB.en: What's wrong?
Do you have a fever?
Go home and rest.
Good idea. Feel better soon!
I feel dizzy and I have a stomachache.
Maybe the fish at lunch. I'm not sure.
I think so. I'll tell my boss.
Thanks. You're a good friend.

scenarios.scenario: At the clinic reception
scenarios.context: A patient arrives at the clinic and talks to the receptionist.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want to see the doctor.
Yes. My name is Tom Lee.
How long do I wait?
Thank you.
Hello. I have an appointment at ten thirty.
It's Laura Green. I'm here to see Dr. Adams.
Do I need to pay now?
How long do I have to wait?

speakerB.en: Do you have an appointment?
OK. Please sit down.
About ten minutes.
You're welcome.
What's your name, please?
Please fill out this form and take a seat.
No, you can pay after the visit.
The doctor will see you in about fifteen minutes.

scenarios.scenario: At the doctor's office
scenarios.context: A patient talks to the doctor.

speakerA.en: Hello, doctor.
My stomach hurts.
Is it serious?
Thank you, doctor.
What seems to be the problem?
Do you have a cough or a sore throat?
Take this medicine twice a day after meals.
For five days. Drink a lot of water and rest.

speakerB.en: Hello. What's the problem?
Did you eat something bad?
No, it isn't. You need rest.
Drink a lot of water.
I've had a fever since yesterday.
I have a cough, and my body hurts.
How long should I take it?
Thank you, doctor. Should I come back?

scenarios.scenario: At the pharmacy
scenarios.context: A customer buys medicine at a pharmacy.

speakerA.en: I need some medicine.
I have a headache.
Is it expensive?
OK. I'll take it.
Good afternoon. Can I help you?
Try these tablets. Please read the instructions on the box.
No, you can buy them without one.
They're $6. Please follow the instructions carefully.

speakerB.en: What's the problem?
Take this pill two times a day.
No. It's five dollars.
Here you are. Feel better!
Yes, I need something for a headache.
Do I need a prescription for them?
OK. How much are they?
I understand. Thank you for your advice.

scenarios.scenario: A toothache
scenarios.context: A patient goes to the dentist.

speakerA.en: My tooth hurts.
It hurts a lot.
Is it bad?
Thank you.
Good morning. What can I do for you?
Let me look. Open your mouth, please.
You have a small hole in this tooth.
Yes. It will take half an hour, and you won't feel pain.

speakerB.en: Sit here, please.
Open your mouth, please.
No, it isn't. I can help you.
Don't eat for one hour.
I have a toothache. It hurts when I eat.
Is it a serious problem?
Do you need to fix it today?
That's a relief. Thank you, doctor.

scenarios.scenario: Healthy habits
scenarios.context: Two friends talk about staying healthy.

speakerA.en: Do you eat fruit every day?
Do you drink water?
Do you sleep well?
You are very healthy!
You look fit. Do you exercise a lot?
I should start exercising too. Where do you run?
What about food? Do you eat healthy?
How many hours do you sleep?

speakerB.en: Yes, I do. I like apples.
Yes. I drink eight glasses a day.
Yes. I sleep eight hours every night.
Thank you. Health is important.
I run three times a week and I swim on Sundays.
In the park near my house. Come with me!
I try. I eat a lot of vegetables and little sugar.
About eight hours. Sleep is very important.

scenarios.scenario: Describing symptoms to a doctor
scenarios.context: A patient explains his symptoms during an appointment.

speakerA.en: What seems to be the problem today?
Have you had a fever, or any trouble breathing?
Let me take a look at your throat. It's a little red, but nothing serious.
It looks like a viral infection, so antibiotics won't help. Rest and plenty of fluids are best.

speakerB.en: I've had a headache and a sore throat for about four days, and I feel very tired.
I had a slight fever on the first night, but it's gone now.
Do you think I need antibiotics? I have an important trip next week.
All right. If I don't feel better in a few days, should I come back?

scenarios.scenario: Getting advice about a healthy lifestyle
scenarios.context: A patient asks the doctor how to improve his health.

speakerA.en: Your test results are mostly fine, but your cholesterol is a bit high.
Yes, a healthier diet and more exercise would make a big difference.
Walking for thirty minutes a day is a good start. You could also take the stairs at work.
Try to eat less fried and processed food, and more vegetables, fish, and whole grains.

speakerB.en: That's worrying. Is there something I can do to bring it down?
I sit at a desk all day, so I rarely move. What kind of exercise would you suggest?
That seems manageable. Should I avoid certain foods completely?
I'll start this week. Should I come back for another test in a few months?

scenarios.scenario: Picking up a prescription at the pharmacy
scenarios.context: A customer asks the pharmacist about her medicine.

speakerA.en: Hello, I have a prescription from Dr. Lopez. Could you prepare it for me, please?
Here you are. Could you explain how often I should take the tablets?
Are there any side effects I should know about?
That's good to know. Can I take it together with my usual vitamins?

speakerB.en: Of course. Could I see some ID? It will take about ten minutes.
Take one tablet in the morning and one in the evening, preferably with food.
Some people feel a little sleepy, so I'd avoid driving until you know how it affects you.
Yes, that's fine. If you notice a rash or any other unusual symptoms, contact your doctor.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing treatment options with a specialist
scenarios.context: A patient consults a specialist about a recurring back problem.

speakerA.en: Having reviewed your scans, I don't think surgery is necessary at this stage.
A structured course of physiotherapy, combined with changes to your posture and daily habits.
Not at all. Prolonged sitting is one of the main contributors to chronic back pain.
Typically, six to eight weeks, although it varies from patient to patient.

speakerB.en: That's a relief. I was bracing myself for the worst. What would you recommend instead?
I spend most of the day at a desk, so I suppose that hasn't helped.
How long before I notice an improvement, assuming I follow your advice faithfully?
I'll commit to it. If the pain persists after that, would you reconsider other options?

scenarios.scenario: Getting a second opinion
scenarios.context: A patient explains why he sought another doctor's view.

speakerA.en: I'd like to hear your thoughts on the diagnosis I was given last month.
He suggested the headaches were caused by stress, but they've persisted despite my taking time off.
Such as what? I'd rather know the full range of possibilities, however unlikely.
I'd welcome that. I've been anxious that something was being overlooked.

speakerB.en: Certainly. Could you tell me what your previous doctor concluded, and on what grounds?
Stress can certainly play a role, but I'd want to rule out other causes first.
Eyesight problems, sleep disorders, or even high blood pressure. A few simple tests should clarify matters.
It's wise to ask questions. Let's start with the blood pressure test and take it from there.

scenarios.scenario: Talking about mental health with a doctor
scenarios.context: A patient opens up about feeling constantly overwhelmed.

speakerA.en: I haven't been sleeping properly for months, and I can't seem to concentrate at work.
My workload has doubled, and I've been caring for my father in the evenings as well.
I don't want to appear weak. Everyone else seems to cope with the same pressures.
What would you suggest I do? I can't simply stop working.

speakerB.en: I'm glad you've come to talk about it. Has anything changed in your life recently?
That's a considerable burden for anyone. It isn't surprising that you're feeling worn down.
Seeking help is a sign of good judgment, not weakness. Many people struggle quietly for far too long.
We could begin with some practical strategies and, if you're open to it, a referral to a counselor.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing test results
scenarios.context: A doctor explains slightly abnormal blood test results and outlines the next steps.

speakerA.en: Thank you for coming in. I have your test results, and there are a few things I'd like to go over with you.
Nothing alarming, but your cholesterol and blood sugar are both higher than I'd like. Left unaddressed, they could lead to complications down the line.
Not necessarily. I'd prefer to start with changes to your diet and exercise, and then retest in three months to see how you respond.
Cut back on processed foods and sugary drinks, and aim for thirty minutes of brisk walking most days. I'll give you a leaflet with practical guidance.

speakerB.en: I've been anxious since I got your message. Is it something serious?
I suppose I haven't been looking after myself as well as I should. Will I need medication?
That seems manageable. Is there anything specific I should avoid in the meantime?
Thank you. I'll make an honest effort. It's a relief to hear it's not more serious.

scenarios.scenario: Giving informed consent for a procedure
scenarios.context: A surgeon explains the risks and benefits of an operation before the patient decides.

speakerA.en: Before you sign the consent form, I want to be sure you understand both the benefits and the risks of the operation.
The procedure has a high success rate and should relieve most of your pain. As with any surgery, there's a small risk of infection and, rarely, nerve damage.
Serious complications occur in fewer than two percent of cases. Many patients regain full mobility within three months.
That's a legitimate option. The condition may not worsen quickly, but delay could limit what we can achieve later. The choice is yours, and I'll support whichever you make.

speakerB.en: I'd appreciate that. I've read the leaflet, but I'd rather hear it from you.
How small is small? I'd like to know what I'm weighing against the discomfort I'm living with now.
That's more reassuring than I'd expected. What happens if I decide to wait and see?
Then I'd like a few days to think it over, if that's acceptable. I'd rather decide with a clear head.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing a relative's discharge with a nurse
scenarios.context: A daughter asks a nurse how her father will be cared for after he leaves the hospital.

speakerA.en: I wanted to ask about my father's discharge. I'm concerned about how he'll manage at home, given that he lives alone.
I can stay with him for a week, but I can't be there indefinitely. Are there services that could help?
And what warning signs should I be looking out for once he's home?
That's very helpful. I'm trying to remain calm, but it's difficult seeing him so frail.

speakerB.en: That's a very sensible question. His recovery is going well, but he'll need support for the first few weeks, particularly with mobility and medication.
Yes. Our discharge coordinator can arrange a home care visit and a physiotherapist. I'd recommend speaking with her before he leaves.
A fever, increased swelling around the wound, or sudden confusion should prompt an immediate call. I'll write down the number for you.
That's entirely natural. Please remember to look after yourself too, since he'll need you at your best.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing treatment options and weighing risks
scenarios.context: A patient and a physician consider two courses of action for a persistent condition.

speakerA.en: I've read about both approaches, but I'd value your opinion on which is more appropriate in my circumstances.
What are the chances that the medication alone would resolve the problem, and how would we know if it wasn't working?
And if I opt for surgery, what would the downtime realistically be? I'd need to make arrangements at work.
I think I'd like to start with the medication and keep surgery in reserve. Does that strike you as a sensible compromise?

speakerB.en: The medication is less invasive, but it requires long-term commitment and carries a risk of side effects. Surgery is definitive, yet it entails a longer recovery.
In roughly sixty percent of cases it suffices. We'd review your progress in three months and reconsider if there was no meaningful improvement.
Expect about six weeks before you're fully functional, though most patients return to light duties sooner.
It's a reasonable and conservative approach, and it keeps your options open. I'll prescribe it today and book a follow-up.

scenarios.scenario: Requesting a second opinion diplomatically
scenarios.context: A patient wishes to consult another specialist without offending the first.

speakerA.en: Doctor, I appreciate the thoroughness of your assessment, but given the gravity of the diagnosis, I'd like to seek a second opinion.
I'm relieved to hear you say so. I was concerned that it might be interpreted as a lack of confidence in your judgment.
Would you be willing to forward my records and imaging, so that the other specialist has the full picture?
That's extremely helpful. Might you also recommend someone whose opinion you would trust?

speakerB.en: I'd think less of you if you didn't. It's a perfectly reasonable step, and I'd encourage it for any significant decision.
Not remotely. Medicine involves uncertainty, and a fresh perspective can only improve the quality of the decision.
Of course. I'll send everything this afternoon, and I'm happy to speak with my colleague directly if it would be useful.
I would suggest Dr. Hallam at the university hospital. She's rigorous, and she isn't afraid to disagree with her peers.

scenarios.scenario: Explaining persistent symptoms that are hard to describe
scenarios.context: A patient struggles to articulate a vague but troubling complaint.

speakerA.en: It's difficult to put into words. It isn't quite pain, more a sort of heaviness that comes and goes without any obvious trigger.
About two months ago, and it seems worse in the late afternoon, particularly after a stressful day at work.
My sleep has been fitful, and I've been more irritable than usual, though I'd attributed that to the workload.
I'd welcome that. It's strangely reassuring to hear that vague complaints aren't dismissed out of hand.

speakerB.en: That's perfectly all right. Let's approach it from a different angle. When did you first notice it, and does it vary with the time of day?
Does it affect your sleep or your appetite, or have you noticed any other changes, however minor they may seem?
Quite possibly, but the body and mind are rarely separable. I'd like to run some blood tests to rule out anything physical.
They never should be. Often the vaguest symptoms are the body's way of asking for attention before something more definite arises.

scenarios.scenario: Visiting a friend in the hospital
scenarios.context: A man visits his friend in the hospital.

speakerA.en: Hi, Ali. How are you feeling?
I brought you some fruit.
Do you need anything?
I'll bring one tomorrow. Get well soon!

speakerB.en: I'm better, thank you. I'm happy to see you.
That's very kind of you.
Maybe a book. I'm bored.
Thank you. See you tomorrow.

scenarios.scenario: Booking a check-up at the hospital
scenarios.context: A patient books a check-up at the hospital desk.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want to see a doctor for a check-up.
No, I don't. Can I make one?
Yes, that's fine.
My name is Hassan Karimi. Thank you.

speakerB.en: Do you have an appointment?
