I have playlists for driving, cooking, and studying, and each of them has a different atmosphere. It saves a lot of time.
Sure. I have a calming list for sleeping that might help you, as long as you don't mind a lot of rain sounds.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing the role of music in shaping identity
scenarios.context: Two friends talk about how music influences who we are.

speakerA.en: I was thinking last night about how much of my identity is connected to the music I listened to as a teenager. Certain songs can bring back entire periods of my life in an instant.
I suppose that's because those years are so formative. We're discovering who we are, and the music becomes part of that process. It's almost like a soundtrack to our personal development.
I've noticed that people often judge others by their musical tastes, which is rather superficial. Someone's favorite band says very little about their character or values.
That's true, though music communities can create a strong sense of belonging. When I went to my first concert, I felt that I was surrounded by people who understood me without having to say anything.
I wonder whether streaming has changed that. With everything available at any time, people may not develop such strong attachments to particular artists or genres.
Perhaps. Either way, I think music remains one of the most powerful ways of connecting with other people, regardless of age or background.

speakerB.en: That's a powerful thing about music. A few notes can transport you instantly, even if you haven't thought about the song for twenty years. Memory and emotion are closely linked.
Exactly. Psychologists have found that the songs we hear between the ages of fourteen and twenty-four have a special significance throughout our lives, which would explain why they remain so vivid.
I agree. Taste is shaped by so many factors, such as family, friends, and chance, that it can't be a reliable indicator of personality. Still, people can't resist making assumptions.
That sense of belonging is real. Subcultures built around music have given many young people a sense of identity and community when they felt isolated from the mainstream.
It's an interesting question. The abundance of choice may reduce the intensity of attachment, though it also allows people to discover music they would never have encountered otherwise.
Well said. Whatever the format or the genre, music reminds us that we share the same emotions, and that is something that no technology can change.

scenarios.scenario: Evaluating the pros and cons of learning an instrument late
scenarios.context: Two adults discuss starting a musical instrument later in life.

speakerA.en: I've always wanted to learn the piano, but I'm forty-five, and I keep telling myself that it's too late. Children seem to pick up everything so quickly, and I'm afraid of making a fool of myself.
That's reassuring, but I worry about the time. Between work and family, I'd hardly have an hour a week to practice, and I doubt that would be enough to make any real progress.
I hadn't thought of it that way. Perhaps the key is to set realistic goals, such as learning to play a few pieces that I love, rather than aiming for professional standards.
Do you think it's better to take lessons with a teacher, or to try to learn by myself using online videos? I like the flexibility of the latter, but I'm afraid I'd develop bad habits.
That seems sensible. I'll arrange a trial lesson, and see whether I get along with the teacher. If I don't enjoy it, I can always reconsider.
Thank you for the encouragement. If I'd listened to my own doubts, I'd never have started, and I'd have regretted it for the rest of my life.

speakerB.en: It's never too late. Adults actually have certain advantages. They're more disciplined, they understand the value of practice, and they can set their own goals without being forced by parents.
Quality matters more than quantity. Fifteen minutes a day will produce better results than a single long session each week, because regular repetition is the key to developing muscle memory.
That's the right attitude. Many adult learners find that the process itself is the reward. The pleasure comes from improving, not from performing for an audience.
I'd recommend at least a few lessons with a teacher, particularly at the beginning, to establish the correct posture and technique. After that, online resources can be a useful supplement.
That's a good plan. Be patient, and remember that the first few weeks are always the most frustrating. Once you can play something recognizable, your motivation will rise considerably.
Exactly. And who knows? In a year, you might be playing at family gatherings, and everyone will be amazed that you started so late.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing a disappointing concert experience
scenarios.context: Two friends discuss problems at a concert and what could be improved.

speakerA.en: I've been looking forward to that concert for months, but I have to say that it was a disappointment. The music was excellent, but the organization was a disaster from start to finish.
We waited for an hour and a half in the queue, and when we finally got in, the best places were already taken. We ended up standing behind a pillar, from which I could barely see the stage.

And the sound was terrible, wasn't it? During the first few songs, the vocals were almost inaudible, and by the time they fixed it, half of the set was over. I don't understand how that can happen at a venue of that size.

I agree, and the prices were outrageous. I paid eight euros for a small beer, and the ticket was already expensive. It seems that organizers think that fans will pay anything to see their favorite band.
Perhaps we should have gone to a smaller venue, where the atmosphere is more intimate. I've often found that I enjoy concerts in small clubs far more than in big arenas.
Next time, let's look out for the less famous bands. They're often just as good, and you get to hear them in much better conditions.

speakerB.en: I was feeling the same way. Seeing them live was a dream, but the experience was spoiled by so many practical issues. It seems that nobody planned how to manage such a large crowd.

It was ridiculous. If the doors had opened earlier, or if they'd used more than one entrance, it wouldn't have been so chaotic. I'd read about similar problems at the same venue last year, so I should have been prepared.
I thought the same. The sound engineer clearly didn't do a proper check, and it's the performers who suffer, because the audience blames them. They deserved better, and so did we.

It's become the norm, unfortunately. The cost of a night out has risen enormously. If everyone refused to pay such prices, the organizers might change their policies, but there's always someone willing to pay.
I'd like that. Last year, I saw a local band in a tiny bar, and it was one of the best evenings of my life. The musicians were right in front of me, and I could really feel the music.
That's a good idea. And it's also a way of supporting musicians who need it. Let's check the listings for next month, and choose something together.

scenarios.scenario: Auditioning for a choir
scenarios.context: A candidate speaks with a choir director about experience, expectations and commitment.

speakerA.en: Good evening. I saw your announcement about auditions for the community choir, and I'd like to apply. I haven't sung in a group since school, so I'm a little nervous, but I've always enjoyed it.
I'd say that I have a decent ear, and I can read music at a basic level. I took piano lessons as a child, which helped me to understand the notation, though I'm certainly out of practice.
I think I'm a tenor, although I sometimes have difficulty with the highest notes. I'd be happy to sing whatever you'd like me to, as long as it isn't too demanding for a first audition.

Thank you. I'll sing the piece that I prepared, but could I ask about the time commitment? I have a full-time job, and I'd like to know how often the choir rehearses, and how much practice is expected at home.
That's manageable. And are there any performances planned? I'd love to take part in concerts, but I wouldn't want to promise something that I can't deliver.
I'm very much looking forward to it. Whatever the outcome, thank you for giving me the opportunity to try.

speakerB.en: Good evening, and welcome. We're always glad to see new faces. Please don't be nervous. This isn't a competition, and we just want to find out where your voice fits best. Tell me about your musical background.
That's very useful. Many of our members have a similar background, and they've developed their skills in the choir. Reading music is an advantage, but we also help people to learn as they go along.

Let's start with some simple scales, and see what your range is. Then you can sing your prepared piece, and finally we'll try a short passage in a group. There's no need to worry about the high notes.

We rehearse every Wednesday evening from seven thirty until nine thirty, and I'd expect about thirty minutes of practice at home each week. Before concerts, we sometimes add an extra rehearsal on Saturday.

We have two concerts a year, one in December and one in June, as well as occasional performances at local events. Nobody is obliged to attend all of them, but we like to know in advance who's available.
Thank you for coming. I'll let you know our decision by the end of the week, but I can already say that I enjoyed hearing you, and I think you'd be a good addition to the section.

scenarios.scenario: Persuading a parent to support a career in music
scenarios.context: A young woman tries to explain to a worried parent why she wants to study music professionally instead of choosing a more secure career.

speakerA.en: Dad, I need to talk to you about my university plans. Having thought about it for a long time, I've decided to apply for music rather than economics. Given that you've always supported me, I hoped you'd listen.

Because it's the only thing that makes me happy. Having played the violin since I was seven, I can't imagine doing anything else. Given that I'm good at it, I'd like to see how far I can go. I'd say it's worth trying.

I'd teach, which is a respectable career. Provided that I finish the degree, I'd have plenty of options, in case performing doesn't work. Whatever happens, I'd rather try than wonder for the rest of my life. On the other hand, I know it's difficult.

I'd apply again the following year, and keep practicing meanwhile. Having talked to my teacher, I know that many students succeed on their second attempt. Given that she believes in me, I feel braver. Would you at least come to my audition?

That means everything to me, Dad. Having expected an argument, I'm quite surprised. Given that you were so worried, I didn't dare ask. Could we agree on a budget for lessons, as long as I also find some part-time work?
Thank you. Whatever the future holds, I'll work as hard as I can. Having your support makes it much easier, given that I was so nervous. Shall we go to a concert together next month, to celebrate?

speakerB.en: Of course I'll listen, although I'll be honest: I'm worried. Having worked in a bank for thirty years, I know how hard it is to earn a living in the arts. Bearing in mind your talent, why do you want to take such a risk?

I understand, but talent alone isn't enough. Provided that you work extremely hard, you might succeed, but many don't. Having seen friends' children struggle, I can't help worrying. What would you do if it didn't work out?

Teaching is more stable, I agree. Having heard you play, I can't deny you have something special. Given that the competition is fierce, though, you'd need a plan. Supposing you were rejected by every school, what then?

I'd be proud to. Provided that you don't give up your studies completely, I'd support a trial year. Having thought about it overnight, I realize that I might have been too negative. Whatever you decide, I'll be behind you.

That's a sensible suggestion. Provided that you look for part-time work, I'll help with the lessons. Bearing in mind how expensive instruments are, we should also consider renting. Having a plan will make me feel calmer, to be honest.

I'd love to. Provided that you choose the program, I'll bring your mother, who will be delighted. Having heard you tonight, I feel much more optimistic. Bearing in mind how hard you've worked, you deserve this chance.

scenarios.scenario: Debating whether streaming pays musicians fairly
scenarios.context: A musician and a music fan debate whether streaming services pay artists fairly.

speakerA.en: I've been thinking about how little I earn from streaming. Much as I love having my music online, it's not so much the exposure that matters as the income, and it's tiny. What I get for a thousand plays wouldn't buy a coffee.

It's complicated, to be honest. It's not so much the platform that keeps most of it as the labels and distributors. What I'd like is a system that pays artists directly, as long as it doesn't raise the subscription price too much.

I have, on social media, but it's not so much reaching them as persuading them that's the problem. What I find encouraging is that some listeners now buy albums directly. Much as it's a small group, they make a real difference.

It might, but it's worth it. Much as I dislike self-promotion, what matters is staying independent. It's not so much about getting rich as about covering my costs. What do other fans do, in your experience, to support their favorite bands?

That's an honest view. Much as I'd like it to change, I doubt it will soon. What I hope is that regulators will look at the numbers. It's not so much a question of morality as of simple fairness, as far as I'm concerned.
That's a good idea. It's not so much a complaint as an invitation to talk, so it could work. What I'd need is a few other artists to sign it. Much as I hate asking, it might be the best way forward.

speakerB.en: I'd say that's shocking, although I'm not sure who's to blame. What matters to me is that artists can live from their work. Do you know how the money is divided, or is it too complicated to explain?

Much as I'd pay more for that, many listeners wouldn't. What matters for them is convenience, not fairness. It's not so much that people don't care as that they don't know. Have you tried explaining it to your audience?

That makes sense. I buy your albums, partly because I want you to keep making music. What I'd suggest is selling something more personal, like signed copies. On the other hand, would that take too much of your time, in case you tour as well?

Many go to concerts, since that's where artists earn most. What matters is the live experience, and it's not so much the ticket price as the merchandise that helps. Much as I enjoy streaming, I never thought of it as a way to support anyone.

I agree, and some countries are already discussing it. What matters is public pressure, so you should speak out. Much as it may feel awkward, listeners respond to honesty. Would you consider writing an open letter, perhaps with other musicians?

I'd help you write it, if you like. What matters is a clear message and real numbers. Much as it will take time, I'd say it's worth it. Let's meet on Sunday and draft it together, in case you lose your nerve.

scenarios.scenario: At the bank - opening an account or asking about services
scenarios.context: A person visits the bank to do some financial business.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want to open a bank account.
Yes, here it is.
Is there a monthly fee?
When can I get my card?
I'd like to open a new bank account.
speakerA.fa: می‌خوام یه حساب بانکی جدید باز کنم.

speakerA.en: What documents do I need to open an account?
speakerA.fa: برای افتتاح حساب به چه مدارکی نیاز دارم؟

speakerA.en: Can I transfer money to an international account from here?
speakerA.fa: می‌تونم از اینجا به یه حساب بین‌المللی پول انتقال بدم؟

speakerA.en: What are the fees for a savings account?
speakerA.fa: هزینه‌های حساب پس‌انداز چقدر است؟

speakerA.en: I'd like to withdraw some cash from my account, please.
speakerA.fa: می‌خوام از حسابم پول نقد برداشت کنم، لطفاً.

speakerA.en: Could you please help me update my contact details? I've changed my address.
speakerA.fa: میشه لطفاً کمک کنید اطلاعات تماسم رو به‌روز کنم؟ آدرسم عوض شده.

speakerA.en: I've noticed an unauthorized transaction on my account. I need to report it.
speakerA.fa: یه تراکنش غیرمجاز توی حسابم دیدم. باید گزارشش کنم.

speakerB.en: Welcome. Do you have your ID?
Thank you. Please fill in this form.
No, there is no fee for this account.
You can get it in one week.
Of course. Please fill out this application form.
speakerB.fa: حتماً. لطفاً این فرم درخواست رو پر کنید.

speakerB.en: You'll need a valid ID, proof of address, and a passport photo.
speakerB.fa: به کارت شناسایی معتبر، مدرک آدرس و یه عکس پاسپورتی نیاز دارید.

speakerB.en: Yes, but there might be some charges. Let me explain the exchange rates.
speakerB.fa: بله، اما ممکنه کارمزد داشته باشه. بذارید نرخ ارز رو توضیح بدم.

speakerB.en: There are no monthly fees if you maintain a minimum balance.
speakerB.fa: اگه حداقل موجودی رو نگه دارید، هزینه ماهیانه نداره.

speakerB.en: How much would you like to withdraw?
speakerB.fa: چقدر می‌خواید برداشت کنید؟

speakerB.en: Sure, I'll update that in our system. It'll take just a moment.
speakerB.fa: حتماً، اون رو توی سیستم به‌روز می‌کنم. یه لحظه بیشتر طول نمی‌کشه.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. I'll block your card right now and initiate an investigation.
speakerB.fa: از شنیدن این موضوع متأسفم. همون الان کارتتون رو مسدود و تحقیقات رو شروع می‌کنم.

scenarios.scenario: Withdrawing money at the counter
scenarios.context: A customer takes money out of their account at the bank counter.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I want to take out some money.
I want two hundred dollars.
Yes, here is my card.
OK. Can I have a receipt?
Is there a limit on how much I can withdraw today?
Could I have the money in twenty-dollar bills?
Could you check my balance, please?
Are there any withdrawal fees?

speakerB.en: Good morning. How much do you want?
OK. Do you have your bank card?
Thank you. Please type your PIN.
Yes. Here is your money and your receipt.
Yes, the daily limit is one thousand dollars.
Certainly. I'll count it for you.
Of course. You have two thousand three hundred dollars.
There's no fee at our branches, but ATMs of other banks charge two dollars.

scenarios.scenario: Depositing money
scenarios.context: A customer puts money into their account.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. I want to put money in my account.
It's five hundred dollars.
My account number is 4 5 6 7 8 9.
Here you are. Can I have a receipt?
Can I deposit this check into my savings account?
How long will it take for the money to appear?
Can I also deposit coins?
Could you print my updated balance?

speakerB.en: Sure. How much money is it?
OK. What is your account number?
Thank you. Please give me the money.
Of course. Here you are.
Yes, please sign it on the back.
A check usually takes two to three business days.
Yes, but you need to use the coin machine over there.
Sure. Here is your statement.

scenarios.scenario: Using an ATM
scenarios.context: A person asks for help at an ATM outside the bank.

speakerA.en: Excuse me. Is there an ATM near here?
How do I use it?
Oh no! The ATM has my card.
Thank you very much.
The machine says 'insufficient funds'. What does that mean?
I forgot my PIN. What can I do?
The ATM isn't giving me my card back. What should I do?
Is it safe to use the ATM at night?

speakerB.en: Yes, there is one outside the bank.
Put your card in. Then type your PIN.
Don't worry. I'll call the bank.
You're welcome. Please wait here.
It means there isn't enough money in your account.
You can reset it at the bank or through the mobile app.
Don't leave. Press 'cancel' and call the number on the screen.
Use one inside a bank, and cover the keypad when you type.

scenarios.scenario: Losing a bank card
scenarios.context: A customer reports a lost bank card.

speakerA.en: Hello. I lost my bank card.
My name is Sara Lee.
Please block my card.
Can I get a new card?
I think someone stole my wallet on the bus.
Have there been any suspicious transactions on my account?
Will I get my money back?
How can I use my account until the new card arrives?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. What is your name?
OK. Let me check your account.
Yes, I'll do it now.
Yes. It will come in five days.
I'm sorry. Let me block your card immediately.
Yes, there are two payments from this morning. We'll investigate them.
In most cases, yes. We'll send you a form to fill in.
You can use the mobile app or come to the branch with your ID.

scenarios.scenario: Changing money
scenarios.context: A traveler changes money at an exchange desk.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want to change money.
I have one hundred US dollars.
I want euros, please. What is the rate?
OK, that's fine.
Do you charge a commission for changing money?
Is the exchange rate better in the city center?
Could I change some of the euros back to dollars?
Could you give me some small bills? I need them for taxis.

speakerB.en: Sure. What money do you have?
What money do you want?
Today you get ninety-two euros.
Please sign here. Here is your money.
Yes, it's two percent of the amount.
It's usually similar, but airports often have worse rates.
Yes, if you have the receipt from the first exchange.
Of course. How many would you like?

scenarios.scenario: Transferring money
scenarios.context: A customer sends money to a family member.

speakerA.en: Hello. I want to send money to my sister.
Yes, she does.
Here it is. It's on this paper.
Three hundred dollars. How much is the fee?
How long does an international transfer take?
Can I send money from my phone instead?
Do you need her address or only her bank details?
Will I get a confirmation after the transfer?

speakerB.en: OK. Does she have a bank account?
What is her account number?
Thank you. How much money do you want to send?
The fee is five dollars. It takes one day.
Usually two to three working days.
Yes, you can use our mobile app. It's faster and cheaper.
We need her full name, her account number, and the bank's code.
Yes, we'll send it by text message and by email.

scenarios.scenario: Opening a bank account
scenarios.context: A customer talks to a bank employee about opening an account.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'd like to open a checking account, please.
Yes, here are my passport and a recent electricity bill.
Yes, and I'd like to use online banking as well. Is there a monthly fee?
That's fine. How long will it take to receive the card?

speakerB.en: Certainly. Do you have some form of identification and proof of address with you?
Thank you. Would you like a debit card with the account?
There's no fee as long as you deposit at least five hundred dollars each month.
About five working days. We'll mail it to your home address.

scenarios.scenario: Reporting a lost bank card
scenarios.context: A customer calls the bank after losing a card.

speakerA.en: Hello, I've lost my debit card, and I need to block it immediately.
Of course. It's Daniel Foster, and I was born on May 14, 1988.
No, but I last used it yesterday, so I'm worried someone might have found it.
That's a relief. How soon can I get a replacement?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you confirm your name and date of birth for security?
Thank you. I've blocked the card now. Have you noticed any unusual transactions?
I'll check the recent activity for you. There's nothing suspicious at the moment.
We'll send a new card within three to five days. In the meantime, you can use the mobile app.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about a loan
scenarios.context: A customer asks about borrowing money to buy a car.

speakerA.en: I'm thinking of buying a used car, and I'd like to ask about a personal loan.
About ten thousand dollars, and I'd like to repay it over three years.
I work as an engineer, and I've been with the same company for six years.
What would my monthly payments be, and is there a penalty for paying it off early?

speakerB.en: We offer loans for up to fifty thousand dollars. How much do you need to borrow?
The interest rate depends on your income and credit history. May I ask what you do for a living?
That's a good sign. With those details, the rate would probably be around six percent.
About three hundred dollars a month, and no, early repayment is free.

scenarios.scenario: Discussing mortgage options
scenarios.context: A couple meets a financial adviser to discuss buying their first home.

speakerA.en: We're hoping to buy a house within the next year. Could you outline the mortgage options available to us?
Which would you recommend, given that we'll be stretching our budget as it is?
How large a deposit would we need in order to qualify for a competitive rate?
We've managed to save about fifteen percent so far. Would it be wiser to wait until we reach twenty?

speakerB.en: Certainly. Broadly speaking, you can choose between a fixed rate, which stays constant, and a variable rate, which fluctuates with the market.
A fixed rate offers certainty, which many first-time buyers find reassuring, though you'd forfeit any benefit if rates fell.
The more you can put down, the better the terms. Ten percent is the minimum, but twenty would open up much better deals.
That depends on the property market. It's worth running the numbers both ways before deciding.

scenarios.scenario: Disputing a fraudulent transaction
scenarios.context: A customer reports an unauthorized payment to the bank's fraud department.

speakerA.en: I've just noticed a payment of nine hundred dollars on my account that I did not authorize.
I used it at a grocery store two days ago, and I have it right here in my wallet.
Will I get my money back? I can't afford to be without that sum for long.
That's a relief. In the meantime, how can I access my money for essential expenses?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. When did you last use your card, and is it still in your possession?
It's possible that the card details were copied. I'll freeze the card immediately and open an investigation.
In most cases of confirmed fraud, the funds are credited back within ten working days, pending our review.
We'll issue an emergency card, and you can collect it from any branch tomorrow.

scenarios.scenario: Understanding interest and inflation
scenarios.context: Two friends discuss how rising prices affect savings.

speakerA.en: My savings account pays two percent interest, but prices are rising by five percent. Am I actually losing money?
That's depressing. So what's the point of saving at all?
Such as property or shares? Neither of which I know much about.
I think I should educate myself properly before putting my money into anything.

speakerB.en: In real terms, yes. Your balance is growing, but its purchasing power is shrinking.
It's still prudent to keep an emergency fund. For longer-term savings, you need to look at assets that outpace inflation.
Exactly, and each carries risks. That's why diversification matters.
That's the wisest first step. Many banks offer free workshops for customers who want to learn the basics.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating a business loan
scenarios.context: An entrepreneur meets a bank manager to discuss financing for expanding her bakery.

speakerA.en: Thank you for seeing me. I'd like to apply for a loan to open a second location, and I've brought a business plan and three years of accounts.
Two hundred thousand over seven years. I'd put forward a quarter of that myself, which I hope demonstrates my commitment.
I've budgeted conservatively, and I'd expect the new branch to break even within eight months. I can also offer the equipment as collateral.
I could raise the deposit slightly if the rate dropped to five and a half. Would that be feasible?

speakerB.en: Impressive. Your figures are consistent, and the growth is encouraging. What sum are you hoping to borrow, and over what term?
It certainly does. My concern is the rent for the new premises, which is considerably higher than your current outgoings. How would you cover it during the first year?
That strengthens your application. Our standard rate would be six percent, though a larger deposit might allow me to negotiate something better.
I'll need approval from the credit committee, but I think the case is sound. I'll present it on Thursday and let you know by the end of the week.

scenarios.scenario: Escalating a dispute over unexplained account fees
scenarios.context: A customer insists on a thorough investigation after being charged fees she doesn't recognize.

speakerA.en: I've called twice about these monthly fees, and both times I was told they were standard. Yet nobody can tell me what they're for.
Which was when I was supposedly switched to a premium package I never requested. I'd like to see the signed agreement.
That's precisely my point. I haven't consented to anything, so I expect every fee to be refunded, with interest.
I'll hold, but if I'm not satisfied, I intend to file a formal complaint with the financial ombudsman.

speakerB.en: I apologize for the confusion. Let me look at the account. I can see a service charge of fifteen dollars applied every month since March.
I'm checking the records now. There doesn't appear to be a signed request, only an automated upgrade from a promotional offer.
I can certainly refund the fees, but I'd need a supervisor's approval to add interest. Would you be willing to hold?
That's your right, and I'll note it on the file. In the meantime, I'll ensure the fees are refunded and the package canceled today.

scenarios.scenario: Seeking advice on diversifying savings
scenarios.context: A client asks a financial adviser how to spread a modest inheritance across different assets.

speakerA.en: I recently received an inheritance, and all of it is sitting in a savings account. I know that isn't ideal, but I'm unsure what to do instead.
Mostly for retirement, which is about twenty years away. I'd like it to grow, but I can't stomach the idea of losing a large part of it.
What proportion would you recommend? I've heard people say you should hold your age in bonds, but I'm not sure that still applies.
That's reassuring. What about fees? I've read that high charges can quietly erode returns over time.

speakerB.en: It's wise to seek advice before acting. First, what are your goals? Is this money for retirement, a property, or a safety net?
With a twenty-year horizon, you can accept some volatility. I'd suggest a mix of low-cost index funds and bonds, with a portion kept as cash for emergencies.
It's a reasonable starting point, but not a rule. Your tolerance for risk matters more than a formula, and we should review the mix annually.
They can, which is why I'd favor low-cost funds. I'll provide a full breakdown of every charge, so there are no surprises.

scenarios.scenario: Disputing a fraudulent transaction with the bank
scenarios.context: A customer reports unauthorized charges and seeks recourse.

speakerA.en: I've discovered several transactions on my account that I didn't authorize, totaling nearly two thousand. I'd like to dispute them immediately.
Yesterday afternoon, at a pharmacy. I haven't lost the card, so I suspect my details were compromised.
Will the disputed sum be refunded in the interim? I have a mortgage payment due and can't afford to be short.
I'd like that confirmed in writing, and I'd appreciate a reference number so I can follow up.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. I'll freeze the card at once to prevent further charges. Could you confirm when you last used it?
That's a possibility. We'll investigate, and while we do so, I'll issue a new card with a different number.
In most cases, we provisionally credit the amount within a few working days while the inquiry is carried out.
Certainly. I'll email both within the hour, and I'd advise changing your online banking password as a precaution.

scenarios.scenario: Seeking advice on investing for the long term
scenarios.context: A client consults an adviser about managing risk and expectations.

speakerA.en: I've accumulated some savings, and I'd like to put them to work, but I confess I'm wary of the markets after the last downturn.
Probably not for fifteen years or more. It's intended to supplement my pension.
What about the risk of choosing poorly? I'd hate to see my savings eroded by a single bad decision.
That sounds prudent, if somewhat unexciting. Is there a place for more adventurous investments?

speakerB.en: That's entirely understandable. The first question is your time horizon. When do you anticipate needing the money?
That's a considerable advantage. Over such a period, short-term volatility matters far less than consistent contributions and diversification.
That's precisely why I'd advise against concentrating in individual stocks. A broad, low-cost fund spreads the risk and keeps fees modest.
A small allocation, perhaps, but I'd treat it as money you can afford to lose. The foundation should remain boring, because boring tends to endure.

scenarios.scenario: Negotiating better terms on a loan
scenarios.context: A borrower presses a lender to reconsider the interest rate in light of their record.

speakerA.en: I've been a customer for over fifteen years, with an unblemished repayment history, and I believe the rate you've offered doesn't reflect that.
I understand, but I've received a competing offer that's considerably lower. I'd prefer to stay, though I can't ignore the difference.
Certainly. It's seven-point-two percent fixed over ten years, against your eight-point-five.
Half a point is a start, but I'd hoped for more. Could we meet in the middle, and I'll commit to a longer term?

speakerB.en: I appreciate your loyalty, and I can see that your record is exemplary. The rate is determined partly by current market conditions, however.
Could you share the details of the competing offer? That would help me make a case to my superiors.
That's a significant gap. I can't promise to match it, but I may be able to offer a reduction of half a point, given your history.
Let me consult my manager. I think there's a reasonable prospect of reaching an agreement that suits us both.

scenarios.scenario: Comparing loan terms for home renovation
scenarios.context: A customer asks a bank employee about a personal loan.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I'd like some information about a personal loan.
About five thousand dollars to renovate my kitchen.
What would the monthly payments be if I repay it over two years?
Could I see the exact figures on paper before I decide?

speakerB.en: Of course. How much would you like to borrow, and for what purpose?
For that amount, the interest rate is around seven percent.
Roughly two hundred and twenty dollars, depending on your final rate.
Certainly. I'll print them out and explain each item.

scenarios.scenario: Disputing a charge on a card statement
scenarios.context: A customer reports an unknown payment on his statement.

speakerA.en: I've noticed a payment on my statement that I don't recognize.
It's a hundred and twenty dollars from an online store on the ninth.
No, I've only used the card in shops I know.
Will I get my money back?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Which payment are you referring to?
Have you shared your card details with anyone recently?
Then we'll block your card and open an investigation.
If the payment is confirmed as fraud, yes. It usually takes about ten days.

scenarios.scenario: Opening a savings account
scenarios.context: A customer asks a bank employee about different savings options.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'd like to open a savings account, but I'm not sure which kind would be best for me.
I'd like to save about two hundred euros a month. I don't need the money immediately, but I'd like to be able to take it out in an emergency.
That sounds reasonable. What's the interest rate on that account, and is there any fee for keeping it open?
That's not bad. Can I set up an automatic transfer from my current account, so that I don't have to remember it every month?
I'll do that. Are there any documents I need to bring, or can we do everything today?
Great. Here's my passport and my proof of address. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

speakerB.en: Good morning. Of course. Could you tell me how much you plan to save, and how long you'd like to leave the money in the account?
In that case, I'd recommend our flexible savings account. You can withdraw money whenever you like, and there are no penalties.
At the moment, it's two percent per year, and there are no monthly fees. If you keep a balance above one thousand euros, the rate increases slightly.
Yes, that's very easy. You choose the amount and the day of the month, and the transfer will be made automatically.
You'll need an ID and proof of address, like a recent utility bill. If you have them with you, we can complete everything in about fifteen minutes.
Thank you. Let me make copies of these, and then I'll prepare the contract. Please check the details before you sign.

scenarios.scenario: Blocking a lost debit card by phone
scenarios.context: A customer phones the bank after losing a debit card.

speakerA.en: Hello, I've lost my debit card, and I need to block it immediately. I think I left it in a restaurant yesterday evening.
I called the restaurant this morning, but they said they hadn't found it. I'm worried that someone might use it.
My name is David Klein, and my date of birth is the fourth of March, nineteen eighty-eight. The account number ends in 5521.
That's good to know. Have there been any payments in the last twenty-four hours that I didn't make?
How long will it take to receive a new card, and what can I do in the meantime? I don't have much cash with me.
Thank you for your help. I'll go to the branch this afternoon, and I'll be more careful in future.

speakerB.en: Good morning. I'm sorry to hear that. I'll block the card right away. Can you confirm your name and date of birth, please?
Thank you. Your card has now been blocked, so no one can use it anymore. I'll also check your account for any suspicious activity.
I can see that there were no payments after yesterday afternoon, which is a good sign. Everything seems to be in order.
A new card will be sent to your address within five working days. If you need it sooner, you can collect an emergency card from any branch.
In the meantime, you can withdraw cash at the counter with your ID, and you can use our mobile application to pay in shops.
You're welcome. If you find the old card, please destroy it. And call us again if you notice anything unusual on your statement.

scenarios.scenario: Reporting suspected card fraud to the bank
scenarios.context: A customer reports unauthorized transactions to a bank's fraud department.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm calling because I've noticed several transactions on my statement that I didn't make. The total is almost eight hundred euros, and the payments appear to have been made in another country.
I've still got the card with me, and I haven't shared the PIN with anybody. The only thing that I can think of is that I received an email last week asking me to confirm my details, which I did.
I realize now that it was probably a phishing attempt. The message looked completely genuine, with the bank's logo and everything, so I didn't suspect anything at the time.
I'd be very grateful if you could. Will I be able to recover the money, or does the fact that I responded to the email affect my rights?
That's a relief. In the meantime, I'll need access to my account for rent and bills. How soon can I receive a replacement card?
Thank you for your assistance. I'll be much more careful in future, and I'll warn my family about this kind of scam.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and I'm sorry that you've experienced this. Let me take some details so that we can investigate immediately. First, I'd like to block your card, to prevent any further unauthorized use.

Thank you. That information is helpful. If you gave your details in response to an email, that's the likely source. Fraudsters often impersonate banks very convincingly, and it's an increasingly common problem.
It happens to many people, and there's no need to blame yourself. These messages are professionally designed to look authentic. I'll file a formal report, which will be sent to our security team.

Under the regulations, you're generally entitled to a refund for unauthorized transactions, provided that you report them promptly, and that there was no gross negligence. We'll examine your case, but I'm optimistic.
A new card will arrive within three working days. For urgent expenses, you can use our mobile application to make transfers, and I'll arrange a temporary limit increase for the next week.
That's wise. Never click on links in emails asking for personal information, and remember that we'll never ask for your PIN or full password. If in doubt, call us directly.

scenarios.scenario: Applying for a loan and explaining your finances
scenarios.context: A customer discusses a loan application with a bank advisor.

speakerA.en: Thank you for seeing me. I'd like to apply for a loan to renovate my house. I've received estimates from several builders, and the work will cost about thirty thousand euros.
I've been in the same job for seven years, with a stable income. I also have some savings, which I could use as a deposit, but I'd rather keep a reserve for emergencies.
I see. What happens to the interest rate if I decide to repay the loan earlier than planned? I'd like to avoid any penalties, in case I receive a bonus at some point.
That's good to know. Is it better to choose a fixed rate, or a variable one? I've heard conflicting opinions, and I don't really know which is safer in the present economic climate.
That's a persuasive argument. I prefer predictability, so I think that I'll opt for the fixed rate, even if it's marginally higher at the beginning.
Thank you for explaining everything so clearly. I'll gather the documents that you mentioned, and I'll come back on Friday to submit the application.

speakerB.en: Of course. It's a significant project, so it's important to consider the terms carefully. Could you tell me about your employment situation and your current financial commitments?
That's a strong profile. Stability is exactly what we look for. Keeping a portion of your savings as a safety net is a sensible approach, and it won't negatively affect your application.
Our loans allow early repayment without a penalty for up to ten percent of the capital each year. Beyond that, there's a small fee, but we can discuss alternatives if you expect a larger sum.
A fixed rate gives you certainty, as your payments remain the same throughout the term. A variable rate may start lower, but it can increase, so it carries more risk if rates rise.
It's a sound choice for many borrowers, particularly if you have a limited margin in your monthly budget. I'll prepare a detailed offer so that you can compare it with other options.
You're welcome. You'll need your last three payslips, your tax return, and the builders' quotes. If you bring them, we should be able to give you an answer within a week.

scenarios.scenario: Setting up online banking and understanding security
scenarios.context: A customer asks a bank employee about online banking and how to stay safe.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I've been using my bank only through the branch for years, but I'd like to set up online banking now, because it's becoming so inconvenient to go there every time. How does it work?
I'm a little concerned about security, to be honest. I've heard so many stories about people losing money through online fraud, and I wouldn't like to be one of them.
That sounds reasonable. What should I do if I receive an email that appears to come from the bank, asking me to update my details? How can I tell whether it's genuine?
I see. And if I lose my phone, would someone else be able to access my account, since the application is installed on it?
That's reassuring. Could we go through the registration together, so that I'm sure that I'm doing it correctly? I'd rather do it here with your help than on my own at home.
Thank you so much. I feel much more confident now, and I'll tell my wife about the safety rules, since she's thinking of switching as well.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and welcome. Online banking is quite straightforward. I'll register you for the service, and you'll receive a login code by post within a few days. You can then use the mobile application or the website.

That's a very sensible concern. Our system uses two-step verification. Each time you log in or make a payment, you'll be asked to confirm the transaction with a code sent to your phone, so a thief couldn't get in with a password alone.

The most important rule is that the bank will never ask for your password or full details by email. If you receive a message of that kind, don't click on any links, and call us directly on the number printed on your card.
Your account is protected by a PIN or fingerprint, so a stranger couldn't open the application. And if you lose your phone, you can call us at any hour, and we'll block access immediately.
Of course. Let's sit down and do it now. I'll show you how to set up your PIN, how to check your balance, how to make a transfer, and how to set limits on your payments.
It's a pleasure. Please remember that you can always come back with any question. And if your wife would like to switch, she's welcome to come in, and I'll guide her through the process.

scenarios.scenario: Asking about refinancing a mortgage
scenarios.context: A homeowner discusses options for lowering monthly payments with a bank adviser.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I've had a mortgage with this bank for eight years, and I've been reading that interest rates have fallen recently. I'd like to find out whether it makes sense for me to refinance.

The balance is about one hundred and sixty thousand euros, with twenty-two years remaining. I currently pay a fixed rate of four and a half percent, which was reasonable at the time, but now seems high.

That's quite a difference. But I understand that there are costs associated with refinancing, such as fees and early repayment penalties. How much would those be, and how long would it take to recover them?
I see. In that case, would it be better to keep the same term and reduce the monthly payment, or to keep the payment the same and shorten the duration of the loan?
That's a useful way of looking at it. I think I'd prefer to shorten the term, since I'd like to be mortgage-free before I retire. Could you prepare a detailed comparison for me?
Thank you. I'll take the figures home, and discuss them with my wife. We'll let you know within a week, if we decide to go ahead.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon, and thank you for coming in. You're right that rates have dropped. Let me look at your current loan, and calculate how much you might save. Can you tell me the remaining balance and the term?

Currently, we can offer a fixed rate of three point two percent for a twenty-year term. That's more than a full percentage point lower, and on a loan of your size, it would reduce your monthly payment by about one hundred and eighty euros.

There's an early repayment fee of one percent of the outstanding balance, which would be sixteen hundred euros, plus about five hundred in administrative costs. With your savings, you would recover that in less than a year and a half.

That depends on your priorities. If you keep the same payment, you'd shorten the loan by about five years, and save a substantial amount of interest. If you reduce the payment, you gain flexibility, but pay more in the end.

Of course. I'll prepare a comparison of three scenarios: the lower payment, the shorter term, and a combination of the two. You'll see exactly how much you save in each case, and you can decide at your own pace.

That's a sensible approach. The offer will be valid for thirty days, so you have time. Please don't hesitate to contact me if you have any questions, and I'll gladly explain anything that isn't clear.

scenarios.scenario: Asking a bank adviser about a variable-rate mortgage
scenarios.context: A first-time buyer asks a bank adviser to explain the risks of choosing a variable-rate mortgage instead of a fixed-rate one.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'd appreciate it if you could explain the difference between a fixed and a variable mortgage. Once you've outlined the options, I hope to decide which one suits me. Should I be worried about interest rates rising?
I can afford about nine hundred a month, although I'd prefer to keep some margin. I'd appreciate it if you could tell me how much the payments might change. Should rates double, would I still manage?
Yes, about five thousand. I'd appreciate it if you could tell me which option is cheaper at the start, as the variable rate seems lower. Should I take it and switch later, if rates begin to rise?
I think I do, since it's my first home. I'd appreciate it if you could explain how long a fixed rate normally lasts. Should I choose five years or ten, and what happens when it ends?
That makes sense. I'd appreciate it if you could also mention any penalties for paying early. Should I receive a bonus, I'd like to reduce the loan. Is that allowed, and does it cost extra?

Yes, please. I'd appreciate it if you could email it by tomorrow, so I can discuss it with my partner. Should we have further questions, may we book another appointment? Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

speakerB.en: Good morning, and welcome. Of course. A fixed rate stays the same for a set period, whereas a variable rate changes with the market. Should rates rise, your payments would rise too. Once you've seen the figures, the difference will become clearer. What's your budget?

It depends on the loan size. Should rates rise by two percentage points, your payment would go up by about two hundred. Once you've considered that, I'd say you need a buffer. Do you have savings, in case that happens?

You can, although switching sometimes costs a fee. Once you've paid it, you'd lock in the new rate. Should you value predictability, a fixed rate is safer. On the other hand, it's usually a little higher. To be honest, many first-time buyers prefer certainty.

Five years is common. Once the period ends, you can renegotiate or move to another lender. Should you choose ten years, you'd get stability but less flexibility. I'd say five is a reasonable compromise, as long as you review the terms regularly.

Usually you can repay up to ten percent each year without charge. Once you exceed that, a small penalty applies. Should you plan larger repayments, we can adjust the contract. Would you like me to prepare a written comparison?

Of course. Once I've prepared the comparison, I'll send it this afternoon. Should you want to proceed, we can start the application next week. I'm glad we went through everything, since it's an important decision.

scenarios.scenario: Warning an elderly relative about an online banking scam
scenarios.context: A grandson warns his grandmother after she received a suspicious message that appears to come from her bank.

speakerA.en: Gran, I'm glad you showed me that message. It's a classic scam, and it's exactly the kind of thing that catches people out. It was clever of you to ask before clicking the link.

It's the fear that they're counting on. It's always the threat of losing something that makes people act quickly. What I'd notice first is the sender's address, which is nothing like your bank's. Real banks rarely ask you to click on links.

Honestly, it's the unexpected ones that need checking. It's wise to phone the bank using the number on your card, not the number in the message. As far as I'm concerned, that's the safest rule. Would you like me to write it down?

Gran, it's very important that you tell me about those calls. It was lucky that you hesitated. It's never the bank that asks for your full password or PIN. If anyone does, hang up immediately, and call me.

Keep a list of numbers by the phone: the bank, the police, and me. It's the list that will help you stay calm. Also, it's a good idea to set up alerts, so the bank texts you whenever money leaves your account.
Of course. It's a simple setting, and it'll take five minutes. It was good that you asked, and it's your caution that will protect you. I'll come on Sunday, and we'll go through everything together.

speakerB.en: Is it? It looked so official, and it was the bank's logo that convinced me. What makes you think it's false? The message said that my account would be closed, so I was frightened.
I never knew that. It was your grandfather who always handled these things, and it's only since he passed away that I've had to manage on my own. How do I know which messages are genuine?
Please do. It's my memory that worries me most. What should I do if someone calls me directly, pretending to be from the bank? It was a man who phoned last month, and I nearly gave him my details.
I will. It's reassuring to have you around, dear. On the other hand, I'd hate to bother you every time. What would you suggest I do when you're not available, in case there's a problem?
That sounds sensible. It was the thought of technology that frightened me, but it's the messages that I understand best. Could you set that up for me, since I wouldn't know where to begin?
Thank you, dear. It's you who makes me feel safe. I'll make some tea, and we can sit down properly. It was an unpleasant scare, but it's turned into something useful.

scenarios.scenario: Sending a letter or package
scenarios.context: At the post office, sending items and asking about postal services.

speakerA.en: I'd like to send this letter to the UK. How much will it cost?
Airmail, please. How long does it take?
Yes, it is. Here you are.
Here is the money. Thank you.
Do you have shipping boxes for sale?
speakerA.fa: جعبه‌های حمل و نقل برای فروش دارید؟

speakerA.en: I need to send this package by express mail. It's urgent.
speakerA.fa: باید این بسته رو با پست سریع بفرستم. اضطراریه.

speakerA.en: Can I track the parcel online once it's sent?
speakerA.fa: بعد از ارسال می‌تونم بسته رو آنلاین رهگیری کنم؟

speakerA.en: How many stamps do I need for a postcard to the US?
speakerA.fa: برای کارت‌پستال به آمریکا چند تمبر نیازه؟

speakerA.en: I'm sending some documents. Do I need to register them?
speakerA.fa: دارم چندتا مدرک می‌فرستم. باید ثبت‌شده (سفارشی) بفرستمشون؟

speakerB.en: By standard airmail, it's $5. By sea, it's cheaper but takes longer.
About five days. Is the address on the envelope?
Thank you. That is five dollars.
You're welcome. Have a nice day!
Yes, we have small, medium, and large boxes.
speakerB.fa: بله، جعبه کوچک، متوسط و بزرگ داریم.

speakerB.en: This package is quite heavy. Express shipping will cost more.
speakerB.fa: این بسته نسبتاً سنگینه. حمل سریع هزینه بیشتری داره.

speakerB.en: Yes, you'll receive a tracking number that you can use on our website.
speakerB.fa: بله، یه شماره رهگیری دریافت می‌کنید که می‌تونید توی وب‌سایت ما ازش استفاده کنید.

speakerB.en: You'll need two international stamps, which are $1.50 each.
speakerB.fa: به دو تا تمبر بین‌المللی نیاز دارید که هر کدوم ۱٫۵۰ دلار هست.

speakerB.en: I strongly recommend registered mail for important documents. It's safer.
speakerB.fa: به شدت برای مدارک مهم پست سفارشی رو توصیه می‌کنم. امن‌تره.

scenarios.scenario: Receiving or picking up a package
scenarios.context: Someone has received a package or goes to collect it.

speakerA.en: Has my package arrived yet?
Great! Can I get it now?
Yes, here it is.
OK. Thank you very much.
I got a notification that my delivery is at the post office. Can I pick it up?
speakerA.fa: یه اعلان گرفتم که بسته‌ام توی اداره پسته. می‌تونم بردارمش؟

speakerA.en: What time does the post office open?
speakerA.fa: اداره پست چه ساعتی باز می‌شه؟

speakerA.en: I missed the delivery. How can I reschedule?
speakerA.fa: تحویل رو از دست دادم. چطور می‌تونم دوباره تنظیمش کنم؟

speakerA.en: The package was delivered to the wrong address. What should I do?
speakerA.fa: بسته به آدرس اشتباه تحویل داده شده. چیکار کنم؟

speakerB.en: Let me check the system. I think it arrived yesterday.
Yes. Do you have your ID card?
Thank you. Please sign here.
You're welcome. Here is your package.
Yes, you'll need to bring your ID and the collection notice.
speakerB.fa: بله، باید کارت شناسایی و اعلان دریافت رو بیارید.

speakerB.en: We open at 8:30 AM and close at 5 PM on weekdays.
speakerB.fa: روزهای کاری ساعت ۸:۳۰ صبح باز و ۵ عصر تعطیل می‌شیم.

speakerB.en: You can call the courier company and ask for a redelivery.
speakerB.fa: می‌تونید به شرکت پیک زنگ بزنید و درخواست تحویل مجدد بدید.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry about that. We'll launch an investigation and try to locate it.
speakerB.fa: از این موضوع متأسفم. ما تحقیقات رو شروع می‌کنیم و سعی می‌کنیم پیداش کنیم.

To Canada.

How long will it take to arrive in Canada?
Do you have any stamps with a special design?
Can I buy a book of ten stamps?
Do the stamps have an expiry date?
Can I send a registered letter?
Could I get a stamp for a letter inside the country, too?
That's all. Thank you for your help.

speakerB.en: For letters or postcards?
Where are they going?

It is twelve dollars.
Yes, you can. Please put your card here.
Certainly. It will arrive in two or three days.
Yes, standard mail takes a week, and it costs half the price.
Yes, please write the contents and the value.
Not automatically. Insurance costs four dollars more.
Yes, I'll give you a tracking number on your receipt.
Yes, it does. You can use the tape on that table.
Yes, but you need to mark the box as 'fragile'.
Then you can make a claim, and we'll check it right away.

Write it here, in the box.

Yes, otherwise the mail carrier can't find the right door.
Of course. Here's a new one.
Write your full name and your address in the top left corner.
Use English or the local language, and write the country name clearly.
No, please use a pen. Pencil can fade.
Sure. Everything looks fine now.

Tomorrow? That's good. Thank you.

What if it doesn't arrive by Friday?

Nobody was home when the courier came. What happens now?

Thank you for explaining everything.

Do you have the tracking number?
Let me check. It will arrive tomorrow.
You're welcome. Sorry for the problem.
Let me check the system. It was shipped on the third.
Yes, it's still there. There were delays because of the weather.
It should arrive by Friday, but we can't be sure.
Then please come back, and we'll start a search for it.
Yes, we can change the address. I'll update it now.
They left a notice. You can collect it from the local office.
Yes, bring the notice and a photo ID.
You're welcome. We apologize for the delay.

scenarios.scenario: Finding a mailbox
scenarios.context: A person asks where to mail a letter and when the post office is open.

What time is the last collection today?
Is there another mailbox closer to the station?
How long will my letter take to arrive if I post it now?
What time does the post office open on weekdays?
Does the post office also sell envelopes?
Can I send a letter without a stamp?
Is there a post office near the university?

speakerB.en: It's next to the bank.
No, it's two minutes on foot.
Yes, but only until twelve.
No problem. Have a good day!
It's at five o'clock. The mail will go out this evening.
Yes, there's a red one in front of the station.
Probably two days, if it's within the country.
It opens at eight and closes at six.
Yes, you can buy them at the counter.
No, you need a stamp, or the letter will be returned.
Yes, on the main street, across from the bookshop.
You're welcome. It's right next to the bus stop.

scenarios.scenario: Sending a package abroad
scenarios.context: A customer wants to send a parcel overseas.

speakerA.en: Hello, I'd like to send this package to Canada. How long will it take?
How much more does the express option cost?
It's a birthday gift, so I'd like it to arrive by the end of next week.
Not yet. What do I need to write on it?

speakerB.en: By standard mail, about two weeks. With express service, it takes four or five days.
Twenty dollars more. For a package of this weight, the total would be thirty-five.
Then I'd recommend express. Have you filled in the customs form?
A description of the contents and their value. I'll give you the form.

scenarios.scenario: Picking up a missed delivery
scenarios.context: A person goes to the post office after missing a delivery.

speakerA.en: Hi, I received a note saying that a courier tried to deliver a parcel while I was out.
Here it is. The tracking number is at the bottom.
Of course. Here's my driver's license. Do I need to pay anything?
Thanks. In the future, can I arrange for packages to be delivered to a neighbor?

speakerB.en: May I see the note, please? I'll check whether it's here.
Yes, we have it. Could I see some ID, please?
No, but you'll need to sign for it. It's quite heavy, so be careful.
Yes, you can set that up on the website, or you can choose a collection point.

scenarios.scenario: Sending a registered letter
scenarios.context: A customer wants to send an important document.

speakerA.en: I need to send some important documents, and I want to be sure they arrive safely.
Does the recipient have to sign for it?
How much does it cost, and how long does it usually take?
That's fine. Could you also check whether the address is complete?

speakerB.en: In that case, I'd suggest registered mail. You get a receipt and can track the letter.
Yes, and you'll receive a confirmation once it has been delivered.
It's eight dollars, and it normally arrives within two or three working days.
It looks right, but the postal code is missing. Could you add it, please?

scenarios.scenario: Tracking a delayed international parcel
scenarios.context: A customer inquires about a package that has been missing for weeks.

speakerA.en: I sent a parcel to my sister in Australia a month ago, and it still hasn't arrived. Could you trace it for me?
Here they are. The last update says it left the country, but nothing has been recorded since.
A month seems excessive, though. The contents were quite valuable, and I insured them.
And if it turns out to be lost, how do I claim on the insurance?

speakerB.en: Certainly. Do you have the tracking number and the receipt from when you posted it?
That's not unusual with international shipments. Sometimes the scans aren't uploaded until the parcel clears customs.
In that case, I'll open an inquiry with the postal service in the destination country. It may take a couple of weeks to get a response.
You'd fill in a claim form, and we'd need proof of the item's value, such as a receipt.

scenarios.scenario: Dealing with a mix-up in mail delivery
scenarios.context: A resident complains to the post office about misdelivered letters.

speakerA.en: For the past two months, I've been receiving mail intended for the people who lived in my apartment before me.
I have, repeatedly, but it doesn't seem to make a difference. Meanwhile, some of my own mail is going astray.
A bank statement and a letter from my insurer haven't arrived, and I'm worried about the risk of identity theft.
Thank you. Could you also tell me how I can make sure my mail is redirected properly in the future?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry for the inconvenience. Have you tried writing 'not at this address' and returning the items?
That's more serious. Could you tell me whether anything important has gone missing?
I'll file a formal complaint and ask the local depot to update their records with your name.
You can register on our website, or I can help you fill in a form at the counter right now.

scenarios.scenario: Sending an oversized or unusual item
scenarios.context: A customer asks about shipping a fragile object.

speakerA.en: I need to send a ceramic vase to a friend, and I'm terrified it will arrive in pieces.
I wrapped it in newspaper and put it in a shoebox, but I doubt that's sufficient.
Would that add considerably to the cost? I'm already paying a lot for express delivery.
That seems sensible. How much coverage can I get for a vase worth around three hundred dollars?

speakerB.en: How is it currently packed? We have specialized boxes and padding for fragile items.
I wouldn't risk it. A sturdier box with bubble wrap and a layer of foam on all sides is what's needed.
The packaging itself is inexpensive, but I'd advise insuring the parcel as well, in case of damage.
We can insure it up to five hundred for a small fee, and I'll mark the box as fragile.

scenarios.scenario: Filing a claim for a damaged parcel
scenarios.context: A customer reports a package that arrived broken and asks about compensation.

speakerA.en: I'd like to file a claim. A package I sent to my sister arrived with its contents shattered, even though I'd labeled it fragile.
I did, and I've brought the receipt and photographs of the damaged contents that my sister sent.
She's kept it, but it will take a few days to reach me. Will that delay the claim?
And how long does the process usually take? The item was a gift, and I'd like to replace it as soon as possible.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry to hear that. Did you purchase insurance when you sent it, and do you have the receipt?
That's very helpful. I'll need the original packaging as well, since the assessor will want to examine how it was packed.
It won't, provided you submit the form today. The assessment can follow once the packaging arrives.
Typically three to four weeks. If the claim is approved, you'll be reimbursed up to the insured value.

scenarios.scenario: Clearing customs on an incoming package
scenarios.context: A customer queries unexpected import charges on a parcel from abroad.

speakerA.en: I've received a notice that I owe import duty on a parcel from overseas, but nobody told me about this when I ordered it.
The item cost eighty dollars. The notice asks for nearly thirty in charges, which seems disproportionate.
Here it is. I also notice that the declared value appears higher than what I actually paid.
I have the order confirmation on my phone. Would a screenshot suffice, or do I need a printed invoice?

speakerB.en: I understand the surprise. Goods valued above a certain threshold are subject to duty and tax, regardless of what the seller said.
That figure includes sales tax and a handling fee, which we charge for processing the customs declaration. May I see the paperwork?
That could indeed be the cause. If the seller overstated it, you can dispute the assessment with proof of purchase.
A digital copy is fine. Submit it with the dispute form, and the charges will be recalculated before the parcel is released.

scenarios.scenario: Setting up mail forwarding after moving abroad
scenarios.context: A customer arranges for his mail to follow him to a new country.

speakerA.en: I'm moving abroad next month, and I'd like to arrange for my mail to be forwarded to my new address. Is that possible?
Probably two years, so I'd rather not change every sender's records immediately. I'd prefer a gradual transition.
What happens with registered letters or official documents? I can't afford to miss anything from the tax office.
That seems wise. I assume the service must be paid for in advance?

speakerB.en: It is, though international forwarding is more complicated than domestic. How long will you be at the new address?
In that case, I'd suggest a twelve-month forwarding service, renewable if necessary. We can also hold non-urgent items at the depot.
Those require a signature, so they'll be forwarded by tracked courier at an additional cost. I'd recommend informing the tax office directly as well.
Yes, the fee covers the full period. If you'd like, I can fill in the form now, and you can sign it after confirming your new address.

scenarios.scenario: Tracking a missing international parcel
scenarios.context: A customer pursues a package that has stalled somewhere in transit.

speakerA.en: I'm inquiring about a parcel that was dispatched three weeks ago. The tracking shows it arrived at a sorting center and then simply vanished.
That's what troubles me. It contained a gift for a colleague's wedding, and the date is fast approaching.
That's rather longer than I'd hoped. Is there any way to expedite it, given the circumstances?
I have it here, along with the insurance receipt. Would a claim be possible if it's not found?

speakerB.en: I'm sorry about that. Let me see what the system says. Yes, it was scanned at the border but has not been logged since.
I'll open a formal inquiry, which will prompt a search at the relevant facilities. It can take up to ten working days.
I can flag it as urgent, though I can't guarantee faster results. In the meantime, I'd recommend keeping your proof of postage.
Yes, if the parcel hasn't surfaced after the inquiry. I'll provide you with the form and a reference number to keep.

scenarios.scenario: Sending a fragile and valuable item abroad
scenarios.context: A customer asks for guidance on posting a delicate antique safely.

speakerA.en: I need to send an antique vase to a buyer overseas. It's extremely fragile, and I'm worried about it surviving the journey.
And in terms of insurance, what cover would be appropriate? Its value is considerable.
What about customs? The buyer mentioned that there may be import duties.
I'd never dream of it. I'd rather pay the proper charges than risk the vase being seized.

speakerB.en: Understandable. I'd recommend a double-boxing method, with the vase wrapped in bubble film and cushioned within a smaller box inside a larger one.
You can declare its value and purchase additional cover, though I'd advise requesting a signature on delivery so it can't be left unattended.
You'll need to complete a customs declaration describing the contents and their value accurately. Understating it could lead to penalties.
A wise attitude. I'll provide the forms, and you can pack it here if you'd like our staff to inspect the arrangement.

scenarios.scenario: Resolving a redirected mail issue after moving house
scenarios.context: A resident deals with letters that are still arriving at an old address.

speakerA.en: I moved six weeks ago and arranged for my mail to be forwarded, yet important correspondence still seems to be going to my old address.
That explains a great deal. My partner's letters have been going astray, including some from the tax authority.
I've been working through that list, though it's astonishing how many organizations I've neglected to inform.
That would be helpful, provided it doesn't impose on them unduly. I'd hate to become a nuisance to strangers.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry for the inconvenience. Let me check the records. It seems the redirection was set up for only one name, not the whole household.
I can amend the redirection immediately and extend it for another twelve months, but you'll also need to notify the senders directly.
It's a common oversight. In the meantime, I could arrange for the new occupants to return any letters they receive.
It's a routine process, and there's no obligation on their part. I'll send them a polite note this afternoon.

scenarios.scenario: Sending a gift abroad
scenarios.context: A customer sends a birthday gift to another country.

speakerA.en: Hello. I'd like to send this gift to Canada.
How long will it take to arrive?
My friend's birthday is in ten days. Will it arrive in time?
Here is the address. How much is it?

speakerB.en: Certainly. Please put it on the scale.
About a week by air mail.
Yes, it should. Please write the address clearly.
That's twenty-two dollars. You can pay at the counter.

scenarios.scenario: Changing an address
scenarios.context: A customer asks the post office about moving house.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm moving next month. What should I do about my mail?
Will my letters come to my new home?
Do I need to show any documents?
I'll bring them tomorrow. Thank you.

speakerB.en: You can fill in this form with your new address.
Yes, for six months after the change.
Yes, your ID card and a bill with the new address.
You're welcome. Have a nice day.

scenarios.scenario: Tracking a lost parcel
scenarios.context: A customer asks a post office clerk about a parcel that has not arrived.

speakerA.en: Hello, I'm waiting for a parcel that was supposed to arrive last week.
Of course. It's this one, starting with RB.
So what should I do? It contains an important document.
Could you give me a reference number in case I need to call?

speakerB.en: May I see your tracking number, please?
The system says it left the sorting center five days ago, but it hasn't been delivered.
I'll open an investigation, and we'll contact you within three working days.
Certainly. I'll write it on this form for you.

scenarios.scenario: Sending documents internationally
scenarios.context: A customer sends important papers to another country.

speakerA.en: I need to send some documents to Australia. What's the fastest way?
How much would it cost for a small envelope?
Do I need to fill in a customs form?
It's only papers. Can the receiver sign for it on delivery?

speakerB.en: Express service takes two to three days, but it's more expensive.
Around forty dollars, including tracking and insurance.
Yes, but only if the envelope contains anything other than paper.
Yes, and you'll get an email as soon as it's delivered.

scenarios.scenario: Shipping a gift parcel to another country
scenarios.context: A customer asks about shipping options and customs for an international parcel.

speakerA.en: Hello. I'd like to send this package to my cousin in Canada. Could you tell me how long it will take and what it costs?
It contains a few books and some clothes. The weight is about three kilos. I'd like it to arrive before her birthday on the twentieth.
Standard delivery is cheaper, but I'm afraid that it won't arrive in time. What's the difference in price for the faster one?
I'll take the express service, then. Do I need to fill in any forms for the customs, since it's going to another country?
That's good to know. Can I track the parcel online, so that I can tell my cousin when to expect it?
Perfect. Here's the address. Thank you for your help. I hope it gets there on time.

speakerB.en: Good morning. Let me weigh it first. Three kilos... Where in Canada is it going, and what's inside the package?
Standard delivery takes about two weeks and costs thirty euros. The express service takes four to five days, and costs fifty-five euros.
If you want it to arrive by the twentieth, then express is the only safe option. We can send it today, and it should be there on Monday.
Yes, you need to fill in this customs declaration. Write a short description of the contents and their approximate value, and sign it at the bottom.
Of course. I'll give you a tracking number, and you can enter it on our website to see where your package is at any time.
You're welcome. I've attached the form, so everything is ready. If there's any delay, please contact us with the tracking number.

scenarios.scenario: Collecting a parcel that couldn't be delivered
scenarios.context: A resident goes to the post office to pick up a package after a failed delivery.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. I received a note saying that a courier tried to deliver a parcel to me yesterday, but I wasn't at home.
I was at work, and I didn't expect anything, so I didn't ask anyone to wait for it. Is it ready for collection?
Here's the note, and my passport. The parcel should be in my name. It's something that I ordered online last week.
Thank you. Is there a fee for storing it, or is it free to collect, since the delivery was attempted?
I see. For the future, is there any way to choose the delivery time, so that I'm sure to be at home?
That's very helpful. I'll sign up for that service. Thank you for your time, and have a good day.

speakerB.en: Good afternoon. Let me check. May I see the note, please, and some identification, so that I can find your parcel?
I'll go and look. It's possible that it's still at the sorting center, but normally parcels are brought here the next day.
Yes, it's here. Could you sign here, please? I need to make sure that the person collecting it is the one named on the label.
There's no fee if you collect it within seven days. After that, we charge a small amount for each day that it stays in our storage.
Yes, you can register for our notification service. We'll send you a text message with a delivery window, and you can change it if it doesn't suit you.
You're welcome. Here's your parcel. It's quite heavy, so be careful when you carry it. Have a pleasant afternoon.

scenarios.scenario: Resolving a lost international shipment
scenarios.context: A customer pursues a missing parcel with the postal service and discusses compensation.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'm here regarding a parcel that I sent to Australia six weeks ago. According to the tracking information, it was last scanned at your sorting center, and nothing has happened since.
The package contained a handmade gift for my sister's wedding, which took me months to make, and I insured it for two hundred euros. It's irreplaceable, so I'm desperate to find it.
I appreciate your help. How long will it take for the investigation to be completed? The wedding is in a month, and if it can't be found, I need to make alternative arrangements.
I understand that the process can't be rushed, but would it be possible to have a preliminary answer within a week? I'd like to know whether I should begin making another gift.
That seems acceptable. And if the parcel is declared lost, how is the compensation calculated? Is it based on the value I declared, or on the cost of the materials?
Thank you for being so helpful. I'll fill in the form, and I'll bring the receipt and a photograph of the item tomorrow.

speakerB.en: Good morning. I'm sorry to hear about the difficulty. Let me look up the tracking number. Indeed, it appears that the last recorded scan was on the second of the month at our international center.

I can imagine how upsetting that is. I'll open a formal inquiry with the sorting center and the destination country's postal service. They'll trace the parcel along the entire route, and we'll find out where it went missing.
Investigations of this kind usually take between two and six weeks, depending on how quickly the other postal service responds. I'll mark the case as urgent, since you've mentioned the wedding.
I'll ask for an interim update after seven days. I can't promise that they'll have found anything by then, but I'll contact you either way, so that you can plan accordingly.

If it's confirmed as lost, you'll receive the insured amount, which is two hundred euros in your case. Sentimental value, unfortunately, isn't covered, but we'll make sure that the claim is processed without delay.
It's the least I can do. Please bring the documents tomorrow, and ask for me by name. I'll make sure that your case is handled with priority.

scenarios.scenario: Debating the future of traditional mail
scenarios.context: Two friends discuss whether postal services will survive in the digital age.

speakerA.en: I sent a handwritten letter to my grandmother last week, and it occurred to me that I can't remember the last time I'd posted one. Do you think traditional mail has a future?
